text: During a Daily Scrum, a senior team member repeatedly criticizes junior members' ideas, causing them to withdraw from participating. What should the Scrum Master do first?

options.A: Ask the Product Owner to resolve the issue
options.B: Coach the senior member privately on the impact of their behavior and facilitate a team working agreement
options.C: Remove the senior member from the team
options.D: Do nothing, since the Daily Scrum belongs to the development team

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master is a servant-leader who protects psychological safety; private coaching followed by a team working agreement is the appropriate response.

text: A project manager notices that a key stakeholder consistently changes requirements late in the schedule, causing confusion for the team. What communication competency is most useful here?

options.A: Ignore the stakeholder's requests going forward
options.B: Exclude the stakeholder from future meetings
options.C: Accept every change immediately without documentation
options.D: Clarify the formal change management process with the stakeholder and document each request for traceability

justification: Correct: clarifying and enforcing the formal change management process channels requests while ensuring traceability and consistency for the team.

text: A new team member joins an established Scrum team and feels lost among existing practices. Which action best supports their integration?

options.A: Give them only technical documentation with no human support
options.B: Let them observe without intervention for several sprints
options.C: Assign them immediately to the most complex tasks to accelerate learning
options.D: Organize structured onboarding including the team's working agreement, a peer mentor, and regular check-ins

justification: Correct: structured onboarding with peer mentoring fosters rapid integration and understanding of team norms.

text: Two team members from different departments disagree persistently about resource priorities. Which conflict resolution style prioritizes long-term relationships over immediate gain?

options.A: Collaborate/Problem Solve
options.B: Withdraw/Avoid
options.C: Smooth/Accommodate
options.D: Force/Direct

justification: Correct: accommodating means yielding one's own needs to preserve harmony and the long-term relationship.

text: A Scrum Master notices the team never questions the estimates of the most senior member, even when they seem unrealistic. What bias does this illustrate and what should be done?

options.A: Remove team estimation entirely
options.B: Ask the senior member to estimate everything alone from now on
options.C: No bias, it's normal to trust experience
options.D: An authority bias; introduce anonymous voting (Planning Poker) so everyone estimates independently before discussion

justification: Correct: Planning Poker with simultaneous, anonymous voting reduces authority influence and encourages fairer collective estimation.

text: A project manager must resolve a disagreement between two sub-teams that formed informally, creating unhealthy competition. What leadership action is most appropriate?

options.A: Foster shared cross-functional goals and activities to rebuild a unified team identity and reduce fragmentation
options.B: Ignore the fragmentation as long as the work progresses
options.C: Disband the entire team and start over
options.D: Encourage the competition between sub-groups to stimulate performance

justification: Correct: shared cross-functional goals and activities rebuild a unified team identity and reduce competing sub-group dynamics.

text: A junior Product Owner lacks confidence to make difficult prioritization decisions and systematically escalates to their manager. What action best supports their development?

options.A: Coach the PO on prioritization techniques and gradually build their decision-making autonomy, reinforcing their legitimacy with management
options.B: Make the prioritization decisions on their behalf
options.C: Report their lack of competence to leadership for replacement
options.D: Ignore the situation since it's not the team's problem

justification: Correct: progressive coaching and reinforcing the PO's legitimacy with management builds durable autonomy.

text: A project manager must select the most appropriate leadership style for a team member with low competence but high commitment to a new task. Which situational leadership style is most appropriate?

options.A: Supporting only, with no direction
options.B: Directing/Coaching
options.C: Delegating
options.D: Laissez-faire

justification: Correct: for low competence but high commitment, a directing/coaching style provides the guidance needed while nurturing enthusiasm.

text: An Agile Coach observes that a high-performing team shows signs of burnout (rising absenteeism, irritability). What is the priority action to preserve sustainable performance?

options.A: Investigate the signs of burnout, adjust workload, and reinforce the agile principle of sustainable pace
options.B: Ignore the signs as long as velocity remains stable
options.C: Maintain the same pace since results are excellent
options.D: Praise the team and give them even more work to capitalize on their performance

justification: Correct: investigating and adjusting workload per the sustainable pace principle prevents burnout and preserves long-term performance.

text: A project manager must recognize an exceptional team contribution with no budget available for a financial bonus. Which non-financial recognition is most effective?

options.A: Promise a future bonus with no certainty of delivering it
options.B: Do nothing due to lack of budget
options.C: Ignore the contribution to avoid creating expectations for others
options.D: Public recognition of the contribution, professional development opportunities, and expanded responsibilities

justification: Correct: public recognition and development opportunities are powerful non-financial motivators aligned with esteem and achievement needs.

text: In a retrospective, a team member expresses chronic feelings of work overload. What is the Scrum Master's most appropriate response?

options.A: Ignore it and wait for the person to adapt
options.B: Collectively explore the causes (over-commitment, technical debt, interruptions) and adjust future workload with the team
options.C: Downplay the remark since sprints are supposed to be intense
options.D: Add more tasks to test their resilience

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master must facilitate a collective exploration of root causes and adjust future planning for a sustainable pace.

text: A project manager must choose between two internal candidates for a key role: one has more technical experience, the other has better collaborative skills in a highly interdependent team context. Which factor should weigh most heavily here?

options.A: The lowest salary
options.B: Technical experience only, since it always takes priority
options.C: Seniority within the organization
options.D: Collaborative skills, given the team's high interdependence for this role

justification: Correct: in a highly interdependent team, collaborative and interpersonal skills often have more impact on overall performance than technical expertise alone.

text: A Product Owner frequently changes sprint priorities mid-sprint, disrupting the development team. What is the Scrum Master's best action?

options.A: Let the team decide alone without involving the PO
options.B: Prevent the PO from attending ceremonies
options.C: Accept all changes without discussion to avoid upsetting the PO
options.D: Coach the PO on the principle of sprint immutability and channel new priorities into the product backlog for the next sprint

justification: Correct: the Scrum Guide protects sprint content; the Scrum Master should coach the PO on this principle while respecting their authority over the backlog.

text: A project manager must manage a virtual team spread across multiple time zones. Which practice most improves effective collaboration?

options.A: Schedule all meetings in the project manager's time zone regardless of impact
options.B: Establish agreed overlapping working hours, document decisions in writing, and use asynchronous collaboration tools
options.C: Schedule no synchronous meetings at all
options.D: Limit all communication to email only

justification: Correct: agreed overlap hours, written documentation of decisions, and asynchronous tools optimize collaboration for a multi-timezone virtual team.

text: A Product Owner lacks availability to answer the team's questions during the sprint, slowing development. What is the best durable solution?

options.A: Halt the sprint until the PO is available
options.B: Ignore the problem and hope for spontaneous improvement
options.C: Negotiate dedicated availability windows with the PO or designate a trained proxy PO for routine decisions
options.D: The team makes all product decisions without the PO permanently

justification: Correct: negotiating dedicated windows or establishing a trained proxy PO maintains velocity while respecting the PO's role on strategic decisions.

text: A project manager notices a team member excels technically but lacks communication skills, causing friction with others. What development action is most appropriate?

options.A: Offer coaching or training in communication skills to complement their recognized technical expertise
options.B: Ignore the problem since technical skills compensate
options.C: Sanction them for their lack of relational skills
options.D: Remove them from all interactions with other members

justification: Correct: targeted communication skills development complements their technical expertise and reduces observed friction.

text: During a sprint review, a stakeholder harshly criticizes the presented work in front of the whole team, demoralizing developers. What is the Scrum Master's best immediate reaction?

options.A: Let the situation unfold without intervening
options.B: Politely refocus the discussion on constructive, solution-oriented feedback, then privately address the tone with the stakeholder afterward
options.C: Immediately cancel the sprint review
options.D: Respond with the same aggressiveness to defend the team

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master facilitates by constructively refocusing the discussion in the moment, then addresses the problematic tone privately to preserve the relationship and psychological safety.

text: A project manager must engage a highly influential but low-interest stakeholder, per the power/interest grid. Which stakeholder management strategy is appropriate?

options.A: Inform them in detail about everything, as if they had high interest
options.B: Manage closely with detailed daily meetings
options.C: Keep satisfied with infrequent, high-level updates
options.D: Monitor only, with no communication

justification: Correct: for high power and low interest, the 'Keep Satisfied' strategy provides infrequent, sufficient high-level information to maintain their support.

text: An Agile Coach notices that one team resists all retrospectives, deeming them useless. What approach should be taken first?

options.A: Mandate participation without explanation
options.B: Replace the entire team
options.C: Understand the reasons behind the negative perception and co-create a retrospective format that delivers immediate perceived value
options.D: Remove retrospectives for this team

justification: Correct: understanding the causes of the negative perception (poorly facilitated retros, no follow-through on actions) allows co-creating a format that restores perceived value.

text: A project manager must manage a team with a persistent personality conflict despite several mediation attempts. What is the appropriate last-resort option?

options.A: Ignore the conflict indefinitely
options.B: Immediately fire both individuals without an HR process
options.C: Force the two individuals to work even more closely together
options.D: Consider reorganizing roles or separating tasks between the two individuals as a last resort after mediation has failed

justification: Correct: after mediation fails, reorganizing roles or separating tasks is a pragmatic last resort to preserve collective performance.

text: A distributed agile team across several countries has seen a decline in social cohesion since moving to 100% remote work. What action best rebuilds team connection?

options.A: Increase only the frequency of formal work meetings
options.B: Organize dedicated informal moments (virtual coffees, icebreakers) alongside formal ceremonies to reinforce human connection
options.C: Ban all informal communication to focus on productivity
options.D: Ignore the decline in social cohesion since it doesn't affect performance

justification: Correct: dedicated informal moments recreate the social bond lost from physical proximity, fostering cohesion and team psychological safety.

text: A project manager must integrate a team member with a disability requiring reasonable accommodations. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Systematically refuse any special accommodation
options.B: Remove the person from the project to avoid complications
options.C: Discuss with the person to understand their specific needs and implement reasonable accommodations in coordination with HR
options.D: Ignore the accommodation request to avoid setting a precedent

justification: Correct: discussing specific needs and coordinating with HR for reasonable accommodations is the inclusive and legally compliant appropriate practice.

text: A Scrum Master notices a highly technically skilled member adopts a dismissive tone toward others' questions, hindering their learning. What action should the Scrum Master take?

options.A: Ignore the situation as long as delivery isn't affected
options.B: Address the behavior directly with the person, explain its negative impact on collective learning and psychological safety, and set clear expectations of mutual respect
options.C: Tolerate the behavior because their technical skills are valuable to the team
options.D: Discourage other members from asking questions to avoid friction

justification: Correct: directly addressing the behavior with clear expectations of mutual respect protects psychological safety and collective learning without denying the person's technical value.

text: A project manager must decide how to allocate work when two team members have very different competence levels for the same critical task. What is the most balanced approach?

options.A: Consistently assign all critical tasks to the more competent member, exhausting their availability
options.B: Assign the critical task only to the less experienced member to challenge them
options.C: Combine the more competent member as lead with mentoring of the less experienced member to develop their skills while securing delivery
options.D: Split the work equally without regard to competence level

justification: Correct: combining leadership from the experienced member with structured mentoring secures delivery while developing team skills.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team member consistently criticizes group decisions after the fact, without ever speaking up during meetings. What phenomenon does this illustrate, and what action should be taken?

options.A: This illustrates a lack of psychological safety in meetings; create alternative expression spaces and explicitly encourage speaking up during decisions, not after
options.B: Exclude this member from future decisions
options.C: Systematically ignore their after-the-fact criticism
options.D: This is normal and has no consequences for the team

justification: Correct: systematic after-the-fact criticism without in-meeting expression often signals a lack of psychological safety; alternative spaces and explicit encouragement foster more constructive real-time expression.

text: A project manager must motivate a temporary team assembled only for the duration of the project, with a risk of demotivation due to lack of long-term prospects. What motivational action is appropriate?

options.A: Ignore the topic since the team is temporary anyway
options.B: Clarify project objectives and offer learning and skill development opportunities valuable for members' future careers
options.C: Systematically promise permanent positions with no certainty
options.D: Lower performance expectations to compensate for the lack of prospects

justification: Correct: offering valuable learning and career development opportunities is durable intrinsic motivation, even for a temporary team.

text: A Product Owner and the development team have divergent views on 'value' for a feature (one prioritizes revenue, the other user experience). Which approach best resolves this disagreement?

options.A: Impose the PO's view without discussion, since they have backlog authority
options.B: Let the development team alone decide the definition of value
options.C: Facilitate an explicit discussion on value criteria (business, user, technical) to build a shared, balanced definition
options.D: Ignore the disagreement and move forward without alignment

justification: Correct: building a shared, multidimensional definition of value (business, user, technical) aligns team and PO on common priorities.

text: A project manager must decide how to give corrective feedback to a team member about a repeated mistake. Which feedback approach is most constructive?

options.A: Send a formal email without any verbal discussion
options.B: Publicly criticize in front of the whole team to make a lasting impression
options.C: Avoid all feedback to prevent tension
options.D: Give private, factual feedback based on specific examples and oriented toward solutions

justification: Correct: effective feedback is private, factual, specific, and solution-oriented for concrete improvement.

text: A Scrum Master must integrate an external consultant for a one-off expertise on a complex technical component. Which action best facilitates their integration without disrupting team dynamics?

options.A: Never document their work to stay flexible
options.B: Include them in relevant ceremonies, clarify the scope and duration of their engagement, and facilitate knowledge transfer to the permanent team
options.C: Exclude them from all ceremonies so as not to slow the team down
options.D: Give them final decision authority over the entire architecture

justification: Correct: targeted inclusion, clear scope, and planned knowledge transfer maximize the value of external expertise while preserving the permanent team's autonomy.

text: A project manager notices that a stakeholder has a misunderstanding of the project scope, which could generate unrealistic expectations. What communication action is a priority?

options.A: Proactively clarify the scope with concrete examples and document a shared understanding to prevent future misunderstandings
options.B: Avoid any contact with this stakeholder
options.C: Ignore the misunderstanding until it causes a visible problem
options.D: Let the stakeholder discover reality at the time of delivery

justification: Correct: proactively clarifying with concrete examples and documenting shared understanding prevents costly misunderstandings later in the project.

text: An experienced agile team asks the Scrum Master to reduce their involvement, feeling sufficiently autonomous. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Categorically refuse to reduce their involvement
options.B: Jointly assess where real autonomy exists, shift the role toward on-demand coaching and facilitation, while remaining available for organizational impediments
options.C: Leave the team entirely with no transition
options.D: Ignore the team's request

justification: Correct: progressively shifting toward on-demand coaching while remaining available for organizational impediments respects growing autonomy while maintaining a safety net.

text: A project manager must gain buy-in from a skeptical sponsor regarding the value of an enhanced risk management methodology. Which negotiation and influence approach is most effective?

options.A: Immediately abandon the idea in the face of skepticism
options.B: Bypass the sponsor and implement the method without their approval
options.C: Present concrete data (costs avoided, similar project examples) demonstrating the added value of the proposed approach
options.D: Impose the method without justification

justification: Correct: evidence-based influence (return on investment, benchmarks) is the most effective technique to convince a skeptical decision-maker.

text: A Scrum Master notices the team systematically blames external factors for problems without ever examining its own practices. What intervention fosters a culture of accountability?

options.A: Use retrospective techniques focused on what the team actually controls (circle of influence) to refocus on possible internal actions
options.B: Confirm that problems always come from outside
options.C: Publicly blame the team for its lack of accountability
options.D: Ignore the blame pattern

justification: Correct: refocusing the retrospective on the team's 'circle of influence' helps identify concrete internal actions, fostering accountability.

text: A project manager must decide how to manage a highly skilled team member who consistently refuses to document their work, creating a bus factor risk. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Explain the organizational risk of lacking documentation and make documentation an explicit performance expectation
options.B: Document their work for them indefinitely
options.C: Replace them immediately without discussion
options.D: Accept the situation because their technical skills are indispensable

justification: Correct: explaining the organizational risk and making documentation an explicit performance expectation holds the person accountable while reducing dependency risk.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team avoids discussing difficult topics in retrospectives to preserve a harmonious atmosphere. What risk does this represent, and what action should be taken?

options.A: No risk, a good atmosphere is more important than anything else
options.B: Remove retrospectives since they serve no purpose in this case
options.C: Force artificial conflicts to test the team
options.D: Risk of accumulating unresolved issues (artificial harmony); introduce structured techniques to address sensitive topics constructively (e.g., Sailboat retrospective)

justification: Correct: structured facilitation techniques allow sensitive topics to be addressed constructively without breaking trust, while avoiding the buildup of unspoken issues.

text: A project manager must select the best technique to generate a maximum number of creative ideas during a problem-solving session with the team. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.A: Network diagram
options.B: Structured brainstorming
options.C: Earned value analysis
options.D: RACI matrix

justification: Correct: structured brainstorming is specifically designed to generate a maximum number of creative ideas in a collaborative problem-solving setting.

text: A Product Owner makes prioritization decisions without ever explaining their reasoning to the team, generating frustration. What action facilitates better collaboration?

options.A: Coach the PO on the importance of sharing the reasoning behind priorities (business context, value) to strengthen team engagement and understanding
options.B: Accept that the PO doesn't need to justify themselves to the team
options.C: Ask the team to ignore the PO's priorities if they aren't explained
options.D: Make the prioritization decisions in place of the PO

justification: Correct: coaching the PO on the importance of sharing context and value strengthens transparency, engagement, and mutual understanding without undermining their authority.

text: A project manager must manage a disagreement between the sponsor and a key stakeholder over the definition of project success. What facilitation action is appropriate?

options.A: Organize a joint clarification session to align success criteria and formally document them in the charter or project management plan
options.B: Arbitrarily choose one viewpoint without discussion
options.C: Ignore the disagreement and hope it resolves itself
options.D: Let the team decide the success criteria without involving the sponsor

justification: Correct: a formal clarification session with documented, aligned success criteria prevents future misunderstandings about the definition of project success.

text: A distributed team primarily uses asynchronous written communication, which sometimes causes misunderstandings on complex topics. What balanced recommendation is appropriate?

options.A: Completely ban asynchronous written communication
options.B: Require all communication to go only through synchronous meetings
options.C: Reserve synchronous communication (video, calls) for complex or sensitive topics, and asynchronous writing for simple factual updates
options.D: Ignore misunderstandings as long as work progresses

justification: Correct: reserving synchronous for complex, sensitive topics while keeping asynchronous for factual exchanges balances efficiency and clarity.

text: A project manager must decide how to develop the leadership skills of a high-potential team member. Which development action is most effective?

options.A: Do nothing and wait for them to develop skills on their own
options.B: Keep them strictly in their current role with no growth opportunity
options.C: Gradually assign coordination responsibilities on sub-tasks, with mentoring and regular feedback
options.D: Immediately promote them to a leadership position without preparation

justification: Correct: gradually assigning responsibilities with mentoring and regular feedback is a proven, structured approach to leadership development.

text: A multicultural Scrum team has different interpretations of 'being open and honest' in retrospectives, with some avoiding direct criticism out of cultural respect. What adaptation supports an effective retrospective?

options.A: Require the same direct frankness from everyone regardless of cultural context
options.B: Remove retrospectives for this multicultural team
options.C: Use retrospective formats that allow indirect or written expression (e.g., anonymous cards) and explicitly value any constructive form of feedback
options.D: Hold retrospectives only with the culturally more direct members

justification: Correct: formats allowing indirect or written expression respect cultural diversity while preserving the retrospective's continuous improvement goal.

text: A project manager notices two departments have an unresolved conflict negatively impacting the project team's morale. What is the best first step?

options.A: Take sides with one department against the other
options.B: Ignore the conflict since it's external to the project
options.C: Resign from the project manager role
options.D: Facilitate a structured discussion between the department leads to clarify issues and seek common ground

justification: Correct: the PM should proactively facilitate a structured resolution even for inter-departmental conflicts affecting their project.

text: A Product Owner and an external stakeholder publicly contradict each other about a feature's priority during a sprint review. What action is appropriate in the moment?

options.A: Immediately cancel the sprint review
options.B: Decide the priority themselves in place of the PO
options.C: Politely refocus the discussion by proposing to address the prioritization question outside the review, with the PO as final decision-maker for the backlog
options.D: Let the debate escalate in front of the team

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master facilitates by refocusing the discussion and reaffirming that final prioritization authority belongs to the PO, outside the review setting.

text: A project manager must decide how to handle a team member who openly disagrees with a strategic decision already approved by governance. What leadership approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Ban any expression of disagreement going forward
options.B: Ignore their concerns entirely with no explanation
options.C: Remove them from the project immediately for insubordination
options.D: Listen to their concerns, explain the context of the decision, and clarify the expectation of 'disagree and commit' once governance has decided

justification: Correct: listening, explaining context, and clarifying the 'disagree and commit' principle respects both legitimate expression and the need to move forward collectively after a governance decision.

text: A Scrum Master joining as an external consultant on an existing team perceives initial distrust toward their role. What approach best builds trust?

options.A: Ignore the distrust and continue as planned
options.B: First observe existing dynamics, actively listen to the team's concerns, and demonstrate value through concrete facilitation actions before introducing changes
options.C: Immediately impose strict new rules to establish authority
options.D: Complain to leadership about the team's lack of cooperation in the first week

justification: Correct: observing, listening, and progressively demonstrating value is the most effective approach to building trust with a distrustful team facing a new consultant.

text: A project manager notices two key team members have very different communication styles (one direct and factual, the other more relational and indirect), causing frequent misunderstandings. What action fosters better collaboration?

options.A: Raise mutual awareness of communication style differences and establish explicit team norms for key exchanges
options.B: Ask one of the two to completely change their natural style
options.C: Permanently separate them to avoid any contact
options.D: Ignore the misunderstandings as long as they don't block the project

justification: Correct: mutual awareness of communication styles and explicit team norms durably reduce misunderstandings.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team interprets Scrum ceremonies strictly as an end in themselves rather than as tools serving value. What action refocuses the team on the essentials?

options.A: Add even more strict rules for each ceremony
options.B: Continue insisting on strict adherence to format without ever questioning its purpose
options.C: Facilitate a discussion on the 'why' of each ceremony (underlying agile values and principles) rather than mechanical adherence to format
options.D: Remove all ceremonies to avoid excessive formalism

justification: Correct: refocusing the discussion on the 'why' of each ceremony reconnects the team to underlying agile values and principles, beyond mechanical compliance.

text: A project manager must prepare a team for a transition to a new complex project management tool. Which change management approach minimizes resistance best?

options.A: Deploy the tool overnight without any prior training or communication
options.B: Communicate the reasons for the change, progressively train the team, designate internal champions, and gather feedback to adjust the transition
options.C: Let each member freely choose to use the old or new tool indefinitely
options.D: Impose the tool without explaining expected benefits

justification: Correct: clear communication of reasons, progressive training, internal champions, and a feedback loop constitute a structured change management approach that minimizes resistance.

text: A Scrum Master notices that a distributed, culturally diverse team struggles to agree on a common work rhythm due to time zone differences and local holidays. What balanced solution is appropriate?

options.A: Require all members to work in the same time zone regardless of location
options.B: Co-create a shared working calendar with the team that respects local constraints as much as possible, with clearly defined overlap windows
options.C: Ignore cultural and time zone differences
options.D: Impose the Scrum Master's own country's work calendar on the whole team

justification: Correct: co-creating a shared calendar respecting local constraints, with defined overlap windows, promotes fairness and effective collaboration in a multicultural distributed team.

text: A project manager must decide how to respond to a team member expressing a desire to leave the project for career development reasons, while the project is in a critical phase. What is the most professional approach?

options.A: Understand their motivations, explore progressive transition solutions (training a replacement, planning the departure), and respect their legitimate professional aspirations
options.B: Categorically refuse their departure and force them to stay until project completion
options.C: Let them leave immediately with no transition planning
options.D: Penalize them for expressing this wish

justification: Correct: understanding motivations and organizing a progressive transition respects legitimate professional aspirations while minimizing impact on the critical-phase project.

text: A Scrum Master notices a member is systematically over-committing to work out of fear of disappointing others. What is the best intervention?

options.A: Let them continue since it shows commitment
options.B: Ignore it, it's not the Scrum Master's role
options.C: Discuss privately about realistic workload, encourage transparency about capacity, and reinforce that it's acceptable to say no
options.D: Publicly reduce their workload in front of the team to force change

justification: Correct: a private, caring conversation reinforces psychological safety and helps the person honestly express their real capacity.

text: A project manager must decide how to give recognition to a mentoring role that a senior team member takes on informally, creating extra unrecognized workload. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Ask the junior to stop seeking help
options.B: Ignore the extra workload since mentoring is supposed to be free
options.C: Ban informal mentoring between colleagues
options.D: Formally recognize the mentoring role in the senior member's workload and performance objectives

justification: Correct: formally recognizing the mentoring role values this precious contribution and avoids unrecognized overload of the experienced member.

text: An Agile Coach observes several Scrum Masters feel isolated in their practice, with no support community. What organizational action fosters their continuous professional development?

options.A: Let each Scrum Master train alone with no framework
options.B: Remove the Scrum Master role to avoid this isolation
options.C: Impose a single rigid method on all Scrum Masters with no exchange
options.D: Create a community of practice (guild) for Scrum Masters with regular sessions of experience sharing and collective problem-solving

justification: Correct: a community of practice (guild) with regular experience sharing reduces isolation and fosters continuous professional development of Scrum Masters organization-wide.

text: A project manager must decide how to structure a kickoff meeting to maximize engagement of the team and stakeholders. What element is most important to include?

options.A: A clear presentation of project objectives and vision, followed by discussion time for everyone to express expectations and concerns
options.B: Only a detailed budget presentation with no strategic context
options.C: A two-hour unilateral presentation by the project manager with no interaction
options.D: No particular structure, an informal meeting with no agenda

justification: Correct: combining a clear vision presentation with discussion time fosters engagement, mutual understanding, and collective ownership of the project from the start.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team member struggles with the digital tools used (low digital literacy), which slows their contribution. What inclusive action is appropriate?

options.A: Permanently remove them from tasks requiring these tools
options.B: Offer personalized support (training, tutorials, peer support) to strengthen their tool mastery without stigmatizing them
options.C: Leave them struggling with no support
options.D: Publicly mock their struggles to motivate them to learn faster

justification: Correct: personalized, non-stigmatizing support allows the person to develop digital skills while preserving their dignity and team integration.

text: A project manager must recognize a team member's contribution who solved a critical problem outside normal working hours. What recognition is most appropriate?

options.A: Explicitly recognize their contribution, fairly compensate the extra time per organizational policy, and clarify future expectations about working hours
options.B: Do nothing to avoid encouraging work outside normal hours
options.C: Completely ignore the incident
options.D: Require this to happen systematically going forward with no compensation

justification: Correct: recognizing the contribution, fairly compensating extra time, and clarifying future expectations balance appropriate recognition and sustainable pace management.

text: A Scrum Master notices a very cohesive team unconsciously excludes ideas from a new member with a different background (groupthink). What action fosters better diversity of thought?

options.A: Remove the new member from the team to avoid tension
options.B: Ignore the groupthink phenomenon
options.C: Let the group continue, cohesion takes priority over diversity of opinion
options.D: Deliberately introduce techniques favoring divergent perspectives (devil's advocate, systematic round-robin) and explicitly value the new member's contributions

justification: Correct: structured techniques like devil's advocate or systematic round-robin actively counter groupthink and value diverse perspectives.

text: A project manager must decide how to manage a change in composition of 50% of the team mid-project. According to Tuckman's model, which stage should the team likely revisit?

options.A: Forming, since a major composition change calls established norms and relationships into question
options.B: Performing directly, since the team already existed
options.C: Adjourning, since the previous team is dissolved
options.D: No stage, the model doesn't apply to team composition changes

justification: Correct: a significant change in composition (50%) generally returns the team to a Forming stage, requiring rebuilding of trust and norms.

text: A Scrum Master must handle a situation where the Product Owner and an external stakeholder disagree publicly on a feature's priority during a sprint review. Which underlying skill matters most here?

options.A: Financial forecasting skills
options.B: Contract negotiation expertise
options.C: Conflict facilitation and stakeholder management skills, redirecting the discussion constructively
options.D: Technical architecture expertise

justification: Correct: conflict facilitation and stakeholder management skills allow the Scrum Master to redirect the discussion constructively while preserving relationships and the review's purpose.

text: A project manager discovers that an official project financial report contains a significant error favorable to the project, unnoticed by the finance team. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Correct the error secretly without informing anyone
options.B: Wait to see if someone else notices before acting
options.C: Leave the error in place since it's favorable to the project
options.D: Immediately report the error to the relevant parties and correct the report, regardless of whether it is favorable or unfavorable

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics requires reporting and correcting any significant reporting error, whether favorable or unfavorable, in the name of transparency and honesty.

text: A project manager must decompose the project scope into manageable components. Which tool produces a hierarchical decomposition of the work to be performed?

options.A: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
options.B: The communications management plan
options.C: The Gantt chart
options.D: The risk register

justification: Correct: the WBS hierarchically decomposes the entire project scope into manageable work packages.

text: A team using a Kanban board wants to better visualize recurring blockers in its workflow. Which visual practice is most effective?

options.A: Mark blocked items visually on the board (e.g., red stickers) and prioritize discussing blockers during the daily synchronization
options.B: Remove blocked items from the board so problems aren't visible
options.C: Wait until the end of the month to analyze blockers
options.D: Ignore blockers as long as work generally progresses

justification: Correct: visually marking blockers and prioritizing them in daily synchronization is a standard Kanban practice for quickly resolving flow obstacles.

text: A project manager must determine the total project duration accounting for dependencies between activities. Which technique calculates project duration and identifies the critical path?

options.A: Earned value management (EVM)
options.B: The Critical Path Method (CPM)
options.C: The affinity diagram
options.D: SWOT analysis

justification: Correct: the Critical Path Method (CPM) calculates the minimum project duration by identifying the longest sequence of activities with no float.

text: A team using Scrumban wants to combine sprint predictability with continuous flow flexibility. Which hybrid practice characterizes this approach?

options.A: Use exclusively the classic waterfall cycle
options.B: Use no visual board at all
options.C: Fully abandon fixed iterations while retaining WIP limits and key Scrum ceremonies adapted to flow
options.D: Remove all flow or velocity measurements

justification: Correct: Scrumban typically combines removing strict fixed iterations (Kanban-style continuous flow) while retaining some Scrum ceremonies and WIP limits to manage flow.

text: A project manager must verify that costs incurred to date correspond to work actually performed. Which EVM indicator represents the actual cost spent?

options.A: Actual Cost (AC)
options.B: Planned Value (PV)
options.C: Earned Value (EV)
options.D: Cost Performance Index (CPI)

justification: Correct: Actual Cost (AC) represents the amount actually spent on the work performed at a given date.

text: A team wants to visualize the overall user journey to organize its backlog for a complex product. Which technique is most useful?

options.A: Story Mapping
options.B: The RACI matrix
options.C: The control chart
options.D: The Ishikawa diagram

justification: Correct: Story Mapping visualizes the end-to-end user journey, helping identify coherent value slices for MVP releases.

text: A project manager must verify that a critical component's failure would have the most significant impact on the overall system. Which risk analysis technique is most appropriate?

options.A: The affinity diagram
options.B: Informal brainstorming only
options.C: The RACI matrix
options.D: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)

justification: Correct: FMEA systematically identifies potential failure modes and assesses their severity, probability, and detectability to prioritize critical components.

text: A team wants to improve the quality of its user stories before they enter the sprint. Which standard criterion is most useful for evaluating user story quality?

options.A: The alphabetical order of the title
options.B: The number of technical keywords used
options.C: The INVEST criterion (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable)
options.D: The length of the user story text only

justification: Correct: the INVEST criterion is the recognized standard for evaluating whether a user story is well-formed before entering the sprint.

text: A project manager must ensure that modifications to technical deliverable configurations are properly tracked. Which process/tool manages this?

options.A: The Kanban board
options.B: The RACI matrix
options.C: Configuration management
options.D: The Ishikawa diagram

justification: Correct: configuration management ensures systematic tracking of versions and changes to technical deliverables and their characteristics.

text: A team wants to quickly validate a product hypothesis with minimal development effort. Which practice best matches this objective?

options.A: Wait six months before any user feedback
options.B: Ignore user feedback and rely solely on the team's intuition
options.C: Create an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) or rapid prototype to test the hypothesis with real users before investing further
options.D: Develop a complete, exhaustive feature before any user testing

justification: Correct: an MVP or rapid prototype validates a hypothesis with minimal effort before committing greater resources, a key Lean Startup and agile principle.

text: A project manager must calculate how much additional time is needed to complete the project given current schedule performance. Which EVM indicator is used for this forecast?

options.A: Planned Value (PV) alone
options.B: Budget at Completion (BAC) alone
options.C: Actual Cost (AC) alone
options.D: Time Estimate at Completion (TEAC) based on SPI

justification: Correct: the time estimate at completion (often derived from SPI) allows forecasting the likely total project duration given current schedule performance.

text: A team wants to improve the accuracy of its delivery forecasts for upcoming quarters. Which technique combines historical velocity data with an uncertainty margin?

options.A: A single point estimate with no uncertainty margin
options.B: Completely ignore velocity history
options.C: Rely solely on the Product Owner's intuition
options.D: Probabilistic forecasting (Monte Carlo) based on team velocity history

justification: Correct: Monte Carlo probabilistic forecasting uses velocity history to generate a distribution of possible delivery dates with an associated confidence level, more realistic than a point estimate.

text: A project manager must choose the best method to validate that a complex deliverable meets all functional requirements before going to production. Which activity is appropriate?

options.A: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
options.B: The affinity diagram
options.C: SWOT analysis
options.D: Team brainstorming

justification: Correct: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) formally validates that the deliverable meets functional requirements from the end user's perspective before production.

text: A team wants to decide how to handle production defects discovered during an ongoing sprint. What is the recommended practice?

options.A: Stop all new feature development until the end of the project
options.B: Ignore all production defects
options.C: Always wait until the next sprint for any defect, without exception
options.D: Assess the defect's criticality with the PO and team, and integrate it into the current sprint if business impact justifies an interruption, otherwise prioritize it in the backlog

justification: Correct: assessing criticality with the PO allows a pragmatic decision balancing sprint stability with the necessary responsiveness for impactful defects.

text: A project manager must ensure requirements traceability from initial requirements to final deliverables. Which tool ensures this traceability?

options.A: The risk register
options.B: The Gantt chart
options.C: The Kanban board
options.D: The Requirements Traceability Matrix

justification: Correct: the Requirements Traceability Matrix links each requirement to its origin, deliverables, and acceptance tests, ensuring complete coverage.

text: A team wants to continuously improve code quality. Which agile engineering practice best supports early defect detection?

options.A: Reduce release frequency to limit needed testing
options.B: Never automate tests to maintain full manual control
options.C: Continuous integration with automated tests on every commit
options.D: Test only at the end of each major release

justification: Correct: continuous integration with automated tests detects defects as early as possible, reducing correction cost and improving continuous quality.

text: A project manager must identify all potential stakeholders before the project starts. Which process covers this activity?

options.A: Close Project or Phase
options.B: Control Costs
options.C: Identify Stakeholders
options.D: Acquire Resources

justification: Correct: the 'Identify Stakeholders' process systematically catalogs individuals and organizations impacted by or impacting the project.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage accumulated technical debt that progressively slows velocity. Which practice is most recommended?

options.A: Stop all feature development for six months to refactor everything
options.B: Allocate a regular share of sprint capacity to reducing technical debt, made visible in the backlog
options.C: Transfer responsibility for technical debt to the client
options.D: Ignore technical debt as long as features are delivered

justification: Correct: allocating a regular capacity share to technical debt, made visible and prioritized in the backlog, is the recommended sustainable practice.

text: A project manager must select an outlet for statistical process control to verify a production process stays within acceptable limits over time. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: The affinity diagram
options.B: The control chart with upper and lower control limits
options.C: The RACI matrix
options.D: The Ishikawa diagram

justification: Correct: the control chart monitors process stability over time, identifying variations outside acceptable control limits.

text: A Product Owner must decide how to manage a backlog that has become too large and hard to navigate after months of idea collection. What backlog management action is appropriate?

options.A: Perform regular backlog refinement, archiving or removing obsolete items and reorganizing by theme/value
options.B: Ignore the problem since a large backlog has no impact on the team
options.C: Randomly delete half the backlog without analysis
options.D: Keep all items indefinitely, even obsolete ones, in case they become relevant again

justification: Correct: regular refinement with archiving or removal of obsolete items and reorganization by theme/value maintains a manageable, relevant backlog.

text: A project manager must ensure the budget allocated matches the workload planned over time. Which tool combines schedule and cost for this planning?

options.A: The Ishikawa diagram
options.B: The S-curve (time-phased budget)
options.C: The affinity diagram
options.D: The Kanban board

justification: Correct: the S-curve represents the cumulative budget time-phased across the project, serving as the baseline for earned value analysis.

text: A team working in Kanban wants to reduce its average cycle time. Which action is most directly effective?

options.A: Ignore flow measurements
options.B: Add more validation steps to the process
options.C: Increase the number of items in progress simultaneously
options.D: Reduce work-in-progress (WIP) limits and eliminate identified bottlenecks in the flow

justification: Correct: reducing WIP limits forces resolution of bottlenecks and improves flow, thereby decreasing average cycle time (Kanban/Lean principle).

text: A project manager wants to anticipate potential risks before they occur. Which qualitative technique is commonly used to assess probability and impact of identified risks?

options.A: The Kanban board
options.B: The probability-impact matrix
options.C: The burndown chart
options.D: The Gantt chart

justification: Correct: the probability-impact matrix allows a rapid qualitative assessment of risks to prioritize those requiring a response.

text: A Scrum team wants to improve delivery predictability. Which agile metric is most useful for forecasting future sprint delivery capacity?

options.A: The number of hours physically present at the office
options.B: The average velocity of recent sprints
options.C: The total number of open bugs
options.D: The number of meetings held per sprint

justification: Correct: the average velocity of previous sprints is the standard empirical metric to forecast future delivery capacity.

text: A project manager must select the least risky schedule compression method to catch up on a delay without significantly increasing costs. Which technique is most appropriate if activities can run in parallel without major risk?

options.A: Crashing (adding resources)
options.B: Stopping the project
options.C: Reducing scope without consultation
options.D: Fast-tracking (overlapping activities)

justification: Correct: fast-tracking consists of executing normally sequential activities in parallel, without major additional cost, when risk allows.

text: A regulated healthcare organization developing agile products needs to reconcile fast iteration with strict regulatory traceability requirements. What approach is recommended?

options.A: Fully abandon agility for a complete waterfall cycle
options.B: Adapt the Definition of Done to include regulatory traceability documentation for each increment, produced continuously rather than at the end
options.C: Defer all regulatory documentation to the very end of development
options.D: Ignore regulatory requirements to move faster

justification: Correct: integrating regulatory traceability into the Definition of Done for each increment ensures continuous compliance without sacrificing iterative agility.

text: A project manager must choose a contract for an R&D project with highly uncertain and evolving scope. Which contract type is most appropriate?

options.A: Firm Fixed Price (FFP)
options.B: Cost-Reimbursable, such as Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF)
options.C: No formal contract is necessary
options.D: Fixed Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) only

justification: Correct: cost-reimbursable contracts like CPFF are suited for R&D projects with uncertain scope, allowing scope flexibility with reimbursement of actual costs incurred.

text: Multiple teams working on the same product have different definitions of Done, creating integration problems. What action at the Scrum of Scrums level is appropriate?

options.A: Facilitate cross-team alignment on a common product-level Definition of Done, with team-specific additions if needed
options.B: Impose the most experienced team's definition without discussion
options.C: Remove the concept of Definition of Done
options.D: Let each team keep its own definition indefinitely

justification: Correct: collaborative alignment on a common product-level DoD, with local extensions, resolves integration problems while respecting team autonomy.

text: A project manager must verify the effectiveness of the risk management system after several review cycles. Which process evaluates the overall performance of project risk management?

options.A: Close Project
options.B: Develop Project Charter
options.C: Acquire Resources
options.D: Monitor Risks

justification: Correct: the 'Monitor Risks' process evaluates the ongoing effectiveness of the risk management process, identifies new risks, and verifies the relevance of existing responses.

text: A team wants to visualize dependencies with other teams more clearly. Which coordination tool is most appropriate at multi-team scale?

options.A: A cross-team dependency board updated during the Scrum of Scrums
options.B: An annual summary email
options.C: A single meeting at project start with no follow-up
options.D: Share nothing between teams

justification: Correct: a cross-team dependency board regularly updated during the Scrum of Scrums offers continuous, actionable visibility on technical dependencies.

text: A project manager must guarantee that scope changes are properly controlled. Which document serves as the reference for evaluating whether a request truly constitutes a change?

options.A: The weekly progress report
options.B: The organization chart
options.C: The scope statement and the approved scope baseline
options.D: Team members' resumes

justification: Correct: any request is compared against the approved scope baseline to determine whether it constitutes a deviation requiring a formal change request.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage a critical external dependency on a third-party vendor with uncertain timelines. Which hybrid approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Indefinitely delay all sprints until the dependency is fully resolved
options.B: Track the external dependency via a dedicated risk register, plan contingencies (buffer, alternative), and factor it into planning of the affected sprints
options.C: Fully transfer responsibility to the vendor with no active follow-up
options.D: Completely ignore the external dependency in sprint planning

justification: Correct: actively tracking the dependency with a dedicated risk register and contingency plans, while factoring it into sprint planning, is a pragmatic hybrid approach combining predictive rigor with agile flexibility.

text: A project manager must decide how to handle minor change requests that don't significantly affect scope, cost, or schedule. Which approach is most efficient?

options.A: Define delegation thresholds allowing the project manager to directly approve minor changes per predefined criteria, while documenting the decision
options.B: Systematically submit every request, even minor ones, to the full change control board
options.C: Ignore all minor change requests without documenting them
options.D: Systematically refuse any change, even minor ones

justification: Correct: predefined delegation thresholds allowing the PM to directly approve minor changes, with documentation, optimize efficiency while maintaining traceability.

text: A team practicing mob programming occasionally finds that some developers feel it slows their perceived individual productivity. What is the best way to objectively evaluate the practice?

options.A: Continue indefinitely without ever evaluating impact
options.B: Abandon it immediately based on individual impressions
options.C: Impose mob programming 100% of the time without discussion
options.D: Objectively measure the impact on shared metrics (code quality, defect resolution time, knowledge sharing) rather than perceived individual productivity

justification: Correct: evaluating objective shared metrics allows a data-driven decision rather than one based on subjective perceived individual productivity.

text: A project manager must determine which activities have zero float and determine the project's minimum duration. What are these activities collectively called?

options.A: Project milestones
options.B: Intermediate deliverables
options.C: The critical path
options.D: The near-critical path

justification: Correct: the critical path groups activities with zero (or minimal) total float that determine the project's minimum duration.

text: A team wants to improve the effectiveness of its retrospectives over time without them becoming repetitive. Which practice helps maintain their effectiveness?

options.A: Reduce retrospective frequency to once a year
options.B: Vary facilitation formats (e.g., Start-Stop-Continue, 4Ls, Sailboat) and ensure decided actions are actually followed up sprint to sprint
options.C: Remove follow-up actions between retrospectives
options.D: Always use exactly the same retrospective format without variation

justification: Correct: varying formats and ensuring real follow-up on decided actions maintains engagement and effectiveness of retrospectives over time.

text: A project manager must finalize all administrative documents and obtain the client's final sign-off at the end of the project. Which process formalizes this step?

options.A: Plan Scope Management
options.B: Close Project or Phase
options.C: Direct and Manage Project Work
options.D: Develop Team

justification: Correct: the 'Close Project or Phase' process finalizes all administrative activities, obtains final acceptance, and archives project documents.

text: A financial services organization developing agile products must comply with regulatory resilience (stress testing) requirements. How can this be integrated without breaking the agile rhythm?

options.A: Ignore resilience requirements to keep pace with sprints
options.B: Integrate automated, incremental resilience tests with each increment delivered, with regular compliance reviews rather than a single final test
options.C: Defer all resilience testing to the very end of the project, just before the regulatory audit
options.D: Abandon agility entirely in favor of a full waterfall cycle dedicated only to testing

justification: Correct: integrating automated, incremental resilience tests with each increment, with regular compliance reviews, reconciles strict regulatory requirements with continuous agile rhythm.

text: A project manager must vary the compression method for the schedule when the budget is very limited. Which method should be prioritized?

options.A: Outsource the entire project to a new vendor
options.B: Fast-tracking, which overlaps activities without significant additional cost
options.C: Crashing, which adds paid additional resources
options.D: Double the team without cost analysis

justification: Correct: fast-tracking reduces duration without significant additional cost by executing certain activities in parallel, suited to a strong budget constraint.

text: A Scrum team wants to better forecast delivery capacity for the next quarters. Which data source is most reliable for this forecast?

options.A: Historical velocity data combined with a probabilistic forecasting technique
options.B: The number of team members regardless of experience
options.C: The Product Owner's personal opinion alone
options.D: The project sponsor's expectations alone

justification: Correct: historical velocity data combined with a probabilistic technique (e.g., Monte Carlo) provides a realistic, empirically grounded forecast.

text: A project manager must verify that quality control activities planned are sufficient for the project's risk level. Which quality principle states it is less costly to prevent defects than to correct them?

options.A: Little's Law
options.B: Parkinson's Law
options.C: The Pareto principle only
options.D: Cost of Quality, notably the prevention versus inspection principle

justification: Correct: the Cost of Quality concept establishes that prevention and appraisal costs are generally lower than costs of non-conformance (rework, corrections, warranties).

text: A team wants to decide how to manage user stories that turn out to be much more complex than estimated once development has begun. What practice is appropriate?

options.A: Discuss the discovery transparently with the PO, consider splitting or deferring the story, and adjust the sprint accordingly
options.B: Hide the problem until the sprint review
options.C: Force completion within the current sprint at all costs, even if quality is compromised
options.D: Abandon the story completely without communication

justification: Correct: a transparent discussion with the PO allowing informed splitting or deferring of the story is the appropriate agile practice when unexpected complexity is discovered.

text: A project manager must decide how to leverage resource leveling to manage constrained resource availability. What technique adjusts the schedule based on resource constraints?

options.A: The Ishikawa diagram
options.B: Resource Leveling
options.C: The affinity diagram
options.D: SWOT analysis

justification: Correct: resource leveling adjusts activity start and end dates to respect resource availability constraints, potentially modifying the critical path.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage a defect discovered late in a sprint that isn't critical but affects a minor part of the deliverable. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Fix it silently without informing the PO or the team
options.B: Immediately stop the sprint and address only this defect
options.C: Document the defect, discuss its priority with the PO, and decide whether it fits in the current sprint or should be added to the backlog
options.D: Ignore the defect permanently

justification: Correct: documenting and discussing priority with the PO enables an informed decision, balancing sprint continuity with proper defect management.

text: A project manager must determine the number of parallel paths in the network diagram that reduce overall schedule delay risk. Which technique assesses the project's sensitivity to delays on near-critical paths?

options.A: The Ishikawa diagram
options.B: The RACI matrix
options.C: Critical path and near-critical path sensitivity analysis
options.D: The Kanban board

justification: Correct: sensitivity analysis of the critical path and near-critical paths identifies delay risk areas to monitor closely, especially when multiple paths have low float.

text: A team wants to improve visibility into technical dependencies with other teams at scale. Which scaled agile mechanism supports this?

options.A: Purely informal, undocumented conversations
options.B: Program Increment (PI) Planning with visualized cross-team dependencies
options.C: A single annual meeting with no follow-up
options.D: No coordination between teams at all

justification: Correct: PI Planning in scaled agile frameworks explicitly visualizes and coordinates cross-team dependencies for the upcoming increment.

text: A project manager must anticipate all activities that must precede others due to the physical nature of the work (e.g., foundations before walls). What dependency type does this illustrate?

options.A: Mandatory dependency (Hard Logic)
options.B: No dependency is necessary
options.C: Discretionary dependency (Soft Logic)
options.D: External dependency

justification: Correct: a mandatory dependency (hard logic) results from the intrinsic physical nature of the work, such as needing foundations before walls.

text: A team wants to decide how to handle a Product Owner who lacks availability, slowing decision-making during the sprint. What durable solution is appropriate?

options.A: The team makes all product decisions without the PO permanently
options.B: Halt the sprint until the PO is available
options.C: Negotiate dedicated availability windows with the PO or designate a trained proxy PO for routine decisions
options.D: Ignore the problem and hope for spontaneous improvement

justification: Correct: negotiating dedicated windows or establishing a trained proxy PO maintains velocity while respecting the PO's role on strategic decisions.

text: A project manager must vary a formal system for managing change requests throughout the project. Which body is generally responsible for approving or rejecting these requests?

options.A: Any team member individually
options.B: No formal body is necessary
options.C: The Change Control Board (CCB)
options.D: The external vendor only

justification: Correct: the CCB is the formal body generally responsible for reviewing, approving, or rejecting change requests per a defined project governance process.

text: A Product Owner must decide how to prioritize the backlog considering both business value and regulatory constraints. Which prioritization technique best integrates both dimensions?

options.A: Let each developer choose what they prefer
options.B: Prioritize only by technical complexity
options.C: Use multi-criteria weighting (WSJF or MoSCoW) including value, risk, and compliance constraints
options.D: Prioritize only by order of arrival of requests (FIFO)

justification: Correct: techniques like WSJF or MoSCoW allow multi-factor prioritization including value, regulatory urgency, and risk.

text: A project manager must verify that a supplier respects contractual terms regarding interim delivery deadlines. Which process actively monitors supplier performance?

options.A: Identify Stakeholders
options.B: Develop Team
options.C: Plan Communications Management
options.D: Control Procurements

justification: Correct: the 'Control Procurements' process monitors supplier performance against contractual terms, including interim delivery deadlines.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage code quality in continuous delivery when tests take too long to run. What practice addresses this challenge?

options.A: Optimize the test suite (parallelization, prioritizing fast unit tests) while maintaining sufficient coverage for critical paths
options.B: Only run tests once a month regardless of delivery frequency
options.C: Delegate all testing responsibility to end users after release
options.D: Remove all tests to speed up delivery

justification: Correct: optimizing the test suite through parallelization and prioritization maintains fast feedback while preserving sufficient coverage for critical paths.

text: A project manager must determine the free float of a non-critical activity. What does this measure represent precisely?

options.A: The total time available before the end of the project
options.B: The remaining budget allocated to the activity
options.C: The number of resources available for the activity
options.D: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the early start date of the following activity

justification: Correct: free float is the delay possible for an activity without impacting the early start date of the immediately following activity.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage a backlog item that spans multiple teams' responsibilities. What coordination practice is appropriate?

options.A: Duplicate the entire item across all teams to avoid coordination
options.B: Leave it unassigned indefinitely until a team volunteers
options.C: Break the item into smaller pieces aligned with each team's ownership, coordinate through a shared dependency board, and clarify integration points
options.D: Assign it entirely to one team without discussion, regardless of dependencies

justification: Correct: breaking the item into smaller pieces with clear ownership and shared dependency tracking ensures coordinated, efficient cross-team delivery.

text: A project manager must ensure lessons learned from a major quality incident benefit future organizational projects. What action is essential?

options.A: Inform only the sponsor verbally with no documentation
options.B: Wait until project closure to discuss the incident
options.C: Document nothing to avoid exposing the team's mistakes
options.D: Document the incident, its root causes, and corrective actions in the lessons learned register and organizational process assets

justification: Correct: documenting the incident, its root causes, and corrective actions in lessons learned and organizational process assets enables real capitalization for future projects.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage flaky (intermittently failing) automated tests that undermine trust in the CI pipeline. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Identify and quarantine flaky tests, prioritize fixing their root causes, and track flakiness as a quality metric
options.B: Ignore flaky tests and let developers manually re-run failed builds indefinitely
options.C: Disable the entire CI pipeline until further notice
options.D: Delete all tests that fail intermittently without investigation

justification: Correct: identifying, quarantining, and prioritizing root-cause fixes for flaky tests, while tracking flakiness as a metric, restores CI reliability systematically.

text: A project manager must guarantee consistency between the cost management plan, the schedule management plan, and the scope management plan. Which document integrates all these subsidiary plans?

options.A: Team members' resumes
options.B: The weekly status report
options.C: The risk register only
options.D: The Project Management Plan

justification: Correct: the Project Management Plan integrates all subsidiary plans (cost, schedule, scope, quality, etc.) in a coherent, coordinated manner.

text: A team wants to decide how to handle a spike (research task) that reveals a feature is technically infeasible as originally envisioned. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Proceed with the original plan regardless of the spike's findings
options.B: Hide the findings to avoid disappointing stakeholders
options.C: Share the spike findings transparently with the PO and team, and collaboratively redefine the feature's scope or approach based on the new information
options.D: Abandon the entire product initiative based on one spike

justification: Correct: transparently sharing spike findings and collaboratively adjusting the approach is the appropriate empirical response to new technical information.

text: A project manager must select the simplest progress measurement method for very short-duration activities (less than a week). Which EVM formula is generally used?

options.A: Monte Carlo analysis
options.B: Detailed daily subjective estimation
options.C: The Pareto diagram
options.D: The 0/100 formula (0% until complete, 100% once complete)

justification: Correct: for very short-duration activities, the 0/100 formula is simple and avoids the bias of a hard-to-justify intermediate estimate.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage the transition of knowledge to an operations team before a product handoff, in an agile context. What action ensures a successful transition?

options.A: Document operational runbooks incrementally throughout development, pair operations staff with the team during the last sprints, and organize a transitional support period
options.B: Transfer only a contact list with no technical documentation
options.C: Consider that knowledge transfer is not the development team's responsibility
options.D: Defer all documentation until after the official handoff

justification: Correct: incremental runbook documentation, pairing operations staff during final sprints, and a transitional support period ensure a smooth handoff and reduce post-transition risks.

text: A new environmental regulation takes effect during the execution of a construction project. What is the first appropriate step for the project manager?

options.A: Ignore the regulation until project closure
options.B: Suspend the project indefinitely
options.C: Assess the impact on the project and update the risk register and compliance documentation
options.D: Inform only the sponsor with no further action

justification: Correct: the PM must assess the enterprise environmental factors (EEF), document the impact, and adjust the risk management plan.

text: An organization undergoing agile transformation faces strong cultural resistance from middle management. What strategic action is most effective for project leadership?

options.A: Bypass middle management by working directly with the teams
options.B: Involve middle management in co-designing the change and demonstrate value through pilot projects
options.C: Force adoption through strict top-down directives
options.D: Postpone the transformation until full consensus is reached

justification: Correct: effective organizational change management involves relevant stakeholders and uses evidence of value (pilots) to build buy-in.

text: A company evaluates several candidate projects with limited budgets. Which financial method allows comparing the relative profitability of projects of different sizes?

options.A: The number of employees assigned to the project
options.B: Net Present Value (NPV) only in absolute value
options.C: The project duration only
options.D: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) or benefit-cost ratio, which normalize comparison regardless of size

justification: Correct: IRR or benefit-cost ratio normalize profitability as a percentage or ratio, allowing fair comparison between projects of different sizes.

text: An organization wants to assess whether its culture is open enough to support a large-scale agile transformation. Which cultural factor is most determinant?

options.A: Tolerance for failure, trust in teams, and openness to decentralized decision-making
options.B: The size of the physical offices
options.C: The number of certifications held by employees
options.D: The number of digital tools available

justification: Correct: a durable agile culture relies on tolerance for failure (learning), trust, and decentralized decision-making, fundamental cultural elements.

text: A project manager must ensure the project respects the organization's information security policy when processing sensitive customer data. What action is a priority?

options.A: Wait for a security incident before acting
options.B: Integrate information security requirements into the project management plan and consult the security/compliance team early in planning
options.C: Ignore the policy if it slows the project
options.D: Process sensitive data without any particular protection measure

justification: Correct: security requirements must be integrated from planning, in consultation with relevant security/compliance experts.

text: A company measures the success of its initiatives via an OKR (Objectives and Key Results) framework rather than a traditional project plan. What is the main advantage of this framework in an agile context?

options.A: It imposes a rigid detailed 12-month plan
options.B: It aligns teams on measurable, ambitious objectives while leaving flexibility on the means (the 'how')
options.C: It completely replaces the need for communication between teams
options.D: It completely eliminates the need to measure performance

justification: Correct: OKRs align teams on measurable key results while preserving autonomy on how to achieve them, consistent with the agile spirit.

text: A project manager notices a competitor just launched a similar product, threatening the strategic relevance of the ongoing project. What is the best action?

options.A: Completely ignore the competitive threat
options.B: Stop the project without consulting governance
options.C: Immediately copy the competitor's product without analysis
options.D: Inform governance and reassess the business case to adjust project strategy if necessary (differentiation, acceleration)

justification: Correct: the PM must escalate to governance and reassess the business case to adjust strategy (differentiation, schedule acceleration, etc.).

text: An organization wants to assess the value delivered by its digital product beyond internal production metrics. Which type of external indicator is most relevant?

options.A: The number of code commits
options.B: The number of user stories created
options.C: The number of internal meetings held
options.D: Net Promoter Score (NPS) and user adoption/retention rates

justification: Correct: NPS and adoption/retention rates directly measure user satisfaction and perceived value, key external indicators of product success.

text: A project manager must integrate corporate social responsibility (CSR) requirements into a construction project. Which action best illustrates this integration?

options.A: Ignore CSR if it slightly increases costs
options.B: Fully delegate CSR to the marketing department with no link to project execution
