options.C: Integrate CSR criteria (environmental impact, fair labor conditions) into vendor selection criteria and the project management plan
options.D: Treat CSR as optional with no impact on project decisions

justification: Correct: integrating concrete CSR criteria into vendor selection and the project management plan is the practice aligned with professional and societal responsibility.

text: A startup developing an agile product must decide whether to invest more in acquiring new customers or retaining existing ones with a limited budget. What data should guide this decision?

options.A: The size of the development team
options.B: A comparative analysis of customer acquisition cost (CAC) and lifetime value (LTV), as well as current retention rates
options.C: The founder's personal preference only
options.D: The number of features already developed

justification: Correct: comparing CAC, LTV, and retention rates provides a factual basis for arbitrating between acquisition and retention investment.

text: A project manager must integrate digital accessibility requirements (e.g., WCAG) imposed by a new law into an already-ongoing web development project. What is the best approach?

options.A: Assess the current compliance gap, update requirements and the project management plan accordingly, prioritizing critical fixes
options.B: Ignore the law since the project is already underway
options.C: Indefinitely postpone compliance without a plan
options.D: Stop the project completely

justification: Correct: assessing the compliance gap and integrating necessary corrections into the project management plan is the proactive compliance approach, even mid-execution.

text: An organization evaluates whether to continue funding a digital product after 18 months without meeting adoption targets. Which Lean Startup principle guides this decision?

options.A: Automatically double the budget without analysis
options.B: Continue indefinitely as a matter of persistence
options.C: The 'pivot or persevere' principle based on hypothesis validation data (build-measure-learn)
options.D: Stop immediately without analyzing the causes of underperformance

justification: Correct: the build-measure-learn cycle guides the 'pivot or persevere' decision based on actual adoption and hypothesis validation data.

text: A project manager evaluates whether a project remains viable after a major shift in company strategic direction. What governance action is appropriate?

options.A: Decide alone to stop the project
options.B: Continue the project without reassessment
options.C: Conduct a formal strategic alignment review with portfolio governance to decide on continuation, adjustment, or termination
options.D: Ignore the change in strategic direction

justification: Correct: a major strategic change requires a formal portfolio governance review to determine the project's future.

text: A nonprofit organization using agile methods must report on the social impact of its projects to donors, beyond velocity metrics. Which measurement approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Ignore any impact measurement since agile methods don't lend themselves to it
options.B: Only communicate velocity and the number of sprints completed
options.C: Limit reporting to the number of completed user stories
options.D: Develop specific social impact indicators (e.g., beneficiaries reached, measured behavior change) aligned with the organization's theory of change

justification: Correct: specific social impact indicators, aligned with the organization's theory of change, meet donor accountability expectations, complementing internal agile metrics.

text: A project manager must evaluate the impact of a major exchange rate fluctuation on an international project financed in a foreign currency. Which enterprise environmental factor (EEF) is concerned?

options.A: The software tools used by the team
options.B: The project manager's management style
options.C: Marketplace conditions and external economic factors
options.D: Internal organizational culture

justification: Correct: currency fluctuations and marketplace conditions are external EEFs to monitor and integrate into risk management.

text: An organization considers adopting an inner source approach (internal open-source-style code sharing) to improve reuse across teams. What is the main organizational benefit of this approach?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for code governance
options.B: It removes the need for automated tests
options.C: It makes all technical documentation unnecessary
options.D: It fosters component reuse across teams, reduces duplicated effort, and improves technical consistency organization-wide

justification: Correct: inner source fosters component reuse, reduces duplicated effort, and improves technical consistency across teams, a key organizational benefit.

text: An international project manager must ensure the project simultaneously complies with anti-corruption laws in both the home country and the country of execution. What practice is essential?

options.A: Apply the stricter standard between the two jurisdictions and document compliance for both legal frameworks
options.B: Ignore anti-corruption laws if local practices differ
options.C: Apply only the less restrictive law of the two countries
options.D: Fully delegate to a local third party with no oversight

justification: Correct: applying the stricter standard between jurisdictions is the prudent compliance practice for extraterritorial laws like anti-corruption legislation (e.g., FCPA).

text: An organization wants to evaluate if its target market is evolving faster than its current agile delivery capability. Which external strategic indicator should be monitored as a priority?

options.A: The number of sprints completed
options.B: The evolution of customer needs and competing offerings (market intelligence) compared to the organization's value delivery pace
options.C: The number of user stories in the backlog
options.D: The number of planning meetings held

justification: Correct: comparing market and competitive evolution to value delivery pace assesses whether the organization risks losing strategic relevance.

text: A project manager must justify to leadership why a higher initial investment in quality will reduce total costs over the product lifecycle. Which economic concept supports this argument?

options.A: The number of employees involved in the project
options.B: The project duration only
options.C: The initial purchase price only
options.D: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), including non-conformance costs avoided long-term

justification: Correct: TCO demonstrates that an initial investment in quality often reduces non-conformance costs (rework, warranties, dissatisfaction) over the entire lifecycle.

text: An organization must decide whether to prioritize a proprietary closed-development approach or an open one (public APIs, partner ecosystem) for its agile product. Which strategic factor is most determinant?

options.A: Analysis of the competitive ecosystem, growth potential through partnerships, and security/dependency risks associated with each approach
options.B: The product's brand color
options.C: The number of lines of code already written
options.D: The developers' aesthetic preference for one architecture type

justification: Correct: analyzing the competitive ecosystem, partnership growth potential, and security/dependency risks provides a solid strategic basis for this open vs. closed architecture choice.

text: A project manager must ensure the project respects the security of information policy while transferring data internationally. Which action is essential?

options.A: Continue data transfers without any compliance verification
options.B: Consult legal experts to assess compliant transfer mechanisms (standard contractual clauses, certifications) and adjust the architecture if needed
options.C: Ignore the standard if it is not yet fully enforced locally
options.D: Stop all data transfer without exploring alternatives

justification: Correct: consulting legal experts to identify compliant transfer mechanisms and adjust the architecture if necessary is the proactive, responsible approach.

text: An organization developing agile products for the financial sector must comply with data protection regulations while processing customer data. What is essential from the design phase?

options.A: Integrate the 'privacy by design' principle from the outset and document data protection measures
options.B: Ignore data protection if the project is for internal use only
options.C: Fully delegate the matter to the legal department without any project involvement
options.D: Handle compliance only after deployment to production

justification: Correct: 'privacy by design' requires integrating data protection from the design stage, a fundamental requirement of data protection regulations and good compliance practice.

text: A project manager must decide if their organization has the culturally legitimate footing to execute a project in a country with significantly different business practices. What action is a priority?

options.A: Strictly apply headquarters standards with no local adaptation
options.B: Fully adopt local practices even if they contradict core ethical principles
options.C: Cancel the project without prior analysis
options.D: Conduct a local cultural context analysis, consult local experts, and adapt practices while respecting non-negotiable core ethical principles

justification: Correct: analyzing local cultural context with experts and adapting practices while preserving non-negotiable ethical principles balances cultural respect and professional integrity.

text: An organization scaling from 3 to 15 agile teams within a year must anticipate a major organizational risk. What risk should be prioritized?

options.A: The risk that Scrum ceremonies become too short
options.B: Loss of product coherence and cross-team communication without an adapted coordination framework (e.g., Scrum of Scrums, architectural alignment)
options.C: The risk that teams become too small
options.D: No particular risk, agility automatically scales to any size

justification: Correct: rapid growth in the number of teams without a coordination mechanism (Scrum of Scrums, guilds, architectural alignment) risks fragmenting product coherence and communication.

text: A project manager must evaluate the impact of a newly imposed trade embargo on the supply of critical components for an industrial project. What is the first appropriate action?

options.A: Continue without adjustment, hoping the embargo is lifted quickly
options.B: Stop the project without consulting governance
options.C: Assess the impact on the supply chain, identify compliant alternative suppliers, and update the risk register
options.D: Illegally circumvent the embargo through undeclared intermediaries

justification: Correct: assessing the real impact, identifying compliant alternatives, and documenting the risk is the proactive, legal approach appropriate for an embargo.

text: An organization is evaluating whether to invest in generative AI tools to accelerate agile product development. What evaluation approach is most responsible?

options.A: Let each developer decide individually with no organizational framework
options.B: Conduct a structured risk and benefit assessment (data security, algorithmic bias, intellectual property) before large-scale deployment, with controlled pilots
options.C: Completely ignore this technology out of excessive caution
options.D: Adopt immediately with no risk assessment (bias, data security, intellectual property)

justification: Correct: a structured risk and benefit assessment with controlled pilots allows responsible, progressive adoption of a high-potential but genuinely risky emerging technology.

text: A project manager learns that part of the work is subcontracted to an organization with ethically questionable labor practices. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Assess the situation, engage in dialogue with the subcontractor about expected standards, and escalate to governance if practices don't improve
options.B: Continue the collaboration with no verification
options.C: Cover up the questionable practices to avoid jeopardizing the project
options.D: Ignore the subcontractor's practices as long as deadlines are met

justification: Correct: assessing, engaging in dialogue about expected standards, and escalating if necessary reflects responsible, ethical management of a conduct issue with an external partner.

text: An organization is evaluating whether to adopt a subscription-based pricing model (SaaS) rather than a one-time sale for its agile-developed product. Which business analysis is most relevant for this strategic decision?

options.A: The number of sprints needed to develop the product
options.B: The development team's aesthetic preference
options.C: A comparative analysis of customer lifetime value (LTV), the predictability of recurring revenue, and alignment with target market expectations
options.D: The number of user stories already developed

justification: Correct: comparing LTV, recurring revenue predictability, and target market alignment provides a solid factual basis for a strategic pricing model decision.

text: A project manager is asked by a business partner to share confidential competitor information obtained by mistake. What is the correct action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Share the information if it benefits the project
options.B: Refuse to share the inappropriately obtained confidential information and address the situation per the principles of honesty and fairness
options.C: Share the information secretly without informing anyone
options.D: Use the information to negotiate a personal advantage

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics requires refusing to use inappropriately obtained information and handling the situation with transparency and integrity.

text: An organization must decide whether it should outsource part of its agile development to an offshore team. What factor is most determinant for the success of this arrangement?

options.A: The lowest price proposed by the vendor only
options.B: The number of certifications held by the vendor
options.C: The size of the offshore team only
options.D: Compatibility of agile practices, quality of asynchronous communication, and sufficient overlap of working hours

justification: Correct: compatibility of agile practices, effective asynchronous communication, and sufficient time zone overlap are determinant for successful distributed agile collaboration.

text: A project manager must ensure their organization has the mature processes necessary to manage a complex multi-project program. What type of organizational assessment is appropriate?

options.A: No assessment is necessary before starting
options.B: A Program Management Maturity Assessment
options.C: A simple Gantt chart of the program
options.D: The program manager's resume only

justification: Correct: a program management maturity assessment verifies whether the organization has the processes, governance, and skills necessary before engaging in a complex program.

text: An organization wants to establish light but effective governance for its digital products in an agile context. Which mechanism is most appropriate?

options.A: Hierarchical validation for every minor technical decision
options.B: Regular product reviews based on value metrics and OKRs, with rapid escalation in case of drift
options.C: No governance at all
options.D: A monthly steering committee with an exhaustive 100-page document review

justification: Correct: regular reviews based on value metrics and OKRs, with rapid escalation, offer light but effective governance suited to agility.

text: A project manager must evaluate the implications of a new carbon tax on an energy-intensive industrial project. What planning action is appropriate?

options.A: Automatically pass the cost to the client without contract negotiation
options.B: Stop the project immediately without analysis
options.C: Integrate the carbon tax cost into updated financial projections and evaluate energy footprint reduction options
options.D: Ignore the carbon tax since it didn't exist when the project was launched

justification: Correct: integrating the cost into updated projections and evaluating energy reduction options is the proactive, responsible approach to a new environmental regulatory factor.

text: An agile product team must decide how to prioritize between a feature generating quick revenue and another reducing a significant but less visible security risk. What prioritization reasoning is most responsible?

options.A: Completely ignore security concerns if they don't generate direct revenue
options.B: Assess the security risk based on its potential impact (reputation, legal compliance, user trust) and prioritize accordingly, even if less visible short-term
options.C: Let chance decide the priority
options.D: Always prioritize immediate revenue with no other consideration

justification: Correct: responsible prioritization assesses the potential impact of the security risk (even invisible short-term) alongside direct business value, reflecting mature risk management.

text: A project manager evaluates whether to invest in a new system while an existing system still functions, but with rising maintenance costs. What financial analysis helps compare the two options over their full lifetime?

options.A: The number of employees trained on the current system
options.B: Calculation of the initial purchase price only
options.C: The warranty duration of the new system only
options.D: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis

justification: Correct: TCO integrates all costs over the full lifecycle (acquisition, maintenance, operation, end-of-life), enabling a rigorous financial comparison between options.

text: An organization wants to evaluate the maturity of its agile teams before a major investment in a scaled agile tooling platform. What factor is most determinant to justify this investment?

options.A: A cost-benefit analysis accounting for cross-team coordination gains and organization-wide product visibility
options.B: The IT director's personal preference for a particular tool
options.C: The lowest price of the tool, regardless of fit
options.D: The number of marketing features of the tool

justification: Correct: a scaled tooling investment decision should be based on a genuine cost-benefit analysis integrating expected organizational gains.

text: A project manager must evaluate the impact of a major executive leadership change (new CEO) on their project's strategic priorities. What is the most prudent action?

options.A: Decide alone to change the project's objectives without validation
options.B: Continue without inquiring about the new priorities
options.C: Actively seek to understand the new strategic priorities and verify the ongoing alignment of the project with updated governance
options.D: Ignore any leadership change until an official communication is made

justification: Correct: proactively seeking alignment with new leadership and verifying the project's ongoing relevance is a proactive governance management approach.

text: An organization notices its agile teams generate value but that traditional quarterly ROI metrics don't capture this continuous incremental value well. What measurement adaptation is appropriate?

options.A: Abandon all financial measurement in favor of purely qualitative metrics
options.B: Completely ignore value measurement
options.C: Develop continuous incremental value indicators (e.g., value delivered per increment, cumulative return on investment) complementary to traditional financial measures
options.D: Force agile teams to produce classic quarterly financial reports identical to traditional projects

justification: Correct: continuous incremental value indicators, complementary to traditional financial measures, better capture the iterative nature of agile value creation.

text: A project manager must ensure their organization has the security certifications required (e.g., ISO 27001) to respond to a tender requiring this compliance level. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Claim compliance without actual verification to avoid losing the opportunity
options.B: Respond to the tender while hiding the absence of certification
options.C: Rigorously verify the current certification status and, if non-compliant, honestly assess the feasibility of obtaining certification within the deadline before committing
options.D: Ignore the certification requirement in the proposal

justification: Correct: rigorously verifying real status and honestly assessing feasibility before committing reflects responsible, ethical professional practice.

text: An organization developing agile products for a regulated healthcare market must reconcile fast iteration with strict regulatory traceability requirements. What approach is recommended?

options.A: Fully abandon agility for a complete waterfall cycle
options.B: Ignore traceability requirements to move faster
options.C: Defer all regulatory documentation to the very end of development
options.D: Adapt the Definition of Done to include regulatory traceability documentation for each increment, produced continuously rather than at the end

justification: Correct: integrating regulatory traceability into the Definition of Done for each increment ensures continuous compliance without sacrificing iterative agility.

text: A quality certification audit reveals that a project doesn't comply with an applicable ISO standard. What is the best response from the project manager?

options.A: Develop a corrective action plan and integrate it into the project management plan
options.B: Ignore the audit report as it slows the project
options.C: Dispute the audit findings without analysis
options.D: Resign from the project

justification: Correct: the PM must address non-conformances through a formal corrective action plan, integrated into project governance.

text: A nonprofit organization funding an agile project for a social app requires detailed quarterly impact reports. How can this be reconciled with the agile rhythm of continuous delivery?

options.A: Refuse to provide the reports requested by the donor
options.B: Abandon the agile approach for simpler reporting
options.C: Create a reporting process entirely disconnected from the team's actual work
options.D: Build quarterly impact reports from value metrics already tracked continuously (OKRs, adoption, feedback), without a heavy parallel reporting process

justification: Correct: reusing already continuously tracked value metrics to feed quarterly reports avoids duplicate reporting work while meeting donor requirements.

text: A project manager is asked by a partner to disclose confidential information about a competitor obtained inadvertently. What is the correct action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Disclose the information if it benefits the project
options.B: Disclose the information secretly with no notification
options.C: Use the information to negotiate a personal advantage
options.D: Refuse to disclose confidential information obtained inappropriately, and address the matter with honesty and fairness

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics requires refusing to use inappropriately obtained information and addressing the situation with transparency and integrity.

text: An organization automating tasks via AI evaluates the impact on jobs of some agile team members. What is the most socially responsible approach?

options.A: Communicate transparently about upcoming changes, offer reskilling and upskilling plans, and involve employees in the transition
options.B: Automate immediately with no communication or transition plan for affected employees
options.C: Ignore the human impact of automation as long as productivity increases
options.D: Lay off immediately with no notice or support

justification: Correct: transparent communication with reskilling plans and employee involvement reflects social and ethical responsibility toward disruptive technological change.

text: A project manager must evaluate whether continuing to invest in a project should be influenced by costs already incurred (sunk costs). What economic concept should NOT influence this decision?

options.A: The project's current strategic alignment
options.B: Sunk costs already incurred
options.C: Residual project risks
options.D: The expected future value and remaining ROI

justification: Correct: sunk costs should not influence a future decision, as they are already committed and unrecoverable regardless of the decision made.

text: An organization evaluates the impact of a new data privacy regulation on international transfers made by its agile teams working across borders. What is the priority action?

options.A: Ignore the regulation until formally enforced with a fine
options.B: Continue data transfers without any compliance verification
options.C: Consult legal experts to assess compliant transfer mechanisms and integrate necessary safeguards into the product's continuous delivery pipeline
options.D: Stop all cross-border collaboration without exploring alternatives

justification: Correct: consulting legal experts and integrating compliant safeguards into the delivery pipeline is the proactive approach that preserves both compliance and agile delivery speed.

text: A project manager must decide how to allocate limited procurement resources when two candidate suppliers offer different risk-cost profiles. What method of evaluation is appropriate?

options.A: Use a weighted multi-criteria analysis (price, quality, reliability, delivery) for an objective decision
options.B: Let the sponsor decide with no supporting data
options.C: Automatically choose the cheapest option
options.D: Choose at random

justification: Correct: a weighted multi-criteria scoring grid is the standard method to balance cost, quality, and risk in supplier selection.

text: An organization must evaluate the environmental impact (carbon footprint) of the cloud infrastructure used by its continuous development teams. Which action illustrates coherent integration of sustainability criteria in an agile context?

options.A: Completely ignore the carbon footprint since it's not a product priority
options.B: Wait for strict regulation before acting
options.C: Integrate sustainability criteria (infrastructure choice, cloud resource optimization) as acceptance criteria in certain technical user stories
options.D: Address sustainability only in a separate annual report unrelated to the backlog

justification: Correct: integrating sustainability criteria directly into acceptance criteria of technical user stories allows concrete, incremental action consistent with agility.

text: A project manager must ensure the project respects safety-at-work standards required by local law on a construction project. What is the project manager's primary responsibility here?

options.A: Consider that safety is solely the vendor's responsibility
options.B: Fully delegate with no personal oversight
options.C: Ignore minor safety incidents
options.D: Ensure safety standards are integrated into the project management plan, actively monitored, and respected by all parties, including subcontractors

justification: Correct: the PM must integrate and actively monitor compliance with safety standards, including at subcontractors, per legal and ethical obligations.

text: An organization wants to align its agile teams with overall company strategy without imposing excessive control. Which scaling framework allows this balance by combining top-down vision and bottom-up execution?

options.A: Complete absence of coordination between teams and leadership
options.B: Strict hierarchical control over every team decision
options.C: Scaling frameworks like SAFe or LeSS, combining a communicated strategic vision (PI Planning) with team execution autonomy
options.D: Detailed daily reporting from every team to senior leadership

justification: Correct: frameworks like SAFe or LeSS explicitly structure the balance between communicated strategic alignment and team execution autonomy.

text: A project manager must evaluate whether the organization has the internal technological capabilities to support a project requiring advanced cloud infrastructure. What analysis is appropriate?

options.A: A gap analysis between current capabilities and project needs
options.B: No analysis is necessary, the organization always has the necessary capabilities
options.C: A SWOT analysis of the main competitor only
options.D: A customer satisfaction survey

justification: Correct: a gap analysis between current organizational capabilities and specific project needs identifies necessary investments or training.

text: An organization constates that employee satisfaction in its agile teams is declining despite good delivery results. What organizational factor should be investigated as a priority?

options.A: The exact number of sprints completed per quarter
options.B: No factor, delivery performance alone guarantees satisfaction
options.C: The color of the Kanban boards used
options.D: Work-life balance, recognition, and perceived meaning of work, via a structured engagement survey

justification: Correct: a structured engagement survey exploring work-life balance, recognition, and perceived meaning identifies the root causes of declining satisfaction despite good results.

text: A project manager must ensure their organization respects quality standards imposed by an international certification body (e.g., ISO 9001). What action is essential before final certification?

options.A: Conduct regular internal audits to verify ongoing compliance with standard requirements
options.B: Fully delegate certification with no follow-up on the project
options.C: Ignore standard requirements if they seem excessive
options.D: Wait for the final external audit with no prior verification

justification: Correct: regular internal audits detect and correct compliance gaps before the final external audit, reducing the risk of certification failure.

text: An organization scaling agile at the enterprise level must decide how to fund product teams without stifling agility. Which funding mechanism is most appropriate?

options.A: Budget-based funding by increment/quarter (Lean budgeting) with regular value checkpoints instead of continuous detailed control
options.B: Remove all budget constraints for agile teams
options.C: Return to project-based funding with a full fixed upfront quote
options.D: Line-item budget control at every sprint

justification: Correct: Lean budgeting with regular value checkpoints reconciles financial discipline with execution agility.

text: A project manager discovers that a team member falsifies progress reports slightly to avoid difficult questions from the sponsor. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Ignore it if the discrepancy is minor and seemingly without consequence
options.B: Immediately correct the information, restore transparency with the sponsor, and remind the team of the importance of honesty in reporting
options.C: Cover up the falsification to protect the team member
options.D: Also falsify other reports to maintain consistency

justification: Correct: the Code of Ethics requires immediate corrective action to restore transparency and reaffirm reporting integrity standards with the team.

text: A digital organization is evaluating potential reputational impact of a minor security incident discovered by an agile team during a sprint. What communication action is most responsible?

options.A: Fix it silently without informing anyone within the organization
options.B: Assess the actual severity, inform relevant stakeholders (security, legal, leadership) per internal procedures, and remediate quickly
options.C: Conceal the incident as long as it remains minor and undetected publicly
options.D: Wait for users to discover the problem before acting

justification: Correct: assessing severity, informing relevant stakeholders per internal procedures, and remediating quickly is the responsible, transparent approach to any security incident.

text: A project manager must manage the expectations of a board of directors regarding geopolitical risks affecting an international project. What communication is most appropriate?

options.A: Exaggerate the risks to obtain more contingency budget
options.B: Completely avoid the topic of geopolitical risks
options.C: Downplay geopolitical risks to avoid worrying the board
options.D: Present a factual, balanced analysis of geopolitical risks, with scenarios and associated mitigation plans

justification: Correct: a factual, balanced presentation with scenarios and mitigation plans allows the board to make informed decisions on a complex strategic issue.

text: A project manager must handle a whistleblowing report from an employee about a potentially fraudulent practice on the project. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Take the report seriously, investigate appropriately and confidentially, and escalate to the relevant authorities if fraud is confirmed
options.B: Conceal the situation to avoid any scandal
options.C: Ignore the report to protect the project's reputation
options.D: Sanction the employee who made the report for raising the issue

justification: Correct: taking the report seriously, investigating confidentially and appropriately, and escalating if necessary reflects ethical, responsible management of a potential fraud report.

text: A project manager must evaluate the potential consequences of a political regime change in a country where their project operates. What category of risk does this primarily represent?

options.A: Political risk, a subset of external enterprise environmental factors
options.B: An internal risk related solely to team performance
options.C: No significant risk to consider
options.D: A purely technical risk related to product quality

justification: Correct: political risk is a major external environmental factor that can significantly affect the continuity, regulation, and security of an international project.

text: An organization evaluating whether to adopt an open architecture strategy for its agile product must weigh security implications. What is the most balanced approach?

options.A: Reject any form of openness to eliminate all security risk
options.B: Adopt full openness immediately with no security review, prioritizing speed to market
options.C: Assess security implications of an open architecture (API exposure, third-party access) alongside the ecosystem growth potential, with security requirements embedded in the technical backlog
options.D: Delegate the entire security decision to a single external consultant with no internal review

justification: Correct: assessing security implications alongside ecosystem growth potential, with security requirements embedded in the backlog, balances innovation and responsible risk management.

text: A project manager notices that a key stakeholder consistently changes requirements late in the schedule, causing confusion for the team. What communication competency is most useful here?

options.A: Clarify the formal change management process with the stakeholder and document each request for traceability
options.B: Exclude the stakeholder from future meetings
options.C: Accept every change immediately without documentation
options.D: Ignore the stakeholder's requests going forward

justification: Correct: clarifying and enforcing the formal change management process channels requests while ensuring traceability and consistency for the team.

text: A project manager must decompose the project scope into manageable components. Which tool produces a hierarchical decomposition of the work to be performed?

options.A: The Gantt chart
options.B: The communications management plan
options.C: The risk register
options.D: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

justification: Correct: the WBS hierarchically decomposes the entire project scope into manageable work packages.

text: A new environmental regulation takes effect during the execution of a construction project. What is the first appropriate step for the project manager?

options.A: Suspend the project indefinitely
options.B: Ignore the regulation until project closure
options.C: Inform only the sponsor with no further action
options.D: Assess the impact on the project and update the risk register and compliance documentation

justification: Correct: the PM must assess the enterprise environmental factors (EEF), document the impact, and adjust the risk management plan.

text: Two team members from different departments disagree persistently about resource priorities. Which conflict resolution style prioritizes long-term relationships over immediate gain?

options.A: Collaborate/Problem Solve
options.B: Withdraw/Avoid
options.C: Smooth/Accommodate
options.D: Force/Direct

justification: Correct: accommodating means yielding one's own needs to preserve harmony and the long-term relationship.

text: A project manager must determine the total project duration accounting for dependencies between activities. Which technique calculates project duration and identifies the critical path?

options.A: SWOT analysis
options.B: The affinity diagram
options.C: Earned value management (EVM)
options.D: The Critical Path Method (CPM)

justification: Correct: the Critical Path Method (CPM) calculates the minimum project duration by identifying the longest sequence of activities with no float.

text: A company evaluates several candidate projects with limited budgets. Which financial method allows comparing the relative profitability of projects of different sizes?

options.A: Internal Rate of Return (IRR) or benefit-cost ratio, which normalize comparison regardless of size
options.B: The number of employees assigned to the project
options.C: Net Present Value (NPV) only in absolute value
options.D: The project duration only

justification: Correct: IRR or benefit-cost ratio normalize profitability as a percentage or ratio, allowing fair comparison between projects of different sizes.

text: A project manager must select the most appropriate leadership style for a team member with low competence but high commitment to a new task. Which situational leadership style is most appropriate?

options.A: Laissez-faire
options.B: Delegating
options.C: Directing/Coaching
options.D: Supporting only, with no direction

justification: Correct: for low competence but high commitment, a directing/coaching style provides the guidance needed while nurturing enthusiasm.

text: A project manager must verify that costs incurred to date correspond to work actually performed. Which EVM indicator represents the actual cost spent?

options.A: Earned Value (EV)
options.B: Actual Cost (AC)
options.C: Cost Performance Index (CPI)
options.D: Planned Value (PV)

justification: Correct: Actual Cost (AC) represents the amount actually spent on the work performed at a given date.

text: A project manager must ensure the project respects the organization's information security policy when processing sensitive customer data. What action is a priority?

options.A: Ignore the policy if it slows the project
options.B: Integrate information security requirements into the project management plan and consult the security/compliance team early in planning
options.C: Wait for a security incident before acting
options.D: Process sensitive data without any particular protection measure

justification: Correct: security requirements must be integrated from planning, in consultation with relevant security/compliance experts.

text: A project manager notices a team member excels technically but lacks communication skills, causing friction with others. What development action is most appropriate?

options.A: Remove them from all interactions with other members
options.B: Ignore the problem since technical skills compensate
options.C: Offer coaching or training in communication skills to complement their recognized technical expertise
options.D: Sanction them for their lack of relational skills

justification: Correct: targeted communication skills development complements their technical expertise and reduces observed friction.

text: A project manager must ensure requirements traceability from initial requirements to final deliverables. Which tool ensures this traceability?

options.A: The risk register
options.B: The Gantt chart
options.C: The Requirements Traceability Matrix
options.D: The Kanban board

justification: Correct: the Requirements Traceability Matrix links each requirement to its origin, deliverables, and acceptance tests, ensuring complete coverage.

text: A project manager must integrate corporate social responsibility (CSR) requirements into a construction project. Which action best illustrates this integration?

options.A: Ignore CSR if it slightly increases costs
options.B: Fully delegate CSR to the marketing department with no link to project execution
options.C: Treat CSR as optional with no impact on project decisions
options.D: Integrate CSR criteria (environmental impact, fair labor conditions) into vendor selection criteria and the project management plan

justification: Correct: integrating concrete CSR criteria into vendor selection and the project management plan is the practice aligned with professional and societal responsibility.

text: A project manager must decide how to give corrective feedback to a team member about a repeated mistake. Which feedback approach is most constructive?

options.A: Send a formal email without any verbal discussion
options.B: Publicly criticize in front of the whole team to make a lasting impression
options.C: Avoid all feedback to prevent tension
options.D: Give private, factual feedback based on specific examples and oriented toward solutions

justification: Correct: effective feedback is private, factual, specific, and solution-oriented for concrete improvement.

text: A project manager must identify all potential stakeholders before the project starts. Which process covers this activity?

options.A: Control Costs
options.B: Identify Stakeholders
options.C: Close Project or Phase
options.D: Acquire Resources

justification: Correct: the 'Identify Stakeholders' process systematically catalogs individuals and organizations impacted by or impacting the project.

text: A project manager must evaluate the impact of a major exchange rate fluctuation on an international project financed in a foreign currency. Which enterprise environmental factor (EEF) is concerned?

options.A: The software tools used by the team
options.B: Internal organizational culture
options.C: The project manager's management style
options.D: Marketplace conditions and external economic factors

justification: Correct: currency fluctuations and marketplace conditions are external EEFs to monitor and integrate into risk management.

text: A project manager must recognize an exceptional team contribution with no budget available for a financial bonus. Which non-financial recognition is most effective?

options.A: Public recognition of the contribution, professional development opportunities, and expanded responsibilities
options.B: Do nothing due to lack of budget
options.C: Ignore the contribution to avoid creating expectations for others
options.D: Promise a future bonus with no certainty of delivering it

justification: Correct: public recognition and development opportunities are powerful non-financial motivators aligned with esteem and achievement needs.

text: A project manager must decide how to leverage resource leveling to manage constrained resource availability. What technique adjusts the schedule based on resource constraints?

options.A: The Ishikawa diagram
options.B: The affinity diagram
options.C: SWOT analysis
options.D: Resource Leveling

justification: Correct: resource leveling adjusts activity start and end dates to respect resource availability constraints, potentially modifying the critical path.

text: An international project manager must ensure the project simultaneously complies with anti-corruption laws in both the home country and the country of execution. What practice is essential?

options.A: Ignore anti-corruption laws if local practices differ
options.B: Apply only the less restrictive law of the two countries
options.C: Fully delegate to a local third party with no oversight
options.D: Apply the stricter standard between the two jurisdictions and document compliance for both legal frameworks

justification: Correct: applying the stricter standard between jurisdictions is the prudent compliance practice for extraterritorial laws like anti-corruption legislation (e.g., FCPA).

text: A project manager must decide how to allocate work when two team members have very different competence levels for the same critical task. What is the most balanced approach?

options.A: Combine the more competent member as lead with mentoring of the less experienced member to develop their skills while securing delivery
options.B: Split the work equally without regard to competence level
options.C: Consistently assign all critical tasks to the more competent member, exhausting their availability
options.D: Assign the critical task only to the less experienced member to challenge them

justification: Correct: combining leadership from the experienced member with structured mentoring secures delivery while developing team skills.

text: A project manager must select the least risky schedule compression method to catch up on a delay without significantly increasing costs. Which technique is most appropriate if activities can run in parallel without major risk?

options.A: Crashing (adding resources)
options.B: Fast-tracking (overlapping activities)
options.C: Stopping the project
options.D: Reducing scope without consultation

justification: Correct: fast-tracking consists of executing normally sequential activities in parallel, without major additional cost, when risk allows.

text: A project manager notices a competitor just launched a similar product, threatening the strategic relevance of the ongoing project. What is the best action?

options.A: Stop the project without consulting governance
options.B: Inform governance and reassess the business case to adjust project strategy if necessary (differentiation, acceleration)
options.C: Completely ignore the competitive threat
options.D: Immediately copy the competitor's product without analysis

justification: Correct: the PM must escalate to governance and reassess the business case to adjust strategy (differentiation, schedule acceleration, etc.).

text: A project manager must gain buy-in from a skeptical sponsor regarding the value of an enhanced risk management methodology. Which negotiation and influence approach is most effective?

options.A: Impose the method without justification
options.B: Bypass the sponsor and implement the method without their approval
options.C: Present concrete data (costs avoided, similar project examples) demonstrating the added value of the proposed approach
options.D: Immediately abandon the idea in the face of skepticism

justification: Correct: evidence-based influence (return on investment, benchmarks) is the most effective technique to convince a skeptical decision-maker.

text: A project manager must anticipate all activities that must precede others due to the physical nature of the work (e.g., foundations before walls). What dependency type does this illustrate?

options.A: Mandatory dependency (Hard Logic)
options.B: Discretionary dependency (Soft Logic)
options.C: External dependency
options.D: No dependency is necessary

justification: Correct: a mandatory dependency (hard logic) results from the intrinsic physical nature of the work, such as needing foundations before walls.

text: An organization evaluates whether to continue funding a digital product after 18 months without meeting adoption targets. Which Lean Startup principle guides this decision?

options.A: Automatically double the budget without analysis
options.B: The 'pivot or persevere' principle based on hypothesis validation data (build-measure-learn)
options.C: Continue indefinitely as a matter of persistence
options.D: Stop immediately without analyzing the causes of underperformance

justification: Correct: the build-measure-learn cycle guides the 'pivot or persevere' decision based on actual adoption and hypothesis validation data.

text: A project manager must decide how to develop the leadership skills of a high-potential team member. Which development action is most effective?

options.A: Keep them strictly in their current role with no growth opportunity
options.B: Gradually assign coordination responsibilities on sub-tasks, with mentoring and regular feedback
options.C: Do nothing and wait for them to develop skills on their own
options.D: Immediately promote them to a leadership position without preparation

justification: Correct: gradually assigning responsibilities with mentoring and regular feedback is a proven, structured approach to leadership development.

text: A project manager must determine the free float of a non-critical activity. What does this measure represent precisely?

options.A: The remaining budget allocated to the activity
options.B: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the early start date of the following activity
options.C: The total time available before the end of the project
options.D: The number of resources available for the activity

justification: Correct: free float is the delay possible for an activity without impacting the early start date of the immediately following activity.

text: A project manager must justify to leadership why a higher initial investment in quality will reduce total costs over the product lifecycle. Which economic concept supports this argument?

options.A: The project duration only
options.B: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), including non-conformance costs avoided long-term
options.C: The initial purchase price only
options.D: The number of employees involved in the project

justification: Correct: TCO demonstrates that an initial investment in quality often reduces non-conformance costs (rework, warranties, dissatisfaction) over the entire lifecycle.

text: A project manager must manage a team with a persistent personality conflict despite several mediation attempts. What is the appropriate last-resort option?

options.A: Force the two individuals to work even more closely together
options.B: Immediately fire both individuals without an HR process
options.C: Ignore the conflict indefinitely
options.D: Consider reorganizing roles or separating tasks between the two individuals as a last resort after mediation has failed

justification: Correct: after mediation fails, reorganizing roles or separating tasks is a pragmatic last resort to preserve collective performance.

text: A project manager must vary a formal system for managing change requests throughout the project. Which body is generally responsible for approving or rejecting these requests?

options.A: No formal body is necessary
options.B: The external vendor only
options.C: The Change Control Board (CCB)
options.D: Any team member individually

justification: Correct: the CCB is the formal body generally responsible for reviewing, approving, or rejecting change requests per a defined project governance process.

text: A project manager evaluates whether a project remains viable after a major shift in company strategic direction. What governance action is appropriate?

options.A: Decide alone to stop the project
options.B: Ignore the change in strategic direction
options.C: Continue the project without reassessment
options.D: Conduct a formal strategic alignment review with portfolio governance to decide on continuation, adjustment, or termination

justification: Correct: a major strategic change requires a formal portfolio governance review to determine the project's future.

text: A project manager must decide how to respond to a team member expressing a desire to leave the project for career development reasons, while the project is in a critical phase. What is the most professional approach?

options.A: Categorically refuse their departure and force them to stay until project completion
options.B: Penalize them for expressing this wish
options.C: Understand their motivations, explore progressive transition solutions (training a replacement, planning the departure), and respect their legitimate professional aspirations
options.D: Let them leave immediately with no transition planning

justification: Correct: understanding motivations and organizing a progressive transition respects legitimate professional aspirations while minimizing impact on the critical-phase project.

text: A project manager must finalize all administrative documents and obtain the client's final sign-off at the end of the project. Which process formalizes this step?

options.A: Close Project or Phase
options.B: Develop Team
options.C: Direct and Manage Project Work
options.D: Plan Scope Management

justification: Correct: the 'Close Project or Phase' process finalizes all administrative activities, obtains final acceptance, and archives project documents.

text: A project manager must evaluate whether their organization has the mature processes necessary to manage a complex multi-project program. What type of organizational assessment is appropriate?

options.A: A simple Gantt chart of the program
options.B: No assessment is necessary before starting
options.C: A Program Management Maturity Assessment
options.D: The program manager's resume only

justification: Correct: a program management maturity assessment verifies whether the organization has the processes, governance, and skills necessary before engaging in a complex program.

text: A project manager must decide how to structure a kickoff meeting to maximize engagement of the team and stakeholders. What element is most important to include?

options.A: A clear presentation of project objectives and vision, followed by discussion time for everyone to express expectations and concerns
options.B: A two-hour unilateral presentation by the project manager with no interaction
options.C: No particular structure, an informal meeting with no agenda
options.D: Only a detailed budget presentation with no strategic context

justification: Correct: combining a clear vision presentation with discussion time fosters engagement, mutual understanding, and collective ownership of the project from the start.

text: A project manager must choose a contract for an R&D project with highly uncertain and evolving scope. Which contract type is most appropriate?

options.A: Firm Fixed Price (FFP)
options.B: No formal contract is necessary
options.C: Fixed Price with Economic Price Adjustment (FP-EPA) only
options.D: Cost-Reimbursable, such as Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF)

justification: Correct: cost-reimbursable contracts like CPFF are suited for R&D projects with uncertain scope, allowing scope flexibility with reimbursement of actual costs incurred.

text: A project manager must decide if their organization has the culturally legitimate footing to execute a project in a country with significantly different business practices. What action is a priority?

options.A: Cancel the project without prior analysis
options.B: Strictly apply headquarters standards with no local adaptation
options.C: Conduct a local cultural context analysis, consult local experts, and adapt practices while respecting non-negotiable core ethical principles
options.D: Fully adopt local practices even if they contradict core ethical principles

justification: Correct: analyzing local cultural context with experts and adapting practices while preserving non-negotiable ethical principles balances cultural respect and professional integrity.

text: A project manager applies a leadership style that gives precise instructions to inexperienced team members while offering more autonomy to experts. Which leadership model best describes this approach?

options.A: Situational leadership (adapted to each person's competence and commitment level)
options.B: Autocratic leadership for everyone
options.C: Transactional leadership only
options.D: Laissez-faire leadership for everyone

justification: Correct: situational leadership adjusts style (directing, coaching, participating, delegating) based on each individual's maturity and experience.

text: A project manager must define formal acceptance criteria for deliverables with the client. Which process does this primarily belong to?

options.A: Validate Scope
options.B: Estimate Costs
options.C: Develop Project Charter
options.D: Identify Stakeholders

justification: Correct: the 'Validate Scope' process involves obtaining formal acceptance of completed deliverables by the client/sponsor per defined criteria.

text: A project manager must evaluate the implications of a new carbon tax on an energy-intensive industrial project. What planning action is appropriate?

options.A: Stop the project immediately without analysis
options.B: Integrate the carbon tax cost into updated financial projections and evaluate energy footprint reduction options
options.C: Ignore the carbon tax since it didn't exist when the project was launched
options.D: Automatically pass the cost to the client without contract negotiation

justification: Correct: integrating the cost into updated projections and evaluating energy reduction options is the proactive, responsible approach to a new environmental regulatory factor.

text: A project manager notices two team members have very different communication styles (one direct and factual, the other more relational and indirect), causing frequent misunderstandings. What action fosters better collaboration?

options.A: Raise mutual awareness of communication style differences and establish explicit team norms for key exchanges
options.B: Permanently separate them to avoid any contact
options.C: Ask one of the two to completely change their natural style
options.D: Ignore the misunderstandings as long as they don't block the project

justification: Correct: mutual awareness of communication styles and explicit team norms durably reduce misunderstandings.

text: A project manager must determine which activities have zero float and determine the project's minimum duration. What are these activities collectively called?

options.A: The critical path
options.B: Project milestones
options.C: The near-critical path
options.D: Intermediate deliverables

justification: Correct: the critical path groups activities with zero (or minimal) total float that determine the project's minimum duration.

text: A project manager must ensure their organization has the security certifications required (e.g., ISO 27001) to respond to a tender requiring this compliance level. What is the appropriate action?

options.A: Rigorously verify the current certification status and, if non-compliant, honestly assess the feasibility of obtaining certification within the deadline before committing
options.B: Respond to the tender while hiding the absence of certification
options.C: Ignore the certification requirement in the proposal
options.D: Claim compliance without actual verification to avoid losing the opportunity

justification: Correct: rigorously verifying real status and honestly assessing feasibility before committing reflects responsible, ethical professional practice.

text: A project manager must decide how to manage a highly skilled team member who consistently refuses to document their work, creating a bus factor risk. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Replace them immediately without discussion
options.B: Document their work for them indefinitely
options.C: Accept the situation because their technical skills are indispensable
options.D: Explain the organizational risk of lacking documentation and make documentation an explicit performance expectation

justification: Correct: explaining the organizational risk and making documentation an explicit performance expectation holds the person accountable while reducing dependency risk.

text: A project manager must guarantee consistency between the cost management plan, the schedule management plan, and the scope management plan. Which document integrates all these subsidiary plans?

options.A: The weekly status report
options.B: The Project Management Plan
options.C: The risk register only
options.D: Team members' resumes

justification: Correct: the Project Management Plan integrates all subsidiary plans (cost, schedule, scope, quality, etc.) in a coherent, coordinated manner.

text: A project manager evaluates the impact of a rapidly evolving competitive landscape on their organization's ability to sustain a project's strategic relevance. Which strategic external indicator should be monitored?

options.A: The size of the project team
options.B: The number of internal status reports issued
options.C: Market intelligence on customer needs and competing offerings, compared against the project's value delivery timeline
options.D: The internal number of team meetings held

justification: Correct: comparing market and competitive evolution to the project's value delivery timeline assesses whether the project risks losing strategic relevance.

text: A project manager must gain agreement from two departments on a shared resource allocation conflict between competing organizational priorities. What is the first appropriate step?

options.A: Abandon the affected activities of their own project
options.B: Escalate to the PMO or portfolio governance committee for arbitration based on strategic priorities
options.C: Decide alone without consulting other project managers
options.D: Negotiate directly with the other project manager with no formal framework and take the resources

justification: Correct: a cross-project resource conflict falls under PMO/portfolio governance arbitration, based on organizational priorities.

text: A project manager notices deliverable quality doesn't consistently meet defined standards despite quality controls. Which action falls under quality assurance rather than quality control?

options.A: Reject non-conforming deliverables one by one
options.B: Inspect each deliverable individually to detect defects
options.C: Audit and improve production processes to prevent defects upstream
options.D: Do nothing until the client complains

justification: Correct: quality assurance focuses on auditing and improving processes to prevent defects at the source, rather than detecting them after the fact.

text: A project manager learns that part of the work is subcontracted to an organization with ethically questionable labor practices. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Ignore the subcontractor's practices as long as deadlines are met
options.B: Cover up the questionable practices to avoid jeopardizing the project
options.C: Continue the collaboration with no verification
options.D: Assess the situation, engage in dialogue with the subcontractor about expected standards, and escalate to governance if practices don't improve

justification: Correct: assessing, engaging in dialogue about expected standards, and escalating if necessary reflects responsible, ethical management of a conduct issue with an external partner.

text: A project manager must motivate a team facing intense workload over an extended period before a critical milestone. Which action is most durable to maintain performance?

options.A: Plan recovery periods after the peak load, clearly communicate the milestone's importance, and recognize the efforts made
options.B: Reduce breaks and time off for the entire project duration
options.C: Require unlimited overtime until the milestone
options.D: Ignore signs of fatigue in the team

justification: Correct: planning recovery periods, communicating the milestone's meaning, and recognizing effort are durable practices for managing performance under temporary high load.

text: A project manager must determine the order of activities considering Finish-to-Start (FS) type constraints. What does this dependency relationship mean?

options.A: The successor activity must finish before the predecessor starts
options.B: Both activities must start at the same time
options.C: The successor activity cannot start until the predecessor activity finishes
options.D: There is no constraint between the two activities

justification: Correct: the Finish-to-Start (FS) relationship is the most common and means the successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes.

text: A project manager must ensure their organization respects quality standards imposed by an international certification body (e.g., ISO 9001). What action is essential before final certification?

options.A: Fully delegate certification with no follow-up on the project
options.B: Ignore standard requirements if they seem excessive
options.C: Conduct regular internal audits to verify ongoing compliance with standard requirements
options.D: Wait for the final external audit with no prior verification

justification: Correct: regular internal audits detect and correct compliance gaps before the final external audit, reducing the risk of certification failure.

text: A project manager must decide how to give recognition to a mentoring role that a senior team member takes on informally, creating extra unrecognized workload. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Ban informal mentoring between colleagues
options.B: Formally recognize the mentoring role in the senior member's workload and performance objectives
options.C: Ask the junior to stop seeking help
options.D: Ignore the extra workload since mentoring is supposed to be free

justification: Correct: formally recognizing the mentoring role values this precious contribution and avoids unrecognized overload of the experienced member.

text: A project manager must select the best technique to generate a maximum number of creative ideas during a problem-solving session with the team. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.A: Earned value analysis
options.B: Structured brainstorming
options.C: RACI matrix
options.D: Network diagram

justification: Correct: structured brainstorming is specifically designed to generate a maximum number of creative ideas in a collaborative problem-solving setting.

text: A project manager evaluates the impact of a major exchange in company leadership (new CEO) on their project's strategic priorities. What is the most prudent action?

options.A: Actively seek to understand the new strategic priorities and verify the ongoing alignment of the project with updated governance
options.B: Ignore any leadership change until an official communication is made
options.C: Continue without inquiring about the new priorities
options.D: Decide alone to change the project's objectives without validation

justification: Correct: proactively seeking alignment with new leadership and verifying the project's ongoing relevance is a proactive governance management approach.

text: A project manager must decide how to manage a team member who openly disagrees with a strategic decision already approved by governance. What leadership approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Ignore their concerns entirely with no explanation
options.B: Remove them from the project immediately for insubordination
options.C: Ban any expression of disagreement going forward
options.D: Listen to their concerns, explain the context of the decision, and clarify the expectation of 'disagree and commit' once governance has decided

justification: Correct: listening, explaining context, and clarifying the 'disagree and commit' principle respects both legitimate expression and the need to move forward collectively after a governance decision.

text: A project manager must choose the best method to validate that a complex deliverable meets all functional requirements before going to production. Which activity is appropriate?

options.A: The affinity diagram
options.B: SWOT analysis
options.C: Team brainstorming
options.D: User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

justification: Correct: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) formally validates that the deliverable meets functional requirements from the end user's perspective before production.

text: A project manager is asked by a partner to disclose confidential information about a competitor obtained inadvertently. What is the correct action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Disclose the information secretly with no notification
options.B: Disclose the information if it benefits the project
options.C: Refuse to disclose confidential information obtained inappropriately, and address the matter with honesty and fairness
options.D: Use the information to negotiate a personal advantage

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics requires refusing to use inappropriately obtained information and addressing the situation with transparency and integrity.

text: A project manager must choose the best approach for integrating a team member with a disability requiring reasonable accommodations. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Systematically refuse any special accommodation
options.B: Ignore the accommodation request to avoid setting a precedent
options.C: Discuss with the person to understand their specific needs and implement reasonable accommodations in coordination with HR
options.D: Remove the person from the project to avoid complications

justification: Correct: discussing specific needs and coordinating with HR for reasonable accommodations is the inclusive and legally compliant appropriate practice.

text: A project manager must choose the best diagram to represent cause-and-effect relationships for a recurring quality problem. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: The Gantt chart
options.B: The Ishikawa diagram (fishbone diagram)
options.C: The RACI matrix
options.D: The Kanban board

justification: Correct: the Ishikawa diagram (cause-and-effect) visually structures the potential causes of a quality problem by category (manpower, method, material, etc.).

text: A project manager discovers that an official project financial report contains a significant error favorable to the project, unnoticed by the finance team. What is the appropriate action per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Immediately report the error to the relevant parties and correct the report, regardless of whether it is favorable or unfavorable
options.B: Leave the error in place since it's favorable to the project
options.C: Correct the error secretly without informing anyone
options.D: Wait to see if someone else notices before acting

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics requires reporting and correcting any significant reporting error, whether favorable or unfavorable, in the name of transparency and honesty.

text: During a Daily Scrum, a senior team member repeatedly criticizes junior members' ideas, causing them to withdraw from participating. What should the Scrum Master do first?

options.A: Do nothing, since the Daily Scrum belongs to the development team
options.B: Remove the senior member from the team
options.C: Ask the Product Owner to resolve the issue
options.D: Coach the senior member privately on the impact of their behavior and facilitate a team working agreement

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master is a servant-leader who protects psychological safety; private coaching followed by a team working agreement is the appropriate response.

text: A team using a Kanban board wants to better visualize recurring blockers in its workflow. Which practice is most effective?

options.A: Ignore blockers as long as work generally progresses
options.B: Mark blocked items visually (e.g., red stickers) and prioritize discussing blockers during daily synchronization
options.C: Remove blocked items from the board so problems aren't visible
options.D: Wait until the end of the month to analyze blockers

justification: Correct: visually marking blockers and prioritizing them in daily synchronization is standard Kanban practice for quickly resolving flow obstacles.

text: An organization undergoing agile transformation faces strong cultural resistance from middle management. What strategic action is most effective for project leadership?

options.A: Involve middle management in co-designing the change and demonstrate value through pilot projects
options.B: Force adoption through strict top-down directives
options.C: Bypass middle management by working directly with the teams
options.D: Postpone the transformation until full consensus is reached

justification: Correct: effective organizational change management involves relevant stakeholders and uses evidence of value (pilots) to build buy-in.

text: A new team member joins an established Scrum team and feels lost among existing practices. Which action best supports their integration?

options.A: Assign them immediately to the most complex tasks to accelerate learning
options.B: Let them observe without intervention for several sprints
options.C: Organize structured onboarding including the team's working agreement, a peer mentor, and regular check-ins
options.D: Give them only technical documentation with no human support

justification: Correct: structured onboarding with peer mentoring fosters rapid integration and understanding of team norms.

text: A team using Scrumban wants to combine sprint predictability with continuous flow flexibility. Which hybrid practice characterizes this approach?

options.A: Use no visual board at all
options.B: Remove all flow or velocity measurements
options.C: Fully abandon fixed iterations while retaining WIP limits and key Scrum ceremonies adapted to flow
options.D: Use exclusively the classic waterfall cycle

justification: Correct: Scrumban typically combines removing strict fixed iterations (Kanban-style continuous flow) while retaining some Scrum ceremonies and WIP limits to manage flow.

text: A company measures the success of its initiatives via an OKR framework rather than a traditional project plan. What is the main advantage of this framework in an agile context?

options.A: It aligns teams on measurable, ambitious objectives while leaving flexibility on the means (the 'how')
options.B: It completely replaces the need for communication between teams
options.C: It imposes a rigid detailed 12-month plan
options.D: It completely eliminates the need to measure performance

justification: Correct: OKRs align teams on measurable key results while preserving autonomy on how to achieve them, consistent with the agile spirit.

text: A Scrum Master notices the team never questions the estimates of the most senior member, even when they seem unrealistic. What bias does this illustrate and what should be done?

options.A: Ask the senior member to estimate everything alone from now on
options.B: No bias, it's normal to trust experience
options.C: An authority bias; introduce anonymous voting (Planning Poker) so everyone estimates independently before discussion
options.D: Remove team estimation entirely

justification: Correct: Planning Poker with simultaneous, anonymous voting reduces authority influence and encourages fairer collective estimation.

text: A team wants to visualize the overall user journey to organize its backlog for a complex product. Which technique is most useful?

options.A: The control chart
options.B: The Ishikawa diagram
options.C: The RACI matrix
options.D: Story Mapping

justification: Correct: Story Mapping visualizes the end-to-end user journey, helping identify coherent value slices for MVP releases.

text: An organization wants to assess whether its culture is open enough to support a large-scale agile transformation. Which cultural factor is most determinant?

options.A: The number of digital tools available
options.B: The number of certifications held by employees
options.C: Tolerance for failure, trust in teams, and openness to decentralized decision-making
options.D: The size of the physical offices

justification: Correct: a durable agile culture relies on tolerance for failure (learning), trust, and decentralized decision-making, fundamental cultural elements.

text: A junior Product Owner lacks confidence to make difficult prioritization decisions and systematically escalates to their manager. What action best supports their development?

options.A: Make the prioritization decisions on their behalf
options.B: Ignore the situation since it's not the team's problem
options.C: Coach the PO on prioritization techniques and gradually build their decision-making autonomy, reinforcing their legitimacy with management
options.D: Report their lack of competence to leadership for replacement

justification: Correct: progressive coaching and reinforcing the PO's legitimacy with management builds durable autonomy.

text: A team wants to quickly validate a product hypothesis with minimal development effort. Which practice best matches this objective?

options.A: Create an MVP (Minimum Viable Product) or rapid prototype to test the hypothesis with real users before investing further
options.B: Develop a complete, exhaustive feature before any user testing
options.C: Ignore user feedback and rely solely on the team's intuition
options.D: Wait six months before any user feedback

justification: Correct: an MVP or rapid prototype validates a hypothesis with minimal effort before committing greater resources, a key Lean Startup and agile principle.

text: An organization considers adopting an inner source approach (internal open-source-style code sharing) to improve reuse across teams. What is the main organizational benefit of this approach?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for code governance
options.B: It removes the need for automated tests
options.C: It makes all technical documentation unnecessary
options.D: It fosters component reuse across teams, reduces duplicated effort, and improves technical consistency organization-wide

justification: Correct: inner source fosters component reuse, reduces duplicated effort, and improves technical consistency across teams, a key organizational benefit.

text: A Product Owner frequently changes sprint priorities mid-sprint, disrupting the development team. What is the Scrum Master's best action?

options.A: Let the team decide alone without involving the PO
options.B: Coach the PO on the principle of sprint immutability and channel new priorities into the product backlog for the next sprint
options.C: Accept all changes without discussion to avoid upsetting the PO
options.D: Prevent the PO from attending ceremonies

justification: Correct: the Scrum Guide protects sprint content; the Scrum Master should coach the PO on this principle while respecting their authority over the backlog.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage accumulated technical debt that progressively slows velocity. Which practice is most recommended?

options.A: Stop all feature development for six months to refactor everything
options.B: Allocate a regular share of sprint capacity to reducing technical debt, made visible in the backlog
options.C: Transfer responsibility for technical debt to the client
