options.D: Ignore technical debt as long as features are delivered

justification: Correct: allocating a regular capacity share to technical debt, made visible and prioritized in the backlog, is the recommended sustainable practice.

text: A nonprofit organization using agile methods must report on the social impact of its projects to donors, beyond velocity metrics. Which measurement approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Develop specific social impact indicators (e.g., beneficiaries reached, measured behavior change) aligned with the organization's theory of change
options.B: Limit reporting to the number of completed user stories
options.C: Only communicate velocity and the number of sprints completed
options.D: Ignore any impact measurement since agile methods don't lend themselves to it

justification: Correct: specific social impact indicators, aligned with the organization's theory of change, meet donor accountability expectations, complementing internal agile metrics.

text: A Product Owner lacks availability to answer the team's questions during the sprint, slowing development. What is the best durable solution?

options.A: Halt the sprint until the PO is available
options.B: The team makes all product decisions without the PO permanently
options.C: Ignore the problem and hope for spontaneous improvement
options.D: Negotiate dedicated availability windows with the PO or designate a trained proxy PO for routine decisions

justification: Correct: negotiating dedicated windows or establishing a trained proxy PO maintains velocity while respecting the PO's role on strategic decisions.

text: A financial services organization developing agile products must comply with regulatory resilience (stress testing) requirements. How can this be integrated without breaking the agile rhythm?

options.A: Ignore resilience requirements to keep pace with sprints
options.B: Abandon agility entirely in favor of a full waterfall cycle dedicated only to testing
options.C: Defer all resilience testing to the very end of the project, just before the regulatory audit
options.D: Integrate automated, incremental resilience tests with each increment delivered, with regular compliance reviews rather than a single final test

justification: Correct: integrating automated, incremental resilience tests with each increment, with regular compliance reviews, reconciles strict regulatory requirements with continuous agile rhythm.

text: An organization is evaluating whether to invest in generative AI tools to accelerate agile product development. What evaluation approach is most responsible?

options.A: Adopt immediately with no risk assessment (bias, data security, intellectual property)
options.B: Completely ignore this technology out of excessive caution
options.C: Let each developer decide individually with no organizational framework
options.D: Conduct a structured risk and benefit assessment (data security, algorithmic bias, intellectual property) before large-scale deployment, with controlled pilots

justification: Correct: a structured risk and benefit assessment with controlled pilots allows responsible, progressive adoption of a high-potential but genuinely risky emerging technology.

text: Two team members from different departments disagree persistently about resource priorities in a cross-functional agile initiative. Which conflict resolution style prioritizes long-term relationships over immediate gain?

options.A: Force/Direct
options.B: Withdraw/Avoid
options.C: Collaborate/Problem Solve
options.D: Smooth/Accommodate

justification: Correct: accommodating means yielding one's own needs to preserve harmony and the long-term relationship.

text: A Product Owner must decide how to manage a backlog that has become too large and hard to navigate after months of idea collection. What backlog management action is appropriate?

options.A: Randomly delete half the backlog without analysis
options.B: Ignore the problem since a large backlog has no impact on the team
options.C: Keep all items indefinitely, even obsolete ones, in case they become relevant again
options.D: Perform regular backlog refinement, archiving or removing obsolete items and reorganizing by theme/value

justification: Correct: regular refinement with archiving or removal of obsolete items and reorganization by theme/value maintains a manageable, relevant backlog.

text: An organization evaluates if it should continue funding a digital product after 18 months without meeting adoption targets. Which Lean Startup principle guides this decision?

options.A: The 'pivot or persevere' principle based on hypothesis validation data (build-measure-learn)
options.B: Stop immediately without analyzing the causes of underperformance
options.C: Continue indefinitely as a matter of persistence
options.D: Automatically double the budget without analysis

justification: Correct: the build-measure-learn cycle guides the 'pivot or persevere' decision based on actual adoption and hypothesis validation data.

text: A Scrum Master remarks that some team members never actively participate in retrospectives. Which facilitation technique can improve participation?

options.A: Vary retrospective formats (e.g., prior silent writing, anonymous polls) to give voice to all participation styles
options.B: Reserve speaking time only for the most experienced members
options.C: Force each member to speak in turn with no variation in format
options.D: Remove retrospectives since they aren't useful

justification: Correct: varying formats (silent writing, anonymous polls, visual workshops) includes different participation styles and yields richer feedback.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage a critical external dependency on a third-party vendor with uncertain timelines. Which hybrid approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Fully transfer responsibility to the vendor with no active follow-up
options.B: Completely ignore the external dependency in sprint planning
options.C: Indefinitely delay all sprints until the dependency is fully resolved
options.D: Track the external dependency via a dedicated risk register, plan contingencies (buffer, alternative), and factor it into planning of the affected sprints

justification: Correct: actively tracking the dependency with a dedicated risk register and contingency plans, while factoring it into sprint planning, is a pragmatic hybrid approach combining predictive rigor with agile flexibility.

text: An organization scaling from 3 to 15 agile teams within a year must anticipate a major organizational risk. What risk should be prioritized?

options.A: The risk that teams become too small
options.B: Loss of product coherence and cross-team communication without an adapted coordination framework (e.g., Scrum of Scrums, architectural alignment)
options.C: No particular risk, agility automatically scales to any size
options.D: The risk that Scrum ceremonies become too short

justification: Correct: rapid growth in the number of teams without a coordination mechanism (Scrum of Scrums, guilds, architectural alignment) risks fragmenting product coherence and communication.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team member excels technically but adopts a dismissive tone toward others' questions, freezing their learning. What action should be taken?

options.A: Ignore the situation as long as delivery isn't affected
options.B: Address the behavior directly, explain its negative impact on collective learning and psychological safety, and set clear expectations of mutual respect
options.C: Tolerate the behavior because their technical skills are valuable
options.D: Discourage others from asking questions to avoid friction

justification: Correct: directly addressing the behavior with clear expectations of mutual respect protects psychological safety and collective learning without denying the person's technical value.

text: A team practicing mob programming occasionally finds that some developers feel it slows their perceived individual productivity. What is the best way to objectively evaluate the practice?

options.A: Impose mob programming 100% of the time without discussion
options.B: Continue indefinitely without ever evaluating impact
options.C: Objectively measure the impact on shared metrics (code quality, defect resolution time, knowledge sharing) rather than perceived individual productivity
options.D: Abandon it immediately based on individual impressions

justification: Correct: evaluating objective shared metrics allows a data-driven decision rather than one based on subjective perceived individual productivity.

text: An organization wants to align its agile teams with overall company strategy without imposing excessive control. Which scaling framework allows this balance by combining top-down vision and bottom-up execution?

options.A: Complete absence of coordination between teams and leadership
options.B: Scaling frameworks like SAFe or LeSS, combining a communicated strategic vision (PI Planning) with team execution autonomy
options.C: Strict hierarchical control over every team decision
options.D: Detailed daily reporting from every team to senior leadership

justification: Correct: frameworks like SAFe or LeSS explicitly structure the balance between communicated strategic alignment and team execution autonomy.

text: An Agile Coach observes that a high-performing team shows signs of burnout (rising absenteeism, irritability). What is the priority action to preserve sustainable performance?

options.A: Investigate the signs of burnout, adjust workload, and reinforce the agile principle of sustainable pace
options.B: Maintain the same pace since results are excellent
options.C: Praise the team and give them even more work to capitalize on their performance
options.D: Ignore the signs as long as velocity remains stable

justification: Correct: investigating and adjusting workload per the sustainable pace principle prevents burnout and preserves long-term performance.

text: Multiple teams working on the same product have different definitions of Done, creating integration problems. What action at the Scrum of Scrums level is appropriate?

options.A: Facilitate cross-team alignment on a common product-level Definition of Done, with team-specific additions if needed
options.B: Impose the most experienced team's definition without discussion
options.C: Remove the concept of Definition of Done
options.D: Let each team keep its own definition indefinitely

justification: Correct: collaborative alignment on a common product-level DoD, with local extensions, resolves integration problems while respecting team autonomy.

text: An organization notices its agile teams generate value but that traditional quarterly ROI metrics don't capture this continuous incremental value well. What measurement adaptation is appropriate?

options.A: Abandon all financial measurement in favor of purely qualitative metrics
options.B: Develop continuous incremental value indicators (e.g., value delivered per increment, cumulative return on investment) complementary to traditional financial measures
options.C: Force agile teams to produce classic quarterly financial reports identical to traditional projects
options.D: Completely ignore value measurement

justification: Correct: continuous incremental value indicators, complementary to traditional financial measures, better capture the iterative nature of agile value creation.

text: A Scrum Master joining as an external consultant on an existing team perceives initial distrust toward their role. What approach best builds trust?

options.A: First observe existing dynamics, actively listen to the team's concerns, and demonstrate value through concrete facilitation actions before introducing changes
options.B: Immediately impose strict new rules to establish authority
options.C: Complain to leadership about the team's lack of cooperation in the first week
options.D: Ignore the distrust and continue as planned

justification: Correct: observing, listening, and progressively demonstrating value is the most effective approach to building trust with a distrustful team facing a new consultant.

text: A team wants to improve the accuracy of its delivery forecasts for upcoming quarters. Which technique combines historical velocity data with an uncertainty margin?

options.A: Probabilistic forecasting (Monte Carlo) based on team velocity history
options.B: A single point estimate with no uncertainty margin
options.C: Rely solely on the Product Owner's intuition
options.D: Completely ignore velocity history

justification: Correct: Monte Carlo probabilistic forecasting uses velocity history to generate a distribution of possible delivery dates with an associated confidence level, more realistic than a point estimate.

text: An organization automating tasks via AI evaluates the impact on jobs of some agile team members. What is the most socially responsible approach?

options.A: Ignore the human impact of automation as long as productivity increases
options.B: Communicate transparently about upcoming changes, offer reskilling and upskilling plans, and involve employees in the transition
options.C: Lay off immediately with no notice or support
options.D: Automate immediately with no communication or transition plan for affected employees

justification: Correct: transparent communication with reskilling plans and employee involvement reflects social and ethical responsibility toward disruptive technological change.

text: A distributed agile team across several countries has seen a decline in social cohesion since moving to 100% remote work. What action best rebuilds team connection?

options.A: Increase only the frequency of formal work meetings
options.B: Organize dedicated informal moments (virtual coffees, icebreakers) alongside formal ceremonies to reinforce human connection
options.C: Ignore the decline in social cohesion since it doesn't affect performance
options.D: Ban all informal communication to focus on productivity

justification: Correct: dedicated informal moments recreate the social bond lost from physical proximity, fostering cohesion and team psychological safety.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage user stories that turn out to be much more complex than estimated once development has begun. What practice is appropriate?

options.A: Hide the problem until the sprint review
options.B: Abandon the story completely without communication
options.C: Force completion within the current sprint at all costs, even if quality is compromised
options.D: Discuss the discovery transparently with the PO, consider splitting or deferring the story, and adjust the sprint accordingly

justification: Correct: a transparent discussion with the PO allowing informed splitting or deferring of the story is the appropriate agile practice when unexpected complexity is discovered.

text: An organization is evaluating whether to prioritize a proprietary closed-development approach or an open one (public APIs, partner ecosystem) for its agile product. Which strategic factor is most determinant?

options.A: The developers' aesthetic preference for one architecture type
options.B: The product's brand color
options.C: Analysis of the competitive ecosystem, growth potential through partnerships, and security/dependency risks associated with each approach
options.D: The number of lines of code already written

justification: Correct: analyzing the competitive ecosystem, partnership growth potential, and security/dependency risks provides a solid strategic basis for this open vs. closed architecture choice.

text: A Scrum Master notices a very cohesive team unconsciously excludes ideas from a new member with a different background (groupthink). What action fosters better diversity of thought?

options.A: Remove the new member from the team to avoid tension
options.B: Ignore the groupthink phenomenon
options.C: Let the group continue, cohesion takes priority over diversity of opinion
options.D: Deliberately introduce techniques favoring divergent perspectives (devil's advocate, systematic round-robin) and explicitly value the new member's contributions

justification: Correct: structured techniques like devil's advocate or systematic round-robin actively counter groupthink and value diverse perspectives.

text: A team wants to decide how to handle a spike (research task) that reveals a feature is technically infeasible as originally envisioned. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Hide the findings to avoid disappointing stakeholders
options.B: Abandon the entire product initiative based on one spike
options.C: Share the spike findings transparently with the PO and team, and collaboratively redefine the feature's scope or approach based on the new information
options.D: Proceed with the original plan regardless of the spike's findings

justification: Correct: transparently sharing spike findings and collaboratively adjusting the approach is the appropriate empirical response to new technical information.

text: An organization evaluating whether to adopt an open architecture strategy for its agile product must weigh security implications. What is the most balanced approach?

options.A: Adopt full openness immediately with no security review, prioritizing speed to market
options.B: Reject any form of openness to eliminate all security risk
options.C: Assess security implications of an open architecture (API exposure, third-party access) alongside the ecosystem growth potential, with security requirements embedded in the technical backlog
options.D: Delegate the entire security decision to a single external consultant with no internal review

justification: Correct: assessing security implications alongside ecosystem growth potential, with security requirements embedded in the backlog, balances innovation and responsible risk management.

text: An experienced agile team asks the Scrum Master to reduce their involvement, feeling sufficiently autonomous. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Leave the team entirely with no transition
options.B: Ignore the team's request
options.C: Jointly assess where real autonomy exists, shift the role toward on-demand coaching and facilitation, while remaining available for organizational impediments
options.D: Categorically refuse to reduce their involvement

justification: Correct: progressively shifting toward on-demand coaching while remaining available for organizational impediments respects growing autonomy while maintaining a safety net.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage flaky (intermittently failing) automated tests that undermine trust in the CI pipeline. What action is appropriate?

options.A: Disable the entire CI pipeline until further notice
options.B: Identify and quarantine flaky tests, prioritize fixing their root causes, and track flakiness as a quality metric
options.C: Delete all tests that fail intermittently without investigation
options.D: Ignore flaky tests and let developers manually re-run failed builds indefinitely

justification: Correct: identifying, quarantining, and prioritizing root-cause fixes for flaky tests, while tracking flakiness as a metric, restores CI reliability systematically.

text: A digital organization is evaluating potential reputational impact of a minor security incident discovered by an agile team during a sprint. What communication action is most responsible?

options.A: Wait for users to discover the problem before acting
options.B: Conceal the incident as long as it remains minor and undetected publicly
options.C: Assess the actual severity, inform relevant stakeholders (security, legal, leadership) per internal procedures, and remediate quickly
options.D: Fix it silently without informing anyone within the organization

justification: Correct: assessing severity, informing relevant stakeholders per internal procedures, and remediating quickly is the responsible, transparent approach to any security incident.

text: A Scrum Master must handle a situation where the Product Owner and an external stakeholder disagree publicly on a feature's priority during a sprint review. What action is appropriate in the moment?

options.A: Politely refocus the discussion by proposing to address the prioritization question outside the review, with the PO as final decision-maker for the backlog
options.B: Let the debate escalate in front of the team
options.C: Decide the priority themselves in place of the PO
options.D: Immediately cancel the sprint review

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master facilitates by refocusing the discussion and reaffirming that final prioritization authority belongs to the PO, outside the review setting.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage a backlog item that spans multiple teams' responsibilities. What coordination practice is appropriate?

options.A: Assign it entirely to one team without discussion, regardless of dependencies
options.B: Duplicate the entire item across all teams to avoid coordination
options.C: Leave it unassigned indefinitely until a team volunteers
options.D: Break the item into smaller pieces aligned with each team's ownership, coordinate through a shared dependency board, and clarify integration points

justification: Correct: breaking the item into smaller pieces with clear ownership and shared dependency tracking ensures coordinated, efficient cross-team delivery.

text: A nonprofit organization funding an agile project for a social app requires detailed quarterly impact reports. How can this be reconciled with the agile rhythm of continuous delivery?

options.A: Build quarterly impact reports from value metrics already tracked continuously (OKRs, adoption, feedback), without a heavy parallel reporting process
options.B: Abandon the agile approach for simpler reporting
options.C: Create a reporting process entirely disconnected from the team's actual work
options.D: Refuse to provide the reports requested by the donor

justification: Correct: reusing already continuously tracked value metrics to feed quarterly reports avoids duplicate reporting work while meeting donor requirements.

text: A multicultural Scrum team has different interpretations of 'being open and honest' in retrospectives, with some avoiding direct criticism out of cultural respect. What adaptation supports an effective retrospective?

options.A: Hold retrospectives only with the culturally more direct members
options.B: Require the same direct frankness from everyone regardless of cultural context
options.C: Remove retrospectives for this multicultural team
options.D: Use retrospective formats that allow indirect or written expression (e.g., anonymous cards) and explicitly value any constructive form of feedback

justification: Correct: formats allowing indirect or written expression respect cultural diversity while preserving the retrospective's continuous improvement goal.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage code quality in continuous delivery when tests take too long to run. What practice addresses this challenge?

options.A: Only run tests once a month regardless of delivery frequency
options.B: Optimize the test suite (parallelization, prioritizing fast unit tests) while maintaining sufficient coverage for critical paths
options.C: Remove all tests to speed up delivery
options.D: Delegate all testing responsibility to end users after release

justification: Correct: optimizing the test suite through parallelization and prioritization maintains fast feedback while preserving sufficient coverage for critical paths.

text: An organization must evaluate the environmental impact (carbon footprint) of the cloud infrastructure used by its continuous development teams. Which action illustrates coherent integration of sustainability criteria in an agile context?

options.A: Wait for strict regulation before acting
options.B: Address sustainability only in a separate annual report unrelated to the backlog
options.C: Integrate sustainability criteria (infrastructure choice, cloud resource optimization) as acceptance criteria in certain technical user stories
options.D: Completely ignore the carbon footprint since it's not a product priority

justification: Correct: integrating sustainability criteria directly into acceptance criteria of technical user stories allows concrete, incremental action consistent with agility.

text: A Scrum Master notices a team member is systematically over-committing to work out of fear of disappointing others. What is the best intervention?

options.A: Ignore it, it's not the Scrum Master's role
options.B: Discuss privately about realistic workload, encourage transparency about capacity, and reinforce that it's acceptable to say no
options.C: Let them continue since it shows commitment
options.D: Publicly reduce their workload in front of the team to force change

justification: Correct: a private, caring conversation reinforces psychological safety and helps the person honestly express their real capacity.

text: A Product Owner must decide how to prioritize the backlog considering both business value and regulatory constraints. Which prioritization technique best integrates both dimensions?

options.A: Let each developer choose what they prefer
options.B: Use multi-criteria weighting (WSJF or MoSCoW) including value, risk, and compliance constraints
options.C: Prioritize only by technical complexity
options.D: Prioritize only by order of arrival of requests (FIFO)

justification: Correct: techniques like WSJF or MoSCoW allow multi-factor prioritization including value, regulatory urgency, and risk.

text: An organization is evaluating whether to outsource part of its agile development to an offshore team. What factor is most determinant for the success of this arrangement?

options.A: Compatibility of agile practices, quality of asynchronous communication, and sufficient overlap of working hours
options.B: The number of certifications held by the vendor
options.C: The size of the offshore team only
options.D: The lowest price proposed by the vendor only

justification: Correct: compatibility of agile practices, effective asynchronous communication, and sufficient time zone overlap are determinant for successful distributed agile collaboration.

text: A distributed, culturally diverse team struggles to agree on a common work rhythm due to time zone differences and local holidays. What balanced solution is appropriate?

options.A: Ignore cultural and time zone differences
options.B: Require all members to work in the same time zone regardless of location
options.C: Co-create a shared working calendar with the team that respects local constraints as much as possible, with clearly defined overlap windows
options.D: Impose the Scrum Master's own country's work calendar on the whole team

justification: Correct: co-creating a shared calendar respecting local constraints, with defined overlap windows, promotes fairness and effective collaboration in a multicultural distributed team.

text: A team wants to improve visibility into technical dependencies with other teams at scale. Which scaled agile mechanism supports this?

options.A: No coordination between teams at all
options.B: Purely informal, undocumented conversations
options.C: A single annual meeting with no follow-up
options.D: Program Increment (PI) Planning with visualized cross-team dependencies

justification: Correct: PI Planning in scaled agile frameworks explicitly visualizes and coordinates cross-team dependencies for the upcoming increment.

text: A regulated healthcare organization developing agile products needs to reconcile fast iteration with strict regulatory traceability requirements. What approach is recommended?

options.A: Fully abandon agility for a complete waterfall cycle
options.B: Adapt the Definition of Done to include regulatory traceability documentation for each increment, produced continuously rather than at the end
options.C: Ignore regulatory requirements to move faster
options.D: Defer all regulatory documentation to the very end of development

justification: Correct: integrating regulatory traceability into the Definition of Done for each increment ensures continuous compliance without sacrificing iterative agility.

text: A Scrum Master remarks that a team systematically avoids discussing difficult topics in retrospectives to preserve a harmonious atmosphere. What risk does this represent, and what action should be taken?

options.A: Force artificial conflicts to test the team
options.B: No risk, a good atmosphere is more important than anything else
options.C: Remove retrospectives since they serve no purpose in this case
options.D: Risk of accumulating unresolved issues (artificial harmony); introduce structured techniques to address sensitive topics constructively (e.g., Sailboat retrospective)

justification: Correct: structured facilitation techniques allow sensitive topics to be addressed constructively without breaking trust, while avoiding the buildup of unspoken issues.

text: A team wants to decide how to manage the transition of knowledge to an operations team before a product handoff, in an agile context. What action ensures a successful transition?

options.A: Document operational runbooks incrementally throughout development, pair operations staff with the team during the last sprints, and organize a transitional support period
options.B: Defer all documentation until after the official handoff
options.C: Consider that knowledge transfer is not the development team's responsibility
options.D: Transfer only a contact list with no technical documentation

justification: Correct: incremental runbook documentation, pairing operations staff during final sprints, and a transitional support period ensure a smooth handoff and reduce post-transition risks.

text: An organization must decide whether it should outsource part of its agile development to an offshore team focused on a regulated market. What additional compliance factor must be assessed?

options.A: None, standard offshore vendor evaluation is sufficient
options.B: The offshore vendor's ability to meet the same regulatory and data protection standards required in the target market
options.C: Only the vendor's hourly rate
options.D: Only the vendor's office location aesthetics

justification: Correct: verifying the offshore vendor's ability to meet the same regulatory and data protection standards is essential to avoid compliance gaps in a regulated market.

text: A Scrum Master notices that some team members never actively participate in Sprint Planning. Which facilitation technique can improve engagement?

options.A: Force each member to speak in a fixed order every time
options.B: Cancel Sprint Planning since engagement is low
options.C: Use varied facilitation techniques (small-group breakouts, silent brainstorming) to draw out contributions from quieter members
options.D: Only let the most vocal members speak to save time

justification: Correct: varied facilitation techniques create multiple avenues for contribution, helping quieter members engage meaningfully.

text: A team wants to decide how to handle a recurring pattern of scope creep within sprints, where small 'just this once' additions accumulate. What practice addresses this systematically?

options.A: Ban any conversation about new ideas during the sprint
options.B: Extend sprint length indefinitely to absorb the extra work
options.C: Reinforce sprint scope protection by routing all new requests through backlog refinement for the next sprint, and track the pattern in retrospectives
options.D: Allow all small additions since they seem harmless individually

justification: Correct: routing new requests to backlog refinement and surfacing the pattern in retrospectives protects sprint integrity while still capturing legitimate new ideas for proper prioritization.

text: An organization evaluating the impact of a rapidly evolving competitive landscape on its agile product roadmap should prioritize which action?

options.A: Establish a regular competitive intelligence review cadence feeding directly into backlog prioritization discussions
options.B: Copy every competitor feature immediately without strategic assessment
options.C: Freeze the roadmap for the next 12 months to maintain stability
options.D: Ignore competitor moves since the team's velocity is already strong

justification: Correct: a regular competitive intelligence cadence feeding into prioritization keeps the roadmap responsive to market shifts while maintaining agile discipline.

text: A senior Scrum team member repeatedly criticizes junior members' ideas during the Daily Scrum, reducing their participation. What should the Scrum Master do first?

options.A: Ignore it, since the Daily Scrum belongs to the development team
options.B: Ask the Product Owner to settle the matter
options.C: Remove the senior member from the team
options.D: Coach the senior member privately on the impact of their behavior and facilitate team working agreements

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master is a servant-leader who protects psychological safety; individual coaching followed by a team working agreement is the appropriate approach.

text: A project manager on a predictive-cycle project finds a Cost Performance Index (CPI) of 0.85 and a Schedule Performance Index (SPI) of 0.78 at month 6 of a 12-month project. What is the best first action?

options.A: Conduct a root cause analysis of the deviations before proposing corrective actions
options.B: Close the project because it is failing
options.C: Immediately increase the project's total budget
options.D: Reduce scope without consulting stakeholders

justification: Correct: before any corrective action, EVM requires understanding the causes (resources, estimation, risks) to target the right response.

text: A new environmental regulation takes effect during the execution phase of a construction project. What is the first appropriate step for the project manager?

options.A: Suspend the project indefinitely
options.B: Inform only the sponsor with no further action
options.C: Ignore the regulation until project closure
options.D: Assess the impact on the project and update the risk register and compliance documentation

justification: Correct: the PM must assess the enterprise environmental factors (EEF), document the impact, and adjust the risk management plan.

text: Two agile team members have a persistent disagreement on the technical approach for a user story, slowing the sprint. Which conflict resolution technique is most appropriate?

options.A: Imposition by the Scrum Master of their own technical solution
options.B: Collaboration/problem-solving to find a win-win solution
options.C: A quick compromise to close the topic before the sprint review
options.D: Avoidance, to prevent worsening the relationship

justification: Correct: collaboration is the most effective long-term technique, especially for legitimate technical disagreements requiring joint exploration.

text: During planning, a project manager must choose an estimation method for a project whose activities are similar to a well-documented prior project. Which method is most appropriate?

options.A: Analogous estimating based on the prior project
options.B: Expert judgment only, with no historical data
options.C: Bottom-up estimating
options.D: Three-point estimating (PERT)

justification: Correct: analogous estimating directly leverages historical data from a similar project, which is fast and relevant here.

text: An organization undergoing agile transformation faces strong cultural resistance from middle management. Which strategic action is most effective for project leadership?

options.A: Bypass middle management and work directly with the teams
options.B: Force adoption through strict top-down directives
options.C: Involve middle management in co-designing the change and demonstrate value through pilot projects
options.D: Postpone the transformation until full consensus is reached

justification: Correct: effective organizational change management involves relevant stakeholders and uses evidence of value (pilots) to build buy-in.

text: A project manager notices a key team member has been demotivated since the project's reorganization. According to Maslow's motivation theory, which action best addresses esteem needs?

options.A: Increase only their salary
options.B: Publicly recognize their contributions and give them valued responsibilities
options.C: Reassign them to another team without discussion
options.D: Do nothing; motivation is intrinsic

justification: Correct: recognition and valued responsibilities directly address the 'esteem' level of Maslow's pyramid.

text: A scope change is requested by an important client during execution. What is the correct first step per the integrated change control process?

options.A: Submit a formal change request and assess its impact before having it approved by the CCB
options.B: Systematically refuse any change request
options.C: Implement it immediately since the client is a priority
options.D: Add the change to scope without updating documentation

justification: Correct: any change request must be documented, analyzed (cost, schedule, risk), and validated by the governance body (CCB) before execution.

text: A compliance audit reveals that the project doesn't meet an applicable ISO standard. What is the best response from the project manager?

options.A: Develop a corrective action plan and integrate it into the project management plan
options.B: Dispute the audit findings without analysis
options.C: Ignore the audit report since it slows the project
options.D: Resign from the project

justification: Correct: the PM must address non-conformances through a formal corrective action plan, integrated into project governance.

text: A self-organizing agile team has struggled to meet its sprint commitments for 3 consecutive sprints. What is the Scrum Master's appropriate role?

options.A: Facilitate an in-depth retrospective to identify systemic impediments and help the team self-correct
options.B: Unilaterally reduce the target velocity without consulting the team
options.C: Report the team to leadership for disciplinary action
options.D: Reassign tasks themselves to speed things up

justification: Correct: the retrospective is the dedicated tool for continuous improvement; the SM facilitates identifying impediments without imposing a solution.

text: In a hybrid project, the predictive portion manages infrastructure and the agile portion manages application development. How should the project manager synchronize the two streams?

options.A: Force the agile team to fully adopt the waterfall cycle
options.B: Force the infrastructure team to adopt sprints with no adaptation
options.C: Establish common integration milestones and align agile releases with the predictive schedule via a shared backlog
options.D: Manage both streams entirely independently with no synchronization points

justification: Correct: an effective hybrid approach maintains common integration milestones while respecting each stream's cadence autonomy.

text: The Product Owner must prioritize the backlog considering both business value and regulatory constraints. Which prioritization technique best integrates both dimensions?

options.A: Prioritize only by order of arrival of requests (FIFO)
options.B: Let each developer choose what they prefer
options.C: Prioritize only by technical complexity
options.D: Use multi-criteria weighting (WSJF or MoSCoW) including value, risk, and compliance constraints

justification: Correct: techniques like WSJF or MoSCoW allow multi-factor prioritization including value, regulatory urgency, and risk.

text: A project manager identifies that a key supplier lacks the skills necessary to deliver a critical technical component. Which resource management action is a priority?

options.A: Transfer responsibility to the sponsor with no proposal
options.B: Evaluate options (training, technical support, replacement) and document a risk mitigation plan
options.C: Immediately terminate the contract without impact analysis
options.D: Continue with no adjustment, hoping the supplier improves

justification: Correct: the PM must evaluate concrete options and document a risk response (mitigation), consistent with the risk management plan.

text: The critical path of a project shows zero total float on several activities. What is the implication for the project manager?

options.A: The budget must be immediately compressed
options.B: No impact; zero float is normal and inconsequential
options.C: Any delay on these activities will directly delay the project end date, requiring closer monitoring
options.D: The project is automatically late

justification: Correct: critical path activities with zero float must be closely monitored, as any slip directly affects the end date.

text: An international project must deliver a product compliant with the laws of two countries with contradictory requirements. What is the best approach for the project manager?

options.A: Engage legal experts and relevant stakeholders to define a documented compliance solution for both markets
options.B: Arbitrarily choose the requirements of one country
options.C: Ignore the least restrictive requirements
options.D: Indefinitely delay the project with no communication

justification: Correct: facing contradictory regulatory constraints, the PM must mobilize legal expertise and stakeholders for a documented, defensible solution.

text: A Product Owner frequently changes sprint priorities mid-sprint, disrupting the development team. What is the Scrum Master's best action?

options.A: Accept all changes without discussion to avoid upsetting the PO
options.B: Coach the PO on the principle of sprint immutability and channel new priorities into the product backlog for the next sprint
options.C: Prevent the PO from attending ceremonies
options.D: Let the team decide alone without involving the PO

justification: Correct: the Scrum Guide protects sprint content; the Scrum Master should coach the PO on this principle while respecting their authority over the backlog.

text: At project closure, several important lessons learned have been identified. What is the best practice for managing them?

options.A: Don't document them since the project is over
options.B: Share them only with the sponsor verbally
options.C: Keep them only in the project manager's personal notes
options.D: Formally document them in the lessons learned register and share them with the PMO for future projects

justification: Correct: formal documentation and PMO sharing turn lessons learned into reusable organizational assets.

text: A project sponsor changes mid-execution following a reorganization. What is the first action for the project manager?

options.A: Continue the project without informing the new sponsor
options.B: Organize a transition meeting to align the new sponsor on the charter, objectives, and current project status
options.C: Redefine the project's objectives alone without validation
options.D: Suspend the project until further notice

justification: Correct: a governance transition requires a formal alignment meeting on the charter and project status.

text: A project manager must build a team for a critical project and has a choice of several profiles. Per Tuckman's model, which development phase corresponds to when roles and norms stabilize?

options.A: Norming
options.B: Adjourning
options.C: Storming
options.D: Forming

justification: Correct: Norming is the phase where roles, working norms, and relationships stabilize after Storming conflicts.

text: An identified risk has high probability and high cost impact. Which negative risk response strategy is generally preferred first?

options.A: Active avoidance or mitigation of the risk
options.B: Passive acceptance
options.C: Systematic transfer with no analysis
options.D: Ignore the risk until it materializes

justification: Correct: for a risk with high probability and high impact, avoidance or active mitigation are the priority strategies to reduce exposure.

text: A project's business case shows an expected ROI below the organization's minimum threshold after a market revision. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Hide the information from the steering committee
options.B: Unilaterally stop the project
options.C: Continue the project without regard to it
options.D: Present the updated analysis to the governance committee for a decision on continuation, revision, or termination

justification: Correct: the business case must be regularly reassessed (benefits review), and any major deviation must be escalated to governance for decision.

text: A team member works remotely and feels isolated from team rituals. Which action best fosters inclusion per agile principles?

options.A: Ignore the situation since remote work is a personal choice
options.B: Remove them from ceremonies so as not to bother them
options.C: Ask the member to return to the office immediately
options.D: Adapt ceremonies to guarantee equitable participation (collaborative tools, video, speaking rounds) and regularly check on their well-being

justification: Correct: agility values individuals and interactions; adapting practices for remote inclusion is a servant leadership responsibility.

text: A project manager must determine the appropriate contingency reserve for identified risks. Which method is most rigorous?

options.A: Don't plan any reserve
options.B: Ask the sponsor to set an amount without analysis
options.C: Add an arbitrary 10% to the total budget
options.D: Calculate the expected monetary value (EMV) of each identified risk and sum the results

justification: Correct: EMV (probability x impact) for each risk, summed, provides a rigorous quantitative basis for the contingency reserve.

text: An organization adopts scaled agile for several teams working on the same product. What is the main organizational benefit sought?

options.A: Completely eliminate the need for coordination
options.B: Reduce the total number of meetings to zero
options.C: Centralize all decision-making at the executive level
options.D: Align teams on a common product vision while synchronizing releases through shared cadences (PI Planning, Scrum of Scrums)

justification: Correct: the goal of scaled agile is strategic alignment and cross-team synchronization around a shared vision and cadences.

text: A project manager must manage a multicultural team with very different communication styles. Which is the best communication management practice?

options.A: Let each member communicate however they want, with no framework
options.B: Impose a single communication style based on the project manager's culture
options.C: Avoid all informal communication
options.D: Adapt the communication plan to identified cultural preferences and explicitly clarify shared expectations

justification: Correct: the communications management plan must be adapted to the cultural context while establishing explicit common norms.

text: A Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract is used with a supplier. The supplier requests a price increase due to an unforeseen rise in raw material costs. What is the correct contractual position?

options.A: Automatically accept the increase
options.B: Immediately terminate the contract
options.C: Renegotiate the whole contract with no legal basis
options.D: Refuse in principle, since cost risk is borne by the supplier in an FFP contract, unless a specific clause states otherwise

justification: Correct: in an FFP, financial risk related to costs is transferred to the supplier; an increase is only due if a specific clause (e.g., indexation) provides for it.

text: A project must demonstrate its contribution to the organization's strategic objectives during a portfolio review. Which document is most relevant to present?

options.A: Internal team meeting minutes
options.B: The detailed daily task schedule
options.C: The updated business case showing strategic alignment and expected benefits
options.D: The list of unresolved minor risks

justification: Correct: the updated business case explicitly links the project to strategic objectives and expected benefits, which is the purpose of a portfolio review.

text: The Scrum Master notices the team doesn't truly practice self-organization despite the Scrum framework being in place; the line manager keeps assigning tasks. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Bypass the manager without discussion
options.B: Dialogue with the manager to clarify Scrum roles and coach the team to progressively take ownership of its own decisions
options.C: Accept the situation because the manager has hierarchical authority
options.D: Abandon the Scrum framework to align with traditional management

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master must serve the organization by clarifying roles and supporting gradual cultural change toward self-organization.

text: A project manager must choose between two suppliers for a critical component. Supplier A offers a lower price but has a delay history; Supplier B is more expensive but reliable. Which selection method is most appropriate?

options.A: Let the sponsor decide with no data
options.B: Automatically choose the cheapest
options.C: Use a weighted multi-criteria analysis (price, quality, reliability, delivery) for an objective decision
options.D: Choose at random

justification: Correct: a weighted multi-criteria scoring grid is the standard method to balance cost, quality, and risk in supplier selection.

text: A project generates an unanticipated environmental impact during its execution phase (e.g., local pollution). What is the project manager's primary responsibility?

options.A: Continue the project with no adjustment
options.B: Transparently report the impact, initiate corrective measures, and inform relevant stakeholders
options.C: Wait for someone else to report it
options.D: Downplay the incident in reports

justification: Correct: ethical and professional responsibility requires transparency, rapid corrective action, and communication to relevant stakeholders.

text: A project manager observes recurring performance issues in a team member. After investigating, they learn the person is going through a difficult personal situation. What is the most appropriate approach?

options.A: Remove the person from the project without dialogue
options.B: Immediately sanction the performance decline
options.C: Show empathy, temporarily adjust the workload if possible, and refer them to available support resources (HR, EAP)
options.D: Ignore the personal situation and maintain the same expectations

justification: Correct: people-centered leadership acknowledges the human context and directs toward appropriate support while reasonably adjusting workload.

text: A project manager must determine the best method to measure progress on a construction project whose deliverables are difficult to partially quantify. Which earned value measurement method is most appropriate?

options.A: Use only hours worked as the indicator
options.B: Fixed formula (0/100 or 20/80) based on clearly defined completion milestones
options.C: Subjectively estimated percentage complete
options.D: Only measure progress at the end of the project

justification: Correct: for activities difficult to partially quantify, fixed formulas (0/100, 20/80) offer an objective measure based on completing milestones.

text: A company decides to launch a project to capture a market opportunity before a competitor does. Which project selection technique best reflects this context?

options.A: Completely ignore financial analysis
options.B: Random project selection
options.C: Analysis of strategic value and competitive advantage in addition to financial criteria
options.D: Payback period analysis only

justification: Correct: in this context, selection must combine financial criteria and strategic value/competitive advantage to justify the urgency.

text: During a retrospective, the team identifies it has systematically underestimated the complexity of user stories. Which concrete action should the Scrum Master facilitate?

options.A: Reduce the backlog size without adjusting the estimation method
options.B: Impose a new estimation method with no team consultation
options.C: Facilitate an estimation recalibration workshop (e.g., Planning Poker) using shared reference stories
options.D: Ignore the topic since estimation isn't critical

justification: Correct: a collaborative recalibration workshop (e.g., Planning Poker with reference stories) helps the team improve future estimation accuracy.

text: A project manager must administratively close a contract with a supplier. What is the essential step before formal closure?

options.A: Verify that all contractual deliverables have been formally accepted and final payments are settled
options.B: Close based only on a verbal agreement
options.C: Close with no verification to save time
options.D: Wait for the supplier to request closure

justification: Correct: procurement closure requires formal verification of deliverable acceptance and final payment settlement before any administrative closure.

text: A project manager must ensure the project respects local labor laws in a country where they are deploying a temporary team. What is the best practice?

options.A: Apply the home country's laws everywhere
options.B: Fully delegate the matter with no follow-up
options.C: Consult a local legal expert and ensure compliance with the labor laws of the country of execution
options.D: Ignore local legal differences

justification: Correct: local legal compliance requires expert consultation and active verification, a key element of enterprise environmental factors.

text: A project manager applies a leadership style that consists of giving precise instructions to inexperienced team members while offering more autonomy to experts. Which leadership model best describes this approach?

options.A: Situational leadership (adapted to each person's competence and commitment level)
options.B: Autocratic leadership for everyone
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership for everyone
options.D: Transactional leadership only

justification: Correct: situational leadership adjusts style (directing, coaching, participating, delegating) based on each individual's maturity and experience.

text: A project manager must define formal acceptance criteria for deliverables with the client. Which process does this primarily belong to?

options.A: Identify Stakeholders
options.B: Estimate Costs
options.C: Validate Scope
options.D: Develop Project Charter

justification: Correct: the 'Validate Scope' process involves obtaining formal acceptance of completed deliverables by the client/sponsor per defined criteria.

text: An organization wants to measure the business value delivered by an agile team beyond velocity. Which metric is most relevant?

options.A: The return on investment of delivered features and measured customer satisfaction
options.B: The number of meetings held
options.C: The size of the team
options.D: The number of hours worked per sprint

justification: Correct: business value is measured by the real impact (ROI, adoption, customer satisfaction) of delivered features, beyond effort metrics like velocity.

text: An agile coach observes a team practicing 'Dark Scrum' (ceremonies followed mechanically with no real collaboration or continuous improvement). What is the most likely root cause?

options.A: The project management tool is inadequate
options.B: The team is too small
options.C: A lack of understanding of underlying agile values and principles, reduced to mere ritual compliance
options.D: The Product Owner doesn't exist

justification: Correct: 'Dark Scrum' occurs when ceremonies are applied mechanically without integrating agile values (transparency, inspection, adaptation).

text: A project manager must determine the best organizational structure for a project requiring strong PM authority and dedicated resource access. Which structure is most suitable?

options.A: Pure functional organization
options.B: Strong matrix or projectized organization
options.C: Weak matrix organization
options.D: Total absence of formal structure

justification: Correct: strong matrix or projectized structures give the PM high authority and dedicated access to project resources.

text: A post-implementation benefits review reveals that expected project benefits were realized only 60%. What is the best organizational action?

options.A: Only blame the project manager
options.B: Analyze the causes of the gap and adjust the benefits realization plan or transition/adoption actions
options.C: Don't document anything to avoid criticism
options.D: Ignore the gap since the project is closed

justification: Correct: the benefits management plan must be reviewed to understand gaps and adjust actions favoring full value realization.

text: A project manager must resolve a resource allocation conflict between two priority organizational projects. What is the appropriate first step?

options.A: Abandon the affected activities of their own project
options.B: Escalate to the PMO or portfolio governance committee for arbitration based on strategic priorities
options.C: Negotiate directly with the other project manager with no formal framework and take the resources
options.D: Decide alone with no consultation of other project managers

justification: Correct: a cross-project resource conflict falls under PMO/portfolio governance arbitration, based on organizational priorities.

text: A project manager notices deliverable quality doesn't consistently meet defined standards despite quality controls. Which action falls under quality assurance rather than quality control?

options.A: Do nothing until the client complains
options.B: Audit and improve production processes to prevent defects upstream
options.C: Inspect each deliverable individually to detect defects
options.D: Reject non-conforming deliverables one by one

justification: Correct: quality assurance focuses on auditing and improving processes to prevent defects at the source, rather than detecting them after the fact.

text: A project manager must evaluate if their organization has the maturity needed to manage a complex project. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.A: The project's Gantt chart
options.B: The risk register only
options.C: The work breakdown structure (WBS)
options.D: An organizational project management maturity model (e.g., OPM3)

justification: Correct: an organizational maturity model (like OPM3) assesses the organization's capabilities and processes in project, portfolio, and program management.

text: A senior developer threatens to leave the team if their technical preferences aren't consistently followed, pressuring architecture decisions. What is the Scrum Master's best response?

options.A: Immediately fire the developer
options.B: Directly address the behavior, reaffirm the team's collective decision-making principles, and involve management if necessary
options.C: Systematically yield to their demands to retain them
options.D: Ignore the threat hoping it will pass

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master must directly address the problematic behavior, reaffirm team norms, and involve HR/management if the behavior persists.

text: A project manager plans communications for a project with many stakeholders having varying levels of interest and power. Which tool is most useful for prioritizing communication efforts?

options.A: The power/interest stakeholder matrix
options.B: The risk register
options.C: The project budget
options.D: The Gantt chart

justification: Correct: the power/interest matrix allows classifying stakeholders and adapting communication strategy and frequency based on their influence and interest.

text: A company must decide between building capacity internally or outsourcing part of the project to a vendor. Which analysis best guides this decision?

options.A: Systematically choosing internal delivery for every project
options.B: A decision based solely on the project manager's personal preference
options.C: A make-or-buy analysis comparing costs, risks, internal skills, and timelines
options.D: Systematically choosing outsourcing for every project

justification: Correct: make-or-buy analysis objectively evaluates cost, risk, available skills, and timelines to guide the outsourcing decision.

text: A project manager must give corrective feedback to a team member about a repeated mistake. Which feedback approach is most constructive?

options.A: Send a formal email without any verbal discussion
options.B: Avoid all feedback to prevent tension
options.C: Publicly criticize in front of the whole team to make a lasting impression
options.D: Give private, factual feedback based on specific examples and oriented toward solutions

justification: Correct: effective feedback is private, factual, specific, and solution-oriented for concrete improvement.

text: A project manager must decide whether to prematurely stop a project due to major overruns. Which economic concept should NOT influence this decision?

options.A: The project's current strategic alignment
options.B: Residual project risks
options.C: Sunk costs already incurred
options.D: The expected future value and remaining ROI

justification: Correct: sunk costs should not influence a future decision, as they are already committed and unrecoverable regardless of the decision made.

text: A project manager works in a heavily regulated sector (pharmaceutical). Which compliance management practice is essential throughout the project?

options.A: Consider compliance optional if it slows the project
options.B: Fully delegate compliance to the legal department with no PM involvement
options.C: Verify compliance only at project closure
options.D: Integrate continuous regulatory compliance checks at each phase and document evidence of compliance

justification: Correct: in a regulated sector, compliance controls must be continuous and documented at each phase to avoid costly non-conformances.

text: A mature agile team requests more decision-making autonomy over technical choices, currently validated by an external architecture committee. What is the recommended approach for leadership?

options.A: Immediately delegate 100% of authority with no control
options.B: Assess the team's maturity and progressively delegate decision-making authority with appropriate guardrails (guidelines, retrospective reviews)
options.C: Dissolve the architecture committee with no transition
options.D: Categorically refuse any delegation of authority

justification: Correct: delegation of authority must be progressive and based on team maturity, with guardrails to maintain organization-wide architectural coherence.

text: A project manager must identify dependencies between activities to build the project's logical network. Which dependency type represents a constraint imposed by an external contractual requirement?

options.A: No formal dependency is necessary
options.B: Mandatory internal dependency (hard logic)
options.C: Discretionary dependency (soft logic)
options.D: External dependency

justification: Correct: an external dependency involves a relationship between a project activity and a factor outside the team's control, such as a contractual requirement from a third party.

text: A project manager must present a status report to a leadership committee unfamiliar with technical details. Which communication approach is most effective?

options.A: Present all technical details with no filtering
options.B: Adapt the level of detail and language to the audience, focusing on key indicators and required decisions
options.C: Present no numerical data at all
options.D: Send only a written report with no oral presentation

justification: Correct: effective communication adapts content and level of detail to the audience, prioritizing key indicators and expected decisions.

text: A project manager must motivate a team after a significant failure of the previous project. Which leadership approach best fosters rebuilding trust?

options.A: Openly analyze the causes of the failure with no individual blame, celebrate the learnings, and set realistic, progressive goals
options.B: Publicly blame those responsible for the previous failure
options.C: Immediately set very ambitious goals to compensate
options.D: Avoid discussing the previous failure

justification: Correct: an open, non-punitive analysis of causes, combined with progressive goals, restores trust and psychological safety for future performance.

text: A project manager must determine the most suitable contract type for a project with a well-defined and stable scope. Which contract type minimizes buyer risk?

options.A: Firm Fixed Price (FFP)
options.B: Cost Plus (Cost-Reimbursable) only
options.C: Time and Materials (T&M)
options.D: Cost Plus Incentive Fee (CPIF)

justification: Correct: for a well-defined, stable scope, FFP minimizes buyer risk by fixing a firm price, with cost risk borne by the supplier.

text: An organization evaluates whether a product should continue development after several increments failed to reach expected business results. Which agile concept guides this continue/stop decision?

options.A: Strict adherence to the original schedule
options.B: Team velocity only
options.C: Regular review of product-market fit and value hypotheses using market data and user feedback
options.D: The number of completed user stories

justification: Correct: the agile approach favors continuous validation of value hypotheses through real market data and feedback, to decide whether to pivot, persevere, or stop.

text: The Scrum Master notices some team members never actively participate in retrospectives. Which facilitation technique can improve participation?

options.A: Remove retrospectives since they aren't useful
options.B: Force each member to speak in turn with no variation in format
options.C: Vary retrospective formats (e.g., prior silent writing, anonymous polls) to give voice to all participation styles
options.D: Reserve speaking time only for the most experienced members

justification: Correct: varying formats (silent writing, anonymous polls, visual workshops) includes different participation styles and yields richer feedback.

text: A project manager must verify that the project management plan is coherent before starting execution. Which process covers this verification?

options.A: Develop Project Management Plan (integration and consistency validation of subsidiary plans)
options.B: Direct and Manage Project Work
options.C: Control Costs
options.D: Close Project or Phase

justification: Correct: the 'Develop Project Management Plan' process integrates and harmonizes all subsidiary plans before execution begins.

text: A project manager identifies a potential conflict of interest: a member of the proposal evaluation committee has a family relationship with one of the candidate suppliers. What should the project manager do, per the PMI Code of Ethics?

options.A: Manage the situation secretly to avoid tension
options.B: Let the person participate but ask them to be objective
options.C: Ignore it since it's uncertain whether it will influence the decision
options.D: Immediately disclose the potential conflict of interest to relevant parties and remove the person from the decision-making process

justification: Correct: the PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct requires immediate, transparent disclosure of any conflict of interest and removal of the person from the decision-making process.

text: During Sprint Planning, the team realizes actual capacity is lower than planned due to unexpected absences. What should the team do?

options.A: Ask present members to compensate with overtime
options.B: Maintain the same sprint commitment despite reduced capacity
options.C: Cancel the sprint
options.D: Readjust the sprint content based on actual available capacity, in agreement with the Product Owner

justification: Correct: the sprint backlog must reflect actual capacity; the team negotiates content with the PO based on priorities.

text: A new member joins an established Scrum team and feels lost among existing practices. Which Scrum Master action best facilitates their integration?

options.A: Give them only technical documentation with no human support
options.B: Assign them immediately to the most complex tasks to accelerate learning
options.C: Let them observe without intervention for several sprints
options.D: Organize structured onboarding including the team's working agreement, a peer mentor, and a regular check-in

justification: Correct: structured onboarding with peer mentoring fosters rapid integration and understanding of team norms.

text: A project manager must manage a disagreement between two departments over shared resource priorities. Which conflict resolution style prioritizes the long-term relationship over immediate gain?

options.A: Withdraw/Avoid
options.B: Force/Direct
options.C: Smooth/Accommodate
options.D: Collaborate/Problem Solve

justification: Correct: accommodating means yielding one's own needs to preserve harmony and the long-term relationship.

text: A project manager notices an experienced member consistently resists adopting new working methods. Which individual change management approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Exclude them from decisions about the change
options.B: Force them to comply under threat of sanction
options.C: Ignore their resistance, hoping it disappears
options.D: Understand the causes of their resistance (ADKAR model) and actively involve them in designing the change

justification: Correct: models like ADKAR (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) help diagnose resistance, and active involvement fosters buy-in.

text: The Product Owner and the development team have different interpretations of a user story, causing significant rework. Which agile practice best prevents this problem?

options.A: Write longer, more detailed user stories like a formal specification
options.B: Define clear acceptance criteria and practice collaborative refinement before the sprint
options.C: Remove ambiguous user stories from the backlog without discussion
options.D: Let the team interpret freely without PO validation

justification: Correct: collaborative backlog refinement and clear acceptance criteria (INVEST/Definition of Ready) reduce ambiguity before the sprint.

text: A project manager must decide how to distribute decision authority on a project involving several departments with competing expectations. Which tool helps formalize roles and responsibilities?

options.A: The Ishikawa diagram
options.B: The control chart
options.C: The Pareto diagram
options.D: The RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed)

justification: Correct: the RACI matrix clarifies who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed for each activity, reducing ambiguities between departments.

text: A Scrum Master observes the team consistently ends the sprint with untested work. Which root cause and corresponding action are most appropriate?

options.A: Cause: lack of discipline; Action: sanction the developers
options.B: Cause: too many tests required; Action: reduce quality requirements
options.C: Cause: sprint too short; Action: remove sprints
options.D: Cause: incomplete or unrespected Definition of Done; Action: clarify and collectively enforce the DoD

justification: Correct: a vague or unrespected Definition of Done is a frequent cause of untested work; clarifying and collectively enforcing it resolves the problem at its root.

text: A project manager identifies that a key supplier communicates very little proactively about problems. Which interpersonal skill should the project manager use to improve the relationship?

options.A: Active listening and building trust through regular, transparent communication
options.B: Systematic threats of contractual penalties
options.C: No action; this isn't the project manager's responsibility
options.D: Avoiding all direct contact with the supplier

justification: Correct: active listening and regular communication build the trust needed to encourage proactive transparency from the supplier.

text: Two agile teams working on the same product have different Definitions of Done, creating integration problems. What action at the Scrum of Scrums level is appropriate?

options.A: Remove the concept of Definition of Done
options.B: Let each team keep its own definition indefinitely
options.C: Facilitate cross-team alignment on a common product-level Definition of Done, with team-specific additions if needed
options.D: Impose the most experienced team's definition without discussion

justification: Correct: collaborative alignment on a common product-level DoD, with local extensions, resolves integration problems while respecting team autonomy.

text: A project manager must build a project team accounting for skills available in the organization. Which document describes the skills, availability, and costs of human resources?

options.A: The risk register
options.B: Human resource inventory registers / skills matrix
options.C: The quality management plan
options.D: The project network diagram

justification: Correct: resource registers/inventories and skills matrices provide the information needed on availability, skills, and costs for team formation.

text: A team member expresses a feeling of chronic work overload in a retrospective. What is the Scrum Master's most appropriate response?

options.A: Ignore it and wait for the person to adapt
options.B: Collectively explore the causes (over-commitment, technical debt, interruptions) and adjust future workload with the team
options.C: Add more tasks to test their resilience
options.D: Downplay the remark since sprints are supposed to be intense

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master must facilitate a collective exploration of root causes and adjust future planning for a sustainable pace (agile sustainable pace principle).

text: A project manager must assess the training needs of their team before starting a project using a new technology. What is the best practice?

options.A: Recruit only new employees who are already experts
options.B: Assume the team will learn on the job with no formal plan
options.C: Conduct a skills gap analysis and develop a targeted training plan before startup
options.D: Defer training until after project closure

justification: Correct: a skills gap analysis followed by a targeted training plan is a proactive resource management plan practice.

text: An Agile Coach working across several teams finds one resists all retrospectives, deeming them useless. What approach should be taken first?

options.A: Replace the entire team
options.B: Mandate participation without explanation
options.C: Understand the reasons behind the negative perception and co-create a retrospective format that delivers immediate perceived value
options.D: Remove retrospectives for this team

justification: Correct: understanding the causes of the negative perception (poorly facilitated retros, no follow-through on actions) allows co-creating a format that restores perceived value.

text: A project manager must manage a virtual team spread across multiple time zones. Which practice most improves effective collaboration?

options.A: Schedule no synchronous meetings at all
options.B: Establish agreed overlapping working hours, document decisions in writing, and use asynchronous collaboration tools
options.C: Schedule all meetings in the project manager's time zone regardless of impact
options.D: Limit all communication to email only

justification: Correct: agreed overlap hours, written documentation of decisions, and asynchronous tools optimize collaboration for a multi-timezone virtual team.

text: A Product Owner lacks availability to answer the team's questions during the sprint, slowing development. What is the best durable solution?

options.A: Negotiate dedicated availability windows with the PO or designate a trained proxy PO for routine decisions
options.B: The team makes all product decisions without the PO permanently
options.C: Ignore the problem and hope for spontaneous improvement
options.D: Halt the sprint until the PO is available

justification: Correct: negotiating dedicated windows or establishing a trained proxy PO maintains velocity while respecting the PO's role on strategic decisions.

text: A project manager must choose between two internal candidates for a key project role: one has more technical experience, the other better collaborative skills in a highly interdependent team context. Which factor should weigh most heavily here?

options.A: Collaborative skills, given the team's high interdependence for this role
options.B: Technical experience only, since it always takes priority
options.C: Seniority within the organization
options.D: The lowest salary

justification: Correct: in a highly interdependent team, collaborative and interpersonal skills often have more impact on overall performance than technical expertise alone.

text: During a sprint review, a stakeholder harshly criticizes the presented work in front of the whole team, demoralizing developers. What is the Scrum Master's best immediate reaction?

options.A: Let the situation unfold without intervening
options.B: Respond with the same aggressiveness to defend the team
options.C: Politely refocus the discussion on constructive, solution-oriented feedback, then privately address the tone with the stakeholder afterward
options.D: Immediately cancel the sprint review

justification: Correct: the Scrum Master facilitates by constructively refocusing the discussion in the moment, then addresses the problematic tone privately to preserve the relationship and psychological safety.

text: A project manager must engage a highly influential but low-interest stakeholder, per the power/interest grid. Which stakeholder management strategy is appropriate?

options.A: Inform them in detail about everything, as if they had high interest
options.B: Manage closely with detailed daily meetings
options.C: Monitor only, with no communication
options.D: Keep satisfied with infrequent, high-level updates

justification: Correct: for high power and low interest, the 'Keep Satisfied' strategy provides infrequent, sufficient high-level information to maintain their support.

text: An agile team practices pair programming, but some developers oppose it, deeming it a waste of time. How should the Scrum Master address this resistance?

options.A: Sanction those who refuse to practice pair programming
options.B: Impose pair programming 100% of the time without discussion
options.C: Immediately abandon the practice without experimenting
options.D: Facilitate a discussion on perceived benefits and drawbacks, experiment with variants (partial pairing), and measure the impact on quality

justification: Correct: an empirical approach (discussing, experimenting with variants, measuring real impact) lets the team decide collectively based on concrete data.

text: A project manager must decompose the project scope into manageable components. Which tool produces a hierarchical decomposition of the work to be performed?

options.A: The communications management plan
options.B: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
options.C: The Gantt chart
options.D: The risk register
