text: An agile team's organization is undergoing a merger, and the newly combined leadership is unclear about which product priorities to fund. What should the project/product leader do to help the team maintain focus?

options.A: Make prioritization decisions unilaterally without leadership input
options.B: Halt all work until the merger is fully resolved
options.C: Continue working on the current backlog exactly as-is until formal direction arrives, regardless of duration
options.D: Proactively engage new leadership to clarify priorities and timebox a decision, while keeping the team focused on the highest-confidence, low-risk backlog items in the meantime

justification: Correct. Proactively engaging leadership for timely clarity, while keeping the team productively focused on low-risk, high-confidence items, balances business environment uncertainty with maintaining delivery momentum.

text: A team's Definition of Done requires automated tests, code review, and documentation for every user story. Under deadline pressure, a team member suggests skipping documentation for the current story to save time. What is the BEST response from the team?

options.A: Agree to skip documentation for this one story to hit the deadline
options.B: Let each team member decide individually whether to follow the Definition of Done
options.C: Maintain the Definition of Done and treat the story as not-done if the criteria are not fully met, addressing scope/timeline separately
options.D: Remove documentation from the Definition of Done permanently

justification: Correct. The Definition of Done is a quality commitment; if a story cannot meet it, it should not be counted as done. Timeline or scope pressures should be resolved through prioritization, not by lowering quality standards.

text: A distributed agile team spans three time zones, making real-time collaboration difficult. Team members report feeling disconnected from each other. What should the project leader do to improve team cohesion?

options.A: Establish overlapping core hours for key ceremonies and create asynchronous communication channels and informal virtual social touchpoints
options.B: Mandate that all team members work the same hours regardless of time zone
options.C: Split the team permanently into separate, disconnected sub-projects by region
options.D: Reduce team communication to only written status reports to avoid scheduling conflicts

justification: Correct. Establishing overlapping core hours for essential ceremonies, combined with asynchronous tools and informal social touchpoints, is the standard approach for building cohesion in distributed teams.

text: Which of the following are valid quality management techniques used to identify the root cause of a defect? (Select TWO)

options.A: Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram
options.B: Five Whys analysis
options.C: Resource leveling
options.D: Fast tracking

justification: Correct. The Fishbone diagram is a root cause analysis tool that categorizes potential causes of a defect or problem across dimensions such as people, process, and materials. / Correct. The Five Whys technique iteratively asks 'why' to drill down from a symptom to its underlying root cause.

text: A predictive infrastructure project is delayed because a critical import permit from a government agency is taking longer than expected. The project manager had identified this as a risk during planning. What is the BEST NEXT step?

options.A: Escalate to executive management without first checking the planned response
options.B: Implement the pre-defined contingency response documented in the risk register for this identified risk
options.C: Wait passively since the risk was already identified and therefore no action is needed
options.D: Remove the risk from the register since it has already materialized

justification: Correct. When a previously identified risk materializes into an issue, the project manager should execute the pre-planned contingency response documented in the risk register.

text: During a Retrospective, the team identifies that unclear acceptance criteria from the Product Owner caused rework in the last two Sprints. The Product Owner becomes defensive when this is raised. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to handle this?

options.A: Side with the team publicly and criticize the Product Owner's performance
options.B: Skip the topic to avoid conflict with the Product Owner
options.C: Facilitate the discussion constructively, focusing on the process issue and collaboratively defining an improvement action, such as a shared acceptance criteria template
options.D: Remove the Product Owner from future Retrospectives

justification: Correct. The Scrum Master facilitates Retrospectives constructively, keeping focus on process improvement rather than blame, and helps the team co-create actionable solutions like a shared template.

text: A Product Owner wants to release a new feature to a small subset of users before the full Sprint Review to gather early feedback. What is the BEST way to support this within the Scrum framework?

options.A: Cancel the current Sprint to accommodate the early release
options.B: Support a controlled release (e.g., feature flag or beta group) as an additional feedback mechanism, complementing rather than replacing the Sprint Review
options.C: Delay the Sprint Review until after the full public release
options.D: Prevent the release since only the Sprint Review can be used to gather stakeholder feedback

justification: Correct. Controlled releases such as feature flags or beta groups are common techniques to gather early, real user feedback and complement formal Scrum events without disrupting the Sprint.

text: Match each business environment factor to the correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: A new data protection law requiring changes to how customer data is stored
A competitor launching a similar product with additional features
A company's established norms around risk tolerance and decision-making speed
A new cloud platform capability that changes how the product can be architected

justification: Regulatory factors are external legal requirements the organization must comply with, often triggering scope or process changes such as new data handling requirements. / Competitive pressure from other market players is a business environment factor that can drive urgency, reprioritization, or differentiation strategies. / Internal organizational culture, including risk tolerance and decision norms, shapes how projects are planned, escalated, and executed within that organization. / Emerging technology can create new opportunities or constraints that influence architecture, tooling, and delivery approach decisions.

text: A project sponsor frequently bypasses the project manager and gives direct instructions to team members, causing confusion about priorities. What is the BEST way for the project manager to address this?

options.A: Instruct the team to ignore any instructions that do not come through the project manager
options.B: Have a direct, respectful conversation with the sponsor about the impact of bypassing the PM and agree on a clearer communication protocol
options.C: Escalate to the PMO immediately without speaking to the sponsor first
options.D: Accept the situation since the sponsor has more organizational authority

justification: Correct. Direct, respectful communication about the impact of the behavior and agreeing on a clear protocol is the standard first approach to resolve a stakeholder communication/governance issue.

text: A Scrum team's velocity has dropped by 40% over the last three Sprints, but the team insists nothing has changed. What is the BEST diagnostic action for the Scrum Master?

options.A: Ignore the velocity trend since it is only a forecasting metric
options.B: Assume the team is underperforming intentionally and report it to management
options.C: Facilitate a deeper Retrospective or 1:1 conversations to explore hidden factors such as increased complexity, interruptions, or team changes
options.D: Lower future Sprint commitments permanently without investigation

justification: Correct. A drop in velocity often signals hidden factors (increased complexity, interruptions, attrition, technical debt); deeper facilitated discussion is needed to surface and address the real cause.

text: An agile team is developing a product for a market where user internet connectivity is often unreliable. Which action BEST reflects incorporating this business environment consideration into the product backlog?

options.A: Ignore connectivity concerns since the team follows an agile approach focused on iterative delivery
options.B: Assume all users have reliable connectivity to simplify the technical design
options.C: Add offline-capable functionality and data-sync features as backlog items and prioritize them based on target market needs
options.D: Postpone any connectivity-related features until after the product's initial launch

justification: Correct. Recognizing the target market's real-world constraints (unreliable connectivity) and translating them into prioritized backlog items ensures the product will genuinely serve its intended users.

text: A project's schedule network diagram shows that Activity C can only start after both Activity A and Activity B are complete. Activity A takes 5 days and Activity B takes 8 days, both starting on day 0. What is the earliest start day for Activity C?

options.A: Day 5
options.B: Day 13
options.C: Day 8
options.D: Day 0

justification: Correct. Since Activity C depends on completion of both A (5 days) and B (8 days) starting at day 0, it cannot start until the longer duration path (Activity B) finishes on day 8.

text: A highly skilled but introverted developer rarely participates verbally in team discussions, though their code quality is excellent. A more vocal team member suggests the introverted developer 'isn't a team player.' What should the project leader do?

options.A: Exclude the introverted developer from discussions entirely since they prefer not to speak
options.B: Agree with the vocal team member's assessment and address it as a performance issue
options.C: Require the introverted developer to speak a minimum number of times per meeting
options.D: Recognize different communication and collaboration styles, coach the team on valuing diverse contributions, and find alternative ways for the introverted developer to contribute their perspective (e.g., written input)

justification: Correct. Recognizing diverse working and communication styles and providing alternative contribution channels reflects inclusive, effective team leadership that values all contributions, not just vocal ones.

text: Which of the following are appropriate techniques to size or estimate a Product Backlog item in agile? (Select TWO)

options.A: Planning Poker
options.B: T-shirt sizing
options.C: Critical path method
options.D: Reserve analysis for contingency budget

justification: Correct. Planning Poker is a widely used consensus-based estimation technique where team members reveal estimates simultaneously using a numeric card sequence. / Correct. T-shirt sizing is a relative sizing technique (S, M, L, XL) used, especially for high-level or early-stage estimation of backlog items.

text: A project operates under a fixed-price contract. Midway through execution, the client requests significant additional scope not covered in the original statement of work. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Absorb the additional work within the existing budget without informing the client of any impact
options.B: Refuse the request outright without discussion
options.C: Complete the additional scope immediately to maintain client satisfaction
options.D: Submit a formal change request through the change control process to evaluate impact on cost, schedule, and contract terms before proceeding

justification: Correct. Any scope change, especially under a fixed-price contract, must go through formal change control to assess cost, schedule, and contractual impact before commitment, protecting both parties.

text: Match each servant-leadership behavior to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: Working with IT to resolve a blocked deployment pipeline that is stalling the team's progress
Allowing the team to decide how to technically implement a backlog item rather than dictating the solution
Asking guiding questions to help a team member arrive at their own solution to a problem
Managing external interruptions so the team can focus on the Sprint Goal

justification: Proactively identifying and resolving obstacles that block team progress is a core servant-leadership responsibility that keeps delivery flowing. / Delegating implementation decisions to the team fosters ownership and leverages their expertise, a hallmark of self-organizing agile teams. / Guiding through questions rather than giving direct answers builds the team's own problem-solving capability over time. / Protecting the team's focus from external noise and interruptions preserves their capacity to deliver against the Sprint Goal.

text: A team has just completed Sprint 8 of a 12-Sprint release plan. The release burndown shows the team is trending to finish with approximately 15% of the originally planned scope incomplete, based on current velocity. The Product Owner is concerned about the fixed launch date, which was communicated externally. What is the BEST course of action for the team and Product Owner?

options.A: Unilaterally move the launch date without involving the Product Owner or stakeholders
options.B: Ignore the burndown trend and hope the team's velocity increases without any changes
options.C: Use the burndown data to have the Product Owner reprioritize the remaining backlog, ensuring the highest-value items are completed by the fixed date and lower-value items are deferred
options.D: Force the team to work unpaid overtime for the remaining Sprints to complete all original scope

justification: Correct. Using empirical burndown data to reprioritize scope against a fixed date (fixing time, varying scope) is the standard agile response, ensuring maximum value delivery within the given constraint.

text: Which of the following are valid components of a project's cost baseline? (Select TWO)

options.A: Time-phased budget
options.B: Aggregated cost estimates for all work packages
options.C: Team member performance reviews
options.D: Marketing strategy for the final product

justification: Correct. The cost baseline is an approved, time-phased budget used as a basis against which to measure, monitor, and control overall cost performance. / Correct. The cost baseline is developed by aggregating the estimated costs of individual work packages (and activities) into control accounts and then the total project budget.

text: A project manager learns that two team members have an unresolved personal conflict from a previous project that is now affecting their collaboration on shared tasks. What is the BEST first step?

options.A: Require both team members to apologize to each other publicly
options.B: Reassign tasks to eliminate all interaction between the two team members
options.C: Report the conflict to HR immediately without attempting direct resolution
options.D: Meet with each individual separately to understand their perspective, then facilitate a joint conversation focused on working effectively together going forward

justification: Correct. Understanding each perspective individually, then facilitating a joint, forward-focused conversation, is the standard conflict resolution approach that addresses the root issue constructively.

text: A Product Owner wants the Development Team to work on two unrelated high-priority Epics simultaneously within the same Sprint. The team is concerned about context switching hurting quality. What should the team do?

options.A: Silently comply and split their attention across both Epics
options.B: Split into two sub-teams permanently to handle each Epic independently
options.C: Explain the impact of context switching on quality and throughput, and propose a sequenced approach that still prioritizes the highest-value Epic first
options.D: Refuse to work on either Epic until the Product Owner reduces scope

justification: Correct. Transparently explaining the trade-offs of context switching, backed by team experience/data, and proposing a value-based sequencing respects both team capacity and Product Owner priorities.

text: An organization's leadership pressures an agile team to reduce the length of Sprint Retrospectives to 'save time,' even though the team has identified valuable process improvements from full-length Retrospectives. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to respond?

options.A: Present the value and evidence of improvements gained from Retrospectives to leadership and negotiate preserving adequate time for inspection and adaptation
options.B: Comply immediately without discussing the impact
options.C: Ignore leadership's request and continue as before without any communication
options.D: Eliminate Retrospectives entirely to fully satisfy leadership's request

justification: Correct. Advocating for the team's practices with evidence of value, while remaining open to negotiation, reflects the Scrum Master's role as a change agent influencing the organization based on demonstrated outcomes.

text: A team practicing Scrum discovers mid-Sprint that a Product Backlog Item they committed to is far more complex than originally estimated. What is the MOST appropriate action?

options.A: Communicate the discovery transparently to the Product Owner and collaboratively decide whether to negotiate scope, split the item, or carry it to the next Sprint
options.B: Silently work overtime to force completion within the Sprint
options.C: Blame the estimation process and stop estimating in future Sprints
options.D: Remove the item from the Sprint without informing the Product Owner

justification: Correct. Transparent communication and collaborative decision-making with the Product Owner reflects Scrum values (transparency, inspection, adaptation) and lets the business make an informed trade-off.

text: A predictive project operating in a country with high inflation is experiencing rising material costs beyond what was budgeted in the cost baseline. What is the BEST way for the project manager to address this business environment factor?

options.A: Absorb the cost increases silently without informing the sponsor
options.B: Reduce quality standards to offset the cost increase without stakeholder approval
options.C: Halt the project immediately without analysis
options.D: Analyze the cost variance, update forecasts (EAC/ETC), and formally communicate the impact and options to the sponsor for a funding or scope decision

justification: Correct. Analyzing variance, updating forecasts, and transparently presenting options to the sponsor is the standard cost control response to an external economic factor affecting the baseline.

text: A team is transitioning from a command-and-control management style to a self-organizing agile approach. Team members frequently defer decisions back to the project leader out of habit. What is the BEST way for the leader to support this transition?

options.A: Redirect decision-making questions back to the team with coaching questions, gradually building their confidence and ownership
options.B: Continue making all decisions to avoid confusion during the transition
options.C: Criticize the team for their lack of independence
options.D: Assign a temporary decision-maker from outside the team

justification: Correct. Coaching through redirected questions builds the team's decision-making muscle over time, which is the core servant-leadership technique for developing self-organizing teams.

text: A project's quality audit reveals that a specific work package has a defect rate three times higher than similar work packages. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Replace the entire team responsible for that work package immediately
options.B: Reject all deliverables from that work package without investigation
options.C: Conduct root cause analysis to determine why the defect rate is elevated before deciding on corrective action
options.D: Ignore the finding since defect rates naturally vary

justification: Correct. Root cause analysis (e.g., fishbone diagram, five whys) is the appropriate quality management response to determine why an anomaly exists before applying corrective action.

text: A company's executive sponsor for an agile initiative frequently changes strategic priorities based on short-term market reactions, causing the Product Backlog to be reprioritized every Sprint with little stability. What is the BEST way for the product leader to manage this?

options.A: Engage the sponsor to establish a clearer prioritization framework (e.g., value-based criteria) and agree on a cadence for major reprioritization to balance responsiveness with team stability
options.B: Allow every request to immediately reorder the Sprint Backlog mid-Sprint
options.C: Escalate the sponsor's behavior to their superior without first attempting direct engagement
options.D: Refuse to make any further changes to the backlog regardless of sponsor input

justification: Correct. Establishing a clear, value-based prioritization framework and an agreed cadence balances the organization's need for responsiveness with the team's need for enough stability to deliver effectively.

text: A team using Scrum notices that several Product Backlog Items lack sufficiently clear acceptance criteria, leading to ambiguity during Sprint Planning. What is the BEST way to prevent this in future Sprints?

options.A: Accept ambiguous items into the Sprint and clarify them only when developers get stuck
options.B: Skip Sprint Planning discussions and let developers interpret requirements as they build
options.C: Strengthen the Backlog Refinement process to ensure items are well-defined with clear acceptance criteria before they enter Sprint Planning
options.D: Ask the Product Owner to write all technical implementation details themselves

justification: Correct. Backlog Refinement is specifically intended to ensure Product Backlog Items are well-understood, appropriately sized, and have clear acceptance criteria before Sprint Planning.

text: A nonprofit organization funding an agile project requires detailed quarterly impact reports for their donors, which is unusual for the agile teams involved. What is the BEST way to integrate this requirement without disrupting agile delivery?

options.A: Pause all Sprints each quarter to compile the report manually from scratch
options.B: Build the donor reporting need into the Definition of Done or a recurring backlog item, using existing Sprint Review outputs and increment data as the primary source
options.C: Refuse the requirement since it is not part of standard Scrum artifacts
options.D: Delegate reporting entirely to a separate team with no connection to the delivery team's data

justification: Correct. Integrating the reporting need into existing artifacts and cadences (Definition of Done, Sprint Review outputs) satisfies the donor requirement efficiently without disrupting the agile delivery rhythm.

text: A project team member requests to work remotely for the remainder of the project due to a personal family situation. Their role requires close daily coordination with other team members. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Discuss with the team member to understand their needs and explore whether remote work with adjusted coordination mechanisms (e.g., scheduled check-ins) could work
options.B: Approve the request without considering any impact on coordination
options.C: Reassign the team member's responsibilities to someone else without discussion
options.D: Deny the request immediately citing coordination needs

justification: Correct. Understanding the team member's needs and exploring practical accommodation (such as adjusted coordination mechanisms) reflects supportive, human-centered leadership while still addressing legitimate coordination concerns.

text: A hybrid project has a predictive-managed hardware component and an agile-managed software component that must integrate at a fixed hardware delivery date. The software team's Sprint cadence does not align neatly with this date. What is the BEST planning approach?

options.A: Force the hardware team to adopt Sprints identical to the software team
options.B: Ignore the hardware delivery date and let the software team proceed independently
options.C: Align a software release plan (grouping several Sprints) to converge with the fixed hardware milestone, using release planning to synchronize the two workstreams
options.D: Convert the entire hardware workstream to agile despite its physical/manufacturing constraints

justification: Correct. Release planning that groups multiple Sprints toward a synchronization milestone is the standard hybrid technique to align an agile workstream's incremental delivery with a predictive workstream's fixed milestone.

text: Which of the following are examples of Enterprise Environmental Factors (EEFs) that can influence a project? (Select TWO)

options.A: Government regulations and industry standards
options.B: Organizational culture and governance structure
options.C: The project's specific risk register
options.D: The project's specific WBS dictionary

justification: Correct. Government regulations and industry standards are external EEFs that constrain or influence how the project must be planned and executed. / Correct. Organizational culture and governance structure are internal EEFs that shape decision-making processes, risk tolerance, and communication norms within the project.

text: During a heated Sprint Planning session, one team member repeatedly interrupts others and dismisses their estimates as 'wrong.' Other team members have stopped contributing. What is the BEST immediate action for the Scrum Master?

options.A: End the meeting and reschedule it for another day without addressing the behavior
options.B: Intervene in the moment to reset the tone, remind the group of working agreements, and ensure equal opportunity for input from all members
options.C: Privately ask the quieter members to be more assertive without addressing the dominant member's behavior
options.D: Let the dominant team member continue since they may have valid technical points

justification: Correct. In-the-moment facilitation to reset tone and reinforce agreed working norms is the Scrum Master's responsibility to protect psychological safety and ensure balanced participation.

text: A project manager is developing the schedule and finds that Activity X has zero total float on the critical path, while Activity Y (not on the critical path) has 4 days of total float. What is the implication for the project manager?

options.A: Both activities have the same impact on the project end date
options.B: Activity X should be removed from the schedule since it has no flexibility
options.C: Activity Y is more critical to monitor since it has more float
options.D: Any delay to Activity X will directly delay the project finish date, while Activity Y can be delayed up to 4 days without impacting the project finish date

justification: Correct. Zero total float means Activity X is on the critical path and any delay directly delays the project finish date; 4 days of float on Activity Y means it has that much flexibility before impacting the finish date.

text: A company adopting agile practices for the first time has a finance department that still requires detailed upfront cost estimates for annual budgeting, which conflicts with agile's iterative planning approach. What is the BEST way to reconcile this?

options.A: Ignore finance's requirements and proceed with agile planning regardless of organizational needs
options.B: Refuse to provide any estimates since agile does not support detailed upfront planning
options.C: Provide a highly detailed, fixed-scope estimate identical to a traditional waterfall budget and commit to it rigidly
options.D: Provide a rolling wave or high-level release-level budget estimate based on historical velocity and refine it each quarter as more is learned

justification: Correct. Rolling wave planning provides a reasonable, progressively refined budget estimate that respects both agile's iterative nature and the organization's need for periodic financial planning.

text: A project manager observes that a team member is highly skilled technically but consistently misses smaller administrative tasks like timesheet updates and status reports. What is the BEST leadership approach?

options.A: Ignore the missed tasks since the person's technical work is strong
options.B: Reassign all administrative tasks to someone else without discussing it with the team member
options.C: Formally reprimand the team member in front of the team to emphasize accountability
options.D: Discuss the pattern directly with the team member, understand any underlying cause, and agree on a practical solution such as reminders or simplified reporting templates

justification: Correct. A direct, understanding conversation that seeks the root cause and co-creates a practical solution is effective coaching leadership that respects the individual while addressing the performance gap.

text: A Product Owner asks the Scrum Master to remove a Development Team member from the team because their velocity contribution seems lower than others. What is the MOST appropriate response from the Scrum Master?

options.A: Immediately remove the team member without any investigation
options.B: Immediately comply with the Product Owner's request since they manage the product
options.C: Explain that team composition is not typically decided by the Product Owner, investigate the actual cause of lower contribution, and address it through coaching or team discussion
options.D: Publicly announce the concern to the whole team during the Daily Scrum

justification: Correct. Clarifying role boundaries while investigating the actual root cause (which could be complexity of assigned work, mentoring newer members, or other factors) reflects appropriate Scrum Master facilitation and coaching.

text: A project operating internationally must comply with export control laws that restrict sharing certain technical data with team members in specific countries. What should the project manager do to address this constraint?

options.A: Exclude all international team members from the project entirely
options.B: Ignore the restriction since it complicates team collaboration
options.C: Share all information with everyone and address any legal issues only if they arise
options.D: Work with legal/compliance to define which data can be shared with which team members and adjust the communication plan and access controls accordingly

justification: Correct. Partnering with legal/compliance to define appropriate data access boundaries and updating the communication plan and access controls is the correct way to manage a legal/regulatory constraint while enabling collaboration.

text: Which of the following are valid Scrum accountabilities (roles)? (Select TWO)

options.A: Product Owner
options.B: Scrum Master
options.C: Project Sponsor
options.D: Business Analyst

justification: Correct. The Product Owner is one of the three formal Scrum accountabilities, responsible for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. / Correct. The Scrum Master is one of the three formal Scrum accountabilities, responsible for establishing Scrum as defined and coaching the team and organization.

text: A project manager assigned to a new project inherits a team where morale is visibly low due to a previous project's failure. What should the project manager do FIRST to rebuild team engagement?

options.A: Hold individual and group conversations to understand the team's experience, acknowledge past challenges, and co-create a fresh team charter for the new project
options.B: Replace most of the team with new members
options.C: Immediately impose new processes to prevent past mistakes from recurring
options.D: Avoid discussing the past project to prevent reopening old wounds

justification: Correct. Listening to the team's experience and acknowledging past challenges before co-creating shared norms builds trust and provides a constructive foundation for the new project.

text: A team's Sprint Review consistently runs over time because stakeholders ask detailed implementation questions better suited for a technical discussion. What is the BEST way to improve this?

options.A: Extend every Sprint Review indefinitely to accommodate all questions
options.B: Refuse to answer any stakeholder questions during the Sprint Review
options.C: Cancel Sprint Reviews and replace them with written status emails
options.D: Set clear expectations at the start of the Sprint Review about its purpose and timebox, and offer a separate follow-up session for deep technical questions

justification: Correct. Clarifying the event's purpose and timebox while offering a separate channel for deep technical discussion keeps the Sprint Review focused and efficient without dismissing stakeholder curiosity.

text: A startup using agile practices secures a major new investor who requests significant influence over the product roadmap, conflicting with the current Product Owner's vision. What is the BEST way for the organization to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the investor's input entirely to protect the current roadmap
options.B: Give the investor unrestricted control over the Product Backlog
options.C: Facilitate a structured conversation between the investor and Product Owner to align on strategic priorities while preserving the Product Owner's accountability for backlog decisions
options.D: Remove the Product Owner and let the investor manage the backlog directly

justification: Correct. Facilitating alignment between key stakeholders while preserving the Product Owner's formal accountability respects both business influence and the integrity of the Scrum framework.

text: A team practicing Scrum notices that the same type of defect keeps recurring across multiple Sprints despite being fixed each time. What is the MOST effective long-term action?

options.A: Use the Retrospective to perform root cause analysis and implement a systemic fix (e.g., additional automated tests, process change) to prevent recurrence
options.B: Continue fixing the defect each time it appears without further investigation
options.C: Assign a single team member to be permanently responsible for fixing that recurring defect
options.D: Remove the affected feature from the product entirely

justification: Correct. Using the Retrospective for root cause analysis and implementing a systemic fix addresses the actual source of the recurring problem, which is the purpose of continuous improvement in Scrum.

text: A junior developer on an agile team makes a mistake that causes a minor production issue. The rest of the team reacts harshly, and the junior developer becomes visibly withdrawn in subsequent meetings. What is the BEST action for the project leader?

options.A: Reassign the junior developer to less critical, isolated tasks going forward
options.B: Say nothing and let the team dynamics resolve naturally over time
options.C: Address the team's reaction, reinforce a blameless learning culture, and privately support the junior developer to rebuild their confidence
options.D: Reprimand the junior developer further to reinforce the seriousness of the mistake

justification: Correct. Reinforcing a blameless, learning-oriented culture and privately supporting the affected individual addresses both the team dynamic and the individual's wellbeing, which is central to servant leadership.

text: Which of the following are inputs typically used when developing a project schedule using the Critical Path Method? (Select TWO)

options.A: Activity list with dependencies
options.B: Activity duration estimates
options.C: Stakeholder satisfaction survey results
options.D: Team member personality assessments

justification: Correct. The activity list with logical dependencies (predecessor/successor relationships) is a fundamental input needed to build the network diagram used in the Critical Path Method. / Correct. Activity duration estimates are essential to calculate the total path length and identify the critical (longest) path through the network.

text: A project manager is informed that a key raw material supplier has gone out of business, threatening the supply chain for a critical deliverable. This risk was not previously identified. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Add the risk to the risk register retroactively and perform qualitative/quantitative analysis, then develop and implement a response strategy
options.B: Escalate to the sponsor immediately without any internal analysis
options.C: Wait to see if an alternate supplier becomes available on its own
options.D: Cancel the project immediately due to the supply disruption

justification: Correct. Even though this risk emerged unexpectedly, the correct process is to formally document it, analyze its probability/impact, and develop an appropriate response (e.g., alternate supplier, expedited sourcing) before further action.

text: An agile team has two members who consistently disagree on nearly every technical decision, creating a pattern of gridlock that slows the team down. Individual conversations have not resolved the pattern. What should the Scrum Master do NEXT?

options.A: Facilitate a structured decision-making technique (e.g., defined decision criteria, a design spike, or a time-boxed trial) that the whole team agrees to use for resolving future technical disagreements
options.B: Make all future technical decisions on the team's behalf to bypass the gridlock
options.C: Let the gridlock continue since technical disagreements are healthy
options.D: Permanently separate the two team members onto different projects

justification: Correct. Introducing a structured, team-agreed decision-making mechanism (like time-boxed spikes or defined criteria) gives the team a repeatable, objective way to resolve recurring gridlock constructively.

text: A Product Owner is unavailable for an extended period due to a medical emergency, and no proxy has been designated. The team has several Product Backlog Items requiring clarification. What is the BEST course of action?

options.A: Work with the organization to designate a temporary proxy Product Owner with appropriate authority to make prioritization and clarification decisions
options.B: Halt all Sprint work until the Product Owner returns
options.C: Ignore ambiguous items and only work on items the team already fully understands, indefinitely
options.D: Let the Development Team make all Product Backlog decisions independently going forward

justification: Correct. Designating an empowered temporary proxy Product Owner ensures business decisions can continue to be made, maintaining delivery continuity during an unavoidable absence.

text: Match each hybrid approach scenario to the MOST appropriate life cycle description.

colonne_gauche.texte: Well-understood requirements, high regulatory documentation needs
Evolving requirements, need for frequent stakeholder feedback
Fixed hardware milestones combined with evolving software features
Requirements unclear at the start but firm up significantly after an initial phase

colonne_droite.texte: Predictive life cycle
Agile life cycle
Hybrid life cycle
Incremental life cycle

justification: A predictive (plan-driven) life cycle suits projects with stable, well-understood requirements and significant upfront planning and documentation needs, such as regulated environments. / An agile life cycle suits projects with evolving requirements, where frequent, iterative feedback from stakeholders helps shape the evolving product. / A hybrid life cycle combines predictive management for fixed, sequential elements (like hardware) with agile management for elements benefiting from iteration and feedback (like software). / An incremental life cycle delivers the product in successive increments, which fits well when requirements become clearer after an initial phase of work or discovery.

text: A project manager discovers that a team member has been quietly covering for a colleague's repeated missed deadlines by doing extra work themselves, leading to signs of burnout. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Reassign all of the underperforming colleague's work to the team member who has been covering
options.B: Wait until performance reviews to address either issue
options.C: Praise the team member publicly for their extra effort and encourage them to continue
options.D: Have a private conversation with the overextended team member to understand the situation, then separately address the root performance issue with the underperforming colleague

justification: Correct. Understanding the overextended team member's situation while separately addressing the root performance issue resolves both the immediate wellbeing concern and the underlying cause.

text: A team's Increment fails to meet the Definition of Done at the end of a Sprint because a dependency on another team's component was not delivered in time. What is the BEST way to handle this in the Sprint Review?

options.A: Present the incomplete work as done to avoid disappointing stakeholders
options.B: Transparently present the actual state of the Increment, explain the dependency issue, and discuss next steps with stakeholders
options.C: Blame the other team publicly during the Sprint Review
options.D: Cancel the Sprint Review entirely since there is nothing to show

justification: Correct. Transparently presenting the true state of the Increment, including the dependency issue, upholds Scrum's transparency and inspection values and enables informed next-step decisions.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a heavily unionized industry where changes to work processes must be negotiated with union representatives. The team wants to implement a new collaborative practice that changes daily work routines. What should the project leader do?

options.A: Avoid making any process changes indefinitely to prevent union involvement
options.B: Engage with union representatives as key stakeholders to understand any process change requirements before implementing the new practice
options.C: Implement the change only for non-union team members
options.D: Implement the change immediately since it is a team-level agile practice

justification: Correct. Engaging union representatives as legitimate stakeholders respects the organization's labor agreements and business environment while still pursuing the desired agile improvement.

text: A project manager is calculating the Estimate at Completion (EAC) for a project where the current cost variance is expected to continue at the same rate for the remainder of the project. Which EAC formula should be used?

options.A: EAC = AC + (BAC - EV)
options.B: EAC = AC + [(BAC-EV) / (CPI x SPI)]
options.C: EAC = BAC / CPI
options.D: EAC = AC + Bottom-up ETC

justification: Correct. EAC = BAC / CPI is used when the current cost performance is expected to continue for the remainder of the project, projecting the same efficiency ratio forward.

text: A team member on an agile team frequently volunteers for the most visible, high-profile tasks while avoiding necessary but less glamorous work like documentation or testing support. This is starting to create resentment among peers. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Say nothing since task selection is up to individual team members in a self-organizing team
options.B: Publicly call out the team member's task choices during the Daily Scrum
options.C: Assign only unglamorous tasks to that team member going forward as a corrective measure
options.D: Have a direct conversation about balanced contribution and work with the team to make task selection during Sprint Planning more transparent and equitable

justification: Correct. A direct, constructive conversation combined with a more transparent, team-agreed task selection process addresses both the individual behavior and the systemic fairness issue.

text: Which of the following are valid purposes of a Sprint Retrospective? (Select TWO)

options.A: Inspect how the last Sprint went with regard to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and Definition of Done
options.B: Plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness for the next Sprint
options.C: Demonstrate the Increment to external stakeholders for feedback
options.D: Finalize the release date with executive sponsors

justification: Correct. The Sprint Retrospective is specifically for the Scrum Team to inspect how the last Sprint went in terms of people, relationships, process, and tools. / Correct. Identifying improvements and planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness going forward is a core purpose of the Retrospective.

text: A predictive project's sponsor organization is acquired by another company midway through execution, and the acquiring company has different strategic priorities. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Cancel the project immediately without confirming new leadership's position
options.B: Avoid contacting the new leadership to prevent uncertainty
options.C: Engage new leadership to reconfirm the project's business justification and alignment with the new organizational strategy, updating the business case if needed
options.D: Continue the project exactly as originally planned since the charter was already approved

justification: Correct. A major organizational change such as an acquisition warrants reconfirming the project's ongoing business justification and strategic alignment with new leadership, updating the business case as needed.

text: Match each team development stage (Tuckman's model) to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Team members are polite and get oriented to the project and each other, with limited real collaboration
Team members begin to challenge ideas and authority, and conflicts about approach may emerge
Team members begin working together more effectively and start trusting and adjusting to each other's habits
The team operates as a well-organized unit with high interdependence and effective collaboration

justification: In this initial stage, team members are typically polite and get acquainted, but have not yet developed real working trust or collaboration patterns. / This stage often involves conflict as team members test boundaries, challenge ideas, and work through differing approaches or opinions. / As the team resolves earlier conflicts, members begin trusting one another and establishing effective working patterns and cohesion. / In this mature stage, the team functions interdependently and efficiently, resolving issues smoothly and delivering consistently.

text: A hybrid program's software team has completed 10 Sprints. Their average velocity has stabilized at 40 story points per Sprint. There are 200 story points of high-priority work remaining in the Product Backlog, and the fixed program end date allows for 4 more Sprints. The Product Owner is reluctant to reduce scope, citing stakeholder commitments made early in the program. What is the MOST appropriate way for the Scrum Master to help resolve this situation?

options.A: Instruct the team to simply work faster to complete all 200 points in the remaining Sprints
options.B: Present the velocity data (40 points/Sprint x 4 Sprints = 160 points capacity vs. 200 points remaining) to help the Product Owner make an informed decision about reprioritizing scope or renegotiating stakeholder commitments
options.C: Silently let the team try to finish and report success regardless of the outcome
options.D: Unilaterally cut 40 points from the backlog without Product Owner involvement

justification: Correct. Using empirical velocity data to clearly show the capacity gap (160 vs. 200 points) empowers the Product Owner to make an evidence-based decision about scope trade-offs or stakeholder renegotiation — the Scrum Master's role in facilitating transparency.

text: Which of the following are valid procurement documents used when soliciting seller responses in a predictive project? (Select TWO)

options.A: Request for Proposal (RFP)
options.B: Request for Quotation (RFQ)
options.C: Sprint Backlog
options.D: Team charter

justification: Correct. A Request for Proposal is a formal procurement document used to solicit detailed proposals from potential sellers, typically when the solution approach is not fully defined. / Correct. A Request for Quotation is a formal procurement document used to solicit price quotes, typically for well-defined, standardized goods or services.

text: A project manager on a healthcare IT implementation notices that clinical staff assigned part-time to the project are frequently pulled away for patient care emergencies, disrupting planned work sessions. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Work with clinical leadership to establish a realistic, flexible engagement plan that respects patient care priorities while securing dedicated project time
options.B: Remove clinical staff from the project team entirely
options.C: Ignore the disruptions and hope the schedule absorbs them
options.D: Insist that clinical staff prioritize the project over patient care

justification: Correct. Collaborating with clinical leadership to build a flexible plan that respects the true operational constraints while still securing needed project time is a realistic, stakeholder-sensitive resource management approach.

text: A marketing team using Scrum for campaign development finds that Sprint Reviews rarely generate actionable stakeholder feedback because stakeholders come unprepared. What is the BEST way to improve the value of these sessions?

options.A: Share the increment and key discussion points with stakeholders in advance and set clear expectations for the kind of feedback needed
options.B: Replace the Sprint Review with a written survey only
options.C: Extend the Sprint Review length until useful feedback eventually emerges
options.D: Stop inviting stakeholders to Sprint Reviews altogether

justification: Correct. Preparing stakeholders in advance with context and clear expectations increases the quality and relevance of the feedback gathered during the session.

text: A retail company's agile team is developing a new e-commerce feature during a period when a major industry-wide data breach at a competitor has significantly raised customer concerns about data security. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Halt all feature development until a full security audit is completed
options.B: Reassess and likely elevate the priority of security-related backlog items to address the shifted market sensitivity to data protection
options.C: Ignore the industry event since it did not happen to their own company
options.D: Wait until the next quarterly planning cycle to consider any changes

justification: Correct. Responding to a significant shift in the business environment, such as heightened market sensitivity to data security, by reprioritizing relevant backlog items reflects adaptive, environment-aware product leadership.

text: A team practicing Scaled Agile across multiple Scrum teams working on the same product notices frequent integration conflicts between teams' code at the end of each Sprint. What is the BEST way to reduce this?

options.A: Have each team work in complete isolation with no coordination until the final release
options.B: Merge all teams into one large team to eliminate coordination needs
options.C: Implement more frequent cross-team integration (e.g., continuous integration and regular cross-team sync points like Scrum of Scrums) throughout the Sprint
options.D: Postpone all integration until the very end of the entire program

justification: Correct. Frequent integration practices, such as continuous integration and regular cross-team synchronization events, surface conflicts early when they are smaller and easier to resolve.

text: A newly formed agile team includes members from very different cultural backgrounds with differing norms around giving direct feedback. This is causing miscommunication during Retrospectives. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Facilitate a conversation to build shared understanding of different communication styles and co-create team working agreements that respect this diversity
options.B: Require all feedback to follow one specific cultural communication style
options.C: Separate team members by cultural background into different sub-teams
options.D: Avoid facilitating open feedback discussions to prevent cultural friction

justification: Correct. Building mutual understanding and co-creating inclusive working agreements respects cultural diversity while still enabling effective, direct team communication — a key cultural awareness and team-building leadership skill.

text: Which of the following are examples of positive (opportunity) risk response strategies? (Select TWO)

options.A: Exploit
options.B: Enhance
options.C: Avoid
options.D: Transfer

justification: Correct. Exploit is a positive risk response strategy used to ensure that an opportunity is realized by eliminating the uncertainty associated with it. / Correct. Enhance is a positive risk response strategy used to increase the probability and/or positive impact of an opportunity.

text: A construction project operating in a region prone to seasonal flooding is scheduled to have critical outdoor work occur during the rainy season. This risk was accepted at project initiation due to schedule constraints. Flooding now threatens to delay the project by several weeks. What is the BEST project manager action?

options.A: Since the risk was accepted, take no action and simply absorb the resulting delay
options.B: Reassess the situation as the accepted risk materializes, and apply an active contingency response if one was planned, or develop a workaround if not
options.C: Ignore the flooding and continue work as scheduled regardless of safety concerns
options.D: Blame the weather and close out the project as failed

justification: Correct. When an accepted risk materializes, the project manager should apply any pre-planned contingency reserve/response, or if none exists, develop a workaround, consistent with active risk management practice.

text: An experienced team member frequently offers to mentor newer team members but has recently stopped doing so, appearing withdrawn. The project leader learns this coincided with a personal loss in the mentor's family. What is the MOST appropriate response?

options.A: Have a private, empathetic conversation to acknowledge their situation, offer flexibility, and let them decide their level of involvement without pressure
options.B: Publicly announce the personal situation to the team to explain the change in behavior
options.C: Reassign all mentoring responsibilities to someone else without discussing it with the affected team member
options.D: Insist they continue mentoring at the same level to maintain team knowledge transfer

justification: Correct. A private, empathetic conversation that offers flexibility and respects the team member's autonomy in a difficult personal time reflects supportive, human-centered leadership.

text: A Product Owner wants to add a 'nice to have' feature mid-Sprint that a major client casually mentioned during a call, without any formal request or clear value assessment. What should the team do?

options.A: Log it as a Product Backlog item for future refinement and prioritization based on actual value assessment, without disrupting the current Sprint
options.B: Reject the idea outright without recording it anywhere
options.C: Add it to the current Sprint immediately since the request came from a major client
options.D: Ask the client to submit a formal contract amendment before considering it at all

justification: Correct. Capturing the idea in the Product Backlog for proper future refinement and value-based prioritization respects the Sprint's current commitment while ensuring the idea isn't lost.

text: Match each organizational structure type to its typical characteristic.

colonne_droite.texte: Project manager has little to no formal authority; team members report primarily to functional managers
Power is shared relatively evenly between the project manager and functional managers
The project manager has significant authority and dedicated administrative support
Team members report directly to the project manager, who holds significant authority over resources

justification: In a functional structure, staff report to functional managers by department, and project managers typically have limited authority, often acting more as coordinators. / In a balanced matrix, authority is shared fairly evenly between functional managers and the project manager, creating dual reporting relationships. / In a strong matrix, the project manager holds significant authority, often supported by dedicated project management staff, though functional managers still exist. / In a projectized structure, the organization is built around projects, and the project manager has full authority over resources dedicated to the project.

text: During project execution, a vendor's key technical representative is replaced without notice, and the new representative lacks context on prior agreements. This is causing delays in vendor deliverables. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Continue interacting with the new representative as if no change occurred
options.B: Escalate to the vendor's executive leadership before attempting direct engagement with the new representative
options.C: Arrange a formal onboarding/handover session with the new representative to transfer context and re-establish clear expectations
options.D: Terminate the vendor contract immediately due to the disruption

justification: Correct. A structured handover/onboarding session to transfer context is the most direct and constructive way to quickly restore effective collaboration with the vendor's new representative.

text: A Scrum team wants to start using a burnup chart in addition to their existing burndown chart. What is the PRIMARY benefit of adding a burnup chart?

options.A: It automatically calculates team velocity without manual tracking
options.B: It clearly visualizes scope changes over time in addition to progress, which a burndown chart alone does not show as clearly
options.C: It replaces the need for a Product Backlog entirely
options.D: It eliminates the need for Sprint Reviews

justification: Correct. A burnup chart shows both completed work and total scope over time as separate lines, making scope changes clearly visible — a distinction that a simple burndown chart can obscure.

text: An agile team's organization decides to pursue a new market segment with significantly different regulatory requirements than their current market. What should the product leader do to prepare the backlog?

options.A: Delay any regulatory considerations until after the product has launched in the new market
options.B: Assume the development team will identify and handle regulatory needs without explicit backlog items
options.C: Apply the current market's regulatory assumptions to the new market without further research
options.D: Research the new market's specific regulatory requirements and incorporate compliance-related items into the backlog with appropriate priority

justification: Correct. Proactively researching and incorporating the new market's specific regulatory requirements into the backlog ensures compliance risk is properly managed as part of planned, prioritized work.

text: A project manager is reviewing the risk register and finds several risks with high probability and high impact that have no assigned risk owner. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Remove the risks from the register since they lack an owner
options.B: Assign all risks to a single team member regardless of expertise to simplify tracking
options.C: Leave the risks unowned since the project manager is ultimately responsible for all risks
options.D: Assign appropriate risk owners with the authority and expertise to manage each specific risk, and confirm their responsibilities

justification: Correct. Assigning risk owners with the appropriate authority and expertise ensures each significant risk has accountable, capable management, which is a core risk management best practice.

text: A project leader notices that during virtual meetings, a few vocal team members dominate discussion while others rarely speak, even when directly invited to contribute. What technique would BEST improve balanced participation?

options.A: Only rely on the most vocal members' input since they are clearly more engaged
options.B: Require every meeting to be conducted via written chat only
options.C: Continue the current format and hope participation improves naturally over time
options.D: Use structured facilitation techniques such as round-robin input, anonymous polling, or breakout discussions to ensure all voices are heard

justification: Correct. Structured facilitation techniques like round-robin input, anonymous tools, or smaller breakout groups actively create space for quieter members to contribute, improving balanced participation.

text: Which of the following are characteristics of a well-written user story? (Select TWO)

options.A: It is independent and can be prioritized or developed with minimal dependency on other stories
options.B: It includes clear, testable acceptance criteria
options.C: It specifies the exact database schema to be used
options.D: It is written exclusively in technical implementation language for developers only

justification: Correct. Independence (as in the INVEST criteria) is a key characteristic of a well-written user story, minimizing dependencies that complicate prioritization and delivery. / Correct. Clear, testable acceptance criteria ensure the team and Product Owner share a common understanding of what 'done' means for that story.

text: A project manager learns that a competitor has just announced a similar product with a faster time-to-market, which threatens the strategic rationale of the current predictive project. What is the BEST course of action?

options.A: Communicate the competitive development to the sponsor and stakeholders, and reassess whether the business case, scope, or schedule needs adjustment
options.B: Continue the project exactly as planned since the business case was already approved
options.C: Ignore the competitive information since it is outside the project manager's control
options.D: Independently decide to cancel the project without consulting the sponsor

justification: Correct. Proactively communicating significant business environment changes to the sponsor and reassessing the business case reflects good project governance and strategic alignment practice.

text: Match each power type to its correct description in the context of project leadership.

colonne_droite.texte: Influence derived from specialized knowledge or skill respected by others
Influence derived from the respect and admiration others have for the leader personally
Influence derived from the ability to provide desirable benefits or recognition
Influence derived from a person's formal position or title within the organization

justification: Expert power comes from possessing specialized knowledge or skills that others rely on and respect, independent of formal title. / Referent power arises from personal charisma, respect, or admiration that others hold for the leader, encouraging them to follow willingly. / Reward power stems from the ability to grant desirable outcomes, such as recognition, opportunities, or other benefits. / Legitimate power is based on the formal authority granted by a person's position or title within the organizational hierarchy.

text: A hybrid program manager oversees a predictive-managed facility construction workstream (currently 70% complete, on schedule) and an agile-managed IoT sensor software workstream (currently in Sprint 9 of a planned 14, with velocity trending 10% below forecast). The two workstreams must integrate for a joint go-live in 8 weeks. The program sponsor requests a unified risk assessment for the integrated go-live. What is the BEST approach for the program manager?

options.A: Report only the construction workstream's schedule performance since it is more predictable and quantifiable
options.B: Assume the software workstream will recover its velocity naturally and exclude it from the risk assessment
options.C: Delay the go-live date unilaterally without consulting the sponsor or either workstream lead
options.D: Assess both workstreams using their respective performance data (schedule variance for construction, velocity trend and remaining backlog for software) to identify the actual integration risk and communicate an integrated risk picture with mitigation options

justification: Correct. An integrated risk assessment should use each workstream's appropriate performance data to build an honest, evidence-based picture of overall program risk, then present mitigation options for informed sponsor decision-making — the essence of effective hybrid program management.

text: Which of the following are valid techniques for compressing a project schedule? (Select TWO)

options.A: Crashing
options.B: Fast tracking
options.C: Resource smoothing
options.D: Monte Carlo simulation

justification: Correct. Crashing is a schedule compression technique that adds resources to critical path activities to shorten duration, typically at increased cost. / Correct. Fast tracking is a schedule compression technique that overlaps activities that would normally be done in sequence, increasing risk but shortening the schedule.

text: A project manager notices that a highly capable team member has been passed over for a leadership opportunity within the organization twice, and morale is visibly declining. The decision was made outside the project manager's authority. What is the BEST action?

options.A: Avoid discussing the topic to prevent an uncomfortable conversation
options.B: Tell the team member there is nothing that can be done and to accept the outcome
options.C: Promise the team member a promotion the project manager cannot actually guarantee
options.D: Have a supportive conversation to understand their career goals, and where appropriate, advocate for their development or provide visible growth opportunities within the current project

justification: Correct. Supporting the team member's career development within the PM's actual sphere of influence, such as advocacy or visible growth opportunities on the project, demonstrates genuine care for their wellbeing and growth.

text: A team notices that Story Points are being interpreted inconsistently between two sub-teams working on the same product, making combined velocity reporting unreliable. What is the BEST way to resolve this?

options.A: Combine the two sub-teams' velocity numbers directly without any calibration
options.B: Force both sub-teams to use identical time-based hour estimates instead of story points
options.C: Facilitate a joint calibration session using common reference stories so both sub-teams align their relative sizing scale
options.D: Ignore the inconsistency since each sub-team's velocity is self-referential anyway

justification: Correct. A joint calibration session using shared reference stories helps align relative sizing understanding across sub-teams, which is the standard technique to make cross-team velocity comparisons more meaningful.

text: An agile team building a mobile banking app must comply with an evolving set of financial regulations that are updated periodically by a regulatory body. What is the BEST way to manage this ongoing business environment factor?

options.A: Assume regulations will remain static for the life of the product
options.B: Establish a recurring process to monitor regulatory updates and translate relevant changes into prioritized backlog items
options.C: Address regulatory changes only once a year during an annual review
options.D: Delegate regulatory monitoring entirely to the development team with no formal process

justification: Correct. A recurring, structured process to monitor and translate regulatory changes into backlog items ensures the product stays compliant continuously, aligned with agile's iterative and adaptive approach.

text: A project manager is using a Pareto chart to analyze the causes of recent quality defects. The chart shows that three of ten defect categories account for 80% of all reported defects. What should the project manager do with this information?

options.A: Prioritize corrective action efforts on the three defect categories responsible for the majority of defects
options.B: Ignore the chart since all ten categories need equal attention
options.C: Focus corrective efforts on the seven least significant defect categories first
options.D: Discard the defect data since Pareto analysis is not applicable to quality management

justification: Correct. The Pareto principle (80/20 rule) directs the project manager to prioritize the small number of categories responsible for the majority of defects, maximizing the impact of corrective action efforts.

text: An agile team's Product Owner and lead developer have very different working styles: the Product Owner prefers detailed written specifications, while the lead developer prefers verbal, iterative discussions. This mismatch is causing repeated misunderstandings. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to help?

options.A: Have the two communicate only through a third party to avoid direct friction
options.B: Ignore the style mismatch since both are technically fulfilling their roles
options.C: Force the lead developer to adopt the Product Owner's preferred communication style exclusively
options.D: Facilitate a conversation to identify a hybrid communication approach that combines brief written summaries with verbal discussion to leverage both styles

justification: Correct. Finding a hybrid communication approach that respects both working styles addresses the root cause of the miscommunication while leveraging the strengths of each preference.

text: Which of the following are valid data-gathering techniques used during Collect Requirements? (Select TWO)

options.A: Facilitated workshops
options.B: Interviews
options.C: Earned value analysis
options.D: Critical path method

justification: Correct. Facilitated workshops bring stakeholders together to define cross-functional requirements collaboratively, a common technique in the Collect Requirements process. / Correct. Interviews are a direct data-gathering technique used to elicit requirements from stakeholders through structured or unstructured conversations.

text: A manufacturing project's primary raw material is subject to significant price volatility on global commodity markets. The project's cost baseline assumed stable pricing. What is the BEST way for the project manager to manage this business environment risk going forward?

options.A: Ignore the volatility since it is outside the project manager's direct control
options.B: Assume prices will remain stable for the rest of the project without further monitoring
options.C: Establish a contingency reserve for price volatility and set up regular monitoring of commodity price trends to trigger timely response
options.D: Lock in a fixed price contract without evaluating whether this is available or cost-effective

justification: Correct. Establishing a contingency reserve specifically for this known volatility risk, combined with ongoing monitoring, is a proactive, standard risk management response to price uncertainty.

text: A Scrum team member consistently completes their individual tasks early but refuses to help teammates who are behind, citing 'that's not my task.' What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Accept the behavior since the individual is meeting their own task commitments
options.B: Publicly criticize the team member's lack of collaboration during the Daily Scrum
options.C: Formally assign that team member additional tasks without any discussion
options.D: Have a private conversation reinforcing the team's shared accountability for the Sprint Goal and explore what might be preventing collaborative behavior

justification: Correct. A private conversation that reinforces the team's shared accountability for the Sprint Goal (a core Scrum principle) while exploring the reason behind the behavior is the constructive coaching approach.

text: A team's Sprint Backlog includes a technical spike to investigate a new third-party API before committing to a full implementation story. The spike reveals significant integration challenges. What should the team do with this information?

options.A: Discard the spike findings since spikes are not meant to influence planning
options.B: Use the spike findings to inform the Product Owner and re-estimate or re-scope the related backlog items before committing to full implementation
options.C: Proceed with the original implementation plan regardless of the spike findings
options.D: Cancel the entire feature without further discussion

justification: Correct. A spike's entire purpose is to generate knowledge that informs subsequent planning; using its findings to re-estimate or re-scope reflects the correct application of empirical, evidence-based planning.

text: Match each governance concept to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Ensures selected projects and programs align with overall organizational strategy and value
Coordinates related projects to realize benefits not achievable by managing them individually
Provides the framework of decision-making, oversight, and control specific to a single project
The framework linking portfolios, programs, and projects to organizational strategy execution

justification: Portfolio governance ensures the mix of selected initiatives across the organization aligns with and maximizes value toward strategic objectives. / Program governance coordinates related component projects and activities to achieve benefits that would not be realized if managed independently. / Project governance provides the specific framework for decision-making, control, and oversight within an individual project's boundaries. / OPM is the overarching framework that connects portfolio, program, and project management practices to the execution of organizational strategy.

text: A project manager needs to communicate a significant schedule delay to a stakeholder group known for reacting emotionally to bad news. What is the BEST way to prepare for this communication?

options.A: Send a brief, vague email without details to soften the impact
options.B: Delay informing the stakeholders as long as possible to avoid the difficult conversation
options.C: Prepare clear, factual information about the cause, impact, and proposed recovery plan, and choose an appropriate communication method and tone for the audience
options.D: Let a more junior team member deliver the news instead

justification: Correct. Preparing clear, factual information along with a recovery plan, and tailoring the communication method and tone to the audience, reflects effective, proactive stakeholder communication for sensitive situations.

text: A team notices that their Definition of Ready (used to determine if a backlog item is ready for Sprint Planning) is being applied inconsistently, with some items entering the Sprint without full clarity. What is the BEST way to fix this?

options.A: Accept the inconsistency as a normal part of agile flexibility
options.B: Eliminate the Definition of Ready entirely to simplify the process
options.C: Reinforce the Definition of Ready during Backlog Refinement and have the team collectively verify criteria are met before items are pulled into Sprint Planning
options.D: Let the Product Owner alone decide readiness without team input going forward

justification: Correct. Reinforcing the criteria during Backlog Refinement and having the whole team collectively verify readiness ensures consistent application and shared accountability for backlog quality.

text: A predictive project's organization introduces a new mandatory enterprise-wide procurement system mid-project, which requires the project team to change how purchase orders are processed. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Assess the impact of the new organizational process asset on the project's procurement plan and update relevant documents and workflows accordingly
options.B: Continue using the old system without informing the organization
options.C: Halt all procurement activities until the project ends
options.D: Refuse to adopt the new system since the project's procurement plan was already approved

justification: Correct. Assessing the impact of a new organizational process asset and updating relevant plans/workflows accordingly is the appropriate way to integrate a mandated organizational change into ongoing project execution.

text: A Development Team wants to change their Sprint length from two weeks to one week to get faster feedback, but the Product Owner is concerned this will increase overhead from more frequent ceremonies. What is the BEST way to resolve this?

options.A: Avoid changing Sprint length ever, regardless of the reasoning, to maintain consistency
options.B: Discuss the trade-offs together as a team, potentially trial the shorter Sprint length for a defined period, and inspect the results before deciding permanently
options.C: The Product Owner should unilaterally veto any change to Sprint length
options.D: The Development Team should unilaterally change the Sprint length since they own the 'how' of delivery

justification: Correct. Empirically trialing the change for a defined period and then inspecting the actual results before deciding permanently reflects the empirical, inspect-and-adapt principle central to Scrum.

text: A team member frequently apologizes excessively for minor mistakes and appears anxious about making errors during Sprint execution. What is the BEST way for the project leader to support this individual?

options.A: Tell the team member to simply stop apologizing without further discussion
options.B: Reduce the team member's task complexity permanently to prevent future mistakes
options.C: Ignore the behavior since it does not affect deliverable quality directly
options.D: Reinforce a psychologically safe, blameless learning environment and have a supportive conversation to understand and address the underlying anxiety

justification: Correct. Reinforcing psychological safety and having a supportive conversation to understand and address the anxiety reflects genuine care for team member wellbeing and helps build a healthier working environment.

text: Which of the following are valid roles or practices found in a Kanban system? (Select TWO)
