options.A: Work-in-progress (WIP) limits
options.B: Explicit workflow policies
options.C: Fixed-length Sprints
options.D: A dedicated Scrum Master role, required by the Kanban method

justification: Correct. WIP limits are a core Kanban practice, limiting the number of items in progress at each workflow stage to improve flow and reduce bottlenecks. / Correct. Explicit workflow policies are a core Kanban principle, making the rules for how work moves through the system clear and visible to everyone.

text: An agile team's organization is piloting a new AI-assisted development tool that could significantly increase coding speed but has not yet been vetted for security or data privacy compliance. What should the team do?

options.A: Let individual developers decide independently whether to use the tool on sensitive work
options.B: Adopt the tool immediately across all backlog items to maximize speed gains
options.C: Avoid ever evaluating new tools to minimize any risk
options.D: Pilot the tool in a limited, low-risk context while security and compliance review is completed before broader adoption

justification: Correct. A limited, low-risk pilot while formal review is completed balances the potential productivity benefit against unassessed compliance risk, a sound risk-informed approach to adopting new technology.

text: Match each leadership style to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Providing specific instructions and closely supervising task completion
Providing direction while also explaining decisions and encouraging input
Facilitating and supporting team members' efforts while sharing decision-making
Turning over responsibility for decisions and problem-solving to the team

justification: A directing style involves close supervision and specific instructions, typically used when team members need significant guidance, such as with new or inexperienced individuals. / A coaching style blends providing direction with explaining the reasoning and inviting input, supporting growing competence and confidence. / A supporting style shifts toward shared decision-making, with the leader facilitating and supporting rather than directing, suited to competent but less confident team members. / A delegating style hands over responsibility for decisions and problem-solving to capable, confident team members, appropriate for high-maturity individuals or teams.

text: A hybrid program includes a predictive-managed regulatory certification workstream (currently blocked, awaiting a third-party audit scheduled 6 weeks out) and an agile-managed product feature workstream that has no blockers and is on track to complete its planned scope in 4 weeks. The program cannot launch until both workstreams are complete. What is the BEST way for the program manager to use the available time?

options.A: Instruct the agile team to work faster to finish earlier, even though they have no blockers to address
options.B: Ignore the mismatch between workstream timelines since the launch date is already fixed regardless
options.C: Pause the agile team's work entirely once their planned scope is done, leaving the 2-week gap idle
options.D: Use the additional 2-week window productively: have the agile team pull additional high-value backlog items or address technical debt, while proactively monitoring the certification workstream for any updates

justification: Correct. Recognizing the regulatory workstream as the binding constraint (critical path) and using the agile team's available capacity productively — for additional value or technical debt reduction — while monitoring the constrained workstream reflects effective, value-maximizing hybrid program management.

text: Which of the following are valid contract types used in project procurement? (Select TWO)

options.A: Firm Fixed Price (FFP)
options.B: Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF)
options.C: Sprint Backlog Agreement
options.D: Definition of Done Contract

justification: Correct. Firm Fixed Price is a standard contract type where the seller agrees to a set price for defined work, placing cost risk primarily on the seller. / Correct. Cost Plus Fixed Fee is a standard cost-reimbursable contract type where the buyer reimburses allowable costs plus a fixed fee, placing more cost risk on the buyer.

text: A project manager finds out that a team member has been secretly working extra unpaid hours at home to keep up with deadlines because they are afraid to admit they are behind. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Praise the team member's dedication and encourage them to continue working extra hours
options.B: Discipline the team member for not reporting their status accurately
options.C: Have a supportive, non-judgmental conversation to understand the underlying workload issue and rebalance tasks or adjust expectations as needed
options.D: Ignore the situation since the work is still getting done

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation to understand the underlying fear and workload imbalance, followed by rebalancing or adjusting expectations, addresses both the wellbeing risk and the root cause of hidden status.

text: A team's Sprint Goal is at risk because an unexpected critical production incident requires immediate developer attention mid-Sprint. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Ignore the production incident to protect the Sprint Goal at all costs
options.B: Silently drop lower-priority Sprint items without informing the Product Owner
options.C: Address the critical incident as a priority, then transparently reassess the Sprint Goal's feasibility with the Product Owner and adjust scope if needed
options.D: Immediately cancel the Sprint regardless of the incident's actual severity

justification: Correct. Prioritizing the critical incident (a legitimate business emergency), then transparently reassessing and adjusting the Sprint scope with the Product Owner, balances urgent needs with Scrum's transparency principle.

text: An agile team supporting a nonprofit's donor management platform must accommodate a sudden influx of new users following a viral social media campaign, straining system performance. What is the BEST way for the product leader to respond?

options.A: Permanently block new user registrations to avoid addressing the performance issue
options.B: Ignore the performance issue since it results from unplanned, external popularity
options.C: Wait until the next quarterly planning session to address the performance strain
options.D: Reprioritize the Product Backlog to elevate performance and scalability items given the shifted urgency from real user impact

justification: Correct. Reprioritizing the backlog to address urgent, real-world performance needs reflects adaptive, value-driven backlog management responding to a genuine shift in business environment/usage conditions.

text: A project manager needs to determine which of several proposed process improvements would have the greatest positive impact on reducing defects. Which quality tool is MOST appropriate for evaluating the relationship between two variables, such as training hours and defect rate?

options.A: Flowchart
options.B: Scatter diagram
options.C: Control chart
options.D: Checksheet

justification: Correct. A scatter diagram plots pairs of data points to show the relationship (correlation) between two variables, such as training hours and defect rate, making it the appropriate tool for this analysis.

text: A team member consistently volunteers to take on impediment-removal tasks that are technically outside their normal role, which is helpful but is starting to distract them from their primary responsibilities. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Praise the behavior without discussing any potential trade-offs
options.B: Take over all impediment-removal duties personally without team input
options.C: Forbid the team member from ever helping with impediments again
options.D: Acknowledge the team member's helpfulness while having a conversation about balancing their primary responsibilities with broader impediment-removal efforts, possibly redistributing some tasks

justification: Correct. Acknowledging positive intent while constructively discussing balance and possibly redistributing impediment-removal efforts reflects thoughtful, supportive facilitation that protects both the individual and team outcomes.

text: Which of the following are examples of active listening techniques a project manager can use in a difficult stakeholder conversation? (Select TWO)

options.A: Paraphrasing what the speaker said to confirm understanding
options.B: Asking open-ended clarifying questions
options.C: Interrupting to correct inaccuracies as soon as they are said
options.D: Planning your response while the other person is still speaking

justification: Correct. Paraphrasing confirms the listener's understanding and shows the speaker they have been heard accurately, a core active listening technique. / Correct. Open-ended clarifying questions encourage the speaker to elaborate and demonstrate genuine engagement with what they are communicating.

text: A project manager overseeing an international infrastructure project must navigate differing labor laws in each country where work is performed. A local subcontractor's labor practices in one country come under public scrutiny during the project. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ignore the scrutiny since it involves the subcontractor, not the project organization directly
options.B: Publicly deny any connection to the subcontractor's practices without investigation
options.C: Investigate the concern, verify compliance with local labor laws and contractual/ethical standards, and take corrective action if warranted
options.D: Terminate the subcontractor's contract immediately without any investigation

justification: Correct. Investigating the concern and verifying compliance reflects responsible project governance and ethical stewardship, ensuring the project (and by extension its subcontractors) upholds appropriate standards.

text: A team's Product Owner frequently praises only the loudest, most visible contributors during Sprint Reviews, unintentionally overlooking quieter team members who did significant work. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Publicly correct the Product Owner during the next Sprint Review
options.B: Privately share the observation with the Product Owner and suggest more structured, inclusive ways to recognize contributions from the whole team
options.C: Instruct quieter team members to advocate loudly for their own recognition
options.D: Say nothing since recognition is the Product Owner's personal choice

justification: Correct. Privately sharing the observation and suggesting more inclusive recognition practices is a constructive coaching approach that helps the Product Owner improve without public embarrassment.

text: A team discovers during Sprint execution that a third-party library they depend on has a newly disclosed critical security vulnerability. What is the BEST immediate action?

options.A: Ignore the vulnerability since it originates from a third-party library, not the team's own code
options.B: Wait for the Sprint Review to discuss the vulnerability with stakeholders
options.C: Continue with planned Sprint work and address the vulnerability in a future Sprint
options.D: Treat it as an urgent priority, informing the Product Owner and adjusting the Sprint scope to patch or mitigate the vulnerability promptly

justification: Correct. A critical security vulnerability warrants urgent prioritization; transparently adjusting Sprint scope with the Product Owner reflects responsible risk management and Scrum's transparency principle.

text: Match each project selection/prioritization method to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Calculates the present value of expected future cash flows minus the initial investment
The discount rate at which the NPV of a project's cash flows equals zero
The time required to recover the initial investment through project cash inflows
Assigns weighted values to multiple criteria to compare and rank competing project options

justification: NPV accounts for the time value of money by discounting future cash flows to present value, then subtracting the initial investment to assess project value. / IRR represents the break-even discount rate for a project's cash flows; a higher IRR relative to the cost of capital generally indicates a more attractive investment. / Payback Period measures how long it takes to recoup the initial investment, though unlike NPV/IRR it does not account for the time value of money. / A weighted scoring model allows decision-makers to compare projects against multiple weighted criteria, useful when purely financial metrics do not capture all relevant strategic factors.

text: A project manager is preparing a performance review for a team member and wants to ensure the feedback is constructive and motivating rather than discouraging. Which approach is MOST effective?

options.A: Focus exclusively on areas needing improvement to drive urgency
options.B: Provide specific, balanced feedback that recognizes strengths and achievements while constructively addressing areas for growth with actionable suggestions
options.C: Keep feedback vague and general to avoid any discomfort
options.D: Compare the team member unfavorably to a higher-performing peer

justification: Correct. Specific, balanced feedback that recognizes strengths while constructively addressing growth areas with actionable suggestions is the most effective and motivating approach to performance feedback.

text: A team is deciding how to handle a large Epic that spans multiple Sprints. What is the BEST practice for managing this within Scrum?

options.A: Assign the entire Epic to one developer to work on in isolation
options.B: Keep the Epic as a single large item in the Sprint Backlog until fully complete
options.C: Break the Epic down into smaller, independently valuable user stories that can be completed and delivered incrementally across Sprints
options.D: Postpone all work on the Epic until it can be fully completed in a single Sprint

justification: Correct. Decomposing large Epics into smaller, independently valuable user stories enables incremental delivery, better estimation accuracy, and earlier feedback, which is standard agile backlog management practice.

text: A project is being executed in a country experiencing political instability, which has led to intermittent government shutdowns affecting permit approvals. What is the BEST way for the project manager to manage this ongoing business environment risk?

options.A: Maintain a contingency plan with buffer time for permit delays, and establish regular monitoring of the political situation to trigger timely response actions
options.B: Proceed with work that requires the delayed permits regardless of legal status
options.C: Cancel the project immediately due to the instability
options.D: Assume the situation will resolve itself and take no proactive action

justification: Correct. Maintaining schedule buffer specifically for this known risk, combined with active monitoring to trigger timely responses, is the appropriate proactive risk management approach for an ongoing external uncertainty.

text: A Scrum team wants to improve their forecasting accuracy for future Sprints. Which combination of data would be MOST useful for this purpose?

options.A: The total number of team meetings held during the project
options.B: The number of email threads related to the project
options.C: The organization's annual revenue figures
options.D: Historical velocity data and trends across multiple recent Sprints

justification: Correct. Historical velocity data and trends across multiple Sprints provide the empirical basis needed to forecast future capacity and refine Sprint planning accuracy.

text: A team member who recently returned from parental leave feels disconnected from decisions made while they were away. What is the BEST way for the project leader to help reintegrate them?

options.A: Provide a structured onboarding-back summary of key decisions and changes, and check in regularly to support their reintegration
options.B: Assume they will naturally catch up within a few days without any special effort
options.C: Expect them to catch up entirely on their own without any support
options.D: Reassign them to a completely different team to avoid the need to catch up

justification: Correct. Providing a structured summary of key changes and regular check-ins reflects supportive, inclusive leadership that helps the returning team member reintegrate effectively and feel valued.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons to split a large user story into smaller stories? (Select TWO)

options.A: To fit the story within a single Sprint's capacity
options.B: To enable earlier delivery of a valuable subset of functionality
options.C: To make the story harder for stakeholders to understand
options.D: To permanently remove the need for acceptance criteria

justification: Correct. Splitting large stories to fit within Sprint capacity ensures the team can realistically commit to and complete the work within a single Sprint. / Correct. Splitting to deliver a valuable subset earlier allows the team to get feedback and realize value sooner, a core benefit of incremental delivery.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring entering a strategic partnership with another company, which could significantly change the product's roadmap depending on the outcome of negotiations. What should the product leader do while negotiations are ongoing?

options.A: Halt all backlog work until the partnership outcome is finalized
options.B: Commit the team publicly to features based on the anticipated partnership before it is finalized
options.C: Continue delivering value on current, stable priorities while staying informed of negotiation progress to adapt the roadmap once the outcome is clearer
options.D: Ignore the potential partnership entirely since it is not yet finalized

justification: Correct. Continuing to deliver against stable, known priorities while staying informed enables the team to adapt quickly once real information is available, balancing progress with appropriate business environment awareness.

text: Match each motivation theory concept to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Suggests people are motivated by fulfilling needs in a progression from basic (physiological) to higher-order (self-actualization)
Distinguishes between hygiene factors that prevent dissatisfaction and motivators that drive true satisfaction
Contrasts an assumption that people dislike work and need control (X) with an assumption that people are self-motivated (Y)
Suggests individuals are primarily driven by needs for achievement, affiliation, or power

justification: This theory proposes that people are motivated to satisfy needs in a hierarchical order, moving from basic survival needs up to self-actualization once lower needs are met. / This theory separates factors that merely prevent dissatisfaction (hygiene factors like pay and conditions) from factors that actively motivate (like recognition and growth). / This theory contrasts two management assumptions about worker motivation: Theory X assumes people need close supervision, while Theory Y assumes people are inherently self-motivated. / This theory suggests individual motivation is driven primarily by one of three needs: achievement, affiliation, or power, which vary by individual.

text: A hybrid program manager is overseeing an agile-managed customer app workstream and a predictive-managed backend infrastructure workstream. The infrastructure workstream just experienced a 3-week delay due to a vendor equipment shortage, pushing its completion beyond the original integration point with the app workstream, which is on track. What is the BEST course of action for the program manager?

options.A: Force the app workstream to also delay by 3 weeks even though they have no direct blocker
options.B: Have the app team use the additional time to pull forward lower-priority backlog items or address technical debt, while working with the infrastructure vendor on recovery options, and communicate the revised integration timeline to stakeholders
options.C: Ignore the delay and proceed with the original integration date regardless of infrastructure readiness
options.D: Cancel the app workstream's remaining Sprints since the infrastructure is delayed

justification: Correct. Using the app team's available time productively while pursuing vendor recovery options and transparently communicating the revised timeline reflects proactive, value-maximizing hybrid program management in response to a workstream-specific delay.

text: Which of the following are examples of emotional intelligence competencies useful for a project manager? (Select TWO)

options.A: Self-awareness of one's own emotional triggers and reactions
options.B: Empathy toward team members' perspectives and feelings
options.C: Strict adherence to procedural rules regardless of context
options.D: Avoiding all emotional discussions in the workplace

justification: Correct. Self-awareness, including understanding one's own emotional triggers and reactions, is a foundational emotional intelligence competency that helps a project manager respond thoughtfully rather than reactively. / Correct. Empathy, the ability to understand and share the feelings of others, is a core emotional intelligence competency that supports effective team leadership and stakeholder engagement.

text: A project manager discovers that a subject matter expert on the team routinely dismisses ideas from less experienced colleagues without consideration. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the behavior since the expert's technical judgment is usually correct
options.B: Privately discuss the impact of this behavior on team contribution and psychological safety, and encourage more inclusive engagement
options.C: Instruct less experienced colleagues to stop sharing ideas to avoid friction
options.D: Remove the expert from group discussions entirely

justification: Correct. A private conversation about the impact on psychological safety and team contribution addresses the root behavioral issue while preserving the expert's valuable input.

text: A team wants to improve the accuracy of their Sprint forecasts. Which practice would MOST directly help achieve this?

options.A: Regularly reviewing past Sprint outcomes against forecasts and refining estimation practices based on those insights
options.B: Increasing the number of stakeholders invited to Sprint Planning
options.C: Removing all estimation from the planning process entirely
options.D: Extending the Sprint length indefinitely until forecasts always succeed

justification: Correct. Reviewing past forecast accuracy against actual outcomes and refining estimation practices accordingly is the empirical, inspect-and-adapt approach that directly improves future forecasting.

text: A project manager learns that a proposed change to a public-facing deliverable might have unintended cultural sensitivities in one of the target markets. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Proceed with the change as planned since the deadline is approaching
options.B: Consult with local subject matter experts or cultural advisors to assess the concern before proceeding
options.C: Make the decision independently without any external input
options.D: Cancel the change entirely without further investigation

justification: Correct. Consulting local subject matter experts or cultural advisors provides the informed perspective needed to properly assess and address the concern before finalizing the change.

text: An agile team member frequently disagrees with decisions made during Sprint Planning but does not voice concerns until after the Sprint has started, then complains about the approach. What is the BEST way to address this pattern?

options.A: Change the Sprint Plan every time this team member complains after the fact
options.B: Exclude the team member from future Sprint Planning sessions
options.C: Have a private conversation encouraging them to voice concerns during Sprint Planning itself, and reinforce that the team values input at the point decisions are made
options.D: Ignore the pattern since complaints do not affect the Sprint outcome directly

justification: Correct. Coaching the team member to voice concerns during the actual decision-making moment addresses the behavioral pattern constructively while reinforcing the value of timely input.

text: A project manager needs to determine the total funding requirements for a project, including management reserves. Which of the following BEST represents this figure?

options.A: The sum of all activity cost estimates before any aggregation
options.B: Only the contingency reserves included in the cost baseline
options.C: The project budget, which equals the cost baseline plus management reserves
options.D: The cost baseline alone

justification: Correct. The project budget is the total funding authorization, calculated as the cost baseline (which includes contingency reserves) plus management reserves for unforeseen work.

text: An agile team's organization begins requiring all vendor contracts to include specific data residency clauses due to new national data sovereignty laws. The team currently uses a cloud hosting vendor that does not meet this requirement. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Continue using the current vendor and address compliance only if legally challenged
options.B: Delegate the entire compliance issue to the legal department with no backlog integration
options.C: Ignore the requirement since changing vendors would be disruptive to the current Sprint cadence
options.D: Add backlog items to evaluate and potentially migrate to a compliant hosting solution, prioritizing this given the legal requirement

justification: Correct. Proactively adding prioritized backlog items to evaluate and migrate to a compliant solution integrates the legal requirement directly into planned, trackable delivery work.

text: Which of the following are appropriate steps in a structured negotiation approach for resolving a resource conflict with a functional manager? (Select TWO)

options.A: Understand the functional manager's constraints and interests before proposing solutions
options.B: Seek a mutually acceptable solution that addresses both parties' underlying needs
options.C: Present only one rigid solution and refuse to consider alternatives
options.D: Avoid any direct communication and rely solely on written memos

justification: Correct. Understanding the other party's constraints and interests is a foundational step in principled negotiation, enabling solutions that address real underlying needs. / Correct. Seeking a mutually acceptable solution reflects an interest-based, collaborative negotiation approach that tends to produce more sustainable outcomes than positional bargaining.

text: A newly-formed agile team is struggling to agree on how to handle disagreements during technical discussions, often resulting in unresolved tension. What is the BEST way for the team to establish healthier norms?

options.A: Wait for the tension to resolve naturally over several months
options.B: Discourage any technical disagreement to maintain surface-level harmony
options.C: Facilitate a session to co-create explicit team working agreements, including how the team will handle disagreements constructively
options.D: Have the project leader unilaterally decide all technical disputes going forward

justification: Correct. Co-creating explicit working agreements, including how to handle disagreements, gives the team a shared, proactive framework for constructive conflict resolution going forward.

text: A Product Owner wants to measure the actual business value delivered by the team, beyond simple output metrics like story points completed. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Define and track outcome-based metrics (e.g., user adoption, revenue impact, customer satisfaction) tied to specific increments delivered
options.B: Count the number of Sprint Reviews held as a proxy for value
options.C: Rely exclusively on velocity as the sole indicator of value delivered
options.D: Avoid measuring value since it is inherently subjective and cannot be tracked

justification: Correct. Defining and tracking outcome-based metrics tied to delivered increments directly measures the actual business value generated, which is distinct from output-focused metrics like velocity.

text: Match each team communication channel to its MOST appropriate use case.

colonne_droite.texte: Discussing a complex, nuanced disagreement that benefits from real-time back-and-forth and visual cues
Sharing routine status information across different time zones without requiring immediate response
Collaboratively designing a complex system architecture
Asking a quick clarifying question that needs a fast but low-stakes answer

justification: Real-time video communication is well suited for nuanced, potentially sensitive discussions where tone, visual cues, and immediate back-and-forth aid understanding and resolution. / Written asynchronous updates work well for routine, non-urgent information shared across time zones, allowing recipients to review on their own schedule. / Visual collaborative tools like whiteboards support complex design discussions where diagramming and iterative visual thinking add significant value. / Instant messaging suits quick, low-stakes questions needing a fast response without the overhead of a scheduled meeting.

text: A project manager wants to communicate overall project health to a diverse group of stakeholders with varying levels of technical understanding. What is the BEST reporting approach?

options.A: Only report status verbally in ad-hoc conversations with no consistent format
options.B: Send the same highly technical, detailed report to all stakeholders regardless of their background
options.C: Tailor the level of detail and visual format of status reports to match each stakeholder group's needs and understanding, using dashboards or summaries where appropriate
options.D: Avoid sending any status reports to prevent overwhelming stakeholders

justification: Correct. Tailoring the level of detail and format to different stakeholder groups' needs, using tools like dashboards for executive audiences, reflects effective, audience-appropriate communication planning.

text: An agile team's organization announces a company-wide hiring freeze due to economic uncertainty, right as the team was planning to add a needed specialist role. What should the product leader do to adapt?

options.A: Continue planning as if the new specialist will be hired on the original timeline
options.B: Reprioritize the backlog to account for the current team's actual capacity, and explore alternative options such as upskilling existing members or targeted contractor support
options.C: Ignore the capacity gap and commit to the same scope as originally planned
options.D: Halt all backlog work until the hiring freeze is lifted

justification: Correct. Reprioritizing the backlog to reflect actual current capacity, while exploring alternative resourcing options, is a pragmatic, adaptive response to a real business environment constraint.

text: A project manager takes over a struggling project mid-execution. The previous project manager had a directive, top-down leadership style, and the team reports feeling disengaged and rarely consulted on decisions. The new project manager wants to rebuild trust and engagement without destabilizing an already fragile team. What is the BEST initial approach?

options.A: Hold individual listening sessions with team members to understand their experience, then gradually introduce more participatory decision-making practices based on what is learned
options.B: Make no changes at all and let the team continue exactly as before
options.C: Immediately reverse all of the previous project manager's decisions to signal a fresh start
options.D: Adopt the same directive leadership style to maintain consistency with what the team is used to

justification: Correct. Listening first to understand the team's actual experience, then gradually introducing more inclusive practices based on those insights, builds trust incrementally without destabilizing shock — a sound approach to leading a team recovering from disengagement.

text: A team's Product Backlog contains several items that have not been touched or refined in over a year. What is the BEST practice for managing this?

options.A: Delete the entire Product Backlog and start over from scratch
options.B: Keep all items exactly as they are indefinitely, regardless of relevance
options.C: Periodically review and either refine, deprioritize, or remove stale items to keep the backlog relevant and manageable
options.D: Automatically move all stale items to the top of the backlog for immediate attention

justification: Correct. Periodically reviewing and refining, deprioritizing, or removing stale items keeps the backlog a healthy, actionable, and relevant tool for planning, which is standard backlog management practice.

text: Which of the following are examples of internal Enterprise Environmental Factors that can affect how a project is executed? (Select TWO)

options.A: The organization's existing infrastructure and facilities
options.B: The organization's risk tolerance and appetite
options.C: Global currency exchange rate fluctuations
options.D: A competitor's newly released product

justification: Correct. The organization's existing infrastructure and facilities are internal EEFs that directly influence how the project can be executed, such as available equipment, space, or systems. / Correct. The organization's risk tolerance and appetite is an internal EEF shaping how the project team approaches risk identification, analysis, and response decisions.

text: A team member proposes an innovative but unconventional technical solution during a Sprint Planning session. A few team members immediately dismiss it as 'too risky' without much discussion. What is the BEST way for the project leader to facilitate this moment?

options.A: Side with the majority immediately and drop the idea
options.B: Encourage the team to explore the idea's potential benefits and risks together before deciding, ensuring the proposer feels heard
options.C: Approve the idea unilaterally without team discussion since innovation should be encouraged
options.D: Move on to the next topic without addressing the dismissal

justification: Correct. Facilitating a balanced exploration of benefits and risks ensures the idea receives fair consideration while maintaining psychological safety for the person who proposed it.

text: A project's Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is being developed, and the team is debating how granular the work packages should be. What is the BEST guideline for determining appropriate work package size?

options.A: Work package size does not matter as long as the total scope is captured somewhere
options.B: Work packages should always be broken down to the smallest possible unit of work, regardless of context
options.C: Work packages should be decomposed to a level that allows for reliable estimating, assignment, and control, often guided by practices like the '8/80 rule' as a general reference
options.D: Work packages should never be smaller than one month of effort

justification: Correct. Work packages should be sized to enable reliable estimating, assignment, and control; general heuristics like the 8/80 rule (between 8 and 80 hours of effort) are often used as practical guides, tailored to the specific project.

text: A public sector agile initiative must operate within strict annual budget cycles set by government appropriations, which conflicts with the team's desire for continuous, ongoing funding of the Product Backlog. What is the BEST way to reconcile this?

options.A: Plan release-level roadmaps and budget requests aligned to the appropriations cycle, using rolling wave planning to accommodate agile delivery within that funding structure
options.B: Request an exception to bypass all government funding rules
options.C: Abandon agile practices entirely in favor of a rigid annual planning approach
options.D: Ignore the appropriations cycle and request funding whenever needed throughout the year

justification: Correct. Aligning release-level roadmaps and funding requests to the appropriations cycle, while still using rolling wave and agile delivery practices within that structure, respects the funding constraint without abandoning agile benefits.

text: A project manager needs to select a team lead for a critical sub-team from among several qualified candidates. One candidate has slightly less experience but demonstrates significantly stronger collaborative and communication skills. What should the project manager MOST heavily weigh in this decision, given the sub-team's history of communication breakdowns?

options.A: The specific leadership and communication skills most needed to address the sub-team's known challenges
options.B: Years of technical experience alone
options.C: Seniority within the organization
options.D: Whichever candidate has the strongest personal relationship with the project manager

justification: Correct. Given the sub-team's documented history of communication issues, prioritizing the candidate whose strengths most directly address that specific challenge is the most contextually appropriate selection criterion.

text: A Scrum Master notices that the team's Daily Scrum has devolved into a status report directed at the Scrum Master rather than a peer-to-peer coordination discussion among Developers. What is the BEST way to correct this?

options.A: Continue attending and receiving updates as the central point of contact
options.B: Cancel the Daily Scrum entirely since it is not functioning as intended
options.C: Coach the team on the purpose of the Daily Scrum as a peer coordination event for the Developers, and consider stepping back to let the team self-facilitate
options.D: Formally document each team member's report and forward it to management

justification: Correct. Coaching the team on the true purpose of the Daily Scrum, and stepping back to encourage self-facilitation, addresses the root cause and helps the team return to genuine peer coordination.

text: Which of the following behaviors reflect servant leadership as commonly applied in agile environments? (Select TWO)

options.A: Prioritizing the growth and wellbeing of team members alongside project outcomes
options.B: Removing organizational impediments that block the team's progress
options.C: Making all technical and process decisions on behalf of the team
options.D: Withholding information from the team to maintain control

justification: Correct. Servant leadership emphasizes putting the needs and growth of team members first, alongside achieving project goals, distinguishing it from purely authority-driven leadership models. / Correct. Actively removing impediments that block team progress is a core servant-leadership responsibility, enabling the team to focus on delivering value.

text: During a quality inspection, the project manager finds that a deliverable meets all documented specifications but the client is still dissatisfied with the outcome. What does this MOST likely indicate?

options.A: The client's dissatisfaction is unfounded and should be disregarded since specifications were met
options.B: There may have been a gap between the documented requirements and the client's actual expectations, indicating a need to revisit requirements elicitation and validation processes
options.C: The deliverable should be redone entirely without further discussion
options.D: The quality management process failed entirely

justification: Correct. Meeting specifications but still causing dissatisfaction typically points to a gap between what was documented and what the client actually needed or expected, highlighting a requirements elicitation/validation issue to investigate.

text: A project manager is informed that a major shareholder of the sponsoring organization strongly opposes the current project direction, though they hold no formal governance authority over it. What is the BEST way to manage this stakeholder?

options.A: Refuse to communicate with the shareholder under any circumstances
options.B: Ignore the shareholder since they lack formal authority over the project
options.C: Assess their level of influence and interest, and engage appropriately to understand their concerns even though they lack formal authority
options.D: Immediately change project direction based solely on this shareholder's opposition

justification: Correct. Assessing influence and interest (per stakeholder analysis techniques) and engaging appropriately, even with informal stakeholders, reflects proper stakeholder management regardless of formal governance authority.

text: A cross-functional agile team includes a designer who often feels excluded from technical planning discussions, despite their work being critical to the product. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Tell the designer that technical discussions are only relevant to developers
options.B: Assume the designer will speak up on their own if they have relevant input
options.C: Create a separate design-only process entirely disconnected from the rest of the team's planning
options.D: Ensure the designer is actively included in relevant planning discussions and that their perspective is explicitly invited and valued

justification: Correct. Actively including the designer and explicitly inviting their perspective ensures the cross-functional team benefits from all relevant expertise and reinforces inclusive collaboration.

text: Match each Scrum artifact to its correct commitment.

colonne_droite.texte: Product Goal
Sprint Goal
Definition of Done

justification: The Product Backlog's commitment is the Product Goal, which describes the future state of the product that serves as a long-term objective for the Scrum Team's planning. / The Sprint Backlog's commitment is the Sprint Goal, the single objective for the Sprint that provides coherence and focus to the selected Product Backlog items. / The Increment's commitment is the Definition of Done, the formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product.

text: A project's sponsor organization undergoes a leadership change, and the new executive has a notably different risk tolerance than the previous leadership, preferring much more conservative approaches. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Continue with the existing risk management approach without any changes
options.B: Ignore leadership's risk tolerance since it was not part of the original project charter
options.C: Review the project's current risk responses and reserves with the new executive to ensure alignment with their risk tolerance, adjusting as needed
options.D: Unilaterally increase all contingency reserves without confirming this is what the new leadership wants

justification: Correct. Reviewing current risk responses and reserves with new leadership to confirm alignment with their stated risk tolerance reflects proper stakeholder engagement and adaptive risk governance.

text: A project manager is assembling a project team and must decide between two equally qualified candidates: one who has worked with the PM before and one who is unfamiliar but has a strong track record elsewhere. What should be the PRIMARY consideration in this decision?

options.A: Choose the unfamiliar candidate solely because a fresh perspective is always preferable
options.B: Flip a coin since both are equally qualified
options.C: Objectively assess both candidates' skills, fit for the specific role requirements, and availability, avoiding bias toward familiarity alone
options.D: Automatically choose the familiar candidate to reduce onboarding effort

justification: Correct. Objectively assessing both candidates against the specific role requirements, avoiding undue bias toward mere familiarity, reflects fair and effective team resourcing practice.

text: Which of the following are appropriate uses of a Sprint Backlog? (Select TWO)

options.A: Providing a real-time picture of the work the Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint to meet the Sprint Goal
options.B: Allowing the Developers to adapt their plan throughout the Sprint as they learn more
options.C: Serving as the sole source of truth for the organization's annual budget
options.D: Replacing the need for a Sprint Goal entirely

justification: Correct. The Sprint Backlog provides a real-time, highly visible picture of the work Developers plan to accomplish during the Sprint to achieve the Sprint Goal. / Correct. The Sprint Backlog is a living plan that Developers update throughout the Sprint as they learn more, reflecting an accurate current picture of remaining work.

text: A project manager overseeing a cross-border infrastructure project must coordinate approvals from two different national regulatory bodies with conflicting requirements. What is the BEST way to manage this business environment complexity?

options.A: Proceed with the project and address regulatory conflicts only if formally challenged
options.B: Choose to comply with only the requirements of the country where the project office is located
options.C: Engage legal/regulatory experts from both jurisdictions to identify overlapping and conflicting requirements, and develop a compliance approach that satisfies both where possible
options.D: Cancel the cross-border aspect of the project entirely to avoid regulatory complexity

justification: Correct. Engaging jurisdiction-specific legal/regulatory experts to map overlapping and conflicting requirements and design a satisfying compliance approach is the proper way to manage complex, multi-jurisdictional regulatory environments.

text: A project manager's organization decides to sunset a legacy system that the current project depends on for data integration, with only three months' notice. What should the project manager do FIRST?

options.A: Immediately halt the project entirely due to the dependency issue
options.B: Assess the impact on the project's scope, schedule, and technical approach, and develop a plan to address the dependency before the sunset date
options.C: Continue relying on the legacy system until it is fully shut down
options.D: Ignore the sunset announcement since it is an organizational IT decision unrelated to the project

justification: Correct. Promptly assessing the impact on scope, schedule, and technical approach, and developing a transition plan before the sunset date, is the appropriate proactive response to this organizational change.

text: A project manager reviews the quality management plan and notices that acceptance criteria for a key deliverable are ambiguous, potentially leading to disputes with the client later. What is the BEST time and action to address this?

options.A: Assign the responsibility of defining acceptance criteria solely to the delivery team without client involvement
options.B: Proactively clarify and formally document specific, measurable acceptance criteria with the client as early as possible
options.C: Wait until the deliverable is submitted and hope no dispute arises
options.D: Leave the criteria ambiguous to allow flexibility in interpretation later

justification: Correct. Proactively clarifying and formally documenting specific, measurable acceptance criteria with the client as early as possible prevents ambiguity-driven disputes and ensures shared understanding.

text: A project manager observes that team meetings have become unproductive, with discussions frequently veering off-topic and running significantly over time. What is the BEST way to improve meeting effectiveness?

options.A: Cancel all team meetings permanently
options.B: Let meetings continue as-is since team input is always valuable regardless of format
options.C: Establish clear agendas, defined objectives, and time limits for each meeting, and actively facilitate to keep discussions on track
options.D: Reduce meeting frequency without addressing the actual structure or facilitation issues

justification: Correct. Establishing clear agendas, objectives, and time limits, combined with active facilitation, directly addresses the root causes of unproductive, off-topic, over-running meetings.

text: A team notices their Increment quality has been declining slightly over the past few Sprints, though it still technically meets the Definition of Done. What is the BEST proactive step?

options.A: Lower the Definition of Done to match the current declining quality level
options.B: Wait for a major quality failure before taking any action
options.C: Take no action since the Definition of Done is still technically being met
options.D: Use the Retrospective to investigate the trend and consider strengthening the Definition of Done or addressing process gaps that may be allowing quality to slip

justification: Correct. Using the Retrospective to investigate a subtle quality trend and considering strengthening standards or fixing process gaps reflects proactive, continuous-improvement-oriented quality management.

text: Which of the following are typical responsibilities of a Project Management Office (PMO) within an organization? (Select TWO)

options.A: Establishing organizational project management standards, methodologies, and templates
options.B: Supporting governance and providing oversight across multiple projects
options.C: Personally executing all technical deliverables for every project
options.D: Setting individual employee salaries across the entire organization

justification: Correct. Establishing standardized methodologies, templates, and best practices across the organization is a core PMO function that promotes consistency and efficiency. / Correct. Providing governance support and oversight across multiple projects, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy, is a typical PMO responsibility.

text: A team's Scrum Master is leaving the organization, and the team is anxious about the transition. What is the BEST way to ensure a smooth handover?

options.A: Assign the Product Owner to permanently take over Scrum Master duties without any transition planning
options.B: Facilitate a structured knowledge transfer, including documenting team norms, known impediments, and coaching insights, and involve the team in selecting or preparing an interim facilitator if needed
options.C: Have the outgoing Scrum Master simply hand over their laptop with no further discussion
options.D: Leave the team without a Scrum Master until a replacement is eventually found, however long that takes

justification: Correct. A structured knowledge transfer covering team norms, known impediments, and coaching context, combined with team involvement in the transition, ensures continuity and reduces disruption during the change.

text: A project manager wants to formally document lessons learned throughout the project rather than only at closure. What is the BEST reason to do this?

options.A: It guarantees the project will not experience any further issues
options.B: It replaces the need for a risk register
options.C: Continuous lessons learned capture allows insights to be applied to the current project while still relevant, rather than only benefiting future projects
options.D: It eliminates the need for a formal project closure process

justification: Correct. Capturing lessons learned continuously throughout the project, rather than only at closure, allows the current project team to apply insights and improvements while they are still relevant and actionable, not just future projects.

text: A team member consistently arrives late to the Daily Scrum, causing the team to either wait or start without full attendance. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Have a private conversation with the team member to understand the cause of the lateness and collaboratively agree on a solution
options.B: Cancel the Daily Scrum permanently to avoid the recurring issue
options.C: Change the Daily Scrum time without informing anyone to see if the team member adjusts on their own
options.D: Publicly shame the team member for their lateness during the event itself

justification: Correct. A private conversation to understand the root cause of the lateness and collaboratively agree on a solution is the constructive, respectful approach to resolving an individual behavior pattern.

text: An agile team's organization is preparing for an external audit related to ISO certification, which requires demonstrable evidence of process consistency across all Scrum Teams. What is the BEST way for the organization to prepare without undermining agile flexibility?

options.A: Force all teams to follow an identical, rigid process with zero variation to simplify the audit
options.B: Create entirely new documentation from scratch shortly before the audit that does not reflect actual practices
options.C: Ensure each team consistently maintains their existing agile artifacts (Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Definition of Done) as living evidence of process discipline, supplemented by light process documentation of team-specific tailoring
options.D: Refuse to participate in the audit since agile teams do not require formal process documentation

justification: Correct. Using existing agile artifacts as genuine, ongoing evidence of process discipline, supplemented by light documentation of any team-specific tailoring, satisfies audit evidence needs without imposing unnecessary rigidity.

text: A project manager notices that two departments contributing resources to the project have a long-standing rivalry that predates the project, occasionally surfacing as passive-aggressive comments in meetings. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the comments since they have not yet caused a formal conflict
options.B: Publicly reprimand both departments during a team meeting
options.C: Assign each department to entirely separate work streams with no interaction
options.D: Proactively establish clear team ground rules around respectful communication and address specific incidents privately as they occur

justification: Correct. Proactively establishing ground rules and addressing specific incidents privately as they arise is a preventive, constructive approach to managing an underlying interpersonal tension before it escalates.

text: A Product Owner asks the Development Team to estimate a set of Product Backlog Items using hours instead of story points, believing it will be more accurate. What is the BEST way for the team to respond?

options.A: Use both hours and story points for every item permanently to avoid the conversation
options.B: Comply immediately without discussing trade-offs
options.C: Explain the benefits of relative sizing (like story points) for forecasting and offer to discuss the Product Owner's underlying concern about accuracy
options.D: Refuse outright without any explanation

justification: Correct. Explaining the benefits of relative sizing and exploring the actual concern behind the request reflects collaborative, informed engagement rather than blind compliance or refusal.

text: An agile team's organization begins offering a subscription-based revenue model in addition to their existing one-time purchase model, requiring significant backlog reprioritization. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Wait until the next fiscal year to make any backlog changes
options.B: Continue with the existing backlog priorities unchanged
options.C: Reassess the Product Backlog against the new business model's requirements and reprioritize items that support the subscription transition
options.D: Immediately discard the entire existing backlog and start from scratch

justification: Correct. Reassessing and reprioritizing the backlog in light of the new business model reflects responsive, value-driven backlog management aligned with the organization's evolving strategy.

text: A project manager needs to determine whether a schedule variance of -5 days is significant enough to warrant corrective action. What is the BEST way to make this determination?

options.A: Compare the variance against pre-established control thresholds defined in the project management plan to determine if it exceeds acceptable limits
options.B: Wait until the project is complete to evaluate whether the variance mattered
options.C: Take corrective action for any variance, regardless of magnitude
options.D: Ignore all schedule variances since they are expected on every project

justification: Correct. Comparing the variance against pre-established control thresholds defined in the project management plan is the standard, objective way to determine whether corrective action is warranted.

text: A Scrum team's newest member has strong technical skills but struggles to understand the team's established shorthand and inside references during discussions, leading to confusion. What is the BEST way to help this person integrate?

options.A: Ask the team to stop using any shorthand or informal references permanently
options.B: Pair the new member with a team buddy and encourage the team to explain context and terminology as it comes up, being mindful of the newcomer's onboarding needs
options.C: Expect the new member to figure out the team's communication patterns entirely on their own
options.D: Delay including the new member in discussions until they have independently learned the team's history

justification: Correct. Pairing with a buddy and encouraging the team to explain context as it arises is a practical, supportive onboarding approach that helps the new member integrate without disrupting normal team communication.

text: Which of the following are common causes of an inaccurate Sprint forecast? (Select TWO)

options.A: Insufficiently refined Product Backlog Items with unclear scope
options.B: Frequent unplanned interruptions during the Sprint
options.C: A well-maintained, prioritized Product Backlog
options.D: Consistent team composition across Sprints

justification: Correct. Items pulled into a Sprint without sufficient refinement often carry hidden complexity that was not accounted for during estimation, causing forecast inaccuracy. / Correct. Frequent unplanned interruptions consume capacity that was not accounted for in the original forecast, directly reducing forecast accuracy.

text: A project manager discovers that a proposed deliverable design may inadvertently infringe on a competitor's patent. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Escalate the concern to legal/intellectual property experts for formal review before proceeding further with that design
options.B: Ignore the concern since it was only a preliminary observation
options.C: Modify the design without consulting anyone to avoid delay
options.D: Proceed with the current design since patent issues are outside the project manager's responsibility

justification: Correct. Escalating to legal/intellectual property experts for a formal review before proceeding is the appropriate way to manage a significant, specialized legal risk.

text: During a Sprint Retrospective, a normally quiet team member unexpectedly raises a significant concern about the team's technical debt, sparking a heated discussion. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to facilitate this moment?

options.A: Quickly move on to the next topic to avoid extending the meeting
options.B: Allow space for the discussion, ensure it stays constructive and focused on actionable outcomes, and adjust the agenda if needed to fully explore the concern
options.C: Ask the team member to raise the topic again at a later, unspecified time
options.D: Dismiss the concern since it was not on the original agenda

justification: Correct. Allowing space for the discussion while keeping it constructive and adjusting the agenda reflects skilled, adaptive facilitation that values emergent, important team input.

text: A project manager is developing a Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RACI chart) and finds that a critical activity has three people marked as 'Accountable.' What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Leave it as is since more accountable people means better oversight
options.B: Remove all 'Accountable' designations from the chart
options.C: Revise the RACI chart to designate a single accountable person for that activity, since accountability should not be shared among multiple people
options.D: Assign accountability randomly among the three people

justification: Correct. Best practice for RACI charts is to designate a single accountable person per activity to ensure clear ownership and avoid diffusion of responsibility, while multiple people can still be Responsible.

text: A team member frequently takes personal credit during stakeholder demos for work that was actually a collaborative team effort. Other team members have expressed frustration about this privately to the Scrum Master. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Tell the frustrated team members to address it themselves without any support
options.B: Publicly call out the individual during the next Sprint Review in front of stakeholders
options.C: Ignore the private complaints since they were not raised in a formal setting
options.D: Have a direct, private conversation with the individual about the impact of their behavior on team trust, while also reinforcing collective ownership norms with the whole team

justification: Correct. A direct private conversation addressing the specific behavior and its impact, combined with reinforcing collective ownership norms for the whole team, addresses both the individual issue and the broader team culture constructively.

text: A team wants to reduce the amount of time spent in Backlog Refinement sessions while still keeping items well-prepared for Sprint Planning. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Eliminate Backlog Refinement sessions entirely
options.B: Skip acceptance criteria definition to save time
options.C: Refine items more incrementally throughout the Sprint in smaller, more frequent sessions or asynchronously, rather than in one large session
options.D: Have only the Product Owner refine items alone without team input

justification: Correct. Spreading refinement across smaller, more frequent sessions (or asynchronous methods) can improve efficiency while still ensuring items are well-prepared, addressing the time concern without sacrificing quality.

text: Match each type of organizational process asset to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: A standardized change control procedure used across all projects
A repository of completed project lessons learned
Established cost estimating templates and historical cost databases
A corporate policy defining required approval levels for procurement contracts

justification: Standardized procedures like change control processes are process-related organizational process assets, providing consistent methods across projects. / Repositories such as lessons learned databases are knowledge-related assets that capture organizational learning for reuse on future projects. / Cost estimating templates and historical cost databases are financial organizational process assets supporting more accurate future estimating. / Formal policies, such as required procurement approval levels, are policy-related organizational process assets that govern how projects must operate within the organization.

text: A project manager is leading a team through a particularly stressful phase near a critical deadline. Several team members appear fatigued and less collaborative than usual. What is the BEST way to support the team through this period?

options.A: Push the team harder to meet the deadline regardless of fatigue signs
options.B: Acknowledge the team's effort, check in on wellbeing, and look for ways to relieve unnecessary pressure while maintaining focus on the critical path
options.C: Ignore the fatigue signs since deadlines take priority over team wellbeing
options.D: Extend working hours further to compensate for reduced collaboration

justification: Correct. Acknowledging effort, checking in on wellbeing, and finding ways to relieve unnecessary pressure while still respecting critical deadlines reflects supportive, sustainable leadership during high-pressure periods.

text: A project manager needs to decide whether to use analogous estimating or parametric estimating for a new activity. The team has limited detailed information but access to a reliable statistical relationship between size and cost from similar past projects. Which technique is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Three-point estimating, regardless of data availability
options.B: Parametric estimating, since a reliable statistical relationship is available
options.C: Bottom-up estimating, regardless of data availability
options.D: Analogous estimating, since detailed information is limited

justification: Correct. Parametric estimating uses a statistical relationship between variables (like size and cost) to calculate an estimate, making it the most appropriate technique when such reliable data exists.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring international expansion, requiring the product to support multiple languages and currencies. This was not part of the original product vision. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Update the Product Goal and backlog to incorporate internationalization requirements, prioritizing them based on the expansion timeline and value
options.B: Reject the internationalization requirement since it was not part of the original vision
options.C: Implement internationalization without any prioritization, ahead of all other planned work regardless of urgency
options.D: Wait for the expansion to be fully finalized before considering any product changes

justification: Correct. Updating the Product Goal and backlog to reflect the new strategic direction, with appropriate value-based prioritization, is the standard way to incorporate significant business environment changes into agile planning.

text: A team's Increment includes a feature that technically works but has a confusing user interface that testers found difficult to navigate during the Sprint Review. The Product Owner still wants to mark it as accepted since it meets the written acceptance criteria. What should the team do?

options.A: Accept the Product Owner's decision without further discussion since they have final authority
options.B: Silently note the concern internally without raising it to the Product Owner
options.C: Refuse to release the feature under any circumstances
options.D: Raise the usability concern with supporting evidence and discuss whether the acceptance criteria adequately captured the actual user experience needs, potentially adjusting them going forward

justification: Correct. Raising the concern with evidence and discussing whether acceptance criteria fully captured user experience needs reflects transparent, collaborative quality advocacy, respecting the Product Owner's ultimate decision while ensuring they have full information.

text: Which of the following are typically included in a project's Scope Baseline? (Select TWO)

options.A: The Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
options.B: The scope statement
options.C: The stakeholder engagement plan
options.D: The resource calendar

justification: Correct. The Work Breakdown Structure is one of the three components of the Scope Baseline, decomposing the project's total scope into manageable work packages. / Correct. The project scope statement, describing the deliverables, boundaries, and acceptance criteria, is another core component of the Scope Baseline.

text: A project manager's organization introduces a new environmental sustainability policy requiring all projects to report their carbon footprint. The current project has no established process for tracking this. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ignore the policy since the project charter did not originally include this requirement
options.B: Estimate carbon footprint figures without any actual data collection to save time
options.C: Work with relevant experts to establish a tracking approach and integrate carbon footprint reporting into the project's monitoring processes
options.D: Delay reporting until the project is fully complete regardless of the policy's stated cadence

justification: Correct. Working with relevant experts to establish a proper tracking approach and integrating it into ongoing monitoring reflects responsible integration of a new organizational compliance requirement.

text: A project leader notices that one team consistently outperforms a similarly-resourced sister team working on comparable work, and sister team members are starting to feel demoralized by comparisons made by upper management. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Address the demoralization by focusing on the sister team's own improvement journey, understanding their specific context, and advocating against unhelpful cross-team comparisons
options.B: Publicly compare the two teams' metrics to motivate the underperforming team
options.C: Ignore the demoralization since performance differences are a normal part of any organization
options.D: Merge the two teams to eliminate the comparison entirely

justification: Correct. Focusing on the sister team's own improvement trajectory, understanding their specific context, and advocating against unhelpful external comparisons protects team morale while still supporting genuine performance improvement.

text: A team using Scrum wants to better understand which types of Product Backlog Items tend to take longer than estimated. What is the BEST way to gain this insight?

options.A: Ask team members to guess which item types take longer without reviewing any actual data
options.B: Avoid this kind of analysis since agile teams should not track historical performance data
options.C: Analyze the team's own historical cycle time and estimation accuracy data, segmented by item type or complexity category
options.D: Rely on general industry benchmarks without analyzing the team's own historical data

justification: Correct. Analyzing the team's own historical cycle time and estimation accuracy, segmented by item type, provides the empirical, context-specific insight needed to improve future estimation and planning.

text: A project manager learns that a team member feels overwhelmed by the number of tools and systems they must use daily (email, project software, chat, spreadsheets) and is starting to miss updates. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Tell the team member to simply be more organized
options.B: Add another tool to help them track the other tools
options.C: Review the team's toolset with them, identify opportunities to consolidate or simplify workflows, and provide any needed training or support
options.D: Reassign all of their communication responsibilities to someone else

justification: Correct. Reviewing the toolset together, simplifying where possible, and providing training addresses the root cause of the overwhelm rather than blaming the individual.

text: A team's Sprint Review consistently attracts only internal stakeholders, with actual end users rarely attending to provide feedback. What is the BEST way to improve the quality of feedback received?

options.A: Assume internal stakeholders can accurately represent end user needs without direct end user input
options.B: Cancel the Sprint Review since useful feedback is not being obtained
options.C: Continue with internal stakeholders only, since their feedback is sufficient
options.D: Actively invite representative end users or conduct supplementary user feedback sessions to complement the Sprint Review

justification: Correct. Actively involving representative end users, either directly in the Sprint Review or through supplementary sessions, ensures feedback reflects genuine user needs, improving the product's real-world fit.

text: An agile team's organization operates in an industry facing increasing public scrutiny over environmental impact. The team's product roadmap does not currently address sustainability features that competitors have started offering. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Research market and stakeholder expectations around sustainability and consider adding relevant backlog items if they align with genuine business value and user needs
options.B: Wait until customers explicitly demand these features before considering any action
options.C: Add sustainability features immediately without any research to keep pace with competitors
options.D: Ignore the trend since sustainability is not a core technical requirement

justification: Correct. Researching actual market and stakeholder expectations before adding backlog items ensures any resulting features genuinely align with real business value and user needs, rather than being a reactive, unfounded addition.

text: A team notices that items pulled into recent Sprints often have hidden dependencies on another team's work that were not identified during Backlog Refinement. What is the BEST way to prevent this going forward?

options.A: Ignore dependencies since they are unavoidable in complex products
options.B: Stop working with any items that could possibly have dependencies
options.C: Strengthen the Backlog Refinement process to explicitly identify and flag cross-team dependencies before items are considered ready for Sprint Planning
options.D: Assign a single person to unilaterally identify all dependencies without team input

justification: Correct. Explicitly checking for cross-team dependencies during Backlog Refinement, before items are marked ready, directly addresses the root cause of the recurring surprise dependencies.

text: A team member consistently takes on too much work each Sprint, leading to repeated overcommitment and unfinished items. When asked why, they say they don't want to seem unhelpful. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Force the team member to take on even more work to build resilience
options.B: Publicly point out their pattern of overcommitment in front of the team
options.C: Have a supportive conversation about sustainable pace and realistic self-assessment of capacity, and reinforce that saying no to excess is healthy and expected
options.D: Take over their task selection permanently to prevent overcommitment

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation about sustainable pace and healthy capacity self-assessment addresses the root motivation (fear of seeming unhelpful) while reinforcing a healthy team norm.

text: Which of the following are valid techniques for validating that project deliverables meet requirements before formal client acceptance? (Select TWO)

options.A: Inspection
options.B: Walkthrough
options.C: Resource leveling
options.D: Critical chain scheduling

justification: Correct. Inspection involves examining a deliverable to determine whether it conforms to documented standards, a standard technique in the Validate Scope process. / Correct. A walkthrough is a structured review technique used to examine a deliverable with stakeholders to confirm it meets requirements before formal acceptance.

text: A project manager's organization faces a sudden currency devaluation in the country where a major project is based, significantly increasing the cost of imported materials in local currency terms. What is the BEST immediate response?

options.A: Reassess the cost baseline impact, update forecasts, and communicate the financial exposure and response options to the sponsor promptly
options.B: Absorb the cost increase silently to avoid alarming the sponsor
options.C: Continue the project without any cost reassessment
options.D: Cancel all remaining procurement activities immediately without analysis

justification: Correct. Promptly reassessing the cost impact, updating forecasts, and transparently communicating options to the sponsor reflects proactive financial risk management in response to a materialized external economic risk.

text: A Scrum Master notices that during team conflicts, the same two people always end up leading the resolution discussion, while others passively wait for a decision. What is the BEST way to build broader conflict-resolution capability across the team?

options.A: Coach other team members on conflict resolution techniques and intentionally create opportunities for them to practice facilitating resolution discussions
options.B: Assign the Scrum Master to resolve all future conflicts personally
options.C: Continue relying on the same two people since they are effective at resolving conflicts
options.D: Forbid the two effective team members from participating in future conflict discussions

justification: Correct. Coaching other team members and creating practice opportunities builds broader team capability over time, which is a core servant-leadership goal of developing team maturity.

text: A Product Owner wants to track how much time elapses between when a Product Backlog Item enters the backlog and when it is actually delivered. What is this metric commonly called?

options.A: Lead time
options.B: Defect density
options.C: Sprint burndown
options.D: Velocity

justification: Correct. Lead time measures the total elapsed time from when a work item is requested (enters the backlog) to when it is delivered, which is exactly what the scenario describes.

text: Match each Agile Manifesto value to its correct paired emphasis.

colonne_droite.texte: Valued over processes and tools
Valued over comprehensive documentation
Valued over contract negotiation
Valued over following a plan

justification: The Agile Manifesto emphasizes that effective people and their interactions matter more than rigid adherence to processes and tools, though the latter still have value. / Delivering functioning software is valued more highly than extensive documentation, though documentation still has its place when needed. / Ongoing collaboration with the customer throughout the project is valued more than rigidly negotiating contract terms upfront, though contracts remain useful. / Adapting to change is valued more than rigidly following an original plan, though planning still has value in providing initial direction.

text: A project manager needs to give critical feedback to a team member from a culture where direct criticism is considered highly disrespectful. What is the BEST way to approach this?

options.A: Adapt the delivery approach to be culturally sensitive (e.g., more indirect, private, relationship-focused) while still ensuring the core message is clearly understood
options.B: Ask another team member from the same culture to deliver the feedback instead
options.C: Avoid giving any critical feedback to this team member to prevent cultural discomfort
