options.D: Deliver the feedback exactly as the project manager would to anyone else, regardless of cultural context

justification: Correct. Adapting the delivery style to be culturally sensitive while still ensuring the core message is understood demonstrates cultural awareness balanced with the need for clear, actionable feedback.

text: A team is debating whether to adopt story points or ideal days for estimating Product Backlog Items. What is a KEY advantage of story points over ideal days?

options.A: Story points are required by the official Scrum Guide
options.B: Story points eliminate the need for any Sprint Planning discussion
options.C: Story points are always more accurate than any time-based estimate
options.D: Story points represent relative size/complexity/effort rather than absolute time, making them less susceptible to individual differences in work speed and easier to keep consistent over time

justification: Correct. Story points represent relative size, complexity, and effort rather than a specific time duration, making estimates less affected by individual differences in work speed and generally more stable as a team's estimation reference over time.

text: A project manager's organization is preparing for a merger with another company, and there is significant uncertainty about whether the current project will continue post-merger. Team morale is affected by this uncertainty. What is the BEST way for the project manager to manage this?

options.A: Avoid discussing the merger with the team at all
options.B: Tell the team to start looking for other projects immediately
options.C: Reassure the team the project will definitely continue, even without confirmation
options.D: Be honest about the uncertainty while providing what information is available, and focus the team on delivering value within the current scope of clarity

justification: Correct. Being honest about genuine uncertainty while sharing available information and maintaining focus on current, clear priorities reflects transparent, supportive leadership during ambiguous organizational transitions.

text: A project manager is reviewing a quality control chart and notices seven consecutive data points all falling on one side of the mean, though all points remain within the control limits. What does this pattern suggest?

options.A: The control chart itself is incorrectly configured
options.B: The process is completely out of control and must be halted immediately
options.C: This is a 'rule of seven' pattern indicating the process may be exhibiting a non-random trend that warrants investigation, even though points are within control limits
options.D: This pattern is meaningless since all points are within control limits

justification: Correct. The 'rule of seven' is a recognized quality control heuristic; seven consecutive points on one side of the mean suggests a non-random pattern that should be investigated even though all points remain within statistical control limits.

text: A team member is highly skilled but has recently become noticeably more irritable and short with colleagues during collaborative sessions. Other team members are starting to avoid working with them. What is the BEST FIRST action for the project leader?

options.A: Publicly address the irritability during a team meeting
options.B: Have a private, empathetic conversation to check in on the team member's wellbeing and understand what might be causing the change in behavior
options.C: Ignore the behavior since technical skill outweighs interpersonal concerns
options.D: Remove the team member from all collaborative work immediately

justification: Correct. A private, empathetic check-in is the appropriate first step to understand a noticeable behavior change, which could stem from stress, burnout, or personal issues warranting support rather than immediate correction.

text: Which of the following are appropriate practices for managing technical debt in an agile environment? (Select TWO)

options.A: Making technical debt visible on the Product Backlog alongside feature work
options.B: Allocating a portion of team capacity regularly to address the highest-priority technical debt
options.C: Hiding technical debt from the Product Owner to avoid difficult prioritization conversations
options.D: Never addressing technical debt unless it causes a production outage

justification: Correct. Making technical debt visible on the backlog alongside feature work ensures it is considered transparently in prioritization decisions rather than being hidden or forgotten. / Correct. Regularly allocating capacity to address the highest-priority technical debt is a proactive, sustainable practice that prevents debt from accumulating unmanaged.

text: An agile team's organization is considering outsourcing part of the development work to reduce costs, which could affect current team members' roles. Team members have heard rumors and are anxious. What is the BEST way for the project leader to handle this?

options.A: Deny that any outsourcing discussion is happening, even if it is
options.B: Confirm the team's worst fears without any actual confirmed information, just to be safe
options.C: Communicate what is actually known transparently, acknowledge the uncertainty, and commit to updating the team as more information becomes available
options.D: Ignore the rumors and hope they die down on their own

justification: Correct. Transparent communication of what is actually known, combined with acknowledging genuine uncertainty and a commitment to future updates, respects the team while managing a sensitive organizational situation responsibly.

text: Match each interpersonal skill to its correct application in project leadership.

colonne_droite.texte: Reaching a mutually acceptable agreement on resource allocation between two competing project priorities
Persuading a stakeholder to support a project decision without having direct authority over them
Understanding informal power dynamics and relationships within the organization to navigate decisions effectively
Guiding a group discussion to reach a shared decision or understanding

justification: Negotiation is used to reach mutually acceptable agreements when interests or resource needs compete, balancing different parties' priorities. / Influence involves persuading others to support a course of action, particularly valuable when the project manager lacks direct formal authority over the stakeholder. / Political awareness involves understanding informal organizational power structures and relationships, helping navigate decisions and stakeholder dynamics effectively. / Facilitation involves skillfully guiding group discussions toward productive outcomes, ensuring participation and clarity without necessarily dictating the outcome.

text: A team has been tracking their Sprint outcomes for the past 6 Sprints. Their velocity has been 35, 38, 32, 40, 30, and 33 story points respectively. The Product Owner asks the team to commit to 45 story points for the next Sprint to meet a stakeholder request. What is the MOST appropriate response from the team?

options.A: Present the historical velocity range (average around 34-35, with a high of 40) and explain that committing to 45 points would be well outside their demonstrated capacity, then discuss options such as reducing scope or extending the timeline
options.B: Agree to the 45-point commitment since the Product Owner requested it
options.C: Refuse to discuss the request at all
options.D: Silently commit to 45 points but plan to under-deliver as has happened before

justification: Correct. Presenting the actual historical velocity data transparently and discussing realistic trade-offs (scope or timeline) with the Product Owner reflects evidence-based, transparent forecasting and collaborative planning.

text: Which of the following are examples of external business environment factors that could affect a project? (Select TWO)

options.A: New tariffs imposed on imported components
options.B: A shift in consumer preferences within the target market
options.C: The project team's internal communication plan
options.D: The project's internal work breakdown structure

justification: Correct. New tariffs are an external economic/regulatory factor originating outside the organization that can significantly affect project costs and supply chains. / Correct. Shifts in consumer preferences are an external market factor that can affect a project's scope, priorities, or business case relevance.

text: A project manager notices that a team member habitually agrees to every request during meetings but then fails to follow through, creating downstream delays. What is the BEST way to address this pattern?

options.A: Publicly call out every instance of failure to follow through
options.B: Have a direct conversation to understand why they over-commit verbally, and establish a practice of confirming realistic commitments before meetings end
options.C: Stop assigning any tasks to this team member going forward
options.D: Assume the team member is being deliberately dishonest and escalate immediately to HR

justification: Correct. A direct conversation to understand the reason behind the over-commitment pattern, paired with a practice of confirming realistic commitments, addresses the root cause constructively.

text: A Scrum team wants to reduce the number of defects that reach production. Which practice would MOST directly help achieve this goal?

options.A: Reducing the frequency of Sprint Reviews
options.B: Removing quality-related acceptance criteria to move faster
options.C: Increasing Sprint length to allow for less frequent releases
options.D: Strengthening the Definition of Done to require automated testing and code review before an item is considered complete

justification: Correct. A stronger Definition of Done that requires automated testing and code review directly builds quality checks into the delivery process, reducing the likelihood of defects reaching production.

text: An agile team's organization is entering a new market where consumer trust in digital products is historically low due to past data misuse scandals by other companies. What should the product leader prioritize?

options.A: Ignore trust concerns since the team's own product has no history of data misuse
options.B: Prioritize transparent data practices and trust-building features (e.g., clear privacy controls, transparent data usage disclosures) as part of the market entry strategy
options.C: Focus solely on marketing messaging without any actual product changes
options.D: Delay market entry indefinitely until consumer trust improves industry-wide

justification: Correct. Prioritizing genuine trust-building features as part of market entry directly addresses the specific business environment challenge (low consumer trust) with substantive product decisions, not just messaging.

text: A team wants to validate a risky new feature idea before investing significant development effort. What is the BEST agile practice to use for this purpose?

options.A: Skip validation entirely and trust the Product Owner's instinct alone
options.B: Build the complete feature first, then ask for feedback afterward
options.C: Postpone the decision indefinitely until there is complete certainty
options.D: Create a minimal viable version or prototype to test the core hypothesis with real users before full investment

justification: Correct. Creating a minimal viable version or prototype to test the core hypothesis with real users is the standard lean/agile approach to validate risky ideas before committing significant development effort.

text: A project leader notices that team members from different generational backgrounds (early-career and late-career) have differing preferences for feedback style, with younger members preferring frequent informal check-ins and older members preferring formal, scheduled reviews. What is the BEST way to accommodate this?

options.A: Offer flexible feedback approaches that respect individual preferences while ensuring consistent, fair standards are applied to everyone
options.B: Give feedback only to the group that prefers formal reviews, since that is the traditional approach
options.C: Impose a single feedback style on the entire team regardless of preference
options.D: Stop giving feedback altogether to avoid navigating generational differences

justification: Correct. Offering flexible feedback delivery approaches tailored to individual preferences, while maintaining consistent underlying standards, respects diversity in the team while ensuring fairness.

text: A project manager is reviewing the Cost Performance Baseline and notices that the S-curve is significantly steeper than typical for similar past projects at this stage. What is the BEST way to interpret this?

options.A: Automatically increase the project budget to match the steeper trend
options.B: Ignore the shape of the curve since only the final total cost matters
options.C: Investigate the reason for the steeper spending curve, which could reflect front-loaded costs, accelerated schedule, or a planning issue requiring further analysis
options.D: This is definitely an error in the baseline and should be immediately discarded

justification: Correct. Investigating the reason behind an unusual S-curve shape, which could reflect legitimate front-loaded costs or a genuine planning concern, is the appropriate analytical response before drawing conclusions.

text: A project manager discovers that a key subcontractor is facing serious financial difficulties that could threaten their ability to complete the contracted work. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Assess the actual risk to the project, engage the subcontractor to understand the situation, and develop contingency options (e.g., alternate suppliers, closer monitoring)
options.B: Ignore the financial difficulties since they are the subcontractor's internal business matter
options.C: Publicly announce the subcontractor's financial troubles to other stakeholders immediately
options.D: Terminate the subcontract immediately without further assessment

justification: Correct. Assessing the actual project risk, engaging directly with the subcontractor, and developing contingency options reflects proactive vendor/risk management appropriate to a credible threat to contract performance.

text: A Product Owner and Scrum Master have differing opinions on how much detail should be included in user stories, causing friction during Backlog Refinement. What is the BEST way to resolve this?

options.A: Have the Product Owner unilaterally dictate the required level of detail without team input
options.B: Facilitate a conversation involving the whole Scrum Team to agree on a shared standard for story detail that works for everyone, particularly the Developers who implement the work
options.C: Have the Scrum Master unilaterally dictate the required level of detail
options.D: Avoid discussing story detail standards altogether to prevent further friction

justification: Correct. Facilitating a whole-team conversation to establish a shared standard, especially involving the Developers who implement the stories, ensures the resulting standard is practical and broadly agreed upon.

text: A team's Sprint Backlog shows several items 'In Progress' for multiple Sprints without completion. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this pattern?

options.A: Automatically move all stalled items to 'Done' to clear the backlog visually
options.B: Allow items to remain in progress indefinitely since work is technically happening
options.C: Remove all stalled items from the Sprint Backlog without investigation
options.D: Facilitate a discussion to understand why items are stalling (e.g., oversized items, unclear scope, external blockers) and address the root cause

justification: Correct. Facilitating a discussion to identify the root cause of stalling items — whether oversized scope, unclear requirements, or external blockers — allows the team to address the actual underlying problem.

text: Match each type of contract/agreement risk allocation to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Seller bears most of the cost risk; price is set regardless of actual seller costs
Buyer bears most of the cost risk; buyer reimburses seller's allowable costs
Risk is shared; buyer pays for actual time and materials used, often with a not-to-exceed cap
Risk is shared through a fee structure that rewards the seller for meeting or exceeding specific performance targets

justification: In a fixed-price contract, the seller commits to delivering the defined scope for a set price, absorbing most of the risk if actual costs exceed the agreed amount. / In a cost-reimbursable contract, the buyer agrees to reimburse the seller's allowable costs plus a fee, placing more of the cost risk on the buyer. / Time and materials contracts share risk between buyer and seller, often used for smaller or less clearly defined scopes, frequently with a not-to-exceed ceiling to limit buyer risk exposure. / Incentive fee contracts share risk through fee structures tied to specific performance targets, motivating the seller toward outcomes valued by the buyer while sharing some risk/reward.

text: A project manager is preparing to onboard several new team members mid-project. What is the BEST way to help them quickly become productive contributors?

options.A: Delay giving them any real work until they have independently read all project documentation
options.B: Provide a structured onboarding process including project context, key documentation, introductions to key stakeholders, and an assigned mentor or buddy
options.C: Expect them to learn everything through trial and error without any formal onboarding
options.D: Assign them immediately to the most critical, high-visibility tasks without any orientation

justification: Correct. A structured onboarding process, including context, documentation, stakeholder introductions, and a mentor, accelerates new team members' integration and productivity effectively.

text: A team is debating whether to hold a Sprint Retrospective even though the Sprint went unusually smoothly with no major issues. What is the BEST guidance?

options.A: Skip the Retrospective since there is nothing to discuss when a Sprint goes smoothly
options.B: Still hold the Retrospective, as it provides value even during smooth Sprints by identifying what worked well and reinforcing effective practices for the future
options.C: Only hold Retrospectives after difficult Sprints
options.D: Replace the Retrospective with an informal celebration only

justification: Correct. Retrospectives provide ongoing value regardless of Sprint difficulty, helping teams understand what worked well (to reinforce) as well as identify any subtle improvement opportunities, consistent with Scrum's continuous improvement principle.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a country where a new law now requires all software handling health data to be independently audited annually. The team's product handles some health-related data. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Remove all health-related data handling from the product to avoid the law entirely
options.B: Wait until the audit is scheduled before considering any preparation
options.C: Add backlog items to prepare for the audit requirement, including any necessary process, documentation, or technical changes, and prioritize based on the compliance deadline
options.D: Ignore the law since the health data handling is a small part of the overall product

justification: Correct. Proactively adding prioritized backlog items to prepare for the audit requirement ensures the organization is ready by the compliance deadline, integrating the legal requirement into planned, trackable work.

text: A project manager is finalizing the risk register and needs to prioritize which risks require detailed quantitative analysis versus which can be managed with qualitative assessment alone. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Avoid analyzing risks that seem unlikely to occur, regardless of potential impact
options.B: Perform detailed quantitative analysis on every single identified risk regardless of significance
options.C: Skip qualitative analysis entirely and rely only on quantitative methods for all risks
options.D: Use qualitative analysis (probability and impact assessment) to prioritize risks, then apply quantitative analysis selectively to the highest-priority risks where more precise numerical insight is valuable

justification: Correct. Using qualitative analysis first to prioritize risks, then applying more resource-intensive quantitative analysis selectively to the highest-priority risks, is the standard, efficient risk analysis progression.

text: Which of the following are examples of legitimate reasons a project might be terminated early (before planned completion)? (Select TWO)

options.A: The business case is no longer valid due to changed market conditions
options.B: The project's risks now outweigh its potential benefits
options.C: The project manager personally dislikes the assignment
options.D: A single team member requests a transfer to another project

justification: Correct. A project's business case becoming invalid due to changed market or organizational conditions is a legitimate, standard reason for considering early termination. / Correct. When a comprehensive reassessment shows risks now outweigh potential benefits, early termination may be the appropriate, responsible decision.

text: A Product Owner frequently changes their mind about priorities within the same day, causing confusion among Developers about what to focus on. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since the Product Owner has full authority over priorities
options.B: Escalate the Product Owner's behavior to senior management immediately without coaching first
options.C: Have the Developers ignore the Product Owner's changing requests entirely
options.D: Coach the Product Owner on the importance of a stable Sprint Backlog once committed, while ensuring there are appropriate channels for capturing emerging priorities for future consideration

justification: Correct. Coaching the Product Owner on protecting the Sprint's stability once committed, while providing proper channels to capture new priorities for future consideration, addresses both the immediate confusion and the Product Owner's legitimate need to track emerging priorities.

text: A project manager needs to select an appropriate contract type for a project with well-defined, low-risk requirements. Which contract type is generally MOST appropriate?

options.A: Cost Plus Percentage of Cost (CPPC)
options.B: Time and Materials with no ceiling
options.C: Firm Fixed Price (FFP)
options.D: Cost Plus Award Fee (CPAF)

justification: Correct. Firm Fixed Price contracts work best for well-defined, low-risk scope, since both parties can confidently agree on a set price with minimal uncertainty about final costs.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to anti-corruption laws that prohibit certain types of gifts or payments to government officials involved in project approvals. A local partner suggests providing an 'expediting fee' to speed up a permit approval. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Make the payment quietly without informing anyone in the organization
options.B: Ask a team member to make the payment personally to avoid direct project involvement
options.C: Decline the suggested fee and consult legal/compliance to ensure the project remains compliant with anti-corruption laws, exploring only legitimate means to expedite approval
options.D: Agree to the fee since it would help meet the schedule

justification: Correct. Declining the improper suggestion and consulting legal/compliance to explore only legitimate means of expediting approval reflects ethical, legally compliant project management.

text: A team member frequently uses humor to deflect during serious discussions about project risks, making it difficult for the team to have focused, productive risk conversations. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Tell the team member to stop using humor entirely in all situations
options.B: Exclude the team member from all future risk discussions
options.C: Privately acknowledge their positive contribution to team morale while discussing the need for focused engagement during risk discussions specifically
options.D: Allow the pattern to continue since humor is generally good for team morale

justification: Correct. Acknowledging the positive aspects of their humor while specifically addressing the need for focus during particular serious discussions balances respect for the individual with the team's need for effective risk conversations.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons for a Scrum Team to cancel a Sprint before its planned end? (Select TWO)

options.A: The Sprint Goal becomes obsolete due to a significant change in business direction
options.B: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint, and they determine it no longer makes sense to continue
options.C: A single Developer personally dislikes the current Sprint's tasks
options.D: The team simply wants a break from work

justification: Correct. A Sprint Goal becoming obsolete due to a significant change in business direction is a legitimate, recognized reason to consider canceling a Sprint. / Correct. Per the Scrum Guide, only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint, and this would be based on a determination that continuing no longer makes sense given current circumstances.

text: A project manager needs to delegate an important decision to a team member who has never made a decision of this scope before. What is the BEST way to approach this delegation?

options.A: Make the decision personally to avoid any risk
options.B: Provide clear context, boundaries, and available support, then check in periodically while allowing the team member genuine ownership of the decision
options.C: Delegate the decision entirely with no guidance or check-in
options.D: Delegate the decision but override it afterward if it differs from what the project manager would have chosen

justification: Correct. Providing context, boundaries, and support while allowing genuine ownership builds the team member's capability and confidence, appropriate for someone developing new decision-making skills.

text: A project manager is facilitating a meeting where two senior stakeholders begin talking over each other, each trying to assert their priority. What is the BEST way to manage this moment?

options.A: Side with whichever stakeholder has more organizational seniority
options.B: Politely intervene to restore order, acknowledge both perspectives, and guide the discussion toward a structured resolution process
options.C: End the meeting immediately without resolution
options.D: Let them continue since senior stakeholders should be allowed to resolve disputes independently

justification: Correct. Politely intervening to restore order, acknowledging both perspectives, and guiding toward structured resolution reflects skilled facilitation that respects both parties while maintaining productive discussion.

text: Which of the following are appropriate ways to build trust with a new project team? (Select TWO)

options.A: Following through consistently on commitments made to the team
options.B: Being transparent about project constraints and challenges
options.C: Withholding information to maintain a sense of control
options.D: Making promises that cannot realistically be kept to boost morale

justification: Correct. Consistently following through on commitments demonstrates reliability, a foundational element of building trust with any team. / Correct. Being transparent about constraints and challenges, rather than hiding them, builds credibility and mutual trust over time.

text: An agile team member consistently completes their assigned work well but rarely engages in helping teammates or contributing ideas beyond their own tasks. What is the BEST way for the project leader to encourage broader engagement?

options.A: Accept their current level of engagement without any further discussion
options.B: Reduce their individual task load to force them into collaborative work
options.C: Formally discipline the team member for insufficient collaboration
options.D: Have a supportive conversation to understand their perspective on collaboration and explore ways to encourage broader engagement that feels natural to them

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation to understand their perspective and explore natural ways to encourage broader engagement respects the individual while working toward healthier team collaboration.

text: A team member on a self-organizing agile team has taken on an informal leadership role, making decisions on behalf of the team without explicit agreement. Other team members feel their input is being bypassed. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since informal leadership can sometimes be helpful
options.B: Have a conversation with the individual about the importance of collective decision-making, and reinforce the team's self-organizing norms with the whole team
options.C: Formally appoint that team member as the official team leader to legitimize their role
options.D: Publicly criticize the team member during a team meeting

justification: Correct. A private conversation about collective decision-making, combined with reinforcing self-organizing norms with the whole team, addresses both the individual behavior and the broader team dynamic constructively.

text: Match each stage of conflict escalation to its correct characteristic.

colonne_droite.texte: Parties focus on facts and differing perspectives with a shared goal of finding a solution
Parties begin protecting their own interests, and communication becomes more guarded
Parties begin trying to win rather than resolve, and personal attacks may emerge
Parties see the conflict as a fundamental cause, often recruiting others to their side

justification: At this earliest stage, parties still share the goal of resolving the issue together, focusing on facts rather than personal positions. / As conflict escalates slightly, parties begin protecting their own interests more, and open, collaborative communication starts to diminish. / At this more escalated stage, the focus shifts from resolving the problem to winning, and interactions may include personal criticism. / At the most escalated stage, the conflict becomes seen as a larger cause, often involving recruiting allies and making resolution significantly more difficult.

text: An agile team's Scrum Master notices that team members frequently apologize for asking questions during planning sessions, suggesting some hesitancy to seek clarification. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Explicitly reinforce that asking questions is valued and encouraged, modeling curiosity and openly welcoming clarifying questions during sessions
options.B: Reduce the number of planning sessions to minimize opportunities for questions
options.C: Tell team members that questions are a waste of time during planning
options.D: Ignore the apologetic pattern since it does not affect the planning outcome directly

justification: Correct. Explicitly reinforcing that questions are valued, and modeling this openly, helps build the psychological safety needed for team members to seek clarity without hesitation.

text: A project manager wants to determine the probability of completing the project within a specific timeframe, accounting for schedule uncertainty across multiple activities. Which technique is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Milestone chart review
options.B: Resource leveling
options.C: Monte Carlo simulation
options.D: Gantt chart review

justification: Correct. Monte Carlo simulation runs many iterations using probability distributions for activity durations to determine the likelihood of completing the project within various timeframes, directly addressing the described need.

text: A project manager discovers that a critical path activity was accidentally omitted from the original schedule, and adding it now would extend the project finish date by two weeks. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Formally document the schedule change, assess its full impact, and communicate it to the sponsor and relevant stakeholders through the change control process
options.B: Silently add the activity and adjust the finish date without informing stakeholders
options.C: Remove the omitted activity from the project entirely to avoid the schedule impact
options.D: Ignore the omission since the original schedule was already approved

justification: Correct. Formally documenting the change, assessing its full impact, and communicating through proper change control is the standard, transparent way to manage a significant schedule correction.

text: Which of the following are components typically found in a project's Communications Management Plan? (Select TWO)

options.A: Stakeholder communication requirements and preferred methods
options.B: Frequency and format of status reports
options.C: The project's technical architecture diagrams
options.D: Detailed individual performance appraisal criteria

justification: Correct. Stakeholder communication requirements and preferred methods are core components of the Communications Management Plan, defining who needs what information and how. / Correct. The frequency and format of status reports is a standard element of the Communications Management Plan, ensuring consistent and predictable information flow.

text: A team wants to increase transparency around their work for stakeholders who cannot attend Sprint Reviews regularly. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Provide accessible, regularly updated artifacts (such as a shared dashboard or recorded summary) that reflect current progress for those who cannot attend live sessions
options.B: Assume stakeholders who miss Sprint Reviews do not need to be kept informed
options.C: Stop tracking progress visibly since not everyone can see it live anyway
options.D: Require all stakeholders to attend every Sprint Review without exception

justification: Correct. Providing accessible, asynchronous artifacts like dashboards or recorded summaries extends transparency to stakeholders who cannot attend live sessions, supporting inclusive communication.

text: A Development Team wants to reduce the risk of a single point of failure related to one team member's specialized knowledge. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Document nothing and hope the knowledge naturally spreads over time
options.B: Continue relying on that one person exclusively since they are highly skilled
options.C: Encourage pair programming, knowledge-sharing sessions, and cross-training to distribute specialized knowledge across the team
options.D: Remove that specialized area of work from the product entirely

justification: Correct. Practices like pair programming, knowledge-sharing sessions, and cross-training actively distribute specialized knowledge, reducing single-point-of-failure risk while building overall team capability.

text: A quality audit reveals that the project team has been inconsistently following the documented change control process, with several changes implemented without formal approval. What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Ignore the finding since the changes turned out fine
options.B: Eliminate the change control process entirely since the team is not following it consistently
options.C: Reverse all previously implemented changes regardless of their outcome
options.D: Reinforce the change control process with the team, retroactively document the unapproved changes for review, and address any root causes of the process gap

justification: Correct. Reinforcing the process, retroactively documenting and reviewing the unapproved changes, and addressing root causes of the process gap is the appropriate corrective response to a governance compliance issue.

text: Which of the following are examples of appropriate metrics for measuring flow efficiency in a Kanban system? (Select TWO)

options.A: Cycle time
options.B: Throughput (number of items completed per time period)
options.C: Net Present Value of the product
options.D: Number of stakeholders invited to a meeting

justification: Correct. Cycle time, the time it takes for an item to move through the workflow from start to finish, is a fundamental Kanban flow metric. / Correct. Throughput, the number of items completed per time period, directly measures the team's delivery flow and capacity within a Kanban system.

text: A team's Product Owner wants to understand which upcoming Product Backlog Items carry the highest uncertainty in order to prioritize discovery work. What is the BEST technique to help identify this?

options.A: Assume uncertainty is evenly distributed across all backlog items
options.B: Sort items purely by size, assuming larger items always carry more uncertainty
options.C: Ignore uncertainty since agile teams address all issues as they arise regardless of prior identification
options.D: Use a technique such as a risk-adjusted backlog review or story mapping to explicitly flag items with unclear requirements, novel technology, or unvalidated assumptions

justification: Correct. Techniques like risk-adjusted backlog review or story mapping that explicitly flag items with unclear requirements, novel technology, or unvalidated assumptions directly help identify where discovery work should be prioritized.

text: A project manager's organization is evaluating whether to continue funding a project after a mid-project business case review shows the projected return on investment has significantly declined due to changed market conditions. What is the BEST role for the project manager in this decision?

options.A: Avoid participating in the business case review to prevent personal bias
options.B: Provide accurate, updated data on project performance and remaining costs/benefits to support the governance body's informed continue/cancel decision
options.C: Withhold unfavorable data to protect the project's continuation
options.D: Unilaterally decide to continue or cancel the project without governance involvement

justification: Correct. Providing accurate, updated performance and cost/benefit data supports the governance body in making a well-informed continue/cancel decision, reflecting the project manager's proper advisory role in this governance process.

text: A project manager's organization is a signatory to an industry-wide code of conduct that includes specific labor and environmental standards for suppliers. A cost-competitive potential supplier does not currently meet these standards. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Select the supplier anyway since they offer the lowest cost
options.B: Ignore the code of conduct since it is not part of the formal procurement contract terms
options.C: Exclude the supplier from consideration unless they can demonstrate a credible path to compliance with the code of conduct standards
options.D: Select the supplier and simply avoid mentioning the compliance gap to anyone

justification: Correct. Excluding non-compliant suppliers unless they can demonstrate a credible compliance path respects the organization's ethical and contractual commitments to the industry code of conduct.

text: An agile team's organization wants to expand into a market with significantly lower average internet bandwidth than their current markets. The team's product currently assumes high-bandwidth connectivity. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Add backlog items to optimize the product for lower bandwidth conditions, prioritized based on the market entry timeline
options.B: Launch the product unchanged in the new market and address complaints as they arise
options.C: Decide the new market is not viable without conducting any technical feasibility assessment
options.D: Assume the market's infrastructure will improve on its own before launch

justification: Correct. Proactively adding prioritized backlog items to optimize for the new market's actual technical conditions reflects responsive, evidence-based product planning for a known business environment constraint.

text: Match each risk category to its correct example in a business environment context.

colonne_droite.texte: A competitor entering the market with a disruptive new business model
A new data privacy regulation requiring significant product changes
A key supplier's production facility experiencing a prolonged outage
Negative public perception following a product recall

justification: Strategic risks relate to the organization's overall market position and business strategy, such as disruptive competitive threats. / Compliance risks relate to legal and regulatory requirements the organization must meet, such as new data privacy laws requiring product changes. / Operational risks relate to the organization's ability to execute its operations effectively, such as supply chain disruptions from a key supplier outage. / Reputational risks relate to public perception and trust, such as negative sentiment following a visible product issue like a recall.

text: An agile team's organization is planning to launch a product in a new region with three regulatory bodies (financial, data privacy, and consumer protection) that each have distinct approval requirements. The launch date is fixed by executive mandate to align with a major industry conference. The team currently has no backlog items addressing any of these regulatory requirements. What is the BEST way for the product leader to proceed?

options.A: Proceed with the fixed launch date and address regulatory requirements only if regulators raise objections after launch
options.B: Immediately engage regulatory/legal experts to scope the requirements from all three bodies, translate them into prioritized backlog items, and assess whether the fixed date is realistically achievable given the required compliance work
options.C: Assume the team can address regulatory requirements informally without dedicated backlog items or expert consultation
options.D: Unilaterally push back the launch date without first assessing the actual scope of regulatory work required

justification: Correct. Promptly engaging expert consultation to scope requirements, translating them into prioritized backlog work, and honestly assessing date feasibility against that scope reflects responsible, proactive business environment management before committing to a fixed public launch.

text: A project manager overhears a team member making a subtly dismissive comment about a colleague's accent during a break. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the comment since it was said informally and not during an official meeting
options.B: Address the comment privately with the team member, explaining its impact and reinforcing the team's expectation of respectful, inclusive behavior
options.C: Wait to see if the comment happens again before taking any action
options.D: Publicly embarrass the team member in front of others to make an example

justification: Correct. Privately addressing the comment, explaining its impact, and reinforcing inclusive behavior expectations is the constructive, respectful way to correct this behavior while protecting the affected colleague's dignity.

text: A project manager wants to improve the team's ability to make decisions collectively rather than always deferring to the project manager. What is the BEST long-term strategy?

options.A: Criticize the team for their current reliance on the project manager
options.B: Delegate all decisions immediately without any support or transition period
options.C: Continue making all decisions to maintain efficiency
options.D: Gradually delegate appropriate decisions to the team, provide coaching support, and build their confidence and capability over time

justification: Correct. Gradually delegating appropriate decisions with coaching support builds the team's confidence and capability incrementally, which is a sustainable, effective approach to developing collective decision-making.

text: Which of the following are examples of transactional (as opposed to transformational) leadership behaviors? (Select TWO)

options.A: Rewarding team members for meeting specific, predefined performance targets
options.B: Correcting deviations from expected performance through defined consequences
options.C: Inspiring the team with a compelling shared vision beyond immediate tasks
options.D: Encouraging team members to challenge existing assumptions and think creatively

justification: Correct. Rewarding performance against predefined targets is a classic transactional leadership behavior, focused on exchange-based motivation. / Correct. Correcting deviations through defined consequences reflects transactional leadership's focus on managing performance against set expectations.

text: A team member consistently expresses frustration about the pace of decision-making within the team, feeling that too much time is spent discussing rather than acting. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this concern?

options.A: Tell the frustrated team member to be more patient without exploring any process changes
options.B: Dismiss the concern since thorough discussion is always valuable regardless of pace
options.C: Discuss with the team ways to make decision-making more efficient, such as timeboxing discussions or using structured decision-making techniques, while still ensuring adequate input
options.D: Eliminate all team discussion and have the project leader make decisions unilaterally going forward

justification: Correct. Exploring efficiency techniques like timeboxing or structured decision-making, while still ensuring adequate input, balances the concern about pace with the value of collaborative discussion.

text: A newly self-organizing agile team is struggling because members are unsure how to divide work fairly without a traditional task assignment structure. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to help?

options.A: Revert the team to a traditional, manager-assigned task structure permanently
options.B: Coach the team on self-organization principles and facilitate a discussion to establish a shared, transparent approach to selecting and distributing work
options.C: Tell the team to figure it out entirely on their own with no facilitation support
options.D: Assign all tasks personally to remove the ambiguity

justification: Correct. Coaching on self-organization principles and facilitating a discussion to establish a shared, transparent work-distribution approach helps the team develop this capability with appropriate support during the transition.

text: Match each type of team to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: All team members work from the same physical location
Team members work from different physical locations, collaborating primarily through digital tools
Team includes members with diverse skill sets needed to deliver a complete product increment
Team determines how to accomplish its work internally, without external direction on the 'how'

justification: Co-located teams share a physical workspace, often facilitating easier informal communication and collaboration. / Virtual teams are geographically dispersed and rely on digital communication and collaboration tools to work together effectively. / Cross-functional teams bring together diverse skills (e.g., design, development, testing) needed to deliver a complete, working increment without excessive external dependency. / Self-organizing teams determine internally how to accomplish their work, choosing their own methods and task allocation without being told how to do it by external leaders.

text: A team member expresses discomfort about a recent organizational restructuring that eliminated their previous manager's role, even though it did not directly affect their own position. What is the BEST way for the project leader to respond?

options.A: Tell them not to worry since their own position was unaffected
options.B: Acknowledge their discomfort with empathy, provide any relevant available information, and check in on how they are processing the change
options.C: Avoid discussing the topic since it is an organizational matter outside the project
options.D: Assume the discomfort will pass quickly without needing any acknowledgment

justification: Correct. Acknowledging discomfort empathetically, sharing available information, and checking in reflects supportive, human-centered leadership even for concerns stemming from broader organizational change.

text: A project manager is comparing two schedule compression options: crashing versus fast tracking. The project has abundant budget but very limited schedule flexibility for sequencing changes due to safety inspection requirements between phases. Which technique is generally MORE appropriate in this situation?

options.A: Crashing, since it adds resources to shorten duration without requiring changes to activity sequencing
options.B: Fast tracking, since it requires no additional cost
options.C: Neither technique, since schedule compression is never appropriate on projects with safety requirements
options.D: Both techniques equally, applied simultaneously to every activity

justification: Correct. Crashing shortens the schedule by adding resources to activities without changing their logical sequence, making it suitable here where abundant budget exists but sequencing flexibility (needed for fast tracking) is limited.

text: A project manager is analyzing stakeholder engagement levels using a stakeholder engagement assessment matrix and finds that a key stakeholder's desired engagement level is 'Leading,' but their current engagement level is only 'Resistant.' What is the BEST interpretation of this gap?

options.A: The gap is not significant and requires no specific action
options.B: The stakeholder should be removed from the project entirely due to their resistance
options.C: The desired engagement level should simply be lowered to match their current resistant status
options.D: This represents a significant gap requiring focused engagement strategies to move the stakeholder from resistant toward a more supportive, leading role

justification: Correct. A large gap between current and desired engagement levels signals a priority stakeholder engagement need; developing focused strategies to move the stakeholder toward the desired level is the appropriate response.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons to use a formal change control process rather than making informal adjustments during project execution? (Select TWO)

options.A: It ensures changes are evaluated for impact on scope, cost, schedule, and quality before approval
options.B: It maintains an auditable record of decisions for accountability and future reference
options.C: It guarantees that no project will ever experience delays
options.D: It eliminates the need for any stakeholder communication about changes

justification: Correct. Formal change control ensures proposed changes are systematically evaluated for their impact across scope, cost, schedule, and quality before being approved or rejected. / Correct. Formal change control creates an auditable, traceable record of change decisions, supporting accountability and providing valuable historical reference.

text: A team wants to establish a shared understanding of quality expectations that applies across all Product Backlog Items, regardless of which specific story is being worked on. What artifact BEST serves this purpose?

options.A: The Product Vision statement
options.B: The Sprint Backlog
options.C: The Definition of Done
options.D: Individual acceptance criteria for each story only

justification: Correct. The Definition of Done is the shared, formal description of the quality state required for any Increment to be considered complete, applying universally across all Product Backlog Items.

text: A team notices that their estimation accuracy improves significantly when the same two experienced developers are involved in Planning Poker sessions, compared to sessions without them. What is a potential RISK of this pattern?

options.A: Over-reliance on two individuals for accurate estimation creates a knowledge concentration risk and may discourage broader team engagement in the estimation process
options.B: Planning Poker should be abandoned entirely in favor of expert judgment by these two individuals alone
options.C: There is no risk since accurate estimation is always beneficial regardless of how it is achieved
options.D: The other team members should be excluded entirely from future estimation sessions

justification: Correct. Over-reliance on a couple of individuals for accurate estimates signals a knowledge concentration risk and could discourage full team engagement, both of which undermine the collaborative, whole-team purpose of Planning Poker.

text: A project's quality management plan specifies that a specific deliverable requires 100% inspection before acceptance, given its safety-critical nature. What is the BEST way to plan for this?

options.A: Skip inspection entirely if the deliverable appears visually acceptable
options.B: Use sampling instead of 100% inspection to save time
options.C: Allocate sufficient schedule and resources to conduct full inspection of every unit as specified, given the safety-critical requirement
options.D: Delegate inspection responsibility to the vendor without any independent verification

justification: Correct. Allocating sufficient schedule and resources to conduct the specified 100% inspection respects the safety-critical quality requirement and ensures the project plan reflects this necessary quality control activity.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons a Product Owner might reject a completed Product Backlog Item during a Sprint Review, even if it meets the Definition of Done? (Select TWO)

options.A: The item no longer aligns with a recent shift in market priorities discovered during the Sprint
options.B: The item, while technically complete, does not deliver the user value originally intended due to a misunderstanding uncovered during the demo
options.C: The Product Owner simply dislikes the color scheme used, despite it matching agreed design specifications
options.D: The item was completed one day earlier than originally planned

justification: Correct. A legitimate shift in market priorities discovered during the Sprint is a valid reason to reconsider an item's value, even if it technically meets the Definition of Done. / Correct. If the demo reveals the item doesn't actually deliver the intended user value due to a genuine misunderstanding, this is valid grounds for reassessment despite technical completion.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of building the wrong solution by validating assumptions early. Which practice BEST supports this goal within an agile approach?

options.A: Building the entire feature set before showing anything to users
options.B: Relying exclusively on the Product Owner's personal assumptions without any user validation
options.C: Waiting until the final release to gather any user feedback
options.D: Regularly conducting user research, prototyping, and incorporating findings into backlog refinement before committing significant development effort

justification: Correct. Regularly conducting user research and prototyping, then incorporating findings into refinement, directly reduces the risk of building the wrong solution by validating assumptions before major investment.

text: A project manager's organization decides to adopt a new enterprise resource planning (ERP) system that will change how projects are financially tracked organization-wide. What is the BEST way for the project manager to prepare their current project for this transition?

options.A: Engage with the ERP implementation team early to understand the transition timeline and requirements, and plan the project's financial tracking accordingly
options.B: Wait until the transition is forced upon the project without any advance preparation
options.C: Ignore the upcoming change since it has not yet been implemented
options.D: Refuse to adopt the new system when it becomes available

justification: Correct. Proactively engaging with the implementation team to understand timeline and requirements, and planning accordingly, reflects responsible adaptation to a known organizational process asset change.

text: A project manager's organization operates in a country where recent political unrest has led to intermittent transportation disruptions affecting the delivery of imported equipment. This risk was not part of the original risk register. What is the BEST way to handle this newly emerging risk?

options.A: Add the risk to the register, perform qualitative analysis, and develop an appropriate response plan (e.g., alternate logistics routes, buffer stock)
options.B: Ignore it since it was not part of the original planning
options.C: Cancel all further equipment orders indefinitely
options.D: Proceed with logistics as planned regardless of the disruption risk

justification: Correct. Adding the newly identified risk to the register, analyzing it, and developing an appropriate response (like alternate logistics or buffer stock) is the standard, proactive way to manage emerging risks throughout the project.

text: An agile team's organization begins requiring formal ethics training for all employees following an industry-wide scandal involving data misuse at other companies. How should this affect the team's current Sprint planning?

options.A: Refuse to allow team members to attend the training to protect Sprint velocity
options.B: Account for the required training time when planning team capacity for the affected Sprint(s), adjusting Sprint commitments accordingly
options.C: Cancel the Sprint entirely to accommodate the training
options.D: Ignore the training requirement since it is not directly related to the product backlog

justification: Correct. Accounting for the required training time when planning Sprint capacity, and adjusting commitments accordingly, reflects realistic, transparent Sprint planning that incorporates legitimate organizational requirements.

text: Match each stakeholder engagement level (per the stakeholder engagement assessment matrix) to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Unaware of the project and its potential impacts
Aware of the project but resistant to change or potential impacts
Aware of the project but neither supportive nor resistant
Aware of the project and supportive of change or potential impacts

justification: An unaware stakeholder does not yet know about the project or its potential effects on them, requiring initial awareness-building engagement. / A resistant stakeholder is aware of the project but opposes it or its impacts, requiring focused engagement to understand and address their concerns. / A neutral stakeholder is aware but has not taken a clear position for or against the project, representing an opportunity to build support. / A supportive stakeholder is aware of the project and favorable toward it, potentially valuable as an advocate or champion.

text: An agile team's organization is preparing for a major industry regulatory shift that will require significant changes to how customer consent is captured across all digital products within 6 months. The team's current product has three separate consent flows built at different times with inconsistent implementations. The Product Owner has limited bandwidth to fully scope this work alongside existing feature commitments. What is the BEST way for the product leader to proceed?

options.A: Engage additional support (e.g., a business analyst or compliance specialist) to help scope the regulatory requirements into well-defined backlog items, and begin prioritizing this work with adequate lead time given its fixed deadline and current implementation inconsistency
options.B: Deprioritize the regulatory work in favor of existing feature commitments since the deadline is still months away
options.C: Assume the existing three consent flows are close enough to compliant without further analysis
options.D: Wait until closer to the deadline to begin any work, given the Product Owner's current bandwidth constraints

justification: Correct. Engaging additional support to properly scope the regulatory work, then prioritizing it with appropriate lead time given the fixed deadline and known implementation inconsistency, reflects proactive, risk-aware business environment management.

text: A project manager notices that a team member who recently received a promotion is now hesitant to make decisions they previously made confidently in their prior role. What is the BEST way to support this person?

options.A: Reduce their responsibilities back to their previous level
options.B: Provide reassurance, clarify the scope of their new decision-making authority, and offer coaching support as they adjust to the expanded role
options.C: Assume the hesitation will resolve on its own without any support
options.D: Publicly question their readiness for the promotion

justification: Correct. Providing reassurance, clarifying authority scope, and offering coaching support helps the individual build confidence in their expanded role, a supportive approach to a common promotion transition challenge.

text: A team wants to make sure their Sprint Reviews consistently produce actionable outcomes rather than just a demonstration. What is the BEST practice to ensure this?

options.A: Limit the Sprint Review to only the Product Owner and Scrum Master
options.B: End the Sprint Review immediately after the demo with no further discussion
options.C: Replace collaborative discussion entirely with a pre-recorded video demo
options.D: Structure the Sprint Review to include collaborative discussion on next steps and explicitly capture any resulting backlog updates or action items

justification: Correct. Structuring the event to include collaborative discussion and explicitly capturing resulting backlog updates or action items ensures the Sprint Review produces genuinely actionable outcomes.

text: An agile team's organization is facing increasing pressure from investors to show faster feature delivery, while the team is also dealing with mounting technical debt that is slowing progress. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Ignore investor pressure entirely and focus exclusively on technical debt
options.B: Ignore technical debt entirely and focus exclusively on feature delivery to satisfy investors
options.C: Promise faster delivery without addressing the actual root cause of the slowdown
options.D: Transparently communicate the trade-off between short-term feature speed and long-term technical health to investors/leadership, and negotiate a balanced approach

justification: Correct. Transparently communicating the trade-off and negotiating a balanced approach respects both the legitimate business pressure and the real technical constraint, enabling an informed, sustainable decision.

text: A team's Product Owner is unsure how to prioritize a set of newly proposed features with different potential values and different implementation costs. What is the BEST prioritization technique to recommend?

options.A: Prioritize purely based on which stakeholder requested the feature most recently
options.B: Use a value-versus-effort prioritization technique (e.g., weighted shortest job first, or a value/effort matrix) to systematically compare relative value and cost
options.C: Prioritize solely based on which feature is technically easiest, regardless of value
options.D: Prioritize randomly to ensure fairness among all requesters

justification: Correct. Using a structured value-versus-effort technique systematically compares relative value and implementation cost, supporting more objective, value-maximizing prioritization decisions.

text: A team member who recently transitioned from an individual contributor role to a Scrum Master role is struggling to stop making technical decisions for the team out of habit. What is the BEST way to support their transition?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since it will likely resolve on its own eventually
options.B: Provide coaching on the servant-leadership Scrum Master mindset, and offer specific, supportive feedback when they slip into their old habits, reinforcing the shift over time
options.C: Move them back to their previous individual contributor role since the transition is difficult
options.D: Criticize them each time they revert to making technical decisions

justification: Correct. Providing coaching on the servant-leadership mindset combined with specific, supportive feedback when old habits emerge helps reinforce the desired behavioral shift over time, a supportive approach to role transition.

text: Which of the following are valid components of a project's risk management plan? (Select TWO)

options.A: Roles and responsibilities for risk management activities
options.B: Risk categories and a risk breakdown structure
options.C: The final list of all approved change requests
options.D: The complete stakeholder communication schedule

justification: Correct. Defining roles and responsibilities for risk management activities is a standard component of the risk management plan, clarifying who is accountable for what. / Correct. Risk categories and a risk breakdown structure provide a structured framework for identifying and organizing risks, a standard component of the risk management plan.

text: A project manager's organization faces a sudden shortage of skilled labor in the local market due to a competing large-scale project nearby that is hiring aggressively. What is the BEST way to manage this business environment risk?

options.A: Assess the impact on project staffing, and consider options such as adjusted compensation, remote/alternate sourcing, or schedule adjustments to address the shortage
options.B: Cancel the project immediately due to the labor market conditions
options.C: Ignore the labor shortage and continue with the current staffing plan unchanged
options.D: Poach staff from the competing project without any consideration of ethical or contractual implications

justification: Correct. Assessing the actual staffing impact and considering legitimate options like adjusted compensation, alternate sourcing, or schedule adjustments reflects a proactive, considered response to a real market constraint.

text: A project manager needs to give feedback to a peer project manager (not a direct report) whose project's poor communication practices are affecting a shared cross-project dependency. What is the BEST way to approach this?

options.A: Publicly criticize the other project manager's communication practices in a shared status meeting
options.B: Say nothing since it is not the project manager's place to give feedback to a peer
options.C: Have a direct, respectful peer-to-peer conversation focused on the specific impact and a collaborative path forward
options.D: Escalate immediately to both project managers' shared supervisor without first attempting a peer conversation

justification: Correct. A direct, respectful peer-to-peer conversation focused on specific impact and collaborative resolution is the appropriate first step for addressing a cross-project dependency issue between peers.

text: A team wants to reduce the time spent in Sprint Planning while still ensuring the team fully understands what they're committing to. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Ensure backlog items are well-refined before Sprint Planning, reducing the need for lengthy clarification discussions during the event itself
options.B: Skip discussing the 'how' of implementation entirely to save time
options.C: Extend Sprint Planning indefinitely until every possible detail is discussed
options.D: Eliminate Sprint Planning entirely and let developers self-select work without any shared planning discussion

justification: Correct. Ensuring backlog items are well-refined beforehand reduces the need for extensive clarification during Sprint Planning itself, since ambiguity has already been addressed earlier, directly reducing meeting time while maintaining understanding.

text: Match each type of organizational structure impact to its correct description in an agile context.

colonne_droite.texte: Creates handoff delays and communication barriers between specialized departments
Enables end-to-end ownership and faster decision-making within a single team
Teams organized around technical layers, often requiring cross-team coordination to deliver a complete feature
Teams organized around delivering complete, end-to-end customer-facing features

justification: Siloed functional structures separate specialists by department, often creating communication barriers and handoff delays that slow cross-functional delivery. / Cross-functional product teams combine diverse skills within a single team, enabling end-to-end ownership and faster decision-making without excessive external dependencies. / Component teams are organized around technical layers or components (e.g., front-end, back-end), often requiring coordination across teams to deliver a complete customer-facing feature. / Feature teams are organized around delivering complete, end-to-end customer-facing features, reducing cross-team dependencies compared to component teams.

text: A project manager needs to select a vendor representative to serve as the primary point of contact for daily coordination. Two candidates are available: one with excellent technical knowledge but poor responsiveness, and one with average technical knowledge but excellent, timely communication. What should the project manager MOST heavily weigh, given that this role's primary function is daily coordination?

options.A: Whichever candidate is available immediately, regardless of fit
options.B: The candidate's seniority within the vendor organization
options.C: The specific skills most relevant to the role's primary function, which in this case is timely coordination and communication
options.D: Technical knowledge alone, regardless of the role's actual requirements

justification: Correct. Given that the role's primary function is daily coordination, prioritizing the skills most relevant to that function (timely, effective communication) reflects appropriate, context-specific resourcing judgment.

text: A team wants to understand whether their recent process changes (e.g., adopting pair programming) have actually improved quality. What is the BEST way to evaluate this?

options.A: Avoid any evaluation since process changes are inherently unmeasurable
options.B: Compare relevant quality metrics (e.g., defect rates, escaped defects) before and after the change over a sufficient time period to draw meaningful conclusions
options.C: Assume the change worked simply because it is a commonly recommended agile practice
options.D: Rely solely on team members' subjective feelings about whether things have improved

justification: Correct. Comparing relevant quality metrics before and after the change, over a sufficient period, provides objective, empirical evidence of whether the change actually improved quality, consistent with data-driven continuous improvement.

text: A project manager's organization is undergoing a significant shift toward remote-first work policies, changing how project teams have traditionally collaborated in person. What should the project manager do to adapt project execution?

options.A: Continue running the project exactly as if all team members were still co-located
options.B: Refuse to adapt since the original project plan was already approved under different assumptions
options.C: Cancel all team meetings entirely to align with remote work
options.D: Reassess and update the communications management plan and collaboration tools/practices to reflect the new remote-first working environment

justification: Correct. Reassessing and updating the communications plan and collaboration practices to reflect the new remote-first environment is the appropriate way to adapt project execution to a significant organizational business environment change.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate level of contingency reserve for a project with high overall uncertainty due to novel technology use. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Set an extremely high contingency reserve without any analysis, simply to be safe
options.B: Base the contingency reserve on a quantitative risk analysis (e.g., expected monetary value or Monte Carlo simulation) that reflects the project's specific identified risks and uncertainty
options.C: Set contingency reserve to zero since the exact risks cannot be perfectly predicted
options.D: Use a flat, arbitrary percentage regardless of the project's actual risk profile

justification: Correct. Basing contingency reserve on quantitative analysis specific to the project's identified risks provides a more accurate, evidence-based reserve amount tailored to the actual level of uncertainty.

text: Which of the following are examples of value delivered through incremental agile delivery that support business environment adaptability? (Select TWO)

options.A: Earlier realization of business value through frequent releases
options.B: The ability to adjust priorities based on real market feedback between increments
options.C: Guaranteed elimination of all project risk
options.D: A fixed, unchangeable scope defined at project initiation

justification: Correct. Frequent releases enable earlier realization of business value, allowing the organization to benefit sooner and respond to changing conditions with real results already delivered. / Correct. The ability to adjust priorities based on real market feedback between increments is a core benefit of incremental agile delivery, directly supporting business environment adaptability.

text: A team member consistently provides overly critical feedback during code reviews without acknowledging what was done well, which is starting to discourage other team members from submitting code for review promptly. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Eliminate code reviews entirely to avoid the discouragement
options.B: Have a private conversation about providing balanced, constructive feedback that includes both strengths and areas for improvement, modeling healthy review practices
options.C: Publicly criticize the team member's review style during a team meeting
options.D: Tell the other team members to simply toughen up and stop being discouraged

justification: Correct. A private conversation about providing balanced, constructive feedback addresses the root behavioral pattern while preserving the valuable code review practice itself.

text: A team wants to reduce work-in-progress across their Kanban board to improve flow. Currently there is no WIP limit set on the 'In Development' column, and the team notices items frequently pile up there. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Collaboratively determine and set an appropriate initial WIP limit for the column based on team capacity, and adjust it iteratively based on observed results
options.B: Immediately set an extremely low WIP limit without any team discussion
options.C: Remove the 'In Development' column entirely from the board
options.D: Ignore the pile-up since it does not affect throughput

justification: Correct. Collaboratively determining an appropriate initial WIP limit based on actual team capacity, then adjusting iteratively based on results, reflects the standard, evidence-based approach to introducing WIP limits effectively.

text: A project manager's organization operates under a specific industry standard (e.g., ISO 9001) that requires documented evidence of quality control processes. A quality auditor requests to review the project's quality records. What is the BEST way for the project manager to respond?

options.A: Delay the audit indefinitely to avoid scrutiny
options.B: Provide the requested quality records, ensuring they are organized and accurately reflect the project's actual quality control activities
options.C: Quickly create new documentation that does not accurately reflect what actually occurred, to appear more compliant
options.D: Refuse the auditor's request since project records are considered confidential

justification: Correct. Providing accurate, organized quality records that reflect actual project activities supports legitimate compliance verification and demonstrates the project's genuine adherence to required quality standards.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that during Sprint Planning, the Developers consistently underestimate the complexity of integration work with external systems, leading to repeated overcommitment. What is the BEST way to help the team improve?

options.A: Tell the team to simply try harder to estimate accurately without any structural changes
options.B: Remove all integration work from the Product Backlog to avoid the estimation challenge
options.C: Facilitate a Retrospective discussion to explore why integration complexity is consistently underestimated and collaboratively develop an improved estimation approach for this type of work
options.D: Have the Scrum Master personally re-estimate all integration work on the team's behalf

justification: Correct. Facilitating a Retrospective discussion to explore the root cause of the consistent underestimation, and collaboratively developing an improved approach, reflects genuine continuous improvement addressing a specific, recurring estimation pattern.

text: Which of the following are valid inputs when developing a project's cost estimates? (Select TWO)

options.A: The scope baseline
options.B: Historical cost information from similar past projects
options.C: The team's individual performance appraisal ratings
options.D: The organization's marketing budget for unrelated products

justification: Correct. The scope baseline, defining what needs to be delivered, is a fundamental input needed to develop accurate cost estimates for the required work. / Correct. Historical cost information from similar past projects (an organizational process asset) provides valuable reference data for developing more accurate cost estimates.

text: A project manager notices that a highly experienced team member consistently undermines the ideas of a less experienced colleague, even when the ideas have merit. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since the experienced team member's judgment is usually sound
options.B: Privately address the pattern with the experienced team member, explaining its impact, and reinforce a culture that values contributions regardless of experience level
options.C: Tell the less experienced colleague to simply stop sharing ideas
options.D: Reassign the less experienced colleague to a different team
