justification: Correct. Privately addressing the undermining pattern and reinforcing a culture of valuing all contributions addresses the root behavior while protecting psychological safety for less experienced members.

text: A project manager must decide how to structure a critical kickoff meeting for a newly formed, diverse team spanning multiple departments. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Include both project scope/objectives and time for the team to get acquainted, establish shared expectations, and begin building working relationships
options.B: Focus the meeting exclusively on the technical scope with no discussion of team dynamics
options.C: Keep the meeting as short as possible with minimal discussion
options.D: Hold separate kickoff meetings for each department without any cross-department session

justification: Correct. Including both project objectives and relationship-building time reflects good practice for kicking off a diverse, newly formed team, setting a foundation for both technical alignment and effective collaboration.

text: A project manager learns that a team member is being considered for a role on another project that would be a better career fit for them, but their departure would create a short-term resource gap. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Pressure the team member to decline the opportunity by emphasizing loyalty to the current project
options.B: Immediately release the team member without any transition planning
options.C: Actively block the team member's transfer to protect the current project's resourcing
options.D: Support the team member's career growth while working with the organization on a reasonable transition plan to manage the resource gap

justification: Correct. Supporting the team member's career growth while working on a reasonable transition plan reflects genuine care for the individual while responsibly managing the resulting resource impact.

text: A project manager is coaching a team lead who tends to avoid difficult conversations with underperforming team members, letting issues persist. What is the BEST coaching approach?

options.A: Replace the team lead since they clearly lack the necessary skills
options.B: Coach the team lead on constructive feedback techniques, role-play difficult scenarios, and provide support as they build confidence having these conversations themselves
options.C: Criticize the team lead publicly for avoiding difficult conversations
options.D: Take over all difficult conversations personally on the team lead's behalf indefinitely

justification: Correct. Coaching on feedback techniques, practicing through role-play, and providing ongoing support builds the team lead's confidence and skill to handle these conversations themselves, a developmental coaching approach.

text: A project manager needs to communicate a difficult organizational decision (e.g., reduced project budget) to the team in a way that maintains morale as much as possible. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Delay communicating the news as long as possible
options.B: Provide clear context for the decision, acknowledge its impact honestly, and allow space for the team to ask questions and express concerns
options.C: Deliver the news abruptly with no context or opportunity for questions
options.D: Downplay the significance of the decision to avoid discomfort

justification: Correct. Providing clear context, honestly acknowledging impact, and allowing space for questions and concerns reflects transparent, respectful communication that supports morale even during difficult news.

text: A project manager wants to build a stronger sense of shared ownership among team members for the project's overall success, not just their individual tasks. What is the BEST way to foster this?

options.A: Keep project goals and overall progress visible only to the project manager
options.B: Assume shared ownership will develop naturally without any deliberate effort
options.C: Focus communication exclusively on individual task assignments with no broader context
options.D: Regularly share overall project progress and context with the whole team, and connect individual contributions to the broader project goals and impact

justification: Correct. Regularly sharing overall progress and connecting individual work to broader goals helps team members see their contribution's impact, fostering genuine shared ownership of project success.

text: A project manager needs to resolve a disagreement between two departments about which one should own a shared deliverable going forward, beyond the current project. What is the BEST way for the project manager to help facilitate this?

options.A: Make the ownership decision personally without involving either department
options.B: Avoid facilitating any discussion and let the departments resolve it entirely on their own
options.C: Randomly assign ownership to end the disagreement quickly
options.D: Facilitate a structured discussion between the departments focused on the criteria for effective long-term ownership, helping them reach a mutually informed decision or escalate with clear recommendations if needed

justification: Correct. Facilitating a structured discussion focused on relevant criteria, and helping reach an informed decision or escalating with clear recommendations, reflects the project manager's appropriate facilitative role in cross-organizational matters.

text: A newly formed agile team includes a mix of contractors and full-time employees. Some full-time employees seem hesitant to fully integrate the contractors into team decisions. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Exclude contractors from all significant team decisions to avoid the tension
options.B: Explicitly reinforce that all team members, regardless of employment type, are valued contributors whose input matters for team decisions
options.C: Ignore the pattern since contractors are temporary and their integration is not a priority
options.D: Only involve contractors in low-stakes decisions permanently

justification: Correct. Explicitly reinforcing that all team members are valued contributors, regardless of employment status, addresses the underlying inclusion issue and supports a genuinely collaborative team culture.

text: A team member frequently disagrees with the Scrum Master's facilitation choices but only raises objections privately afterward, never during the actual event. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Ignore the private feedback since it wasn't raised during the actual event
options.B: Tell the team member their feedback is not welcome unless given publicly
options.C: Thank them for the feedback, encourage them to voice concerns in the moment when possible, and genuinely consider their input for improving future facilitation
options.D: Stop facilitating any events to avoid further disagreement

justification: Correct. Genuinely welcoming the feedback, encouraging more in-the-moment input when comfortable, and incorporating valid points reflects an open, growth-oriented approach to facilitation improvement.

text: A team member who has been a strong performer suddenly starts missing Daily Scrums and seems disengaged during team activities. What is the BEST FIRST action for the project leader?

options.A: Ignore the change since it may just be a temporary phase
options.B: Have a private, supportive conversation to check in on their wellbeing and understand what might be causing the change in engagement
options.C: Publicly ask them during the Daily Scrum why they have been missing meetings
options.D: Immediately begin a formal performance improvement process

justification: Correct. A private, supportive check-in is the appropriate first step to understand what might be causing a sudden disengagement shift, which could stem from workload, personal issues, or other factors warranting support.

text: A Scrum Master notices that during Retrospectives, the team tends to focus only on process issues and never discusses interpersonal team dynamics, even when tension is visibly present. What is the BEST way to broaden the Retrospective's scope?

options.A: Address interpersonal issues only through anonymous surveys, never in open discussion
options.B: Continue focusing only on process topics since interpersonal issues are too sensitive to discuss
options.C: Cancel Retrospectives since they are clearly not addressing the real issues
options.D: Introduce techniques or prompts that create a safe space for discussing team dynamics, and model openness to help normalize these conversations

justification: Correct. Introducing techniques that create psychological safety for discussing team dynamics, combined with modeling openness, helps the team gradually feel comfortable addressing these important but sensitive topics.

text: A team member frequently claims to be 'too busy' to attend Backlog Refinement sessions, causing them to be less informed during Sprint Planning. What is the BEST way to address this pattern?

options.A: Have a conversation to understand their actual capacity constraints and explore ways to ensure they can meaningfully participate in refinement or receive adequate context beforehand
options.B: Exclude them permanently from Sprint Planning since they miss refinement
options.C: Ignore the pattern since attendance is always optional in agile
options.D: Publicly criticize them for their attendance pattern during Sprint Planning

justification: Correct. Understanding their actual capacity constraints and exploring practical solutions ensures they can participate meaningfully, addressing the root cause rather than just the symptom.

text: A team's Product Owner and Scrum Master have a strong personal friendship outside of work, and other team members feel this sometimes leads to decisions being made without full team input. What is the BEST way to address this perception?

options.A: Require the Product Owner and Scrum Master to end their personal friendship
options.B: Ignore the team's perception since personal friendships should not be a concern
options.C: Replace either the Product Owner or Scrum Master to eliminate the perceived conflict
options.D: Acknowledge the concern, and both the Product Owner and Scrum Master should make a deliberate effort to ensure decisions are made transparently with appropriate team involvement

justification: Correct. Acknowledging the concern and making a deliberate effort toward transparent, inclusive decision-making addresses the actual issue (perceived exclusion) without requiring drastic personal life interventions.

text: A team member consistently interrupts others during Sprint Planning to propose alternative approaches before the current speaker finishes their point. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Allow the interruptions to continue since enthusiasm for ideas is generally positive
options.B: Exclude the interrupting team member from future Sprint Planning sessions
options.C: Privately discuss the impact of interrupting on team communication, and reinforce facilitation techniques (e.g., structured turn-taking) during future sessions
options.D: Publicly reprimand the team member during the Sprint Planning session itself

justification: Correct. Privately addressing the impact of interrupting, combined with reinforcing structured facilitation techniques during future sessions, constructively corrects the behavior while preserving the team member's valuable enthusiasm and input.

text: A team member on parental leave will be returning soon, and the team has evolved significantly in their working practices during the absence. What is the BEST way to prepare for a smooth reintegration?

options.A: Prepare a summary of key process and team changes, and schedule time for them to be brought up to speed with support from the team before fully resuming their prior workload
options.B: Expect them to figure out all the changes independently upon return
options.C: Revert all recent team changes back to how things were before their leave
options.D: Assign them to a completely different role upon return without discussion

justification: Correct. Proactively preparing a summary of changes and providing supported ramp-up time reflects thoughtful, inclusive reintegration practice that helps the returning team member get back up to speed effectively.

text: A project leader notices that a team member frequently takes on tasks slightly outside their current skill level, sometimes resulting in extra support needed from others. What is the BEST way to view and address this pattern?

options.A: Prevent them from ever taking on stretch tasks to avoid any extra support burden
options.B: Publicly criticize them for taking on tasks beyond their current skill level
options.C: Recognize this as a growth opportunity, while working with the team member and others to ensure appropriate support is available without overburdening any single person
options.D: Ignore the pattern entirely since skill development happens naturally regardless of support

justification: Correct. Recognizing stretch assignments as legitimate growth opportunities, while ensuring balanced support so no single person is overburdened, supports both individual development and sustainable team capacity.

text: A team's Scrum Master leaves for an extended medical leave with no advance notice. What is the BEST immediate action for the team and organization?

options.A: Leave the team without any Scrum Master support until the original person returns, however long that takes
options.B: Cancel all Scrum events until the original Scrum Master returns
options.C: Permanently eliminate the Scrum Master role since the team can function without it
options.D: Arrange for a qualified interim Scrum Master or have an experienced team member temporarily take on key facilitation responsibilities, with organizational support as needed

justification: Correct. Arranging interim coverage, whether through a qualified interim Scrum Master or a supported team member, ensures continuity of essential facilitation and coaching functions during the unplanned absence.

text: A team member expresses that they feel their contributions are undervalued compared to more vocal teammates, even though their work quality is consistently high. What is the BEST way for the project leader to respond?

options.A: Suggest they become more vocal to match their more talkative teammates
options.B: Listen to their concern, acknowledge their contributions specifically, and explore ways to ensure their work receives appropriate visibility and recognition
options.C: Ignore the concern since work quality should speak for itself
options.D: Tell them their perception is incorrect without further discussion

justification: Correct. Listening, specifically acknowledging their contributions, and exploring ways to increase appropriate visibility addresses the concern constructively while respecting their working style.

text: A team member consistently arrives at Sprint Planning without having reviewed the Product Backlog items beforehand, slowing down the session for everyone. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Do all the preparation work for them going forward to avoid the delay
options.B: Publicly call out their lack of preparation during the session
options.C: Have a conversation to understand the reason for the lack of preparation and reinforce the shared expectation of reviewing items in advance
options.D: Exclude them from Sprint Planning until they change their behavior

justification: Correct. Understanding the reason behind the lack of preparation and reinforcing shared expectations addresses the root cause constructively while respecting the individual.

text: A cross-functional team includes members with very different working hours due to personal circumstances (e.g., caregiving responsibilities). What is the BEST way for the project leader to support effective collaboration?

options.A: Require everyone to work identical hours regardless of personal circumstances
options.B: Identify a reasonable core overlap window for essential collaboration while allowing flexibility outside of it, respecting individual circumstances
options.C: Assign team members with differing hours to entirely separate, disconnected workstreams
options.D: Eliminate all synchronous collaboration entirely to accommodate everyone's differing schedules

justification: Correct. Establishing a reasonable core overlap window while allowing flexibility outside of it balances the need for essential synchronous collaboration with respect for individual circumstances.

text: A team's Scrum Master observes that during Sprint Reviews, the Product Owner tends to speak on behalf of the Developers rather than letting them present their own work. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Require the Product Owner to be silent throughout the entire Sprint Review
options.B: Discuss with the Product Owner the value of Developers presenting their own work directly, as it builds their engagement and provides more authentic insight for stakeholders
options.C: Cancel Sprint Reviews since the current format is not working well
options.D: Ignore the pattern since the Product Owner has final authority over the product

justification: Correct. Discussing the value of Developers presenting their own work directly, both for their engagement and for more authentic stakeholder insight, is a constructive coaching approach to improve the Sprint Review's effectiveness.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate level of detail for a Work Breakdown Structure Dictionary entry for a complex, high-risk work package. What is the BEST guidance?

options.A: Omit the WBS Dictionary entirely for high-risk work packages to save time
options.B: Provide a level of detail proportional to the work package's complexity and risk, including clear scope description, acceptance criteria, and any specific technical requirements
options.C: Include only a work package title with no further description
options.D: Keep all WBS Dictionary entries identically brief regardless of the work package's complexity or risk

justification: Correct. Providing detail proportional to the work package's complexity and risk, including clear scope, acceptance criteria, and technical requirements, ensures adequate clarity where it matters most.

text: A project manager wants to determine how efficiently the project team is using its allocated budget relative to work completed. Which single metric BEST directly answers this?

options.A: Schedule Variance (SV)
options.B: Actual Cost (AC)
options.C: Planned Value (PV)
options.D: Cost Performance Index (CPI)

justification: Correct. The Cost Performance Index directly measures cost efficiency by comparing earned value to actual cost, precisely answering how efficiently the budget is being used relative to work completed.

text: A project manager is finalizing the procurement strategy and must decide whether to bundle several smaller purchases into a single larger contract or keep them as separate contracts. What is a KEY consideration in this decision?

options.A: Bundling always reduces risk regardless of context
options.B: The decision should be made without considering supplier market conditions
options.C: Separate contracts always guarantee lower total cost
options.D: Bundling can offer economies of scale and simplified management, but may reduce competition among smaller suppliers and increase reliance on a single vendor

justification: Correct. Bundling offers potential economies of scale and simpler contract management, but comes with trade-offs like reduced competition among smaller suppliers and increased single-vendor dependency risk, which must be weighed together.

text: A project manager discovers during a routine review that a quality control checkpoint was skipped for a batch of completed work due to schedule pressure. What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Skip quality control checkpoints going forward to maintain the current schedule pace
options.B: Accept the work as-is since it is likely fine
options.C: Discard the entire batch of work without any inspection
options.D: Perform the required quality control checkpoint retroactively before accepting the work, and address the root cause of why it was skipped

justification: Correct. Performing the required checkpoint retroactively, combined with addressing why it was skipped in the first place, ensures both quality assurance and prevention of recurrence.

text: A project manager needs to select the most appropriate estimating technique for a well-understood activity that is very similar to one completed multiple times before, with abundant reliable historical data available. Which technique is generally MOST appropriate?

options.A: Bottom-up estimating requiring extensive new decomposition despite abundant existing relevant data
options.B: Analogous estimating using expert judgment alone with no historical data
options.C: A rough order of magnitude guess with no supporting rationale
options.D: Parametric estimating using the reliable historical data to calculate a statistically grounded estimate

justification: Correct. Parametric estimating uses statistical relationships from reliable historical data to calculate a more precise estimate, making it the most appropriate technique when such abundant, reliable data is available.

text: A project manager is reviewing the project's risk register and notices that several risks have remained at 'identified' status for months with no analysis performed. What is the BEST corrective action?

options.A: Leave the risks as-is since they have not yet materialized
options.B: Assume all unanalyzed risks are low priority since they haven't been addressed yet
options.C: Remove all unanalyzed risks from the register to simplify tracking
options.D: Prioritize and perform qualitative (and quantitative where warranted) analysis on the outstanding risks to determine appropriate response strategies

justification: Correct. Prioritizing and performing proper analysis on outstanding risks ensures appropriate response strategies are developed proactively, rather than reactively after a risk materializes.

text: A project manager wants to ensure the project's lessons learned are actually used by future project teams rather than simply archived and forgotten. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Ensure lessons learned are categorized, easily searchable, and actively referenced during future project planning processes, potentially through a structured knowledge management system
options.B: Avoid documenting lessons learned since future teams rarely use them anyway
options.C: Simply store lessons learned in a document repository with no further action
options.D: Only share lessons learned verbally in informal conversations with no documentation

justification: Correct. Ensuring lessons learned are categorized, searchable, and actively integrated into future planning processes significantly increases the likelihood they will actually be used and provide organizational value.

text: A project manager needs to decide the appropriate frequency for formal status reporting to the steering committee. What is the BEST basis for this decision?

options.A: Report as infrequently as possible to minimize administrative overhead, regardless of project risk or pace
options.B: Report only when problems arise, with no regular cadence otherwise
options.C: Align reporting frequency with the project's risk profile, pace of change, and the steering committee's decision-making needs, as defined in the communications management plan
options.D: Report daily regardless of project characteristics or committee preferences

justification: Correct. Aligning reporting frequency with the project's risk profile, pace of change, and the committee's actual decision-making needs, as documented in the communications plan, reflects appropriate, tailored stakeholder communication.

text: A project manager is reviewing bids from three potential vendors for a critical deliverable. One bid is significantly lower than the other two, with no clear explanation for the difference. What is the BEST way to proceed?

options.A: Select the highest bid, assuming higher price always means better quality
options.B: Investigate the reason for the significantly lower bid to ensure the vendor fully understands the scope and can deliver at that price without compromising quality or reliability
options.C: Automatically eliminate the lowest bid without any investigation
options.D: Automatically select the lowest bid without further investigation

justification: Correct. Investigating the reason for a significantly lower bid ensures the vendor genuinely understands the scope and can deliver reliably, protecting the project from unexpected quality or delivery risks.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of scope creep within a single Sprint. What is the BEST practice to prevent this?

options.A: Eliminate Sprint Planning entirely so there is no defined scope to creep beyond
options.B: Allow the Product Owner to add or remove items freely at any point during the Sprint
options.C: Protect the Sprint Backlog once committed, directing any new urgent needs to the Product Backlog for consideration in future Sprints unless truly critical
options.D: Extend every Sprint whenever new requests arise mid-Sprint

justification: Correct. Protecting the committed Sprint Backlog while directing new needs to the Product Backlog for future prioritization (barring genuine emergencies) is the standard way to prevent scope creep within a Sprint.

text: A team wants to ensure their Increment is always in a releasable state, even if the Product Owner chooses not to release every Sprint. What does this require?

options.A: Only ensuring the code compiles without any further quality checks
options.B: A Definition of Done that includes all necessary quality, testing, and integration criteria to make the Increment genuinely usable
options.C: Releasing to production automatically at the end of every single Sprint regardless of business timing
options.D: Skipping all testing to speed up the Sprint

justification: Correct. A comprehensive Definition of Done that includes all necessary quality, testing, and integration criteria ensures the Increment is genuinely usable and releasable, even if the actual release timing is a separate business decision.

text: A Product Owner wants the team to work on multiple small, unrelated bug fixes and one large new feature within the same Sprint. The team is concerned about achieving a coherent Sprint Goal with such varied work. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Refuse to include any bug fixes in the Sprint
options.B: Proceed without any defined Sprint Goal since the work is too varied to unify
options.C: Automatically deprioritize the new feature in favor of the bug fixes without discussion
options.D: Work with the Product Owner to define a Sprint Goal that provides coherence across the varied work, such as 'improve product stability while delivering the new feature,' or negotiate splitting the work differently

justification: Correct. Working with the Product Owner to define a Sprint Goal that meaningfully ties the varied work together, or negotiating a different split, addresses the team's concern about coherence while still accommodating legitimate priorities.

text: A team's Increment includes a feature built based on an assumption that later proved incorrect during the Sprint Review. What is the BEST way for the team to handle this discovery?

options.A: Hide the incorrect assumption from stakeholders to avoid embarrassment
options.B: Blame whoever made the original assumption in front of stakeholders
options.C: Transparently acknowledge the incorrect assumption, discuss the implications with stakeholders, and incorporate the new understanding into future backlog prioritization
options.D: Ignore the new information and continue as if the assumption were still valid

justification: Correct. Transparently acknowledging the incorrect assumption, discussing implications, and incorporating new understanding into future planning reflects healthy, evidence-based, inspect-and-adapt practice.

text: A team wants to reduce the number of production incidents caused by insufficient testing of edge cases. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Strengthen the Definition of Done to explicitly require edge case testing, and incorporate techniques like exploratory testing or boundary value analysis into the team's practice
options.B: Skip testing entirely for features considered low-risk by the team
options.C: Only test the most common use cases, ignoring less frequent scenarios entirely
options.D: Reduce the amount of testing done to speed up delivery

justification: Correct. Explicitly requiring edge case testing in the Definition of Done, combined with techniques like exploratory testing or boundary value analysis, directly addresses the root cause of missed edge cases.

text: A team's Sprint Backlog visualization shows that most items move quickly through early stages but consistently stall in a 'Testing' column. What is the BEST way to diagnose and address this?

options.A: Ignore the bottleneck since testing naturally takes time
options.B: Investigate the root cause of the testing bottleneck (e.g., insufficient testers, unclear test requirements, environment issues) and address the specific constraint identified
options.C: Remove the Testing column from the board to make the bottleneck less visible
options.D: Simply add more developers to the team without addressing the testing stage specifically

justification: Correct. Investigating the specific root cause of the testing bottleneck and addressing that particular constraint directly (e.g., adding testing capacity, clarifying requirements, fixing environment issues) is the appropriate flow-improvement approach.

text: A team wants to improve how they estimate Product Backlog Items that involve integration with third-party systems, since these have historically been underestimated. What is the BEST way to improve future estimates for this type of work?

options.A: Double every estimate for third-party integration work without any further analysis
options.B: Review past estimation accuracy specifically for third-party integration work, identify common sources of underestimation, and adjust the team's estimation approach accordingly for this type of work
options.C: Stop taking on any work involving third-party integrations
options.D: Continue estimating third-party integration work the same way as before, assuming the pattern will eventually improve on its own

justification: Correct. Reviewing past estimation accuracy specifically for this type of work, identifying common underestimation sources, and adjusting the approach accordingly reflects genuine, evidence-based process improvement.

text: A team's Product Owner wants to understand which features are actually being used by customers after release, to inform future prioritization. What is the BEST way to gather this insight?

options.A: Avoid collecting any usage data since it is considered an unnecessary distraction from delivery
options.B: Ask a small, non-representative sample of internal employees about their personal feature preferences
options.C: Rely solely on the Product Owner's personal assumptions about feature popularity
options.D: Implement usage analytics and tracking for released features, and review this data regularly as part of backlog prioritization discussions

justification: Correct. Implementing usage analytics and regularly reviewing this data as part of prioritization discussions provides objective, evidence-based insight into actual feature usage, directly informing better prioritization decisions.

text: A team is debating whether to include non-functional requirements (e.g., performance, security) as separate backlog items or embed them within the Definition of Done for all items. What is generally the BEST approach for pervasive non-functional requirements?

options.A: Ignore non-functional requirements entirely since they are not visible to end users
options.B: Embed pervasive, broadly applicable non-functional requirements (like baseline performance or security standards) in the Definition of Done, while treating significant, feature-specific non-functional work as its own backlog item when warranted
options.C: Always create separate backlog items for every non-functional requirement, regardless of whether it applies broadly
options.D: Address non-functional requirements only after all functional features are fully complete

justification: Correct. Embedding pervasive, broadly applicable non-functional requirements in the Definition of Done ensures they are consistently applied to all work, while significant feature-specific non-functional needs can still be tracked as their own backlog items when they warrant dedicated attention.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a single Sprint Review becoming overwhelming due to too many completed items to demo. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Skip the Sprint Review demo altogether and only share a written list of completed items
options.B: Prioritize demoing the most valuable or complex items in depth, and provide a concise summary for smaller or routine items, keeping the session focused and valuable
options.C: Demo every single item in exhaustive detail regardless of time constraints
options.D: Cancel the Sprint Review entirely when there are many completed items

justification: Correct. Prioritizing depth for the most valuable or complex items, while summarizing smaller routine items, keeps the session focused, engaging, and an efficient use of stakeholders' time.

text: A team's Product Owner struggles to write clear, testable acceptance criteria for complex features involving multiple user roles. What is the BEST way to help improve this?

options.A: Avoid writing acceptance criteria for complex features since they are inherently difficult to define
options.B: Simplify all complex features into a single generic acceptance criterion regardless of actual complexity
options.C: Introduce a structured technique such as behavior-driven development (Given/When/Then) format, and collaborate with the Product Owner to co-develop clearer criteria for complex, multi-role features
options.D: Have the Development Team write all acceptance criteria without any Product Owner involvement

justification: Correct. Introducing a structured technique like Given/When/Then, combined with collaborative co-development, helps produce clearer, more testable acceptance criteria for genuinely complex, multi-role features.

text: A team notices that their Sprint Retrospective action items are rarely followed up on or completed by the next Retrospective. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Assign all action items to the Scrum Master personally regardless of who is best suited to address them
options.B: Limit the number of action items per Retrospective, assign clear ownership, and explicitly review progress on prior action items at the start of the next Retrospective
options.C: Stop identifying action items during Retrospectives since they are not being completed anyway
options.D: Create action items but never track or follow up on them going forward

justification: Correct. Limiting the number of action items to a manageable set, assigning clear ownership, and reviewing progress at the start of the next Retrospective creates accountability and follow-through, directly addressing the described problem.

text: A team wants to understand whether their current Sprint length (two weeks) is still appropriate given changes in the product's complexity and stakeholder feedback needs. What is the BEST way to evaluate this?

options.A: Periodically reflect during Retrospectives on whether the current Sprint length still serves the team's needs for feedback cadence and delivery, adjusting if warranted based on evidence
options.B: Change Sprint length randomly every few Sprints without any specific rationale
options.C: Assume Sprint length should always remain fixed at two weeks regardless of context, since that is a common industry default
options.D: Never reconsider Sprint length once it has been initially set, regardless of changing circumstances

justification: Correct. Periodically reflecting on whether the current cadence still serves the team's evolving needs, and adjusting based on evidence, reflects appropriate, evidence-based continuous improvement of team practices.

text: A team's Product Owner asks the team to build a feature exactly as described by one specific stakeholder, without considering input from other affected stakeholders. What is the BEST way for the team to respond?

options.A: Refuse to build the feature until every possible stakeholder is consulted
options.B: Build the feature exactly as described without raising any concerns
options.C: Independently reach out to other stakeholders without involving the Product Owner
options.D: Raise the concern about potentially missing other stakeholder perspectives, and suggest the Product Owner gather broader input before finalizing the requirements

justification: Correct. Constructively raising the concern and suggesting broader input reflects the team's collaborative role in supporting good product decisions while respecting the Product Owner's ultimate authority over requirements.

text: A team's velocity has been steadily increasing over several Sprints. The Product Owner wants to use this trend to promise stakeholders an accelerated delivery timeline for all remaining work. What is the BEST way for the team to respond?

options.A: Assume the trend will continue indefinitely without any further analysis
options.B: Refuse to discuss the topic at all
options.C: Agree to the accelerated promise without any further discussion
options.D: Discuss the reasons behind the velocity increase (e.g., team maturity, simpler remaining work) to assess whether the trend is likely to continue before committing to an accelerated timeline

justification: Correct. Discussing the underlying reasons for the velocity increase, and assessing whether it's likely to continue for the remaining, potentially different work, supports a more informed, evidence-based commitment rather than a naive extrapolation.

text: A team's Sprint Backlog includes a technical spike with an unclear expected outcome, leading to some confusion about what would make the spike 'complete.' What is the BEST way to structure a technical spike to avoid this?

options.A: Avoid using spikes altogether since they are inherently too ambiguous to be useful
options.B: Allow the spike to continue indefinitely until every possible related question is answered
options.C: Define a clear, timeboxed scope for the spike, including the specific questions to be answered or knowledge to be gained, so the team knows when it is complete
options.D: Leave the spike entirely open-ended with no defined boundaries or expected outcome

justification: Correct. Defining a clear, timeboxed scope with specific questions to answer gives the spike clear boundaries and a definition of completion, which is standard best practice for structuring effective technical spikes.

text: A project manager's organization announces a new policy requiring all vendor contracts above a certain value to include specific cybersecurity requirements, effective immediately, including for contracts currently in negotiation. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Apply the new requirements only to future contracts, exempting all contracts already in negotiation
options.B: Continue negotiations exactly as originally planned, ignoring the new policy
options.C: Incorporate the new cybersecurity requirements into ongoing vendor negotiations and update the procurement documentation accordingly
options.D: Cancel all ongoing vendor negotiations entirely due to the new requirement

justification: Correct. Incorporating the new requirements into ongoing negotiations and updating documentation accordingly reflects appropriate, timely adaptation to a newly effective organizational policy that explicitly applies to contracts already in progress.

text: A project manager's organization is evaluating whether to enter a joint venture with another company for a large infrastructure project. The project manager is asked to provide input on project-related risks associated with this potential partnership. What is the BEST way to fulfill this request?

options.A: Refuse to engage with the topic since it is a purely strategic business decision
options.B: Provide an objective assessment of project-specific risks (e.g., governance complexity, differing organizational processes, communication challenges) based on relevant project management expertise
options.C: Provide only a personal opinion on whether the joint venture should proceed, without any risk analysis
options.D: Decline to provide input since joint venture decisions are outside typical project manager responsibilities

justification: Correct. Providing an objective, expertise-based assessment of project-specific risks associated with the partnership structure supports informed organizational decision-making while staying within the project manager's relevant domain of expertise.

text: A project manager's organization is facing a class-action lawsuit related to a previous, unrelated product. This has created significant organizational stress and uncertainty. The project manager's current project is unrelated to the lawsuit. What is the BEST way to manage the team through this period?

options.A: Halt the current project entirely due to the organizational uncertainty
options.B: Encourage the team to speculate extensively about the lawsuit's potential outcomes
options.C: Pretend the lawsuit does not exist and avoid any acknowledgment
options.D: Acknowledge the broader organizational stress with empathy, while helping the team maintain focus on their unrelated project's clear, unaffected objectives

justification: Correct. Acknowledging broader organizational stress empathetically, while helping the team maintain focus on their own clear, unaffected objectives, supports both wellbeing and continued productive project execution.

text: A project manager's organization is considering divesting the business unit that owns the current project. What is the BEST role for the project manager in this situation?

options.A: Refuse to provide any information about the project to protect it from being divested
options.B: Make the divestiture decision personally since the project manager understands the project best
options.C: Immediately stop all project work in anticipation of a potential divestiture
options.D: Provide accurate project status and relevant information to support leadership's divestiture evaluation, while continuing to manage the project responsibly until a decision is made

justification: Correct. Providing accurate information to support leadership's evaluation, while continuing responsible project management until an actual decision is made, reflects appropriate professional conduct during organizational strategic uncertainty.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new export control regulations that restrict sharing certain technical specifications with team members based in specific countries. What is the BEST way to address this within the current project?

options.A: Remove all international team members from the project entirely, regardless of whether they are actually affected by the restriction
options.B: Share all information as before and address any compliance issues only if they are formally raised
options.C: Work with legal/compliance to determine which specific information is restricted, and adjust information access and team assignments accordingly to remain compliant
options.D: Ignore the regulations since the project was already underway before they took effect

justification: Correct. Working with legal/compliance to precisely determine what is restricted and adjusting access and assignments accordingly ensures targeted, appropriate compliance without unnecessary overreach.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a potential acquisition of a smaller competitor, which could bring additional product capabilities the team's product currently lacks. What should the product leader do while this is still being evaluated?

options.A: Continue delivering against current, validated priorities while staying informed of the acquisition evaluation, ready to adapt the roadmap once the outcome is known
options.B: Ignore the potential acquisition entirely since it has not yet been confirmed
options.C: Halt all current backlog work in anticipation of the potential acquisition
options.D: Publicly announce the potential acquisition to stakeholders before it is finalized

justification: Correct. Continuing to deliver against current priorities while staying informed and ready to adapt reflects a balanced, pragmatic response to genuine but still-uncertain strategic developments.

text: An agile team's organization introduces a new internal policy requiring all customer-facing product changes to undergo a formal accessibility review before release. The team has not previously had a formal accessibility review process. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Ignore the new policy since it was not part of the team's original way of working
options.B: Integrate an accessibility review step into the team's Definition of Done or release process, and add any necessary remediation work to the backlog
options.C: Refuse to release any further customer-facing changes until the organization removes the policy
options.D: Delegate accessibility compliance entirely to a separate team with no integration into the current team's workflow

justification: Correct. Integrating the accessibility review into the Definition of Done or release process, and adding necessary remediation work to the backlog, reflects proper integration of a new organizational requirement into the team's actual workflow.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a market where a major economic downturn has significantly reduced customer spending on discretionary products, directly affecting the team's product category. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Reassess the Product Backlog priorities in light of the changed economic conditions, potentially emphasizing value-oriented features or cost-saving benefits that resonate during a downturn
options.B: Immediately halt all product development entirely due to the downturn
options.C: Wait until the downturn fully ends before considering any backlog changes
options.D: Continue with the existing roadmap unchanged, assuming customer behavior will not shift due to the downturn

justification: Correct. Reassessing priorities in light of changed economic conditions, potentially emphasizing features that resonate with more cost-conscious customers during a downturn, reflects adaptive, market-aware product leadership.

text: An agile team's organization begins requiring quarterly business reviews where product teams must demonstrate return on investment for their initiatives. What is the BEST way for the product leader to prepare for these reviews?

options.A: Fabricate favorable metrics if actual data does not clearly demonstrate strong ROI
options.B: Delay preparing until the review is imminent, using only anecdotal impressions
options.C: Refuse to participate in the reviews since agile product development should not be subject to ROI scrutiny
options.D: Establish ongoing tracking of relevant value metrics tied to delivered increments throughout each quarter, so the review can draw on genuine, accumulated evidence

justification: Correct. Establishing ongoing tracking of relevant value metrics throughout the quarter ensures the review can draw on genuine, accumulated evidence, reflecting proactive alignment with a legitimate organizational governance requirement.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a strategic pivot into a new industry vertical that would require substantially different domain expertise than the team currently possesses. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Proceed with the pivot without any assessment of the team's readiness
options.B: Refuse to support the pivot since it falls outside the team's current expertise
options.C: Assume the current team can seamlessly handle the new domain without any additional support or learning
options.D: Assess the team's current domain knowledge gaps relative to the new vertical, and plan for necessary training, hiring, or expert consultation to support a successful pivot

justification: Correct. Assessing actual domain knowledge gaps and planning for training, hiring, or expert consultation reflects proactive, realistic preparation for a strategic pivot requiring new expertise.

text: An agile team's organization is required to comply with a new industry-wide standard for interoperability with other companies' products. What is the BEST way for the product leader to plan for this?

options.A: Research the specific interoperability requirements and add prioritized backlog items to achieve compliance within the required timeframe
options.B: Assume the product already meets the standard without verification
options.C: Ignore the standard since interoperability with competitors is not seen as a priority
options.D: Wait until a customer specifically complains about the lack of interoperability before taking any action

justification: Correct. Researching the specific requirements and adding prioritized backlog items ensures the organization achieves compliance within the required timeframe, integrating the standard into planned, trackable work.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a jurisdiction that recently passed a law requiring specific consumer protection disclosures for the product's category. What is the BEST way for the product leader to ensure compliance?

options.A: Ignore the new law since it was passed after the product was already launched
options.B: Assume the legal team will handle all compliance without any need for backlog integration
options.C: Add a vague, generic backlog item without any specific requirements or acceptance criteria
options.D: Coordinate with legal to understand the specific disclosure requirements, then translate them into clear, prioritized backlog items with appropriate acceptance criteria

justification: Correct. Coordinating with legal to understand specifics, then translating them into clear, prioritized backlog items with defined acceptance criteria, ensures the requirement is properly implemented and verifiable.

text: An agile team's organization is negotiating a major partnership agreement that would require the product to support a new third-party payment processor within a tight, externally imposed timeframe. What is the BEST way for the product leader to handle this?

options.A: Assess the technical scope and team capacity required, then provide an honest, evidence-based feasibility assessment to inform the partnership negotiation before final commitment
options.B: Commit to the timeframe without first assessing the technical scope or team capacity required
options.C: Assume the integration will be simple without any actual technical assessment
options.D: Refuse to support the partnership since it involves an externally imposed timeframe

justification: Correct. Providing an honest, evidence-based feasibility assessment before final commitment supports informed negotiation decisions, balancing the business opportunity with realistic delivery capability.

text: An agile team's organization is preparing for a leadership transition as the current CEO plans to retire within the year. The incoming CEO has publicly indicated different strategic priorities than the current leadership. What is the BEST way for the product leader to prepare the team for this transition?

options.A: Halt all current work in anticipation of the leadership change
options.B: Ignore the upcoming transition entirely since it has not yet occurred
options.C: Continue delivering against current validated priorities while staying informed of the incoming CEO's publicly stated direction, preparing to adapt the roadmap as the transition unfolds and more concrete direction emerges
options.D: Immediately pivot the entire roadmap based on the incoming CEO's public statements before they have taken office

justification: Correct. Continuing to deliver against current, still-valid priorities while staying informed and ready to adapt as more concrete direction emerges reflects a balanced, pragmatic response to an anticipated but not yet fully realized organizational change.

text: A project manager discovers that a team member has been quietly resolving a colleague's repeated errors without telling anyone, out of a desire to avoid conflict. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Thank them for their diligence, then address the root performance issue directly with the underperforming colleague and encourage open communication about workload issues
options.B: Reprimand the team member for not following the chain of command
options.C: Praise the team member for handling it quietly and encourage them to continue
options.D: Ignore the situation since the errors are being resolved either way

justification: Correct. Acknowledging the covering team member's diligence while directly addressing the root performance issue with the other colleague, and encouraging open communication, resolves both the immediate and underlying problems constructively.

text: A team's Sprint Backlog contains an item that turns out to require expertise from a team member who is on vacation for the remainder of the Sprint. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Discuss with the team whether the item can be deferred, partially completed, or handled through knowledge transfer/documentation, adjusting the Sprint plan transparently
options.B: Cancel the entire Sprint due to the unavailability
options.C: Force another team member without the needed expertise to complete the item regardless of quality risk
options.D: Wait silently until the team member returns without informing the Product Owner

justification: Correct. Transparently discussing realistic options (deferral, partial completion, or knowledge transfer) and adjusting the plan accordingly reflects Scrum's transparency and adaptive planning principles.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring offering the product in a freemium model, which is a significant departure from their existing subscription-only approach. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Implement the freemium model immediately without any analysis
options.B: Research the business implications of the freemium model, including impact on revenue, user segmentation, and required product changes, before committing significant backlog investment
options.C: Ignore the idea since it deviates from the current business model
options.D: Delegate the entire decision to the Development Team without business input

justification: Correct. Researching the business implications before committing significant backlog investment reflects responsible, evidence-based product strategy for a major business model shift.

text: A project manager is developing the project schedule and needs to determine the sequence of activities. Which technique is MOST commonly used to establish these logical relationships?

options.A: Pareto analysis
options.B: Earned value analysis
options.C: Resource leveling
options.D: Precedence Diagramming Method (PDM)

justification: Correct. The Precedence Diagramming Method is the standard technique used to construct a schedule network diagram showing the logical sequence and dependencies between activities.

text: A team member consistently offers to take notes and handle administrative tasks during meetings, seemingly to avoid participating in technical discussions. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Assume they have nothing valuable to contribute technically
options.B: Have a supportive conversation to understand whether this reflects a genuine preference, a confidence issue, or another underlying cause, and encourage broader participation as appropriate
options.C: Forbid them from taking notes to force participation in discussions
options.D: Continue letting them handle administrative tasks exclusively without further inquiry

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation to understand the underlying reason, followed by appropriate encouragement, respects the individual while addressing any potential confidence or engagement issue constructively.

text: Which of the following are valid outputs of the Develop Schedule process? (Select TWO)

options.A: Schedule baseline
options.B: Project schedule
options.C: Stakeholder register
options.D: Team charter

justification: Correct. The schedule baseline, the approved version of the schedule used for comparison against actual results, is a key output of the Develop Schedule process. / Correct. The project schedule itself, showing planned dates for activities and milestones, is the primary output of the Develop Schedule process.

text: A project manager's organization is required to comply with a newly enacted whistleblower protection law that affects how internal reporting of concerns must be handled. What should the project manager do?

options.A: Ignore the law since it primarily concerns HR policy, not project management
options.B: Wait for HR to independently communicate the change with no project-level follow-up
options.C: Ensure the project team is aware of the new reporting protections and that project-level practices align with the organization's updated compliance requirements
options.D: Actively discourage team members from raising any concerns to avoid triggering whistleblower processes

justification: Correct. Ensuring the team is aware of new protections and that project practices align with updated compliance requirements reflects responsible integration of a legal/organizational change into project-level practice.

text: A team member consistently offers overly optimistic estimates during Planning Poker, then struggles to complete the work within the Sprint. What is the BEST way to address this pattern?

options.A: Automatically double all of that team member's estimates without discussion
options.B: Exclude the team member from future estimation sessions
options.C: Ignore the pattern since estimation is inherently imprecise
options.D: Have a supportive conversation exploring the reasons behind the optimism, and encourage using historical data and considering edge cases during future estimation

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation exploring the reasons behind consistent optimism, combined with encouraging evidence-based practices, addresses the root cause constructively while building better estimation habits.

text: A team wants to visualize dependencies between Product Backlog Items to better plan Sprint sequencing. What is the BEST tool or technique for this purpose?

options.A: A dependency mapping tool or visual board that explicitly shows relationships between backlog items
options.B: A simple flat list with no dependency information
options.C: A generic project status report with no item-level detail
options.D: A financial forecasting spreadsheet

justification: Correct. A dependency mapping tool or visual board explicitly showing relationships between items directly supports better understanding and planning of Sprint sequencing based on actual dependencies.

text: Match each type of organizational culture dimension to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: The degree to which an organization is willing to accept uncertainty in pursuit of opportunity
The degree of formal levels of authority and decision-making layers within the organization
The degree to which the organization values individual achievement versus team/group outcomes
The degree to which the organization embraces or resists organizational change

justification: Risk tolerance reflects how much uncertainty an organization is willing to accept, directly shaping how projects approach risk-taking and innovation. / This dimension reflects the number of formal authority layers, influencing how decisions are made and how quickly they can be reached. / This dimension reflects whether the culture emphasizes individual recognition or collective, team-based outcomes, shaping motivation and collaboration patterns. / This dimension reflects how readily the organization embraces versus resists change, directly affecting how easily new initiatives or process improvements can be adopted.

text: A project manager notices that a team member who recently disclosed a chronic health condition seems hesitant to request reasonable accommodations, fearing it might affect how they are perceived. What is the BEST way to respond?

options.A: Publicly announce their condition to the team to normalize discussing health issues
options.B: Assume no accommodations are needed since the team member hasn't formally requested any
options.C: Wait for the team member to formally request accommodations without proactively addressing the concern
options.D: Have a private, supportive conversation to reassure them that reasonable accommodations are appropriate and welcomed, and connect them with relevant organizational resources if needed

justification: Correct. A private, supportive conversation that reassures and connects them with appropriate resources addresses their hesitation while respecting their autonomy and privacy, supporting genuine inclusion.

text: A team wants to better track how much of their capacity each Sprint is consumed by unplanned work (e.g., production support) versus planned Sprint Backlog items. What is the BEST way to gain this insight?

options.A: Avoid tracking unplanned work since agile teams should not measure such details
options.B: Explicitly track and categorize unplanned work separately from planned Sprint items, reviewing the ratio regularly to inform future capacity planning
options.C: Assume unplanned work is negligible without any tracking
options.D: Combine all work into a single undifferentiated category to simplify tracking

justification: Correct. Explicitly tracking and categorizing unplanned work separately, then reviewing the ratio regularly, provides the empirical insight needed to plan future Sprint capacity more realistically.

text: A project manager's organization operates in an industry where a major professional association just released updated best-practice guidelines, though these are not legally mandatory. What is the BEST way to consider this development?

options.A: Immediately implement every aspect of the guidelines regardless of project context or cost
options.B: Wait until the guidelines eventually become legally mandatory before considering them
options.C: Ignore the guidelines entirely since they are not legally mandatory
options.D: Evaluate the guidelines' relevance and potential value to the project, and consider voluntary adoption where it would improve quality, risk management, or stakeholder confidence

justification: Correct. Evaluating the guidelines' relevance and considering voluntary adoption where beneficial reflects a thoughtful, value-based approach to incorporating emerging industry standards.

text: A project manager is calculating the To-Complete Performance Index (TCPI) and finds it significantly higher than the current CPI. What does this indicate?

options.A: The team will need to perform significantly more efficiently than their current pace to meet the budget, which may not be realistic and warrants further analysis
options.B: The project is performing better than planned and needs no attention
options.C: The TCPI calculation is likely incorrect and should be disregarded
options.D: The project's budget should be immediately increased without further analysis

justification: Correct. A TCPI notably higher than current CPI signals that maintaining the budget will require significantly improved efficiency going forward, which may not be realistic and warrants further analysis of budget or scope options.

text: A team's Product Owner is new to the role and unsure how to balance stakeholder requests with the Development Team's technical recommendations. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to support them?

options.A: Coach the Product Owner on effective prioritization techniques and facilitate structured conversations between them and the Development Team to build their confidence and judgment over time
options.B: Make prioritization decisions on the Product Owner's behalf until they gain more experience
options.C: Provide no support since the Product Owner should learn entirely independently
options.D: Tell the Product Owner to always defer entirely to the Development Team's recommendations

justification: Correct. Coaching on prioritization techniques and facilitating structured conversations builds the new Product Owner's confidence and judgment over time, reflecting the Scrum Master's supportive coaching responsibility.

text: A team wants to identify which parts of their workflow are causing the most delays across multiple Sprints. What is the BEST visualization technique to use?

options.A: A pie chart showing team member headcount by role
options.B: A Cumulative Flow Diagram showing the accumulation of work items across different workflow stages over time
options.C: An org chart showing reporting relationships
options.D: A simple text list of completed items with no visual representation of flow

justification: Correct. A Cumulative Flow Diagram visually shows how work accumulates across workflow stages over time, making bottlenecks (widening bands) clearly visible, directly addressing the need to identify delay-causing stages.

text: A team member frequently brings up unrelated personal grievances about the organization during Sprint Retrospectives, derailing the intended focus on team process improvement. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to handle this?

options.A: Acknowledge the concern respectfully, redirect the discussion back to the Retrospective's intended scope, and suggest an appropriate separate channel for the broader organizational grievance
options.B: Publicly dismiss the team member's concerns as irrelevant and unimportant
options.C: Cancel future Retrospectives to avoid this recurring disruption
options.D: Allow the grievances to continue since all feedback should be welcomed regardless of relevance

justification: Correct. Respectfully acknowledging the concern while redirecting to the appropriate scope, and suggesting a proper channel for the broader issue, maintains both empathy and effective facilitation.

text: Which of the following are appropriate practices for effective Backlog Refinement? (Select TWO)

options.A: Breaking down large items into smaller, more manageable pieces
options.B: Clarifying and adding acceptance criteria to items nearing the top of the backlog
options.C: Finalizing the complete technical implementation details for all future work
options.D: Assigning specific individuals to specific future tasks months in advance

justification: Correct. Breaking down large items into smaller, more manageable pieces is a core practice of effective Backlog Refinement, improving estimability and enabling incremental delivery. / Correct. Clarifying and adding acceptance criteria to items nearing the top of the backlog ensures they are well-understood and ready for future Sprint Planning.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a market where a recent high-profile security breach at a competitor has significantly heightened customer awareness of data security practices. What should the product leader consider doing?

options.A: Reassess the product's security posture and consider communicating relevant security practices transparently to reassure customers, along with prioritizing any needed security improvements
options.B: Avoid any public communication about security to prevent drawing attention to the topic
options.C: Assume the breach is irrelevant since it happened to a different company
options.D: Wait for customers to explicitly ask about security before considering any action

justification: Correct. Reassessing security posture, transparently communicating relevant practices, and prioritizing needed improvements directly addresses the shifted market sensitivity and demonstrates proactive customer trust-building.

text: A project manager needs to formally close out a completed contract with a vendor. What is the BEST FIRST step in this process?

options.A: Simply stop communicating with the vendor once the deliverables are received
options.B: Skip formal closure since the contract work is already complete
options.C: Verify that all deliverables have been formally accepted and all contractual terms and obligations have been satisfactorily fulfilled before proceeding with formal closure
options.D: Immediately release the final payment without any verification of deliverable acceptance

justification: Correct. Verifying formal acceptance of all deliverables and satisfaction of contractual obligations before proceeding with closure is the standard, appropriate first step in procurement closure, protecting both parties' interests.

text: A project manager notices that team members from a recently merged company feel like outsiders compared to original team members, despite having equally relevant skills. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Assume the dynamic will resolve naturally over time without any deliberate action
options.B: Keep the two groups working on separate workstreams indefinitely to avoid friction
options.C: Actively work to integrate the merged team members through inclusive team-building activities, equitable task distribution, and explicit recognition of their contributions
options.D: Ignore the dynamic since the merger was a business decision outside the project manager's control

justification: Correct. Actively fostering integration through inclusive activities, equitable task distribution, and explicit recognition directly addresses the outsider dynamic and builds a more cohesive team.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of losing important context about why certain technical decisions were made in the past. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Rely solely on individual memory with no documentation
options.B: Avoid documenting decisions since agile favors working software over documentation
options.C: Document every minor technical detail exhaustively regardless of significance
options.D: Maintain lightweight architecture decision records or similar documentation capturing the context and rationale for significant technical decisions

justification: Correct. Lightweight architecture decision records capture the rationale for significant decisions efficiently, preserving valuable context without excessive documentation overhead.

text: An agile team's organization is considering entering a strategic alliance with a nonprofit to co-develop a socially impactful feature, which would require balancing commercial and social impact goals. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Refuse to engage with the nonprofit since the organization is primarily commercial
options.B: Explore how the collaboration could align commercial and social impact objectives, incorporating any resulting backlog items based on genuine mutual value
options.C: Delay any engagement indefinitely without exploring the opportunity
options.D: Fully prioritize the nonprofit's needs over all existing commercial priorities without any assessment

justification: Correct. Exploring how the collaboration could align commercial and social objectives, and incorporating resulting work based on genuine mutual value, reflects thoughtful strategic evaluation of a new business environment opportunity.

text: A project manager needs to determine the most appropriate quality control sampling technique for a batch of manufactured components. What is a KEY consideration in this decision?

options.A: The acceptable quality level and the cost/risk trade-off between sampling and 100% inspection
options.B: The number of employees currently on shift
options.C: The color of the components
options.D: The time of year the components were manufactured

justification: Correct. The acceptable quality level and the cost/risk trade-off between sampling and full inspection are key considerations in determining the appropriate sampling technique and sample size for quality control.

text: A team member consistently volunteers for on-call support duties, even when it's not their turn, apparently to avoid other types of work they find less appealing. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Have a conversation to understand their preferences and concerns about other work, while ensuring on-call responsibilities remain fairly distributed across the team
options.B: Allow the pattern to continue since on-call coverage is valuable regardless of motivation
options.C: Permanently assign them to on-call duties exclusively going forward
options.D: Publicly call out the pattern as an attempt to avoid other responsibilities

justification: Correct. Understanding their preferences and concerns, while ensuring fair distribution of on-call duties, addresses both potential underlying issues and team fairness constructively.

text: Which of the following are valid techniques for developing a project budget? (Select TWO)

options.A: Cost aggregation of work package estimates
options.B: Reserve analysis to determine contingency and management reserves
options.C: Stakeholder satisfaction surveys
options.D: Team member vacation schedules

justification: Correct. Cost aggregation, summing work package estimates up through control accounts to the project total, is a fundamental technique for developing the project budget. / Correct. Reserve analysis, determining appropriate contingency and management reserves, is a standard technique used in developing a comprehensive project budget.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new workplace safety regulations following a recent industry accident at another company. What should the project manager do to ensure compliance on a current construction project?

options.A: Continue current safety practices unchanged since the accident happened at a different company
options.B: Wait for a formal audit before considering any changes to safety practices
options.C: Review the new regulations, assess the project's current practices against them, and implement any necessary updates to safety protocols and training
options.D: Halt the entire project indefinitely due to the industry-wide concern

justification: Correct. Reviewing new regulations, assessing current practices, and implementing necessary updates reflects proactive, responsible compliance management following a regulatory change.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that during Sprint Planning, the team routinely defers to the most senior developer's estimates without independently considering their own perspectives. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Require the senior developer to always estimate last in every discussion, with no other changes to the process
options.B: Ask the senior developer to stop participating in estimation entirely
options.C: Continue the current pattern since the senior developer's estimates are usually accurate
options.D: Introduce techniques like anonymous simultaneous estimation (e.g., Planning Poker) that reduce anchoring bias and encourage independent thinking before group discussion

justification: Correct. Techniques like Planning Poker, where estimates are revealed simultaneously, specifically reduce anchoring bias by encouraging independent thinking before group discussion, directly addressing the described pattern.

text: A team's Increment includes a feature that passed all automated tests but received negative feedback from users during a limited beta release regarding usability. What is the BEST way for the team to respond?

options.A: Treat the usability feedback as valuable additional information, and add prioritized backlog items to address the specific concerns raised
options.B: Ignore the usability feedback since automated tests already passed
options.C: Immediately roll back the feature entirely without further investigation
options.D: Dismiss the feedback since it came from a small beta group, not the full user base

justification: Correct. Treating usability feedback as valuable additional information and adding prioritized backlog items to address specific concerns reflects appropriate, evidence-based response to real user feedback.

text: Match each type of value delivery metric to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Measures how satisfied customers are with the delivered product or service
Measures the likelihood of customers recommending the product to others
Measures the elapsed time from concept or decision to actual product availability to customers
Measures the financial return generated relative to the investment made

justification: Customer satisfaction scores directly measure how happy customers are with what has been delivered, a key indicator of value realization. / NPS measures customer loyalty and advocacy by assessing how likely customers are to recommend the product, a valuable indicator of perceived value. / Time to market measures how quickly value reaches customers, an important metric for competitive responsiveness and value realization speed. / ROI measures the financial value generated relative to what was invested, a core metric for assessing overall project or product financial success.

text: A project manager wants to build stronger relationships with functional managers whose resources are frequently needed for the project. What is the BEST long-term strategy?

options.A: Avoid engaging with functional managers directly and communicate only through formal written requests
options.B: Escalate every resource request immediately to senior management rather than working with functional managers directly
options.C: Proactively build ongoing relationships through regular informal check-ins and transparency about upcoming resource needs, beyond just conflict situations
options.D: Only interact with functional managers when a specific resource conflict arises

justification: Correct. Proactively building relationships through regular check-ins and transparency about upcoming needs establishes trust and goodwill before conflicts arise, supporting smoother collaboration overall.

text: A team wants to establish a shared understanding of what 'value' means for their specific product, to guide prioritization decisions more consistently. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Collaboratively define clear value criteria (e.g., customer impact, revenue potential, strategic alignment) with the Product Owner and stakeholders, and consistently apply them during prioritization
