options.D: Ignore the behavior since virtual meetings inherently invite multitasking

justification: Correct. A private conversation addressing the impact while exploring underlying causes (like meeting relevance or workload) constructively addresses both the behavior and potential root issues.

text: A team member consistently takes an unusually long time to respond to direct messages during working hours, causing delays in quick clarifications. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Have a conversation to understand their communication preferences and any workload factors, and agree on reasonable response-time expectations together
options.B: Stop using direct messages entirely for this team member
options.C: Escalate to management immediately without any direct conversation
options.D: Assume they are being deliberately unresponsive and reprimand them

justification: Correct. Understanding their communication preferences and workload, then agreeing on reasonable expectations together, addresses the issue constructively and collaboratively.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a particular team member is often the target of good-natured teasing that seems to have crossed into feeling uncomfortable for that person, though they haven't explicitly complained. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Assume the teasing is fine since it appears good-natured on the surface
options.B: Publicly announce that all teasing must stop immediately without any investigation
options.C: Privately check in with the individual to understand their actual comfort level, and address the team dynamic if the teasing is indeed unwelcome
options.D: Wait until the person explicitly complains before taking any action

justification: Correct. Privately checking in to understand actual comfort level, then addressing the dynamic if genuinely unwelcome, respects the individual's potential discomfort while avoiding unfounded overreaction.

text: A team member consistently volunteers to lead new initiatives but then struggles to follow through once the initial excitement fades. What is the BEST way to support this pattern constructively?

options.A: Publicly criticize them each time they fail to follow through
options.B: Ignore the pattern since enthusiasm for new initiatives is generally positive
options.C: Have a conversation about sustaining follow-through, and help them build structures (like milestones or accountability check-ins) to support completing what they start
options.D: Stop letting them volunteer for anything going forward

justification: Correct. Discussing follow-through challenges and building supportive structures like milestones or check-ins helps address the specific gap while preserving their valuable enthusiasm and initiative.

text: A team's Scrum Master wants to help a newly self-organizing team develop better internal conflict resolution skills, rather than always relying on the Scrum Master to mediate. What is the BEST long-term approach?

options.A: Refuse to help with any conflicts immediately, without any coaching transition
options.B: Continue mediating every conflict personally to ensure quick resolution
options.C: Assign a single team member to be the permanent, sole conflict mediator
options.D: Gradually coach the team on conflict resolution techniques, stepping back to let them attempt resolution themselves first, while remaining available for support if needed

justification: Correct. Gradually coaching and stepping back, while remaining available for support, builds the team's own capability over time, which is the standard approach to developing self-organizing team maturity.

text: A team member frequently expresses that they feel excluded from informal social conversations among other team members, despite being included in all formal meetings. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Explore ways to foster more inclusive informal interactions, such as structured social touchpoints, while being mindful not to force artificial socializing
options.B: Require all team members to socialize with everyone equally at all times
options.C: Ignore the concern since formal meeting inclusion is what matters most
options.D: Assume the exclusion is intentional and reprimand the other team members

justification: Correct. Exploring inclusive informal touchpoints, while avoiding forced socializing, respects natural social dynamics while genuinely working to improve inclusion.

text: A team's Product Owner wants to better understand the Development Team's technical constraints before finalizing priorities, but historically hasn't asked many technical questions. What is the BEST way to encourage this collaboration?

options.A: Avoid discussing technical constraints since the Product Owner has not historically asked about them
options.B: Encourage and facilitate regular technical context-sharing sessions where Developers proactively explain relevant constraints in accessible terms
options.C: Have the Developers make all prioritization decisions without Product Owner input on technical trade-offs
options.D: Tell the Product Owner that technical details are not their concern

justification: Correct. Facilitating regular, accessible technical context-sharing helps the Product Owner make better-informed prioritization decisions, actively building the collaboration the scenario seeks.

text: Which of the following are examples of effective team-building activities for a newly formed cross-functional team? (Select TWO)

options.A: A structured exercise where team members share their working styles and preferences
options.B: Co-creating a team charter defining shared values and working agreements
options.C: Assigning all tasks without any team member input
options.D: Prohibiting any informal conversation during work hours

justification: Correct. Sharing working styles and preferences helps team members understand and adapt to each other, a valuable early team-building exercise for cross-functional teams. / Correct. Co-creating a team charter with shared values and working agreements is a foundational team-building practice that builds shared ownership and clarity.

text: A team member consistently expresses skepticism about whether their individual contributions genuinely matter to the project's overall success. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Dismiss their skepticism as an overreaction without further discussion
options.B: Have a conversation to understand their perspective, and provide specific, concrete examples of how their contributions have meaningfully impacted the project
options.C: Ignore the concern since all team members' contributions are inherently equally valuable regardless of the individual's perception
options.D: Assign them only the most trivial tasks to match their perceived low importance

justification: Correct. Understanding their perspective and providing specific, concrete examples of impact directly addresses their concern with tangible evidence, supporting their sense of purpose and contribution.

text: Match each communication barrier to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: Team members from different technical backgrounds using the same term to mean different things
Poor internet connectivity disrupting a virtual meeting
A team member hesitant to speak up due to fear of judgment
Differing norms about appropriate directness in feedback across cultures

justification: Semantic barriers arise when the same words or terms carry different meanings for different people, causing miscommunication despite using shared vocabulary. / Physical barriers include environmental or technical obstacles, such as poor connectivity, that disrupt effective communication. / Psychological barriers include internal factors like fear of judgment that prevent someone from communicating openly, even when no external barrier exists. / Cultural barriers arise from differing cultural norms and expectations around communication styles, such as varying comfort with direct feedback.

text: A team member consistently provides feedback that is technically accurate but delivered in a way that feels condescending to recipients. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Tell them to stop giving feedback since the tone is problematic
options.B: Ignore the tone issue since the feedback content is technically correct
options.C: Publicly criticize their tone during a team meeting
options.D: Have a private conversation acknowledging the value of their technical insight while specifically addressing the tone and its impact, coaching them on more collaborative delivery

justification: Correct. Acknowledging the valuable technical content while specifically coaching on tone and delivery addresses the actual problem constructively, helping them communicate more effectively without losing their valuable input.

text: A team's Scrum Master wants to help the team become more comfortable with experimentation and occasional failure as part of a healthy innovation culture. What is the BEST way to foster this?

options.A: Punish any failed experiment to discourage future risk-taking
options.B: Model a blameless approach to failed experiments, celebrate the learning gained, and reinforce psychological safety around trying new approaches
options.C: Discourage all experimentation to minimize any risk of failure
options.D: Only allow experimentation by senior team members

justification: Correct. Modeling a blameless approach and celebrating learning from failure reinforces psychological safety, which is essential for fostering genuine experimentation and innovation culture.

text: A project manager needs to onboard a large batch of new team members simultaneously for a major project expansion. What is the BEST way to ensure effective integration at scale?

options.A: Delay all real work indefinitely until every new member has independently mastered every aspect of the project
options.B: Assign all new members immediately to the most complex, high-visibility tasks without any orientation
options.C: Develop a structured onboarding program with clear documentation, buddy assignments, and staged introduction to project context and responsibilities
options.D: Have each new team member figure out onboarding independently with no structured support

justification: Correct. A structured onboarding program with documentation, buddies, and staged introduction ensures consistent, effective integration even when onboarding a large batch simultaneously.

text: A project manager wants to establish a team norm around how quickly team members should respond to urgent versus non-urgent communications. What is the BEST way to establish this norm?

options.A: Facilitate a discussion to explicitly define what constitutes urgent versus non-urgent communication, and agree on reasonable response-time expectations for each
options.B: Leave response-time expectations entirely undefined and informal
options.C: Require all communications to be treated as equally urgent regardless of actual content
options.D: Assume everyone already has the same understanding of what counts as urgent

justification: Correct. Explicitly discussing and agreeing on urgency definitions and response-time expectations creates a clear, shared team norm that reduces ambiguity and frustration.

text: A project manager notices that a team member's contributions in written documentation are excellent, but their verbal communication in meetings is much less clear. What is the BEST way to leverage this team member's strengths?

options.A: Require them to only communicate verbally to force improvement in that area
options.B: Ignore the discrepancy since all communication modes should be treated identically regardless of individual strengths
options.C: Recognize their strength in written communication, leverage it appropriately (e.g., documentation lead), while providing supportive coaching for verbal communication if they wish to develop that skill
options.D: Exclude them from all future meetings since their verbal communication is weaker

justification: Correct. Recognizing and leveraging their written communication strength, while offering supportive coaching for verbal skills if desired, respects individual differences while supporting genuine growth.

text: A newly formed hybrid team combines predictive-experienced engineers who are new to agile with agile-experienced developers who are unfamiliar with the predictive documentation practices required for a regulated portion of the project. Tension has emerged, with each subgroup questioning the other's approach. What is the BEST way for the project leader to build a cohesive team?

options.A: Assign a single leader to make all decisions unilaterally without input from either subgroup
options.B: Facilitate cross-training sessions where each subgroup teaches the other about their approach's strengths, and co-create a shared understanding of when and why each approach applies to different parts of the project
options.C: Have each subgroup work in complete isolation using their own preferred approach with no integration
options.D: Force the entire team to only use the predictive approach, discarding all agile practices to simplify the situation

justification: Correct. Facilitating mutual cross-training and co-creating shared understanding of when each approach applies directly builds genuine cohesion, respect, and effective collaboration in a hybrid environment with genuinely different needs.

text: A project manager wants to ensure that quiet, introspective team members have equal opportunity to influence project decisions as more extroverted, vocal team members. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Require quiet team members to adopt a more extroverted communication style
options.B: Offer multiple input channels, including written/asynchronous options, alongside live discussions, ensuring all styles have a genuine opportunity to contribute
options.C: Rely exclusively on live, verbal group discussions for all decision input
options.D: Assume quiet team members have nothing valuable to add if they don't speak up in meetings

justification: Correct. Offering multiple input channels, including asynchronous written options, ensures all communication styles have genuine opportunity to contribute meaningfully, supporting more equitable input.

text: A project manager needs to address a situation where a team member consistently takes credit for team successes when speaking with senior management, while blaming others for team setbacks. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since it doesn't directly affect the technical work
options.B: Adopt the same behavior personally to counteract their narrative
options.C: Publicly confront the team member in front of senior management
options.D: Have a direct, private conversation about the pattern's impact on team trust, and ensure accurate, balanced information reaches senior management through proper channels

justification: Correct. A direct private conversation addressing the impact on trust, combined with ensuring accurate information reaches management appropriately, addresses both the interpersonal issue and the accuracy of organizational reporting.

text: A project manager wants to help a team member who has expressed interest in eventually becoming a project manager themselves develop relevant skills. What is the BEST way to support this development?

options.A: Provide gradually increasing opportunities for them to practice relevant skills (e.g., leading small initiatives, coordinating with stakeholders), with mentoring and feedback along the way
options.B: Discourage their interest since project management should only be pursued by those with formal certification already
options.C: Ignore their interest since project management skills develop naturally over time without any deliberate support
options.D: Immediately assign them full project management responsibility for a major initiative without any preparation

justification: Correct. Gradually increasing relevant opportunities with mentoring and feedback provides a structured, supportive development path appropriate for someone building toward project management capability.

text: A project manager wants to reduce reliance on any single point of contact for critical stakeholder relationships, in case that person becomes unavailable. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Randomly rotate stakeholder contacts frequently regardless of relationship continuity needs
options.B: Avoid building any stakeholder relationships to prevent dependency risk entirely
options.C: Keep all stakeholder relationships concentrated with a single team member for consistency
options.D: Cultivate secondary relationships and cross-introduce additional team members to key stakeholders, ensuring redundancy without disrupting existing productive relationships

justification: Correct. Cultivating secondary relationships and cross-introducing additional team members builds valuable redundancy while preserving the benefits of existing strong relationships.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Definition of Done becoming outdated as the product and technology evolve. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Remove the Definition of Done entirely once the product reaches a certain maturity level
options.B: Periodically review and update the Definition of Done during Retrospectives to reflect evolving product, technology, and quality needs
options.C: Set the Definition of Done once at project start and never revisit it
options.D: Let each individual team member define their own personal definition of done

justification: Correct. Periodically reviewing and updating the Definition of Done during Retrospectives ensures it stays relevant and reflects evolving needs, consistent with continuous improvement principles.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of overlooking important non-functional requirements (like performance under load) during Sprint Planning. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Only consider non-functional requirements after the product has already launched
options.B: Include relevant non-functional requirement checks as part of the team's Definition of Ready and/or Definition of Done, making them an explicit consideration for applicable items
options.C: Assume non-functional requirements will naturally be addressed without any explicit consideration
options.D: Remove all non-functional requirements from consideration since they slow down feature delivery

justification: Correct. Explicitly including relevant non-functional requirement checks in the Definition of Ready/Done ensures they are consistently considered as part of the team's standard practice, rather than being an afterthought.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being disrupted by unplanned meetings or interruptions from other departments. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Accept all meeting requests without any prioritization or protection of focused work time
options.B: Establish protected focus time or meeting-free periods during the Sprint, and work with other departments to route non-critical requests through agreed channels
options.C: Refuse to attend any meetings whatsoever, regardless of their legitimate necessity
options.D: Ignore the disruption pattern since interruptions are an unavoidable part of any Sprint

justification: Correct. Establishing protected focus time and routing non-critical requests through agreed channels directly addresses the disruption pattern while still accommodating genuinely necessary interactions.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate baseline against which to measure schedule performance after a major, formally approved scope change. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Create a new baseline immediately for every minor variance, regardless of formal approval
options.B: Update the schedule baseline to reflect the approved change, and measure future performance against this revised baseline
options.C: Continue measuring against the original baseline, ignoring the approved change entirely
options.D: Discard all baseline tracking entirely since the change makes historical comparison meaningless

justification: Correct. Updating the schedule baseline to reflect the approved change and measuring future performance against the revised baseline is the standard, correct approach following formal change approval.

text: A project manager wants to determine the most appropriate technique to identify the root cause of repeated scope changes on a project. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Blame the team for poor initial planning without further investigation
options.B: Assume the changes are random and cannot be analyzed
options.C: Simply approve every change request without any pattern analysis
options.D: Use root cause analysis techniques (e.g., five whys, fishbone diagram) to systematically investigate the underlying reasons behind the repeated scope changes

justification: Correct. Using structured root cause analysis techniques systematically investigates the underlying reasons behind repeated scope changes, enabling targeted, effective corrective action.

text: Which of the following are appropriate ways to manage dependencies between multiple agile teams working on the same product? (Select TWO)

options.A: Regular cross-team synchronization events (e.g., Scrum of Scrums)
options.B: A shared, visible dependency board or tracking mechanism across teams
options.C: Ignoring dependencies entirely and hoping they resolve themselves
options.D: Merging all teams into a single undifferentiated group regardless of team size or focus

justification: Correct. Regular cross-team synchronization events like Scrum of Scrums are a standard, effective practice for coordinating dependencies across multiple agile teams. / Correct. A shared, visible dependency tracking mechanism provides transparency into cross-team dependencies, supporting proactive coordination and issue resolution.

text: A project manager wants to determine whether a proposed process improvement is worth implementing given its associated costs. What is the BEST way to make this determination?

options.A: Implement the improvement regardless of cost since all improvements are inherently valuable
options.B: Make the decision based purely on which team member proposed the improvement
options.C: Conduct a cost-benefit analysis comparing the improvement's expected costs against its anticipated benefits before deciding whether to implement it
options.D: Reject any improvement that has any associated cost, regardless of potential benefit

justification: Correct. Conducting a cost-benefit analysis provides an objective, evidence-based basis for deciding whether a proposed improvement's benefits genuinely justify its costs.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of losing important context when handing off a Product Backlog Item between team members mid-Sprint due to unplanned absence. What is the BEST practice to support this?

options.A: Rely solely on the absent team member's memory to be shared verbally once they return
options.B: Maintain clear, up-to-date notes and context on in-progress items within the team's tracking tool, enabling smoother handoffs when needed
options.C: Avoid ever handing off work between team members regardless of circumstance
options.D: Discard any in-progress work when a team member becomes unexpectedly unavailable

justification: Correct. Maintaining clear, up-to-date notes and context within the tracking tool directly supports smoother handoffs when unplanned absences occur, reducing the risk of lost context.

text: A team's velocity has been stable at 40 points per Sprint for the past 6 Sprints. In Sprint 7, the team completes only 25 points, and in Sprint 8, they complete 45 points. The Product Owner is concerned about the fluctuation and asks the Scrum Master to explain what's happening. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to respond?

options.A: Investigate the specific factors behind each Sprint's variance (e.g., Sprint 7 may have had unplanned interruptions, Sprint 8 may have included simpler carryover work), and share findings with the Product Owner along with the overall stable average trend
options.B: Recommend permanently increasing the Sprint commitment to 45 points based on the most recent Sprint's result
options.C: Immediately conclude the team is underperforming based on Sprint 7's lower number alone
options.D: Tell the Product Owner not to worry since velocity naturally fluctuates and no further investigation is needed

justification: Correct. Investigating and sharing the specific factors behind each Sprint's variance, alongside the overall stable average trend, provides the Product Owner with genuinely useful, evidence-based context rather than either alarm or dismissal.

text: A project manager wants to ensure that quality metrics being tracked are actually meaningful and not just easy to measure. What is the BEST way to select appropriate quality metrics?

options.A: Track every conceivable metric regardless of its actual relevance to quality
options.B: Avoid tracking any quality metrics since they are inherently subjective
options.C: Choose metrics based purely on how easy they are to collect, regardless of their relevance to actual quality outcomes
options.D: Select metrics that genuinely reflect the quality standards and outcomes that matter most to stakeholders, even if they require more effort to collect

justification: Correct. Selecting metrics that genuinely reflect stakeholder-relevant quality outcomes, even if more effort is required, ensures the tracked data provides genuinely useful, actionable insight.

text: A team member consistently frames disagreements in technical discussions as personal attacks, making it difficult for the team to have open debate. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Exclude them from all technical discussions to avoid the discomfort
options.B: Avoid all technical debate to prevent the team member from feeling attacked
options.C: Have a private conversation to help them separate disagreement about ideas from personal criticism, while coaching the team on framing feedback around ideas rather than individuals
options.D: Tell them their perception of the discussions is simply wrong without further discussion

justification: Correct. Helping the individual separate idea-disagreement from personal criticism, combined with coaching the broader team on idea-focused feedback framing, addresses both the individual's perception and the team's communication practices constructively.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a quieter team member has started contributing more actively after several supportive coaching conversations. What is the BEST way to reinforce this positive change?

options.A: Continue providing supportive, specific acknowledgment of their contributions, while remaining available for ongoing coaching as needed
options.B: Publicly single them out repeatedly to draw maximum attention to the change
options.C: Stop providing any further support since the change has already occurred
options.D: Assume the change is permanent and requires no further attention

justification: Correct. Continuing supportive, specific acknowledgment while remaining available for further coaching reinforces the positive change sustainably, respecting the individual's ongoing growth journey.

text: A team member consistently over-explains simple concepts to colleagues in a way that some perceive as condescending, though the intent appears to be genuinely helpful. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Ignore the perception issue since their intent is genuinely helpful
options.B: Have a supportive conversation providing specific feedback on how their explanations are being received, and offer suggestions for calibrating their communication to the audience's actual knowledge level
options.C: Publicly criticize their communication style during a team meeting
options.D: Tell them to stop trying to be helpful entirely

justification: Correct. Providing specific feedback on how explanations are being received, along with suggestions for better calibrating communication, addresses the actual perception gap constructively while preserving their helpful intent.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of losing important context about why a particular Product Backlog Item was deprioritized, in case it becomes relevant again later. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Archive deprioritized items with a brief note explaining the reason for deprioritization, making them easy to reference or revisit later if circumstances change
options.B: Delete deprioritized items entirely from any record once removed from the active backlog
options.C: Keep all deprioritized items permanently active at the top of the backlog regardless of current relevance
options.D: Rely solely on individual team members' memory to recall why items were deprioritized

justification: Correct. Archiving with a brief explanatory note preserves useful context for potential future reference while keeping the active backlog focused and uncluttered.

text: A team wants to improve how they estimate the effort required for bug fixes, which have historically been harder to estimate consistently than new feature work. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Assign bug fix estimation exclusively to the most junior team member regardless of their experience with this type of work
options.B: Analyze historical bug fix data to identify patterns by category or complexity, and use this insight to develop more consistent estimation guidelines specific to bug fix work
options.C: Stop estimating bug fixes entirely since they are inherently unpredictable
options.D: Always assign the same fixed estimate to every bug fix regardless of apparent complexity

justification: Correct. Analyzing historical data to identify category-based patterns provides an evidence-based way to develop more consistent, tailored estimation guidelines specifically for bug fix work.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of duplicate effort occurring when two team members unknowingly work on overlapping parts of the same Product Backlog Item. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Maintain a clear, visible task board showing who is working on what, and encourage brief daily check-ins (e.g., Daily Scrum) to surface any potential overlap early
options.B: Assume duplicate effort will never happen since the team is self-organizing
options.C: Avoid any visibility into individual task assignments to respect privacy
options.D: Assign all work exclusively to one person at a time to eliminate any possibility of overlap

justification: Correct. A clear, visible task board combined with regular check-ins like the Daily Scrum directly surfaces overlapping work early, allowing the team to coordinate and avoid duplicate effort.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog Item being marked as done when it actually has known limitations that were not fully resolved. What is the BEST practice to prevent this?

options.A: Allow items with known limitations to be marked done as long as they mostly work
options.B: Ensure the Definition of Done explicitly addresses handling of known limitations, requiring either full resolution or transparent documentation and stakeholder acknowledgment before acceptance
options.C: Let each individual team member decide independently whether known limitations are acceptable
options.D: Never accept any item with even minor imperfections, regardless of their actual significance

justification: Correct. Explicitly addressing how known limitations should be handled in the Definition of Done, requiring transparency and stakeholder acknowledgment when full resolution isn't achieved, maintains quality integrity while allowing pragmatic flexibility.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint Review attracting stakeholders who provide feedback that conflicts with previously agreed priorities, causing confusion. What is the BEST way to handle this during the event?

options.A: Acknowledge the new feedback, note it for consideration in future backlog refinement, and clarify that current priorities remain in effect unless formally reprioritized
options.B: Refuse to acknowledge any feedback that conflicts with previously agreed priorities
options.C: Exclude stakeholders whose feedback might conflict with current priorities from future Sprint Reviews
options.D: Immediately change all priorities based on the most recent feedback received, regardless of prior agreements

justification: Correct. Acknowledging the feedback for future consideration while clarifying that current priorities remain in effect unless formally reprioritized respects both the stakeholder's input and the stability of current commitments.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons to conduct backlog refinement more frequently than once per Sprint? (Select TWO)

options.A: The Product Backlog is growing rapidly and needs more frequent attention to stay well-organized
options.B: The team is working on complex items requiring more frequent, incremental clarification
options.C: The team wants to permanently eliminate the need for Sprint Planning
options.D: The team wants to avoid ever discussing acceptance criteria

justification: Correct. A rapidly growing backlog needing more frequent attention to stay organized is a valid reason to increase refinement frequency. / Correct. Complex items requiring more frequent, incremental clarification is a valid reason for more frequent refinement sessions to properly break down and understand the work.

text: Which of the following are valid ways to measure the health of a team's agile practice beyond simple velocity? (Select TWO)

options.A: Team-reported satisfaction and psychological safety survey results
options.B: Percentage of Sprint Goals successfully achieved over time
options.C: The organization's total annual revenue
options.D: The number of external vendors the organization uses

justification: Correct. Team-reported satisfaction and psychological safety survey results provide valuable insight into team health beyond pure output metrics like velocity. / Correct. The percentage of Sprint Goals successfully achieved over time reflects the team's actual effectiveness at delivering coherent, valuable increments, complementing velocity as a health indicator.

text: Match each Scrum event to its correct primary purpose.

colonne_droite.texte: Establishing what can be delivered in the Sprint and how the chosen work will be achieved
Inspecting progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapting the Sprint Backlog as necessary
Inspecting the outcome of the Sprint and adapting the Product Backlog based on feedback
Planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness for future Sprints

justification: Sprint Planning establishes the Sprint Goal and the plan for delivering it, defining what work will be pursued and how. / The Daily Scrum is a short event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as needed. / The Sprint Review inspects the outcome of the Sprint with stakeholders and adapts the Product Backlog based on feedback and new information. / The Sprint Retrospective focuses on planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness for future Sprints, based on reflection on the past Sprint.

text: A team wants to ensure that the Product Backlog remains the single source of truth for all planned work, avoiding parallel, undocumented task lists maintained by individual team members. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Eliminate the Product Backlog entirely in favor of individual task management systems
options.B: Reinforce the practice of capturing all planned work in the Product Backlog, discouraging parallel undocumented lists, and making the backlog easily accessible and up-to-date for everyone
options.C: Allow team members to maintain personal task lists that are never shared or integrated with the Product Backlog
options.D: Require every team member to memorize all planned work instead of using any tracking system

justification: Correct. Reinforcing the practice of capturing all planned work centrally, while keeping the backlog accessible and current, ensures it genuinely functions as the single source of truth for the team's work.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate level of detail for status reports provided to different levels of organizational hierarchy. What is the BEST guiding principle?

options.A: Tailor the level of detail to each audience's decision-making needs, providing higher-level summaries to executives and more granular detail to those directly managing the work
options.B: Provide identical, highly detailed reports to every level of the organization regardless of their actual needs
options.C: Provide minimal information to everyone regardless of hierarchy level to save time
options.D: Base the level of detail solely on personal preference rather than actual audience needs

justification: Correct. Tailoring the level of detail to each audience's actual decision-making needs, with higher-level summaries for executives and granular detail for operational management, reflects effective, audience-appropriate reporting practice.

text: A project manager needs to determine the most appropriate way to close out a project phase in a multi-phase predictive project. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Discard all documentation from the completed phase since it is no longer needed
options.B: Skip formal phase closure since the overall project is not yet complete
options.C: Immediately begin the next phase without any formal review of the completed phase
options.D: Verify that all phase deliverables have been completed and accepted, document lessons learned, and obtain formal sign-off before transitioning to the next phase

justification: Correct. Verifying deliverable completion and acceptance, documenting lessons learned, and obtaining formal sign-off before transitioning is the standard, appropriate way to properly close a project phase in a multi-phase predictive project.

text: Which of the following are appropriate techniques for validating that a project's deliverables meet the defined acceptance criteria? (Select TWO)

options.A: Formal inspection against documented acceptance criteria
options.B: Structured walkthroughs with relevant stakeholders
options.C: Random guessing about whether the deliverable is likely acceptable
options.D: Ignoring acceptance criteria entirely and relying on the delivery team's subjective judgment alone

justification: Correct. Formal inspection against documented acceptance criteria is a standard, objective technique for validating deliverable conformance. / Correct. Structured walkthroughs with relevant stakeholders provide a collaborative, thorough way to validate that deliverables meet defined acceptance criteria.

text: A project manager discovers during a routine schedule review that three separate work packages, each managed by different team leads, are all scheduled to require the same specialized equipment during the exact same week, though only one unit of the equipment is available. This was not caught during original resource planning. What is the BEST way to resolve this?

options.A: Ignore the conflict since it was only discovered during a routine review, not through a formal escalation
options.B: Cancel two of the three work packages entirely to eliminate the conflict
options.C: Analyze the relative priority, flexibility, and dependencies of each work package, then work with the team leads to resequence or secure additional equipment access to resolve the conflict
options.D: Allow all three work packages to proceed as scheduled and let the team leads sort out the conflict informally among themselves

justification: Correct. Analyzing relative priority, flexibility, and dependencies, then working with team leads to resequence or secure additional resources, reflects proper, structured resource conflict resolution consistent with good resource management practice.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring accepting cryptocurrency as a payment method, which would require significant new backlog work and carries regulatory uncertainty in several markets. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Research the regulatory landscape for cryptocurrency payments across the organization's target markets, and assess the business case before committing significant backlog investment
options.B: Immediately implement cryptocurrency payment support without any research into regulatory implications
options.C: Assume regulatory requirements are the same across all target markets without verification
options.D: Refuse to consider the idea since cryptocurrency is inherently too risky

justification: Correct. Researching the regulatory landscape and assessing the business case before committing significant investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a legitimate but genuinely complex and uncertain opportunity.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring international expansion into a market with significantly different consumer protection laws regarding refunds and cancellations. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Delay market entry indefinitely without evaluating what specific compliance work would actually be required
options.B: Research the specific consumer protection requirements for the new market and add prioritized backlog items to implement compliant refund/cancellation workflows
options.C: Apply the organization's existing home-market refund and cancellation policies universally without any adjustment
options.D: Assume the new market's consumers will simply accept the organization's existing policies regardless of local legal requirements

justification: Correct. Researching specific local requirements and adding prioritized backlog items to implement compliant workflows reflects responsible, proactive integration of a legitimate market-specific regulatory requirement.

text: An agile team's organization operates in an industry where a major trade association just published new voluntary interoperability standards. What is the BEST way for the product leader to consider this?

options.A: Wait until the standards become legally mandatory, if ever, before considering any action
options.B: Ignore the voluntary standards entirely since they are not legally mandatory
options.C: Evaluate the potential business value of adopting the standards (e.g., market positioning, customer expectations, future-proofing) and consider prioritized adoption if genuinely beneficial
options.D: Immediately implement every aspect of the standards regardless of actual relevance or cost

justification: Correct. Evaluating potential business value and considering prioritized adoption if genuinely beneficial reflects thoughtful, evidence-based consideration of emerging voluntary industry standards.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift to a four-day work week as a pilot program, which would significantly change the team's available capacity per Sprint. What should the team do to prepare?

options.A: Refuse to participate in the pilot since it will disrupt established planning norms
options.B: Continue committing to the same Sprint scope as before, assuming productivity will simply increase to compensate
options.C: Ignore the capacity change entirely and let the team figure it out informally without any planning adjustment
options.D: Reassess and adjust Sprint capacity planning based on the reduced available hours, using historical data to inform a realistic new baseline as the pilot begins

justification: Correct. Reassessing and adjusting capacity planning based on actual reduced available hours, informed by historical data as the pilot progresses, reflects realistic, evidence-based adaptation to a significant organizational change.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a partnership with an AI research lab to integrate advanced machine learning capabilities into the product, which would require significant new technical expertise. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Assume the current team can seamlessly integrate advanced AI capabilities without any additional expertise or support
options.B: Proceed with the integration immediately without any capability assessment
options.C: Refuse to explore the partnership since it requires expertise the team doesn't currently have
options.D: Assess the team's current capability gaps relative to the required AI expertise, and plan for necessary training, hiring, or partnership support to enable successful integration

justification: Correct. Assessing actual capability gaps and planning for training, hiring, or partnership support reflects proactive, realistic preparation for integrating genuinely new, advanced technical capabilities.

text: An agile team's organization is subject to a new industry-wide moratorium temporarily halting a specific type of product feature due to unresolved regulatory concerns across the industry. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Continue developing the affected feature as planned, ignoring the moratorium
options.B: Cancel the entire product roadmap due to the moratorium on one specific feature type
options.C: Pause development on the affected feature, reprioritize the backlog to focus on unaffected work, and monitor for regulatory resolution before resuming
options.D: Assume the moratorium doesn't apply to the organization's specific implementation without verification

justification: Correct. Pausing the affected work, reprioritizing to focus on unaffected areas, and monitoring for resolution reflects a proportionate, responsible response to a genuine but temporary regulatory constraint.

text: Which of the following are examples of how business environment changes can appropriately influence agile backlog prioritization? (Select TWO)

options.A: A new competitor feature shifting customer expectations, prompting reprioritization of similar or differentiating capabilities
options.B: A new regulatory requirement necessitating prioritized compliance work
options.C: A team member's personal preference for one programming language over another
options.D: The specific day of the week a Sprint happens to start on

justification: Correct. A competitor's feature shifting customer expectations is a legitimate business environment factor that should influence backlog prioritization to remain competitive. / Correct. A new regulatory requirement necessitating compliance work is a legitimate, often mandatory, business environment factor requiring prioritized backlog attention.

text: Which of the following are appropriate considerations when evaluating whether to pursue a strategic partnership opportunity for an agile product team? (Select TWO)

options.A: Alignment between the partnership's requirements and the team's current capacity and roadmap
options.B: The potential business value and strategic fit of the partnership
options.C: Whether the partnership was suggested by the most senior person in the room, regardless of merit
options.D: The exact number of words used in the partnership's initial proposal email

justification: Correct. Assessing alignment between partnership requirements and the team's actual current capacity and roadmap is essential for evaluating feasibility and realistic impact. / Correct. Evaluating the potential business value and strategic fit is fundamental to determining whether a partnership opportunity is genuinely worth pursuing.

text: Match each type of market entry strategy to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Expanding into a new market by building capabilities and presence internally over time
Collaborating with an established local or complementary organization to enter a new market
Purchasing an existing company to gain immediate market presence and capabilities
Granting or obtaining rights to use intellectual property to enable market entry without full internal development

justification: Organic growth involves building internal capabilities and market presence gradually, without relying on external partnerships or acquisitions. / A strategic partnership involves collaborating with an established organization, often with existing local market knowledge, to facilitate entry. / Acquisition involves purchasing an existing company to gain immediate access to market presence, customers, and capabilities. / Licensing involves granting or obtaining rights to use intellectual property, enabling market entry without needing to fully develop the underlying technology internally.

text: Match each type of compliance requirement to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: Ensuring customer personal data is processed according to applicable privacy laws
Following required accounting standards and financial reporting regulations
Ensuring digital products are usable by people with disabilities per applicable standards
Meeting required emissions or waste disposal regulations for physical operations

justification: Data privacy compliance involves adhering to laws governing how personal data is collected, processed, and protected. / Financial compliance involves following required accounting standards and regulatory financial reporting obligations. / Accessibility compliance involves meeting standards ensuring digital products are usable by people with various disabilities. / Environmental compliance involves meeting regulatory requirements related to environmental impact, such as emissions or waste disposal standards.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new export control regulations affecting the transfer of certain technical specifications to international team members. This was identified mid-project. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Remove all international team members from the project entirely, regardless of whether they are actually affected
options.B: Ignore the new regulations since they were identified mid-project rather than at the start
options.C: Continue sharing all technical specifications as before, since the project began before the new regulations took effect
options.D: Work with legal/compliance to determine which specific specifications are restricted, and adjust information sharing and team assignments accordingly to maintain compliance

justification: Correct. Working with legal/compliance to precisely determine restricted specifications and adjusting sharing/assignments accordingly ensures targeted, appropriate compliance without unnecessary overreach.

text: A project manager's organization is bidding on a government contract that requires specific small business subcontracting participation targets. What should the project manager do to support compliance?

options.A: Ignore the subcontracting targets since they are a bidding/legal matter, not a project management concern
options.B: Work with procurement to identify and structure subcontracting opportunities that meet the required participation targets while still meeting technical and quality needs
options.C: Assume the targets will be met automatically without any deliberate subcontractor selection strategy
options.D: Select subcontractors solely based on meeting the numeric target, regardless of their actual capability to deliver quality work

justification: Correct. Working with procurement to identify subcontracting opportunities that meet both the participation targets and quality/technical needs reflects responsible, balanced compliance with a legitimate contractual requirement.

text: Which of the following are examples of Enterprise Environmental Factors that could constrain a project's procurement options? (Select TWO)

options.A: Government regulations restricting certain types of foreign supplier contracts
options.B: The organization's established, mandatory approved-vendor list
options.C: The project's specific activity list
options.D: The project's specific WBS dictionary

justification: Correct. Government regulations restricting certain supplier contracts are an external Enterprise Environmental Factor that directly constrains available procurement options. / Correct. An organization's mandatory approved-vendor list is an internal Enterprise Environmental Factor that constrains which suppliers a project can legitimately contract with.

text: A project manager's organization is bidding on a major international infrastructure contract. Winning the bid would require committing to environmental impact standards stricter than what is legally required in the host country, but consistent with the organization's own public sustainability commitments. A competing bid from another firm meets only the host country's legally required minimum, offering a lower price. The evaluation committee asks the project manager to weigh in on the trade-off. What is the BEST way to respond?

options.A: Recommend abandoning the organization's own stricter standards entirely to match the lower-priced competing bid
options.B: Present a balanced analysis of the cost difference against the organization's public sustainability commitments and potential reputational/long-term value considerations, allowing the evaluation committee to make an informed decision
options.C: Refuse to participate in the evaluation discussion since it involves a business strategy decision beyond project management
options.D: Unilaterally decide to match the competitor's lower standard without consulting the evaluation committee

justification: Correct. Presenting a balanced, evidence-based analysis of cost versus commitment and reputational considerations respects the evaluation committee's decision authority while providing the substantive input needed for an informed, strategic decision.

text: A project manager notices that a team member frequently takes on tasks outside their formal role without informing anyone, creating confusion about actual task ownership. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Forbid them from ever taking on additional tasks beyond their formal role
options.B: Ignore the confusion since tasks are still getting done regardless
options.C: Acknowledge their initiative while establishing clearer expectations about communicating task ownership changes to maintain team-wide clarity
options.D: Praise the initiative without addressing the lack of communication

justification: Correct. Acknowledging genuine initiative while establishing clearer communication expectations addresses both the positive intent and the actual coordination problem constructively.

text: A team wants to improve how quickly they can respond to critical production incidents without disrupting their planned Sprint work entirely. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Ignore production incidents until the current Sprint's planned work is fully complete
options.B: Cancel the current Sprint every time a production incident occurs, regardless of severity
options.C: Reserve a portion of Sprint capacity for unplanned critical work, and establish a clear process for handling incidents without derailing the entire Sprint
options.D: Assign all incident response exclusively to one dedicated person who never participates in Sprint work

justification: Correct. Reserving capacity for unplanned critical work, combined with a clear incident-handling process, balances responsiveness to genuine emergencies with protecting overall Sprint focus.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring offering the product through a reseller channel in addition to direct sales, which would require supporting reseller-specific features (e.g., multi-tenant management, white-labeling). What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Engage with potential reseller partners to understand actual requirements, and validate the business case before committing significant backlog investment
options.B: Immediately build all conceivable reseller features without validating actual reseller partner requirements
options.C: Ignore the reseller channel opportunity since it deviates from the current direct-sales model
options.D: Assume reseller requirements are identical to existing direct customer requirements

justification: Correct. Engaging with potential partners to understand actual requirements, then validating the business case, reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation before committing to a significant new business channel.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate contingency reserve for a specific identified risk with a 30% probability and a $50,000 potential cost impact if it occurs. What is the expected monetary value (EMV) of this risk?
justification: Correct. Expected Monetary Value is calculated as probability multiplied by impact: 0.30 × $50,000 = $15,000.

text: A team member consistently expresses discomfort with the pace of change in the organization's tools and processes, feeling like they can never fully master one approach before it changes again. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Acknowledge their experience, provide additional support and training resources during transitions, and advocate for reasonable stability where possible
options.B: Tell them to simply adapt faster without any additional support
options.C: Dismiss their discomfort since change is simply a normal part of modern work
options.D: Stop introducing any further changes to accommodate this one team member indefinitely

justification: Correct. Acknowledging their experience, providing extra support during transitions, and advocating for reasonable stability where possible respects their genuine concern while still allowing necessary organizational evolution.

text: Which of the following are valid characteristics of a well-formed Sprint Goal? (Select TWO)

options.A: It provides flexibility regarding the exact work needed to achieve it, while still giving coherence to the Sprint Backlog
options.B: It is created collaboratively during Sprint Planning by the Scrum Team
options.C: It should be set permanently at project initiation and never changed for the life of the product
options.D: It should exhaustively list every task the team plans to complete

justification: Correct. A Sprint Goal provides flexibility on the specific work needed while still giving the team a coherent purpose for the Sprint, guiding decisions without being an exhaustive task list. / Correct. The Sprint Goal is crafted collaboratively during Sprint Planning through discussion between the Product Owner and Developers, reflecting shared Scrum Team input.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new industry-wide safety recall affecting a component used in the current project's manufacturing process. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Cancel the entire project immediately without assessing whether a replacement component is available
options.B: Immediately halt use of the recalled component, assess the impact on the project, and identify a compliant replacement or remediation plan
options.C: Ignore the recall since it was issued by an external industry body, not a direct regulator
options.D: Continue using the existing inventory of the recalled component until it runs out

justification: Correct. Immediately halting use, assessing project impact, and identifying a compliant replacement or remediation plan is the appropriate, responsible response to a safety recall affecting critical materials.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that team members frequently interrupt the Product Owner during Sprint Reviews with detailed technical questions better suited for internal discussion. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Cancel Sprint Reviews entirely to avoid the disruption
options.B: Forbid the Product Owner from attending Sprint Reviews to avoid the interruptions
options.C: Coach the team on distinguishing questions appropriate for the Sprint Review audience versus internal technical discussions, suggesting a parking lot for the latter
options.D: Allow the interruptions to continue since all questions are equally valuable regardless of context

justification: Correct. Coaching the team on audience-appropriate questions, with a parking lot technique for internal technical discussions, directly addresses the described disruption while preserving the value of both types of conversation in their proper venues.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of technical debt accumulating unnoticed across multiple Sprints. What is the BEST way to maintain visibility into this?

options.A: Only address technical debt once it causes a major production failure
options.B: Let each developer track their own personal notes about technical debt with no team-wide visibility
options.C: Avoid tracking technical debt since it is inherently subjective
options.D: Maintain a visible technical debt log or backlog category, periodically reviewed to assess accumulation trends and prioritize remediation

justification: Correct. Maintaining a visible, periodically reviewed technical debt log provides the team-wide transparency needed to track accumulation trends and make informed prioritization decisions.

text: Match each type of market research method to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: In-depth qualitative conversations to understand customer needs and pain points
Structured quantitative data collection from a broad customer sample
Systematic evaluation of competitor products and positioning
Observing real users interacting with a product to identify usability issues

justification: Customer interviews provide rich, qualitative insight into individual needs and pain points through direct conversation. / Surveys collect structured, quantitative data from a broader sample, useful for identifying patterns across many customers. / Competitive analysis systematically evaluates competitors' products, features, and market positioning to inform strategic decisions. / Usability testing involves observing real users interact with a product to identify friction points and usability issues directly.

text: A project manager wants to ensure that a team member returning from an extended sick leave feels welcomed and supported, without making them feel singled out or pitied. What is the BEST way to handle their return?

options.A: Provide a warm, low-key welcome, offer a private check-in about their reintegration needs, and let them set the pace for how much they want to discuss their absence
options.B: Organize a large public celebration specifically focused on their return
options.C: Immediately assign them the same full workload they had before their leave
options.D: Ignore their return entirely to avoid any awkwardness

justification: Correct. A warm, low-key welcome combined with a private check-in, letting them set the pace for discussion, respects their autonomy and privacy while still providing genuine support.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a vendor's request for early payment before their contracted milestone has been formally verified as complete. What is the BEST response?

options.A: Release partial payment based solely on the vendor's verbal assurance of near-completion
options.B: Approve the early payment immediately without any verification of milestone completion
options.C: Refuse to ever discuss the request and ignore all further vendor communication on the topic
options.D: Verify actual milestone completion according to the contract terms before releasing payment, communicating this requirement clearly to the vendor

justification: Correct. Verifying actual milestone completion per contract terms before releasing payment, while clearly communicating this to the vendor, respects contractual obligations and protects the organization's interests.

text: A team member consistently avoids volunteering for tasks involving public-facing stakeholder presentations, preferring to stay behind the scenes. What is the BEST way for the project leader to respond?

options.A: Respect their current preference while occasionally offering, without pressure, lower-stakes opportunities to build comfort with public-facing work if they express any interest in growing in that area
options.B: Assume they have no interest in ever developing this skill and never offer any related opportunities
options.C: Force them to lead the next major stakeholder presentation regardless of their comfort level
options.D: Publicly criticize them for avoiding visible responsibilities

justification: Correct. Respecting their current preference while offering low-pressure growth opportunities if they express interest balances their autonomy with potential support for genuine skill development.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint Review revealing significant misalignment between what was built and what stakeholders actually expected. What is the BEST proactive practice to reduce this risk?

options.A: Engage stakeholders more frequently throughout the Sprint (e.g., informal check-ins, early prototypes) to surface misalignment earlier, before the formal Sprint Review
options.B: Wait until the Sprint Review to share any progress with stakeholders for the first time
options.C: Avoid involving stakeholders at all until the product is fully complete
options.D: Assume initial requirements were perfectly understood and require no further validation during the Sprint

justification: Correct. More frequent stakeholder engagement throughout the Sprint, through informal check-ins or early prototypes, surfaces misalignment earlier when it's easier and cheaper to correct.

text: An agile team's organization operates in a market where a recent regulatory change now requires explicit user consent before certain types of data collection. What is the BEST way for the product leader to handle this compliance need alongside ongoing feature work?

options.A: Prioritize the consent-related backlog items appropriately given the compliance deadline, balancing them with ongoing feature work based on relative urgency
options.B: Halt all feature work entirely until the consent requirement is fully implemented, regardless of the requirement's actual urgency
options.C: Deprioritize the consent requirement indefinitely in favor of feature work with clearer immediate business value
options.D: Ignore the regulatory change since it primarily concerns data collection practices, not the core product features

justification: Correct. Prioritizing consent-related work appropriately relative to its compliance deadline, balanced against ongoing feature work based on genuine urgency, reflects responsible, balanced backlog management.

text: A project manager wants to determine the appropriate resource leveling technique when a key resource is over-allocated across multiple concurrent activities. What is the BEST general approach?

options.A: Ignore the over-allocation and hope the resource manages to complete all assigned work regardless
options.B: Adjust the schedule to resequence or delay non-critical activities using available float, redistributing the resource's workload to eliminate the over-allocation
options.C: Assign the same over-allocated resource to even more concurrent activities to maximize apparent utilization
options.D: Remove the over-allocated resource from the project entirely without replacement

justification: Correct. Resource leveling by resequencing or delaying non-critical activities using available float directly addresses over-allocation by redistributing workload within the schedule's existing flexibility.

text: A team's Scrum Master wants to help the team develop a stronger sense of collective ownership over quality, rather than viewing it as solely the responsibility of dedicated testers. What is the BEST way to achieve this?

options.A: Eliminate dedicated testing roles entirely to force quality ownership onto developers alone
options.B: Ignore quality ownership distribution since it doesn't significantly affect actual product quality
options.C: Keep quality responsibility exclusively with dedicated testers to maintain clear accountability
options.D: Reinforce the Definition of Done as a whole-team quality commitment, encouraging practices like pair testing and shared responsibility for defect prevention across all roles

justification: Correct. Reinforcing the Definition of Done as a whole-team commitment, combined with practices like pair testing, builds genuine collective ownership of quality across all roles, not just dedicated testers.

text: Which of the following are valid outputs of the Monitor and Control Project Work process? (Select TWO)

options.A: Work performance reports
options.B: Change requests
options.C: The original project charter
options.D: The initial stakeholder register created during initiation

justification: Correct. Work performance reports, compiling performance information into a format for decision-making, are a key output of the Monitor and Control Project Work process. / Correct. Change requests, arising from identified deviations or needed corrective/preventive actions, are a standard output of this monitoring and controlling process.

text: A project manager's organization is expanding operations into a region with significant political instability, creating uncertainty about long-term government relations. What is the BEST way to manage this business environment risk?

options.A: Cancel the expansion entirely without any risk mitigation exploration
options.B: Proceed with full, unhedged investment regardless of the acknowledged instability
options.C: Develop contingency plans for various political scenarios, diversify dependencies where possible, and maintain ongoing monitoring of the political situation
options.D: Assume political conditions will remain stable indefinitely without any contingency planning

justification: Correct. Developing contingency plans for various scenarios, diversifying dependencies, and maintaining ongoing monitoring reflects proactive, prudent risk management for a genuinely volatile business environment.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog becoming too focused on technical debt and internal improvements, at the expense of customer-facing value. What is the BEST way to maintain balance?

options.A: Eliminate all technical debt work from the backlog entirely
options.B: Only work on technical debt, ignoring customer-facing feature requests entirely
options.C: Let the allocation between value work and technical debt vary completely randomly each Sprint with no intentional balance
options.D: Establish a reasonable, agreed-upon allocation or ratio between customer-facing value work and technical health work, reviewed periodically for appropriateness

justification: Correct. Establishing a reasonable, periodically reviewed allocation ratio balances the genuine need for both customer-facing value delivery and technical health maintenance.

text: A project manager needs to select a communication approach for delivering critical safety information to a construction crew with varying literacy levels and language backgrounds. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Communicate safety information only once at project kickoff with no ongoing reinforcement
options.B: Assume everyone will understand the safety information regardless of format or language
options.C: Provide only written safety manuals in the project's primary language
options.D: Use multiple communication methods including visual aids, translated materials, and verbal briefings with demonstration, ensuring the critical information is accessible to everyone regardless of literacy or language

justification: Correct. Using multiple accessible communication methods, including visual aids and translated materials, ensures critical safety information genuinely reaches everyone regardless of literacy or language differences.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog Item's acceptance criteria being interpreted differently by the Product Owner and the Development Team during a Sprint Review. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Have the Development Team define acceptance criteria unilaterally without Product Owner input
options.B: Ensure acceptance criteria are clearly defined, specific, and mutually agreed upon during Backlog Refinement or Sprint Planning, before implementation begins
options.C: Leave acceptance criteria intentionally vague to allow flexible interpretation
options.D: Skip defining acceptance criteria entirely to save time

justification: Correct. Ensuring clear, specific, mutually agreed-upon acceptance criteria before implementation begins directly reduces the risk of misinterpretation at review time, since both parties share a common, documented understanding upfront.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring becoming a certified carbon-neutral company, which would require the digital product's infrastructure choices to prioritize energy efficiency and renewable-powered hosting. What should the product/technical leader do?

options.A: Ignore the initiative since infrastructure hosting decisions are considered purely an IT operations matter
options.B: Assess current infrastructure's energy profile, and add relevant backlog items to transition toward more energy-efficient or renewable-powered hosting options where feasible
options.C: Refuse to support the initiative since it deviates from the current infrastructure strategy
options.D: Immediately migrate all infrastructure without any assessment of feasibility, cost, or actual environmental impact

justification: Correct. Assessing the current energy profile and adding relevant, feasible backlog items reflects thoughtful, evidence-based support for a legitimate organizational sustainability initiative.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where two different stakeholders have submitted conflicting requirements for the same feature. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Implement both conflicting requirements simultaneously regardless of the technical or logical contradiction
options.B: Ignore both requirements entirely to avoid taking sides
options.C: Arbitrarily choose one stakeholder's requirement without any discussion or explanation
options.D: Facilitate a discussion between the conflicting stakeholders to understand their underlying needs and work toward a resolution or informed prioritization decision

justification: Correct. Facilitating a discussion to understand underlying needs and reach a resolution or informed decision is the standard, collaborative approach to resolving conflicting stakeholder requirements.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel micromanaged, even though the project leader believes they are simply staying informed about progress. What is the BEST way to address this perception gap?

options.A: Stop checking in on their progress entirely, regardless of legitimate project needs
options.B: Tell them to simply accept the current check-in approach without any changes
options.C: Dismiss their feeling since the leader's intent was not to micromanage
options.D: Have an open conversation to understand specifically what feels like micromanagement to them, and adjust check-in frequency or style to build greater trust and autonomy

justification: Correct. Openly discussing what specifically feels like micromanagement, then adjusting approach accordingly, addresses the perception gap constructively while building greater trust.

text: Which of the following are valid inputs to the Estimate Activity Durations process? (Select TWO)

options.A: Activity list and attributes
options.B: Resource requirements and availability
options.C: The final approved change requests from a previous project
options.D: The organization's marketing budget

justification: Correct. The activity list and its attributes are fundamental inputs needed to estimate how long each activity will take. / Correct. Resource requirements and availability directly affect how long activities will take, making them essential inputs to duration estimating.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new import/export documentation requirements following a change in international trade agreements. What is the BEST way to handle this for a current project involving cross-border shipments?

options.A: Continue using existing documentation processes without any verification against the new requirements
options.B: Work with trade compliance experts to update documentation processes to meet the new requirements, adjusting schedules for shipments as needed
options.C: Ignore the new requirements since the current project's contracts were signed before the trade agreement changed
options.D: Halt all cross-border shipments indefinitely until the requirements are perfectly understood, regardless of actual urgency

justification: Correct. Working with trade compliance experts to update processes and adjusting schedules as needed reflects responsible, proactive adaptation to a legitimate regulatory change affecting cross-border logistics.

text: A team member consistently expresses frustration that the team's Definition of Done feels arbitrary and was set before they joined the team. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore their frustration since Definitions of Done should never be revisited once set
options.B: Immediately change the Definition of Done based solely on this one team member's preference
options.C: Tell them the Definition of Done cannot be questioned since it was already established
options.D: Explain the rationale behind the current Definition of Done, and invite them to raise specific concerns during a Retrospective where the team can collectively consider potential adjustments

justification: Correct. Explaining the rationale while inviting collective consideration of concerns during a Retrospective respects both existing team decisions and the new member's legitimate perspective, using the proper collaborative forum for potential change.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of losing valuable historical context about why certain Product Backlog Items were prioritized the way they were. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Rely solely on individual memory of why prioritization decisions were made
options.B: Avoid documenting any prioritization rationale since priorities change frequently anyway
options.C: Maintain brief prioritization rationale notes alongside key backlog items, especially for significant or non-obvious prioritization decisions
options.D: Document exhaustive rationale for every single backlog item regardless of significance

justification: Correct. Maintaining brief rationale notes for significant or non-obvious decisions preserves useful context efficiently without excessive documentation overhead.

text: Match each type of business model to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Customers pay a recurring fee for ongoing access to a product or service
Basic features are offered free, with premium features available for payment
