The platform facilitates transactions between buyers and sellers, typically earning a commission
Customers pay based on their actual consumption or usage of the product or service

justification: In a subscription model, customers pay a recurring fee, typically monthly or annually, for continued access to a product or service. / A freemium model offers basic functionality for free while charging for premium features, aiming to convert free users into paying customers. / A marketplace model connects buyers and sellers on a platform, with the platform typically earning revenue through transaction commissions. / A usage-based model charges customers according to their actual consumption, aligning cost directly with the value or volume of use.

text: A project manager wants to help a team develop better collective resilience in the face of setbacks, rather than becoming discouraged after each difficulty. What is the BEST way to build this capability?

options.A: Avoid ever discussing setbacks to prevent the team from dwelling on negativity
options.B: Assign blame clearly after every setback to ensure accountability
options.C: Model a constructive, learning-oriented response to setbacks, and facilitate team discussions that focus on lessons learned and forward-looking action rather than dwelling on blame
options.D: Minimize the significance of every setback regardless of its actual impact

justification: Correct. Modeling a constructive, learning-oriented response and facilitating forward-looking, blame-free discussions builds genuine collective resilience by reframing setbacks as learning opportunities rather than sources of discouragement.

text: A project manager wants to determine whether a proposed change to the project's technical approach would introduce unacceptable risk. What is the BEST way to make this determination?

options.A: Approve the change immediately without any risk assessment
options.B: Conduct a risk assessment of the proposed technical change, comparing its risk profile against the project's defined risk tolerance before deciding
options.C: Make the decision based purely on which team member is more senior, regardless of the change's actual risk profile
options.D: Reject the change automatically since any technical change inherently introduces some risk

justification: Correct. Conducting a risk assessment and comparing it against the project's defined risk tolerance provides an objective, evidence-based basis for determining whether the change's risk level is acceptable.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a team member frequently makes self-deprecating jokes about their own competence during technical discussions. What is the BEST way to respond?

options.A: Privately check in on their confidence and wellbeing, and provide specific, genuine positive feedback about their actual contributions and skills
options.B: Publicly correct them every time they make a self-deprecating comment
options.C: Assume the jokes are purely humorous and require no further attention
options.D: Laugh along with the jokes without further consideration

justification: Correct. Privately checking in on confidence and wellbeing, combined with specific positive feedback about genuine contributions, reflects thoughtful, supportive leadership that takes potential confidence concerns seriously.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint Review lacking meaningful stakeholder representation for a critical feature area. What is the BEST proactive step?

options.A: Cancel the Sprint Review entirely if any relevant stakeholder cannot attend
options.B: Proceed with the Sprint Review regardless of stakeholder attendance for critical areas
options.C: Proactively identify and invite specific stakeholders relevant to critical feature areas well in advance, confirming their attendance or arranging an alternative feedback mechanism if they cannot attend
options.D: Assume any attending stakeholder can adequately represent all feature areas regardless of their actual expertise

justification: Correct. Proactively identifying and inviting relevant stakeholders, with an alternative feedback mechanism if needed, ensures critical feature areas receive meaningful stakeholder input even amid scheduling challenges.

text: A project manager's organization is bidding on a contract requiring adherence to a specific quality management standard (e.g., ISO 9001) that the organization has not previously been certified for. What is the BEST way to prepare?

options.A: Assess the gap between current practices and the required standard, and initiate a certification process or partner with a certified subcontractor if the timeline allows
options.B: Assume the standard is not actually enforced and proceed without addressing it
options.C: Bid on the contract claiming compliance without any actual certification process underway
options.D: Withdraw from bidding on any contract requiring standards the organization doesn't currently hold, regardless of the potential value or feasibility of certification

justification: Correct. Assessing the gap and initiating certification or partnering with a certified subcontractor reflects a responsible, feasible approach to meeting a genuine contractual requirement.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their career growth has stagnated within the current team structure. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Dismiss their concern since career growth is entirely the individual's own responsibility
options.B: Immediately promote them regardless of actual readiness or organizational structure constraints
options.C: Tell them to look for opportunities elsewhere since nothing can be done within the current team
options.D: Have a genuine conversation about their career aspirations, and explore concrete opportunities within the current role or project that could support their growth

justification: Correct. A genuine conversation about aspirations, combined with exploring concrete growth opportunities within current constraints, reflects supportive, engaged leadership around a legitimate career concern.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to document a verbal agreement made with a stakeholder during an informal hallway conversation about a scope clarification. What is the BEST practice?

options.A: Assume the stakeholder will remember the exact same details without any written confirmation
options.B: Rely solely on memory of the verbal conversation with no follow-up documentation
options.C: Follow up with written confirmation summarizing the agreed clarification, and update relevant project documentation accordingly
options.D: Ignore the verbal agreement entirely since it wasn't part of a formal meeting

justification: Correct. Following up with written confirmation and updating relevant documentation ensures the agreement is properly captured and reduces the risk of future miscommunication, regardless of the informal setting where it originated.

text: A project manager wants to build a team culture where mistakes are treated as learning opportunities rather than sources of shame. What is the BEST way to model this?

options.A: Never discuss mistakes at all to avoid any negative feelings
options.B: Publicly highlight every individual mistake to ensure accountability
options.C: Openly acknowledge and discuss their own mistakes as project manager, framing them as learning opportunities, and respond to team members' mistakes with curiosity and support rather than blame
options.D: Punish every mistake severely to discourage future errors

justification: Correct. Modeling openness about one's own mistakes and responding to others' mistakes with curiosity and support directly builds the desired learning-oriented, psychologically safe team culture.

text: Which of the following are examples of how technological change in the business environment could affect an ongoing project? (Select TWO)

options.A: A new cloud platform capability that reduces expected infrastructure costs
options.B: A key software dependency reaching end-of-life support, requiring migration
options.C: A team member's personal preference for a specific keyboard layout
options.D: The specific font used in an internal project status report

justification: Correct. A new cloud platform capability reducing infrastructure costs represents a genuine technological change in the business environment that could beneficially affect project planning. / Correct. A key dependency reaching end-of-life support is a significant technological change requiring proactive migration planning to avoid future risk.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment failing acceptance due to overlooked accessibility requirements. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Remove accessibility considerations entirely from scope to simplify delivery
options.B: Address accessibility only if a user with a disability specifically complains after release
options.C: Incorporate accessibility checks into the Definition of Done, ensuring relevant items are tested against accessibility standards before being considered complete
options.D: Assume all features are automatically accessible without any specific testing

justification: Correct. Incorporating accessibility checks into the Definition of Done ensures this important quality dimension is consistently and proactively addressed as part of standard delivery practice.

text: A project manager needs to address a situation where a team member's strong personal opinions about unrelated political topics are causing discomfort among colleagues during breaks. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Privately remind the team member of professional workplace norms around respecting diverse perspectives, without dictating their personal beliefs
options.B: Require the team member to publicly apologize to the entire team
options.C: Publicly forbid any personal conversation topics during breaks
options.D: Ignore the discomfort since personal opinions are outside the project manager's purview entirely

justification: Correct. Privately reminding about professional norms respecting diverse perspectives, without dictating personal beliefs, appropriately addresses workplace comfort while respecting individual freedom of thought.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a critical Product Backlog Item being delayed due to a single external dependency with an uncertain delivery timeline. What is the BEST way to manage this?

options.A: Silently absorb any resulting delay without informing the Product Owner
options.B: Ignore the dependency risk and hope it resolves on its own timeline
options.C: Cancel the affected Product Backlog Item entirely due to the dependency risk
options.D: Communicate the dependency risk transparently to the Product Owner, explore whether the item can be partially decomposed to reduce blocking, and monitor the dependency closely

justification: Correct. Transparent communication, exploring decomposition to reduce blocking, and close monitoring reflects proactive, evidence-based risk management appropriate for an external dependency with uncertain timing.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward a hybrid remote/in-office work model, which will affect how the team collaborates going forward. What is the BEST way for the project leader to prepare?

options.A: Require the entire team to work fully remotely to simplify planning, regardless of the actual hybrid policy
options.B: Assume existing fully in-office collaboration practices will work unchanged in the new hybrid model
options.C: Reassess and adapt team collaboration practices (e.g., meeting formats, communication tools, documentation practices) to genuinely support effective hybrid collaboration
options.D: Refuse to adapt any practices since the shift is an organizational decision outside the team's control

justification: Correct. Reassessing and adapting collaboration practices to genuinely support hybrid work reflects proactive, responsible adaptation to a significant organizational operating model change.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where the project's actual resource utilization is significantly lower than planned, despite the schedule remaining on track. What is the BEST way to interpret this?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy since the schedule remaining on track means nothing else matters
options.B: Investigate the reason for lower-than-planned utilization, which could indicate either efficiency gains or potential underlying issues like scope reduction or resource availability problems
options.C: Immediately reduce the project budget without any further analysis
options.D: Assume this is always a positive sign requiring no further investigation

justification: Correct. Investigating the reason behind lower utilization helps distinguish between a genuinely positive efficiency gain and a potential underlying issue, informing appropriate next steps either way.

text: A team member consistently offers overly detailed technical explanations during Sprint Reviews that lose the attention of business-focused stakeholders. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Coach them on tailoring the level of technical detail to the specific audience present, focusing on business value and outcomes for stakeholder-facing presentations
options.B: Require all technical details to be included regardless of audience, to ensure complete transparency
options.C: Exclude the team member from presenting during Sprint Reviews entirely
options.D: Ignore the pattern since technical accuracy is more important than audience engagement

justification: Correct. Coaching on tailoring technical detail to the audience, focusing on business value for stakeholder-facing contexts, directly addresses the engagement issue while preserving their valuable expertise and presence.

text: Which of the following are valid uses of a burndown chart? (Select TWO)

options.A: Visualizing remaining work against time within a Sprint
options.B: Helping the team identify whether they are trending toward completing the Sprint's forecasted work
options.C: Calculating the organization's total annual revenue
options.D: Determining individual team member performance appraisal ratings

justification: Correct. Visualizing remaining work against time within a Sprint is the primary, standard purpose of a burndown chart. / Correct. Burndown charts help the team see whether they are trending toward completing forecasted work, supporting timely awareness of pace issues.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new workplace harassment prevention training requirements following recent legislative changes. What should the project manager do to ensure project team compliance?

options.A: Coordinate with HR to ensure all project team members complete the required training within the mandated timeframe, adjusting schedules as needed to accommodate this
options.B: Require team members to complete the training entirely on their own personal time without any schedule accommodation
options.C: Assume HR will handle all compliance with no need for project-level follow-up
options.D: Ignore the new requirement since it is not directly related to technical project deliverables

justification: Correct. Coordinating with HR and adjusting schedules to accommodate mandatory training reflects responsible integration of a legal compliance requirement into project-level planning.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a specific pair of team members consistently produce excellent work when collaborating together but struggle when paired with others. What is the BEST way to leverage this observation?

options.A: Always pair these two team members together exclusively for all future work, regardless of other considerations
options.B: Ignore the pattern since pairing effectiveness is purely coincidental and not worth considering
options.C: Recognize their effective collaboration while also intentionally creating opportunities for both to develop collaborative skills with other team members, to avoid over-reliance on this single pairing
options.D: Separate the two team members permanently to force them to develop skills with others

justification: Correct. Recognizing their effective collaboration while intentionally building broader collaborative skills across the team balances leveraging a good pairing with reducing over-reliance risk.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate approach for handling a situation where a critical path activity's actual duration significantly exceeded the original estimate, though the activity is now complete. What is the BEST way to use this information going forward?

options.A: Blame the team member who provided the original estimate without further investigation
options.B: Assume the original estimating approach is fundamentally flawed and abandon all further use of that estimating technique on the project
options.C: Analyze the reasons for the estimation discrepancy, update remaining schedule estimates if similar activities remain, and capture the insight as a lesson learned for future estimating
options.D: Ignore the discrepancy since the activity is already complete and cannot be changed

justification: Correct. Analyzing the discrepancy's cause, updating remaining estimates if similar work remains, and capturing lessons learned reflects proper use of actual performance data to improve ongoing and future planning.

text: Match each type of competitive strategy to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Competing by offering the lowest price in the market while maintaining acceptable quality
Competing by offering unique features or value that competitors don't provide
Competing by targeting a specific, narrow market segment particularly well
Competing by creating uncontested new market space rather than competing directly with existing rivals

justification: Cost leadership strategy focuses on becoming the lowest-cost producer in an industry, competing primarily on price while maintaining acceptable quality. / Differentiation strategy focuses on offering unique features, quality, or value that sets the product apart from competitors, often commanding a premium price. / A focus strategy targets a specific, narrower market segment, serving that niche particularly well rather than competing broadly. / Blue ocean strategy seeks to create new, uncontested market space, making direct competition with existing rivals largely irrelevant.

text: A project manager wants to ensure that a new team member from a different professional discipline (e.g., a data scientist joining a traditionally engineering-heavy team) feels genuinely integrated and valued. What is the BEST way to support this?

options.A: Assume they will naturally integrate without any specific effort or consideration
options.B: Keep their work entirely separate from the rest of the team to avoid any friction
options.C: Actively seek their unique perspective in relevant discussions, and be open to adapting some team practices to better accommodate the value their discipline brings
options.D: Expect them to conform entirely to existing engineering-centric team norms without any adaptation

justification: Correct. Actively seeking their unique perspective and being open to adapting practices reflects genuine inclusion, valuing the diverse expertise a cross-disciplinary team member brings.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Definition of Done criteria being applied inconsistently between different team members. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Create a shared checklist based on the Definition of Done, and encourage team members to use it consistently, discussing any ambiguities collectively to build shared understanding
options.B: Remove the Definition of Done entirely since perfect consistency is impossible to achieve
options.C: Assign a single person to be solely responsible for verifying every item against the Definition of Done
options.D: Let each team member interpret the Definition of Done independently based on personal judgment

justification: Correct. Creating a shared checklist and discussing ambiguities collectively builds genuine shared understanding, improving consistency in how the Definition of Done is applied across the team.

text: An agile team's organization is considering discontinuing a legacy product line that the current team's product depends on for certain integrations. What should the product leader do?

options.A: Assume the discontinuation won't affect the current product without any verification
options.B: Ignore the discontinuation discussion since it involves a different product line
options.C: Assess the potential impact on the current product's integrations, and add relevant backlog items to plan for a transition if the discontinuation proceeds
options.D: Immediately build a completely new integration architecture without confirming whether the discontinuation will actually happen

justification: Correct. Assessing the potential impact and adding relevant contingency backlog items reflects proactive, responsible preparation for a dependency risk tied to another product line's uncertain future.

text: A project manager needs to determine whether a quality issue found in a sample inspection represents a systemic problem or an isolated incident. What is the BEST way to make this determination?

options.A: Assume every quality issue found is automatically systemic regardless of sample size or pattern
options.B: Assume the issue is isolated without any further investigation
options.C: Expand the inspection sample or analyze historical data to determine whether the issue represents a broader pattern or an isolated occurrence
options.D: Ignore the finding entirely since sample inspections are inherently unreliable

justification: Correct. Expanding the inspection sample or analyzing historical data provides the evidence needed to properly distinguish between a systemic pattern and an isolated incident, informing appropriate response.

text: A team member consistently expresses frustration that they are asked to attend meetings that don't seem relevant to their specific work. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Exclude them from all meetings entirely without any review of what might genuinely be relevant
options.B: Ignore their frustration since meeting attendance policies should never be questioned
options.C: Require them to attend every meeting regardless of relevance to maintain consistency
options.D: Review meeting attendance requirements with them, adjusting invitations to better reflect actual relevance while ensuring they still receive necessary information through appropriate channels

justification: Correct. Reviewing and adjusting meeting invitations based on actual relevance, while ensuring necessary information still reaches them, addresses the legitimate concern while maintaining appropriate information flow.

text: Which of the following are appropriate outcomes of a well-facilitated Sprint Retrospective? (Select TWO)

options.A: Specific, actionable improvement items the team commits to trying in the next Sprint
options.B: A shared understanding of what worked well and should be continued
options.C: A finalized annual budget for the entire organization
options.D: A permanent, unchangeable list of team rules that can never be revisited

justification: Correct. Specific, actionable improvement items the team commits to trying is a core, valuable outcome of an effective Sprint Retrospective. / Correct. A shared understanding of what worked well, worth continuing, is an important outcome that reinforces effective practices alongside identifying improvements.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new international sanctions regime affecting business with certain countries. A current subcontractor is based in a now-sanctioned country. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Unilaterally terminate the subcontract without any legal consultation
options.B: Immediately consult with legal/compliance to determine the specific impact of the sanctions on the existing subcontract and identify required actions
options.C: Ignore the sanctions since they were issued by a government body, not directly by an industry regulator
options.D: Continue the subcontract relationship unchanged since the contract was signed before the sanctions took effect

justification: Correct. Immediately consulting legal/compliance to determine the specific, actual impact and required actions reflects the appropriate, responsible first step when facing a serious legal/regulatory change like international sanctions.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a team member consistently expresses that they don't fully understand the 'why' behind certain product decisions, only the 'what.' What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Require the team member to independently research the rationale on their own without any support
options.B: Tell them the 'why' is not necessary for them to know to do their job
options.C: Ignore the concern since understanding the 'why' is a nice-to-have, not essential
options.D: Work with the Product Owner to more consistently share the underlying rationale and context behind product decisions during relevant team discussions

justification: Correct. Working with the Product Owner to more consistently share underlying rationale directly addresses the concern and can improve the whole team's understanding and engagement, not just this individual's.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate response to a stakeholder who requests a change that would violate a legal or regulatory requirement. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Explain the legal/regulatory constraint to the stakeholder, decline the change as requested, and explore whether any compliant alternative could address their underlying need
options.B: Implement the requested change since satisfying the stakeholder is the top priority
options.C: Ignore the stakeholder's request entirely without any explanation
options.D: Implement the change secretly without informing the stakeholder about the legal issue, hoping it goes unnoticed

justification: Correct. Explaining the constraint, declining the non-compliant request, and exploring compliant alternatives respects both the legal requirement and the stakeholder's underlying need, reflecting responsible, transparent stakeholder management.

text: A project manager wants to develop stronger emotional intelligence in recognizing when team members are experiencing stress before it visibly affects their work. What is the BEST way to build this capability?

options.A: Only address stress if a team member explicitly and formally reports it
options.B: Wait until visible performance decline occurs before considering any team member's stress level
options.C: Assume stress is a purely personal matter that project managers should never consider
options.D: Practice regular, genuine check-ins with team members, paying attention to subtle changes in behavior, tone, or engagement that might indicate early signs of stress

justification: Correct. Regular, genuine check-ins with attention to subtle behavioral changes builds the emotional intelligence and early awareness needed to provide timely, supportive intervention before stress significantly affects performance.

text: A project manager wants to ensure that a team member with a physical disability has full and equal opportunity to participate in all project activities, including site visits. What is the BEST way to approach this?

options.A: Assume they will independently arrange any needed accommodations without any support
options.B: Publicly discuss their disability with the rest of the team without their consent to explain any special arrangements
options.C: Exclude them from site visits by default to avoid any accommodation complexity
options.D: Have a private conversation to understand their specific needs, and proactively arrange reasonable accommodations to ensure full, equal participation in all relevant activities

justification: Correct. A private conversation to understand specific needs, followed by proactively arranging reasonable accommodations, ensures full, equal, and respectful participation, reflecting genuine inclusive leadership.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being disrupted by team members taking planned vacation mid-Sprint. What is the BEST way to proactively address this?

options.A: Always assume full team capacity regardless of any known scheduled absences
options.B: Ignore planned vacation entirely when forecasting Sprint capacity
options.C: Account for known planned absences when calculating available capacity for the Sprint, adjusting the forecast accordingly before commitment
options.D: Forbid all vacation during any active Sprint regardless of prior planning

justification: Correct. Explicitly accounting for known planned absences when calculating capacity ensures a realistic, achievable Sprint forecast, directly preventing disruption from anticipated schedule changes.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting multiple currencies for international customers, requiring significant backlog work across payment processing, display formatting, and reporting. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Delegate the entire currency support decision to the finance department with no product input
options.B: Ignore currency support needs since the current single-currency approach has worked so far
options.C: Research which currencies are actually needed based on current and projected customer base, and prioritize backlog work accordingly, starting with the highest-value markets
options.D: Immediately build support for every possible global currency without prioritizing based on actual customer demand

justification: Correct. Researching actual currency needs and prioritizing based on real customer value reflects responsible, evidence-based backlog planning for a significant new capability requiring substantial investment.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate frequency for updating the risk register during project execution. What is the BEST basis for this decision?

options.A: Update the risk register randomly with no consistent schedule or trigger
options.B: Update the risk register regularly throughout the project, with frequency informed by the project's risk profile and rate of change, as specified in the risk management plan
options.C: Update the risk register only when a risk fully materializes into an issue
options.D: Update the risk register only once at project initiation and never again

justification: Correct. Regular updates informed by the project's risk profile and rate of change, as defined in the risk management plan, reflects the standard, appropriate ongoing risk management practice throughout project execution.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel disconnected from the broader company mission, focusing only on their immediate tasks. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Regularly connect the team's work to the broader company mission and impact, helping them see how their specific contributions matter to larger organizational goals
options.B: Ignore the concern since company mission connection is solely an executive-level responsibility
options.C: Require them to memorize the company mission statement without further context or connection
options.D: Dismiss their concern since focusing only on immediate tasks is sufficient for job performance

justification: Correct. Regularly connecting the team's work to the broader mission and impact helps build genuine purpose and engagement, directly addressing their expressed disconnection.

text: Which of the following are valid techniques for developing a project's cost estimate when historical data is limited? (Select TWO)

options.A: Expert judgment from experienced practitioners
options.B: Three-point estimating to account for uncertainty
options.C: Assuming costs will be identical to a completely unrelated project
options.D: Ignoring cost estimation entirely due to limited data

justification: Correct. Expert judgment from experienced practitioners is a valuable technique when historical data is limited, leveraging accumulated professional experience. / Correct. Three-point estimating, using optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely values, helps account for uncertainty when precise historical data isn't available.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new industry-specific licensing requirement for personnel performing certain specialized tasks on the project. What is the BEST way to ensure compliance?

options.A: Ignore the licensing requirement since it was introduced after the project began
options.B: Assume all current team members already meet the new licensing requirement without verification
options.C: Identify which team members require the new licensing, arrange for them to obtain it within any required timeframe, and adjust task assignments in the interim if needed
options.D: Continue having unlicensed personnel perform the specialized tasks since they have relevant experience

justification: Correct. Identifying licensing needs, arranging timely acquisition, and adjusting assignments in the interim reflects responsible, proactive compliance with a new mandatory professional licensing requirement.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their work-life boundaries are not respected, citing frequent after-hours messages even when not urgent. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Ban all communication tools entirely outside of standard working hours, even for genuine emergencies
options.B: Require them to be available and responsive at all hours regardless of urgency
options.C: Establish clear team norms around after-hours communication, reserving it for genuine emergencies, and model respecting these boundaries personally
options.D: Dismiss their concern since occasional after-hours communication is normal in most workplaces

justification: Correct. Establishing clear norms reserving after-hours communication for genuine emergencies, combined with modeling this behavior personally, directly addresses the concern while maintaining necessary flexibility for true emergencies.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a critical defect being introduced without detection due to insufficient automated test coverage in a specific area of the codebase. What is the BEST proactive step?

options.A: Ignore the coverage gap since manual testing alone should be sufficient
options.B: Stop all further development in that area of the codebase indefinitely
options.C: Remove all existing tests in that area since coverage is already insufficient anyway
options.D: Add backlog items to improve automated test coverage in the identified gap area, prioritizing based on the criticality and risk of that part of the codebase

justification: Correct. Adding prioritized backlog items to improve automated test coverage directly addresses the identified risk area, particularly important given its criticality.

text: Match each type of stakeholder power/interest grid quadrant to its correct management strategy.

colonne_droite.texte: Manage closely, engaging them as key partners in decision-making
Keep satisfied, providing enough information to maintain their support without overwhelming them
Keep informed, as they are engaged but have limited ability to directly influence outcomes
Monitor with minimal effort, since they require the least attention

justification: Stakeholders with both high power and high interest should be managed closely as key partners, given their significant ability to influence and stake in the outcome. / Stakeholders with high power but low interest should be kept satisfied with appropriate, efficient information, avoiding overwhelming them with unnecessary detail. / Stakeholders with low power but high interest should be kept informed, as their engagement is valuable even though their direct influence is limited. / Stakeholders with low power and low interest require the least active management effort, monitored with minimal ongoing attention.

text: A project manager wants to help a team develop a stronger sense of psychological safety around admitting when they don't know something. What is the BEST way to model this?

options.A: Criticize team members whenever they admit uncertainty about something
options.B: Model openly admitting their own knowledge gaps when genuine, framing 'I don't know, let's find out' as a positive, normal response
options.C: Avoid ever discussing topics where uncertainty might arise
options.D: Always project complete confidence and never admit any uncertainty as project manager

justification: Correct. Modeling genuine, comfortable admission of one's own knowledge gaps directly builds the psychological safety needed for team members to feel similarly comfortable admitting uncertainty.

text: A project manager needs to determine whether to use a fixed-price or cost-reimbursable contract for a project component with significant technical uncertainty and evolving requirements. What is generally the MORE appropriate contract type?

options.A: The choice should be based purely on which type is administratively easier for the buyer, regardless of the underlying risk profile
options.B: Firm Fixed Price, since it always minimizes buyer risk regardless of context
options.C: Neither type is ever appropriate for uncertain scope; only Time and Materials should be used
options.D: Cost-reimbursable, since it better accommodates significant technical uncertainty and evolving requirements without forcing premature, potentially inaccurate price commitments

justification: Correct. Cost-reimbursable contracts generally accommodate significant technical uncertainty and evolving requirements better, since they don't require locking in a price before the scope is fully understood.

text: A team member consistently expresses concern that their manager (outside the project) doesn't understand or value the agile work they're doing on this project. What is the BEST way for the project leader to help?

options.A: Tell the team member to simply accept their manager's lack of understanding
options.B: Ignore the concern since the manager relationship is entirely outside the project leader's scope
options.C: Directly confront the team member's manager without the team member's knowledge or consent
options.D: Offer to help facilitate better communication between the team member and their manager about the value and nature of the agile work, if the team member would find that helpful

justification: Correct. Offering to help facilitate better communication, with the team member's consent and involvement, respects their agency while providing genuine, supportive assistance with a real cross-organizational challenge.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of misunderstanding between the Product Owner's written requirements and the Development Team's technical interpretation for a complex integration feature. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Skip written requirements entirely and rely solely on verbal instructions
options.B: Rely solely on written requirements with no further discussion
options.C: Have the Development Team implement based purely on assumption without any clarification from the Product Owner
options.D: Combine written acceptance criteria with a collaborative discussion or walkthrough during refinement, allowing the team to ask clarifying questions and confirm shared understanding before implementation

justification: Correct. Combining written criteria with collaborative discussion during refinement allows clarifying questions and confirms shared understanding, directly reducing the risk of misinterpretation for complex work.

text: A project manager's organization is entering into a joint venture agreement with a foreign partner, requiring the project to navigate two different countries' distinct project governance and reporting requirements. What is the BEST way to manage this?

options.A: Work with both partner organizations to establish a harmonized governance and reporting framework that satisfies both countries' requirements where possible
options.B: Apply only one country's governance and reporting requirements, ignoring the other's distinct needs
options.C: Ignore both countries' formal governance requirements in favor of an informal, ad-hoc approach
options.D: Refuse to proceed with the joint venture due to the governance complexity

justification: Correct. Working with both partner organizations to establish a harmonized framework satisfying both sets of requirements reflects responsible, collaborative management of a genuinely complex, multi-jurisdictional governance situation.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that team members consistently defer significant technical decisions to a single 'unofficial' technical lead, even though there is no formally designated tech lead role. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Forbid the informal tech lead from ever offering technical opinions again
options.B: Ignore the pattern since informal leadership naturally emerges and requires no attention
options.C: Formalize the informal tech lead role immediately without any team discussion
options.D: Facilitate a team discussion about how technical decisions should be made collectively, exploring whether a formal role would genuinely help or whether more distributed decision-making would better serve the team

justification: Correct. Facilitating a genuine team discussion about decision-making structure allows the team to collectively determine the best approach, whether formalizing a role or distributing decisions more broadly.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a discovered error in a previously accepted deliverable, weeks after formal acceptance. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Fix the error silently without informing anyone since it was already accepted
options.B: Immediately terminate the vendor or team responsible without any further investigation
options.C: Assess the actual impact and severity of the error, and communicate with relevant stakeholders to determine the appropriate corrective action, even though formal acceptance already occurred
options.D: Ignore the error since the deliverable was already formally accepted

justification: Correct. Assessing the actual impact and severity, then communicating with stakeholders to determine appropriate corrective action, is the responsible approach regardless of prior formal acceptance, since genuine quality issues can still require remediation.

text: Which of the following are examples of appropriate ways an agile product team could respond to a significant shift in customer demographics discovered through market research? (Select TWO)

options.A: Reassessing the Product Backlog to ensure it reflects the needs of the evolving customer base
options.B: Conducting further targeted research to better understand the new demographic's specific needs before making major changes
options.C: Ignoring the demographic shift entirely since the original customer base was well understood
options.D: Immediately discontinuing the entire product without any further analysis

justification: Correct. Reassessing the backlog to reflect an evolving customer base is a responsive, evidence-based way to adapt to a genuine market shift. / Correct. Conducting further targeted research before major changes ensures decisions are based on solid understanding of the new demographic's actual needs, avoiding premature or misinformed pivots.

text: A project manager wants to develop a habit of regularly reflecting on their own leadership effectiveness, beyond just team performance metrics. What is the BEST way to build this practice?

options.A: Rely solely on the project's overall success or failure as the only indicator of personal leadership effectiveness
options.B: Avoid any self-reflection to prevent unnecessary self-doubt
options.C: Assume leadership effectiveness cannot be meaningfully assessed or improved
options.D: Regularly seek honest feedback from the team and peers, reflect on specific leadership moments, and identify concrete areas for personal growth

justification: Correct. Regularly seeking honest feedback, reflecting on specific moments, and identifying concrete growth areas reflects a genuine, evidence-based approach to ongoing leadership development.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment containing subtle regressions in previously working functionality due to new changes. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Rely solely on manual testing of new features, without any regression testing of existing functionality
options.B: Maintain and run an automated regression test suite as part of the team's standard workflow, ensuring previously working functionality is verified alongside new changes
options.C: Skip all testing of previously working features since they were already verified once before
options.D: Only test for regressions once per year regardless of how frequently changes are made

justification: Correct. Maintaining and running an automated regression test suite as standard practice directly addresses the risk of subtle regressions, efficiently verifying existing functionality alongside each new change.

text: A project manager wants to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a team member's personal values seem to conflict with a specific project requirement (e.g., an engineer with environmental concerns working on a project involving certain materials). What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Have an open, respectful conversation to understand their concern, explore whether reasonable accommodation is possible (e.g., reassignment to a different task), while being clear about project requirements that cannot change
options.B: Immediately remove them from the project entirely without any discussion
options.C: Change the project's material requirements based solely on this one team member's personal values
options.D: Dismiss their concern entirely and require them to proceed without discussion

justification: Correct. An open, respectful conversation exploring reasonable accommodation, while being clear about non-negotiable project requirements, balances genuine care for the individual with the project's legitimate needs.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being consistently overestimated due to team members' natural optimism bias. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since optimism is generally a positive team trait
options.B: Use historical velocity data as an objective check against subjective estimates, and discuss the pattern openly during Retrospectives to build more calibrated estimation habits
options.C: Remove estimation entirely since it will always be affected by some bias
options.D: Require the team to always double their initial estimates regardless of actual historical accuracy

justification: Correct. Using historical velocity as an objective check, combined with open Retrospective discussion, helps the team build more calibrated, evidence-based estimation habits over time.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward a B2B2C business model, selling primarily through business partners rather than directly to end consumers. What should the product leader consider?

options.A: Immediately build extensive partner-facing features without validating actual partner requirements or business case
options.B: Refuse to explore the new model since it deviates from the current direct-to-consumer approach
options.C: Research the specific needs of business partners (e.g., white-labeling, partner management dashboards, different support workflows) and add relevant backlog items based on genuine business case validation
options.D: Assume the product's current direct-to-consumer features will work identically for the new B2B2C model without any adjustment

justification: Correct. Researching specific partner needs and validating the business case before committing to backlog work reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a significant business model shift.

text: A project manager wants to determine the appropriate way to validate that a completed activity's actual cost aligns with expectations before closing out that work package. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Compare actual costs against the planned budget for that work package, investigating any significant variance before formal closure
options.B: Assume actual costs always match planned costs without any verification
options.C: Close out the work package regardless of cost variance without any documentation
options.D: Skip cost verification entirely since the work package is already technically complete

justification: Correct. Comparing actual costs against the planned budget and investigating significant variances before closure ensures proper cost control and provides valuable information for ongoing project management.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel undervalued because their role (e.g., quality assurance) is perceived as less prestigious than others (e.g., development) within the team. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Actively reinforce the equal importance of all roles to overall team success, ensuring recognition practices reflect genuine appreciation for diverse contributions including quality assurance
options.B: Suggest they consider transitioning to a development role if they want to be more valued
options.C: Agree that certain roles are inherently more valuable than others
options.D: Ignore the concern since role prestige perceptions are outside the project leader's influence

justification: Correct. Actively reinforcing equal importance and ensuring recognition genuinely reflects diverse contributions directly counters the perceived hierarchy and supports fair, inclusive team culture.

text: Which of the following are valid ways to reduce the risk of a large, monolithic Product Backlog Item blocking Sprint progress? (Select TWO)

options.A: Splitting the item into smaller, independently deliverable pieces during Backlog Refinement
options.B: Identifying a walking skeleton or minimal end-to-end slice that can be delivered first, with additional functionality layered on incrementally
options.C: Assigning the entire large item to a single developer to work on in complete isolation
options.D: Ignoring the item's size and hoping it completes within the Sprint regardless

justification: Correct. Splitting large items into smaller, independently deliverable pieces during refinement is a core technique for managing large backlog items and reducing blocking risk. / Correct. Identifying a minimal end-to-end slice (walking skeleton) to deliver first, with incremental layering, is an effective technique for managing complexity and reducing the risk of large items blocking progress.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory reporting requirement to a national regulator about specific project incidents. What is the BEST way to ensure this is properly integrated into project operations?

options.A: Establish a clear internal process defining what incidents require reporting, who is responsible, and the required timeline, ensuring the project team understands these obligations
options.B: Report every minor issue to the regulator regardless of whether it meets the actual defined reporting threshold
options.C: Assume reporting will happen automatically without any specific process or responsibility assignment
options.D: Ignore the requirement since it originates from an external regulator, not internal project governance

justification: Correct. Establishing a clear internal process with defined responsibilities and timelines, communicated to the team, ensures proper compliance with a new mandatory external reporting requirement.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a team member consistently expresses reluctance to estimate their own work, deferring entirely to others' estimates even for tasks they understand best. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Publicly require them to always estimate first in every session to force participation
options.B: Always assign someone else to estimate their work permanently
options.C: Have a supportive conversation to understand their reluctance, and encourage gradual, low-pressure participation in estimating tasks within their own expertise
options.D: Ignore the pattern since estimation accuracy from others seems sufficient

justification: Correct. A supportive conversation to understand the reluctance, combined with gradual, low-pressure encouragement, respects their comfort level while helping them build confidence in an area where their expertise is valuable.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a discrepancy between two different team members' reported status for the same activity. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Ignore both reports since the discrepancy makes the information unreliable regardless of investigation
options.B: Automatically accept whichever report was received first, regardless of accuracy
options.C: Investigate directly with both team members to understand the source of the discrepancy and establish the actual, accurate status
options.D: Automatically accept the more optimistic report to avoid unnecessary concern

justification: Correct. Directly investigating with both team members to understand and resolve the discrepancy ensures the project manager has accurate, reliable status information to inform decisions.

text: Match each type of go-to-market strategy to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Selling directly to end customers through an internal sales team
Selling through third-party resellers or distributors
Relying on the product itself to drive customer acquisition and expansion, often through free trials or freemium offerings
Building and leveraging an engaged user community to drive awareness and adoption

justification: Direct sales involves an internal sales team engaging directly with end customers to close deals, without intermediary partners. / Channel partnership involves selling through third-party resellers or distributors who have their own established customer relationships. / Product-led growth relies on the product experience itself, often through free trials or freemium models, to drive acquisition and expansion with minimal direct sales involvement. / Community-led growth builds and leverages an engaged community of users or advocates to organically drive awareness, adoption, and loyalty.

text: A project manager wants to develop a team norm where constructive dissent is genuinely welcomed, even from more junior team members toward more senior ones. What is the BEST way to build this norm?

options.A: Discourage junior team members from questioning senior team members' decisions to maintain hierarchy
options.B: Only allow dissent to be expressed privately to the project manager, never openly in team discussions
options.C: Assume junior team members will naturally feel comfortable dissenting without any specific effort to encourage it
options.D: Explicitly invite and visibly welcome dissenting perspectives regardless of seniority, and model gracious, appreciative responses when junior members raise valid concerns

justification: Correct. Explicitly inviting dissent regardless of seniority and modeling gracious responses directly builds the psychological safety needed for genuine constructive dissent across hierarchy levels.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment being incompatible with an upcoming, externally mandated system upgrade scheduled for a future date. What is the BEST way to prepare?

options.A: Halt all current Sprint work indefinitely until the upgrade timeline is finalized
options.B: Add backlog items to assess and address compatibility with the known upcoming upgrade, prioritizing based on the actual timeline and risk of incompatibility
options.C: Assume compatibility will not be an issue without any verification
options.D: Ignore the upcoming upgrade until it actually occurs

justification: Correct. Adding prioritized backlog items to assess and address compatibility, based on the actual timeline and risk, reflects proactive, evidence-based preparation for a known future business/technical constraint.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward offering the product as a white-label solution for other businesses to rebrand and resell. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Immediately build comprehensive white-labeling capabilities without validating actual market demand or business case
options.B: Assume white-label partners will have identical needs to existing direct customers
options.C: Research potential white-label partner demand and validate the business case before committing significant backlog investment in white-labeling capabilities
options.D: Refuse to explore white-labeling since it deviates from the current direct product branding

justification: Correct. Researching actual partner demand and validating the business case before committing significant investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a substantial new business model opportunity.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a subcontractor's deliverable technically meets the contract specifications but falls short of the buyer's actual intended use case due to a specification gap. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Reject the deliverable outright and terminate the contract without discussion
options.B: Accept the deliverable without question since it technically meets the written specifications
options.C: Blame the subcontractor entirely for a specification gap that originated from the buyer's own incomplete requirements
options.D: Discuss the gap with the subcontractor, exploring whether a reasonable amendment or additional scope can address the actual intended use case, potentially through a formal change process

justification: Correct. Discussing the gap and exploring a reasonable amendment or additional scope through formal change process addresses the actual underlying need while respecting the contractual relationship and proper change management.

text: A team member consistently expresses frustration that their ideas are implemented but credited to whoever presents them at the next relevant meeting, rather than to the original source. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Establish a practice of explicitly acknowledging idea originators when their contributions are presented or implemented, reinforcing fair attribution as a team norm
options.B: Ignore the pattern since ideas belong to the team collectively once shared
options.C: Tell the team member to stop sharing ideas if they are concerned about credit
options.D: Publicly reprimand whoever has been taking credit without any further discussion of underlying norms

justification: Correct. Establishing an explicit practice of acknowledging idea originators reinforces fair attribution as a team norm, directly addressing the frustration while supporting a genuinely collaborative, fair culture.

text: Which of the following are appropriate ways to handle a Product Backlog Item that turns out to be significantly more complex than originally understood after work has begun? (Select TWO)

options.A: Transparently communicate the discovery to the Product Owner and discuss options such as splitting the item or adjusting the Sprint plan
options.B: Reassess the item's priority relative to other backlog items given the new complexity information
options.C: Continue working silently without informing anyone, hoping to finish regardless of the added complexity
options.D: Immediately abandon the item entirely without any further discussion or assessment

justification: Correct. Transparently communicating the discovery and discussing options like splitting or adjusting the plan reflects Scrum's transparency principle and supports informed collaborative decision-making. / Correct. Reassessing priority given new complexity information ensures the backlog continues to reflect an accurate, informed understanding of relative value and effort.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory cybersecurity framework requirement following a significant industry-wide breach affecting multiple competitors. What is the BEST way to integrate this into the current project?

options.A: Assume the current project's existing security measures already meet the new framework without any verification
options.B: Conduct a gap assessment against the new framework's specific requirements, and incorporate necessary security enhancements into the project plan with appropriate prioritization
options.C: Ignore the new framework since it was prompted by breaches at other companies, not the organization's own security incident
options.D: Implement the framework requirements without any assessment of current gaps, applying a generic checklist regardless of actual project context

justification: Correct. Conducting a proper gap assessment and incorporating necessary enhancements with appropriate prioritization reflects responsible, evidence-based integration of a new mandatory security framework requirement.

text: A project manager wants to develop a habit of proactively checking in with quieter stakeholders who may not volunteer feedback or concerns as readily as more vocal ones. What is the BEST way to build this practice?

options.A: Only communicate with the most vocal stakeholders since they represent the clearest signal of stakeholder sentiment
options.B: Assume quieter stakeholders have no concerns if they don't proactively raise them
options.C: Establish regular, individual check-ins specifically with quieter stakeholders, creating dedicated space for them to share input they might not otherwise volunteer
options.D: Require all stakeholders to speak up in large group settings regardless of their communication preferences

justification: Correct. Establishing dedicated individual check-ins specifically for quieter stakeholders creates a genuine, comfortable channel for them to share input that group settings might not naturally elicit.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of important architectural decisions being made informally without adequate consideration of long-term implications. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Require every single technical decision, regardless of significance, to go through an extensive formal review process
options.B: Assign all architectural decisions exclusively to a single senior architect with no team input
options.C: Establish a lightweight process for significant architectural decisions, such as brief architecture decision records and appropriate team review for decisions with substantial long-term impact
options.D: Allow all architectural decisions to be made ad-hoc by whoever is working on the relevant code at the time, with no structured review

justification: Correct. A lightweight process with brief decision records and appropriate review for high-impact decisions balances the need for thoughtful consideration of significant architectural choices with agile efficiency.

text: An agile team's organization is considering a shift toward a platform business model, enabling third-party developers to build applications on top of the core product. What is the BEST way for the product leader to approach this exploration?

options.A: Immediately open the platform to all third-party developers without any governance or security framework
options.B: Research the specific requirements for a viable developer platform (e.g., API design, documentation, governance, security), and validate genuine developer interest before committing significant investment
options.C: Refuse to consider the platform model since it represents a significant departure from the current closed product approach
options.D: Build the entire platform infrastructure without any validation of actual third-party developer interest

justification: Correct. Researching platform requirements and validating genuine developer interest before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a substantial and complex strategic business model shift.

text: A project manager needs to address a situation where a team member consistently arrives late to work but stays significantly later than required, completing an equivalent amount of work. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Ignore any potential coordination impact their schedule might have on the rest of the team
options.B: Reprimand them publicly for their late arrivals without considering their overall contribution
options.C: Assess whether a flexible schedule arrangement could formally accommodate their natural working pattern, provided it doesn't disrupt necessary team coordination
options.D: Strictly enforce standard arrival times regardless of overall work output or flexible arrangements

justification: Correct. Assessing whether a formal flexible arrangement could work, while ensuring necessary team coordination isn't disrupted, respects both individual working patterns and legitimate team needs.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment lacking adequate documentation for future maintainability, while still moving at agile speed. What is the BEST way to balance this?

options.A: Include lightweight, essential documentation (e.g., key architectural decisions, API contracts) as part of the Definition of Done, focusing on what genuinely supports future maintainability without excessive overhead
options.B: Require exhaustive documentation of every minor implementation detail regardless of its long-term relevance
options.C: Document everything only at the very end of the entire product's lifecycle
options.D: Skip all documentation entirely to maximize development speed

justification: Correct. Including lightweight, essential documentation focused on genuinely important maintainability needs, as part of the Definition of Done, balances agile speed with necessary long-term support considerations.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory diversity reporting requirement for government contractors, requiring detailed workforce composition data for the project team. What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Fabricate the required data if actual figures don't meet organizational preferences
options.B: Coordinate with HR to ensure the required workforce composition data for the project team is accurately collected and reported within the mandated timeline
options.C: Delay compliance indefinitely since the requirement is new and unfamiliar
options.D: Ignore the requirement since workforce composition is considered an HR matter, not a project management concern

justification: Correct. Coordinating with HR to ensure accurate, timely data collection and reporting reflects responsible integration of a legitimate mandatory compliance requirement into project operations.

text: A project manager wants to determine the appropriate way to validate that a project's risk responses have actually been effective after implementation. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Assume all implemented risk responses are automatically effective without any follow-up assessment
options.B: Only assess risk response effectiveness if a major project failure occurs
options.C: Skip any follow-up assessment since risk responses are inherently uncertain in their effectiveness
options.D: Monitor the actual outcomes following risk response implementation, comparing them against expected results to determine whether the response was genuinely effective

justification: Correct. Monitoring actual outcomes and comparing against expected results provides the objective, evidence-based validation needed to determine whether risk responses were genuinely effective.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their manager (the project leader) doesn't understand the technical complexity of their work, leading to what they perceive as unrealistic expectations. What is the BEST way for the project leader to respond?

options.A: Dismiss the concern since the project leader's role doesn't require deep technical expertise
options.B: Invite the team member to help build the leader's understanding of the technical complexity, fostering a collaborative dialogue about realistic expectations based on genuine mutual understanding
options.C: Insist that expectations remain unchanged regardless of any technical complexity concerns raised
options.D: Assign someone else to manage this team member exclusively without addressing the underlying concern

justification: Correct. Inviting the team member to help build understanding fosters collaborative dialogue, directly addressing the concern while building mutual respect and more realistic, informed expectations.

text: Which of the following are valid components of an effective Issue Log? (Select TWO)

options.A: A clear description of the issue
options.B: An assigned owner responsible for resolution
options.C: The organization's total headcount
options.D: The project sponsor's personal contact preferences unrelated to the issue

justification: Correct. A clear description of the issue is a fundamental component of an effective Issue Log, ensuring everyone understands what needs to be resolved. / Correct. An assigned owner responsible for resolution is essential for accountability and ensuring the issue is actively tracked toward resolution.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting voice-activated interfaces (e.g., smart speakers) for the product, which would require entirely new interaction design paradigms. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Immediately build comprehensive voice interface support without validating actual customer demand or use cases
options.B: Research potential customer use cases and demand for voice interaction, and validate the concept with a minimal prototype before committing significant backlog investment
options.C: Refuse to explore voice interfaces since it represents a significant departure from the current visual interface paradigm
options.D: Assume voice interface design principles are identical to existing visual interface design without any research

justification: Correct. Researching use cases and validating with a minimal prototype before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a significantly different interaction paradigm.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a critical path activity's actual start date was significantly delayed due to an upstream dependency, though the activity itself hasn't yet begun. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Wait until the activity is significantly further delayed before taking any action
options.B: Ignore the delayed start since the activity hasn't technically begun yet
options.C: Reassess the schedule impact of the delayed start, communicate with relevant stakeholders, and explore options like schedule compression if the delay threatens the project finish date
options.D: Cancel the delayed activity entirely without exploring any recovery options

justification: Correct. Reassessing schedule impact, communicating with stakeholders, and exploring compression options if the finish date is threatened reflects proactive, appropriate schedule management for a critical path disruption.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their contributions during pair programming sessions are overshadowed by a more experienced partner who tends to drive most of the coding. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Tell the less experienced team member to simply assert themselves more without any structural change
options.B: Stop all pair programming entirely to avoid this dynamic
options.C: Discuss pairing norms with both individuals, encouraging practices like regularly switching who drives (types) during the session to ensure balanced, active participation
options.D: Permanently separate the two from ever pairing together again

justification: Correct. Discussing pairing norms and encouraging practices like regularly switching the 'driver' role directly addresses the imbalance, ensuring more equitable, active participation from both partners.

text: Match each type of financial metric to its correct application in evaluating a product initiative.

colonne_droite.texte: Measures the cost to acquire a new customer through sales and marketing efforts
Measures the total revenue expected from a customer over their entire relationship with the company
Measures the percentage of customers who stop using the product over a given period
Measures predictable subscription-based revenue generated each month

justification: CAC measures the total sales and marketing cost required to acquire a single new customer, an important efficiency metric for growth investments. / CLV estimates the total revenue a business can expect from a customer throughout their relationship, informing how much can be reasonably spent on acquisition and retention. / Churn rate measures the percentage of customers lost over a period, a key indicator of customer satisfaction and product-market fit. / MRR tracks predictable subscription revenue generated monthly, providing a clear view of the business's recurring revenue health and growth trajectory.

text: A project manager wants to help a team member who has expressed feeling isolated as the only remote worker on an otherwise co-located team. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Require all team meetings to be conducted entirely in person, disregarding the remote team member's participation needs
options.B: Ensure meeting formats and communication practices genuinely accommodate remote participation equally, and create additional touchpoints to help them feel connected to the team
options.C: Ignore their isolation concern since remote work inherently involves some degree of isolation
options.D: Suggest they relocate to be co-located with the rest of the team

justification: Correct. Ensuring genuinely equitable meeting formats and creating additional connection touchpoints directly addresses the isolation concern while respecting their remote working arrangement.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being based on outdated velocity data following a significant team composition change (e.g., two new members joining, one experienced member leaving). What is the BEST way to handle this?

options.A: Stop using velocity data entirely and never resume its use for forecasting
options.B: Immediately assume velocity will double due to having more total team members now
options.C: Continue using the exact same velocity figure as before the team composition change, assuming no impact
options.D: Acknowledge that velocity may temporarily be less reliable following the team change, and use more conservative forecasting with closer monitoring until a new stable velocity baseline is established

justification: Correct. Acknowledging temporarily reduced reliability and using more conservative forecasting with closer monitoring reflects a realistic, evidence-based approach until a new stable baseline is established.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory supply chain transparency requirement, requiring disclosure of certain sourcing information for project materials. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Work with procurement to gather and verify the required sourcing information for project materials, ensuring compliant disclosure within the mandated timeline
options.B: Assume all current suppliers already meet the new transparency requirements without any verification
options.C: Ignore the requirement since supply chain transparency is considered a procurement department matter, not a project management concern
options.D: Provide incomplete or estimated sourcing information rather than verified data, to save time

justification: Correct. Working with procurement to gather and verify accurate sourcing information reflects responsible, proactive compliance with a legitimate new regulatory transparency requirement.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a completed activity's quality inspection reveals a defect rate slightly above the acceptable quality level (AQL) threshold. What is the BEST way to respond?

options.A: Accept the batch anyway since the defect rate is only slightly above the threshold
options.B: Adjust the AQL threshold retroactively to match the actual observed defect rate
options.C: Automatically discard the entire batch without following any defined quality procedure
options.D: Follow the defined quality management plan's procedure for handling batches exceeding the AQL, which may include rejection, rework, or further investigation

justification: Correct. Following the defined quality management plan's procedure for handling threshold breaches, which may include rejection, rework, or further investigation, ensures consistent, appropriate response according to established quality standards.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that team members frequently apologize for taking normal, scheduled vacation time, seeming to feel guilty about being away. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Explicitly normalize and encourage taking earned vacation time without guilt, modeling healthy boundaries around time off personally
options.B: Reinforce the guilt by expressing concern about their absence impact
options.C: Discourage team members from taking vacation during active Sprints entirely
options.D: Ignore the apologetic pattern since vacation guilt is a normal part of most workplace cultures

justification: Correct. Explicitly normalizing vacation time without guilt, combined with personally modeling healthy boundaries, directly counters an unhealthy pattern and supports genuine team wellbeing.

text: Which of the following are appropriate ways to manage a Product Backlog that has grown to include items with vastly different levels of detail (some highly refined, some very rough)? (Select TWO)

options.A: Prioritize refinement effort on items nearing the top of the backlog that are likely to be worked on soon
options.B: Allow items further down the backlog to remain less detailed until they approach being worked on, following the principle of progressive elaboration
options.C: Require every single backlog item, regardless of priority, to have identical, exhaustive detail at all times
