options.D: Refuse to add any new items to the backlog until all existing items reach the same level of detail

justification: Correct. Prioritizing refinement effort on near-term items reflects efficient, just-in-time elaboration, ensuring the most relevant items are ready when needed. / Correct. Allowing lower-priority items to remain less detailed until closer to being worked on follows the progressive elaboration principle, avoiding wasted effort on details that may change before the item becomes relevant.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting Internet of Things (IoT) device integration for the product, which would require significant new technical infrastructure and security considerations. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Research customer demand for IoT integration and assess the security and infrastructure implications before committing significant backlog investment
options.B: Immediately build comprehensive IoT integration without validating actual customer demand or assessing security implications
options.C: Assume IoT security considerations are identical to existing web application security practices without further research
options.D: Refuse to explore IoT integration since it represents a significant technical departure from the current product architecture

justification: Correct. Researching actual demand and assessing security/infrastructure implications before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a technically complex and security-sensitive new capability.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where two different quality metrics show conflicting signals about a deliverable's actual quality (e.g., low defect count but high customer complaint rate). What is the BEST way to investigate this?

options.A: Investigate the underlying reasons for the discrepancy, which could reveal that the defect tracking method is missing certain types of issues that customers are actually experiencing
options.B: Report only the more favorable metric to stakeholders without mentioning the conflicting data
options.C: Assume both metrics are equally unreliable and disregard quality data entirely going forward
options.D: Ignore the conflicting signals and simply choose whichever metric shows more favorable results

justification: Correct. Investigating the underlying reasons for the discrepancy can reveal genuine gaps, such as defect tracking missing certain issue types customers actually experience, providing valuable insight for improving both measurement and actual quality.

text: A project manager wants to develop a stronger practice of celebrating team milestones and achievements, not just addressing problems. What is the BEST way to build this into team culture?

options.A: Only discuss achievements informally, with no structured or intentional recognition practice
options.B: Focus exclusively on problems and areas for improvement, since celebrating success could reduce motivation to keep improving
options.C: Celebrate only major, rare achievements while ignoring smaller, incremental progress entirely
options.D: Establish regular, genuine recognition moments (e.g., at team meetings or milestone completions) that specifically acknowledge team and individual contributions to successes

justification: Correct. Establishing regular, genuine recognition moments that specifically acknowledge contributions builds a positive team culture, supporting morale and reinforcing the value of team members' efforts.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment being delayed due to a dependency on another team's not-yet-completed work. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Ignore cross-team dependencies entirely until they actually cause a delay
options.B: Identify and track cross-team dependencies explicitly during Backlog Refinement, coordinating proactively with the other team to align timing and reduce blocking risk
options.C: Assume the other team will always complete their work exactly on time without any coordination
options.D: Refuse to work on any item that has any cross-team dependency, regardless of its value

justification: Correct. Explicitly identifying and tracking dependencies during refinement, combined with proactive coordination, directly reduces blocking risk by ensuring timing is aligned before commitment.

text: A project manager wants to help a team member develop greater comfort with ambiguity in early project phases, when many details are not yet fully defined. What is the BEST way to support this?

options.A: Acknowledge the genuine uncertainty honestly, while providing what clarity is actually available, and coach them on frameworks for making progress despite incomplete information
options.B: Dismiss their discomfort as an unprofessional reaction
options.C: Assign them only to tasks with complete certainty, avoiding all ambiguous work indefinitely
options.D: Provide artificially precise details even when genuine uncertainty exists, just to reduce their discomfort

justification: Correct. Honestly acknowledging genuine uncertainty while providing available clarity, combined with coaching on frameworks for progressing despite ambiguity, builds genuine comfort and capability over time.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment failing to meet non-obvious edge cases that only appear under specific real-world conditions (e.g., high traffic, unusual input combinations). What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Skip testing entirely for features considered unlikely to encounter edge cases
options.B: Incorporate techniques like exploratory testing, load testing, and boundary value analysis as part of the team's testing practice for relevant features
options.C: Assume edge cases will never actually occur in real-world usage
options.D: Test only the most common, obvious use cases

justification: Correct. Incorporating techniques like exploratory testing, load testing, and boundary value analysis directly targets non-obvious edge cases that standard testing might miss, appropriate for genuinely risk-relevant features.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) governance model for a specific product feature, involving blockchain-based community voting. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Refuse to explore the concept since it represents an unfamiliar and unconventional governance approach
options.B: Immediately implement the DAO governance model without any research into its legal, technical, or business implications
options.C: Assume DAO governance requirements are identical to the organization's existing traditional governance structures
options.D: Research the legal, technical, and business implications of DAO governance, and validate the concept's actual value proposition before committing significant backlog investment

justification: Correct. Researching the multifaceted implications and validating the actual value proposition before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a genuinely novel and complex governance concept.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a completed milestone's actual deliverable quality significantly exceeds the defined acceptance criteria, at additional unplanned cost. What is the BEST way to view this?

options.A: Automatically praise this outcome as unambiguously positive regardless of the unplanned cost
options.B: Assess whether the additional quality and cost were genuinely warranted or represent unnecessary gold-plating beyond what stakeholders actually needed or requested
options.C: Ignore the cost overrun since higher quality is always inherently worth any additional expense
options.D: Immediately terminate the responsible team member for exceeding the defined scope

justification: Correct. Assessing whether the extra quality and cost were genuinely warranted, or represent unnecessary gold-plating beyond actual stakeholder needs, provides an objective basis for evaluating this outcome and informing future practice.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel undervalued because their preferred work format (e.g., focused solo deep work) doesn't align with the team's heavy emphasis on collaborative pairing. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Dismiss their preference since team collaboration is always more valuable than individual working styles
options.B: Explore whether certain types of tasks could reasonably accommodate their preferred solo focus time, while maintaining collaborative practices where they genuinely add the most value
options.C: Require them to abandon their preference entirely and always work collaboratively regardless of task type
options.D: Exclude them from all collaborative work entirely to accommodate their preference

justification: Correct. Exploring reasonable accommodation for certain task types, while maintaining collaboration where it genuinely adds value, balances individual working style preferences with genuine team collaboration needs.

text: Which of the following are valid reasons to use Monte Carlo simulation in project risk analysis? (Select TWO)

options.A: To model the combined effect of multiple uncertain variables on overall project cost or schedule outcomes
options.B: To generate a probability distribution of possible project completion dates or costs
options.C: To determine the exact color scheme for the project's final presentation slides
options.D: To calculate individual team member salary adjustments

justification: Correct. Monte Carlo simulation models the combined effect of multiple uncertain variables, providing insight into overall project outcome uncertainty that simpler techniques might miss. / Correct. Generating a probability distribution of possible completion dates or costs is a primary, valuable output of Monte Carlo simulation for quantitative risk analysis.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new mandatory disclosure requirements regarding artificial intelligence use in customer-facing products. What is the BEST way to address this for a current project incorporating AI features?

options.A: Review the specific new disclosure requirements, assess current gaps, and incorporate necessary disclosure updates into the project's deliverables
options.B: Remove all AI features from the product entirely to avoid the disclosure requirement altogether
options.C: Ignore the requirements since AI disclosure is considered a marketing/legal matter, not a project management concern
options.D: Assume the current product's existing disclosures already satisfy the new requirements without any verification

justification: Correct. Reviewing specific new requirements, assessing gaps, and incorporating necessary updates reflects responsible, proactive integration of a legitimate new regulatory disclosure requirement into project deliverables.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that during Sprint Planning, the team consistently underestimates work involving unfamiliar third-party libraries, leading to repeated overcommitment for this type of work. What is the BEST way to help the team improve?

options.A: Ban the use of any unfamiliar third-party libraries going forward regardless of their potential value
options.B: Continue estimating this type of work the same way, assuming the pattern will resolve itself naturally
options.C: Encourage the use of time-boxed spikes to explore unfamiliar libraries before full estimation, and facilitate a Retrospective discussion to build a more informed approach to estimating this type of work
options.D: Assign estimation for all such work exclusively to the most senior developer regardless of their familiarity with the specific library involved

justification: Correct. Using time-boxed spikes to reduce uncertainty before full estimation, combined with Retrospective discussion, directly addresses the root cause of repeated underestimation for this specific type of work.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog Item's business value being misunderstood due to the Product Owner using overly technical jargon in the item's description. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Accept the jargon-heavy descriptions as-is since the Development Team should be technically fluent enough to understand them regardless
options.B: Ignore the clarity issue since backlog items are primarily an internal team artifact
options.C: Encourage the Product Owner to write backlog items using clear, business-value-focused language accessible to all stakeholders, reserving technical detail for implementation discussions
options.D: Require the Development Team to translate every item into plain language independently without Product Owner involvement

justification: Correct. Encouraging clear, business-value-focused language for backlog items, while reserving technical detail for implementation discussions, improves shared understanding across all who interact with the backlog.

text: Match each type of innovation to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Small, continuous improvements to existing products or processes
A new approach that initially serves a niche market but eventually displaces established competitors
A significant breakthrough that creates an entirely new market or fundamentally changes an existing one
Reconfiguring existing components or technologies in a new way to create value

justification: Incremental innovation involves small, continuous improvements that build on existing products or processes rather than fundamental change. / Disruptive innovation typically starts by serving underserved or niche markets with a simpler or more affordable solution, eventually displacing established market leaders. / Radical innovation represents a significant breakthrough that can create entirely new markets or fundamentally transform existing ones. / Architectural innovation involves reconfiguring existing components or technologies in new combinations, creating value without necessarily inventing entirely new core technology.

text: A project manager wants to build a habit of regularly asking the team for feedback on their own leadership approach, not just project status. What is the BEST way to make this feedback genuinely useful?

options.A: Ask only vague, general questions like 'How am I doing?' with no specific follow-up
options.B: Only ask for feedback from team members who are likely to give uniformly positive responses
options.C: Ask specific, actionable questions about particular leadership behaviors or decisions, and create a genuinely safe space for honest responses, including anonymous options if needed
options.D: Avoid asking for feedback altogether to prevent potential discomfort

justification: Correct. Asking specific, actionable questions and creating genuinely safe response conditions, including anonymous options, is much more likely to elicit honest, useful feedback for genuine leadership development.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a project's actual quality costs (cost of conformance plus cost of nonconformance) are significantly higher than planned. What is the BEST way to investigate this?

options.A: Ignore quality cost tracking entirely since it is inherently too complex to analyze meaningfully
options.B: Reduce all quality-related spending immediately without understanding the underlying cause
options.C: Assume higher quality costs are always acceptable regardless of the underlying cause
options.D: Break down the quality cost components to determine whether the increase stems from higher prevention/appraisal investment or from higher failure costs, informing the appropriate response

justification: Correct. Breaking down cost of quality into its components (prevention, appraisal, internal/external failure) reveals whether the increase reflects proactive investment or reactive failure costs, directly informing the appropriate management response.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their manager only checks in when there's a problem, never for positive reasons. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Dismiss their concern since checking in about problems is a normal, necessary part of the job
options.B: Stop checking in on problems entirely to avoid the perception issue
options.C: Increase problem-focused check-ins even further to demonstrate thorough oversight
options.D: Reflect on and adjust check-in patterns to include regular, genuine positive touchpoints, not just problem-focused conversations

justification: Correct. Reflecting on and adjusting check-in patterns to genuinely include positive touchpoints, alongside necessary problem-focused conversations, addresses the concern while maintaining necessary oversight.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog Item's estimated size proving inaccurate due to hidden complexity in legacy code that will be modified. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Always apply an arbitrary fixed multiplier to any estimate involving legacy code, regardless of actual investigation
options.B: Conduct a brief technical investigation or spike into the relevant legacy code before finalizing the estimate, specifically to surface hidden complexity
options.C: Refuse to ever estimate work involving legacy code modifications
options.D: Assume legacy code modifications are always as simple as new feature development

justification: Correct. Conducting a brief technical investigation or spike specifically targeting the relevant legacy code directly surfaces hidden complexity before finalizing the estimate, producing a more accurate, informed forecast.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory pay transparency law requiring salary ranges to be disclosed in job postings for project team recruitment. What is the BEST way to ensure compliance for ongoing project team hiring?

options.A: Continue posting job listings without salary ranges since hiring is considered purely an HR function
options.B: Coordinate with HR to ensure all project-related job postings include the legally required salary range disclosures
options.C: Ignore the law since it primarily concerns compensation structure, not project delivery
options.D: Provide intentionally vague or misleading salary ranges to technically comply while minimizing actual disclosure

justification: Correct. Coordinating with HR to ensure compliant job postings reflects responsible integration of a legitimate mandatory legal requirement into project-related hiring activities.

text: Which of the following are valid ways to reduce the risk of a Sprint Retrospective becoming repetitive and losing team engagement over time? (Select TWO)

options.A: Vary the facilitation format and techniques used across different Retrospectives
options.B: Ensure action items from previous Retrospectives are genuinely followed up on, so the team sees tangible value from participating
options.C: Use the exact same format and questions in every single Retrospective indefinitely, regardless of team feedback
options.D: Cancel Retrospectives entirely once the team has been together for more than a few months

justification: Correct. Varying facilitation formats and techniques keeps Retrospectives engaging and can surface different types of insights than a single repeated format might reveal. / Correct. Ensuring genuine follow-up on action items helps the team see tangible value from their participation, directly supporting sustained engagement over time.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting augmented reality (AR) features for the product, which would require entirely new design and technical skill sets. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Assume AR development follows identical processes and timelines as the team's existing standard web/mobile development
options.B: Immediately hire an entirely new team and build comprehensive AR features without validating actual customer demand
options.C: Refuse to explore AR since it represents a significant departure from the team's current skill set
options.D: Research customer interest in AR features and validate the concept with a minimal prototype or proof of concept before committing significant investment in new skill sets and infrastructure

justification: Correct. Researching customer interest and validating with a minimal prototype before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a technically demanding new capability area.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a team's actual productivity metrics show significant week-to-week variance, making it difficult to establish a reliable baseline. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Use only the single worst week's data as a conservative baseline for all future planning
options.B: Abandon productivity measurement entirely due to the observed variance
options.C: Use only the single best week's data as the ongoing baseline for future planning
options.D: Use a rolling average over a sufficient number of periods to smooth out short-term variance and establish a more reliable, representative baseline

justification: Correct. Using a rolling average over a sufficient number of periods smooths out short-term variance, providing a more reliable, representative baseline for planning purposes.

text: A project manager wants to build a stronger practice of actively seeking out and valuing dissenting opinions during major project decisions, to avoid groupthink. What is the BEST way to build this into team decision-making?

options.A: Only make major decisions unilaterally to avoid the complexity of managing dissent
options.B: Move quickly to consensus without deliberately seeking any dissenting views
options.C: Explicitly designate a rotating 'devil's advocate' role or ask directly for counterarguments before finalizing significant decisions
options.D: Discourage any disagreement with the majority view once it starts to form

justification: Correct. Explicitly designating a rotating devil's advocate role or directly asking for counterarguments builds a structured mechanism for surfacing dissenting views, directly countering groupthink risk.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment being technically complete but failing to actually solve the underlying user problem it was intended to address. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Assume technical completion automatically means the user problem has been solved
options.B: Skip validating actual problem-solving effectiveness since technical delivery is the team's primary responsibility
options.C: Frame acceptance criteria and Sprint Review discussions around whether the delivered solution genuinely addresses the underlying user problem, not just technical completion
options.D: Focus acceptance criteria purely on technical implementation details, ignoring the underlying user problem entirely

justification: Correct. Framing acceptance criteria and review discussions around genuine problem-solving effectiveness, not just technical completion, directly addresses the risk of building the 'right' thing technically but the 'wrong' thing from a user value perspective.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their contributions to team decisions are only valued when they align with the majority technical approach already favored by the team. What is the BEST way for the project leader to respond?

options.A: Dismiss the concern since majority technical consensus is generally the most efficient approach
options.B: Require the team to always adopt minority viewpoints regardless of their actual technical merit
options.C: Tell them to simply align with the majority to reduce friction
options.D: Explore their specific experiences and work with the team to create explicit space for alternative technical viewpoints to be genuinely considered before decisions are finalized

justification: Correct. Exploring their specific experiences and creating explicit space for alternative viewpoints supports genuinely inclusive technical decision-making and reduces groupthink risk.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that a team member consistently avoids giving direct feedback during Retrospectives, instead only sharing concerns privately afterward. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Thank them for the feedback, and explore what might help them feel more comfortable sharing openly during the Retrospective itself, while still valuing whatever input they provide
options.B: Require them to only ever provide feedback publicly, refusing to hear any private concerns
options.C: Publicly call out their pattern of avoiding open feedback during a team meeting
options.D: Ignore the private feedback since it wasn't shared during the actual event

justification: Correct. Genuinely welcoming the feedback while exploring what might build comfort with open sharing respects the individual while working toward improved psychological safety within the actual Retrospective.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel excluded from technical decision-making because meetings are often held in a specific format (e.g., whiteboard sessions) that doesn't suit their preferred way of processing information. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Exclude them from technical decision-making meetings entirely since the format doesn't suit them
options.B: Dismiss their concern since whiteboard sessions are the team's established, unchangeable practice
options.C: Explore alternative or complementary formats (e.g., written pre-reads, follow-up documentation) that could make technical discussions more accessible to their preferred processing style
options.D: Require them to adapt entirely to the whiteboard format regardless of their processing preferences

justification: Correct. Exploring complementary formats that support their processing style directly addresses the inclusion concern while preserving the value of the existing collaborative format for others.

text: A team member consistently expresses discomfort about the team's practice of publicly displaying individual task assignments on a shared board, feeling it creates unwanted scrutiny. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Dismiss their concern since task board transparency is a standard, unquestionable agile practice
options.B: Remove all visibility into individual task assignments entirely for the whole team
options.C: Discuss their specific concerns about scrutiny, and explore whether adjustments to how the board is presented or discussed could reduce discomfort while maintaining necessary team visibility
options.D: Require them to simply accept the discomfort since transparency benefits the team overall

justification: Correct. Discussing their specific concerns and exploring adjustments to presentation or discussion of the board addresses the underlying discomfort while preserving the genuine coordination value of shared visibility.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel undervalued because their work tends to be less visible to stakeholders compared to more customer-facing feature work (e.g., backend infrastructure improvements). What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Find ways to make their infrastructure work's impact more visible to stakeholders (e.g., connecting it explicitly to improved performance or reliability metrics that stakeholders care about)
options.B: Reassign them exclusively to customer-facing work regardless of their actual skills or interests
options.C: Ignore the visibility gap since it doesn't affect their actual compensation
options.D: Dismiss their concern since infrastructure work is inherently less important than customer-facing features

justification: Correct. Making infrastructure work's impact explicitly visible by connecting it to stakeholder-relevant outcomes directly addresses the recognition gap while preserving the value of their important work.

text: A team member consistently expresses frustration that Sprint Retrospectives feel repetitive, surfacing the same issues without meaningful resolution over time. What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Investigate why previously identified issues haven't been resolved, which may reveal a need for stronger follow-through, different facilitation techniques, or addressing a deeper systemic root cause
options.B: Ignore the frustration since some repetition is a normal part of continuous improvement
options.C: Cancel Retrospectives entirely since they aren't producing new insights
options.D: Simply introduce a new Retrospective format without investigating why previous action items weren't resolved

justification: Correct. Investigating why previously identified issues remain unresolved directly targets the actual cause of the frustration, whether it's follow-through, facilitation, or a deeper systemic issue.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel pressured to always appear busy, even during legitimate lulls in workload, due to a perceived team culture that equates visible activity with value. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Ignore the concern since maintaining visible activity is generally beneficial for team morale
options.B: Reinforce the perception by praising visible busyness regardless of actual productive output
options.C: Explicitly address and correct this cultural misperception, emphasizing that genuine value and outcomes matter more than the appearance of constant busyness
options.D: Assign additional, unnecessary busy-work tasks to fill any perceived lulls in workload

justification: Correct. Explicitly correcting the cultural misperception and emphasizing genuine outcomes over appearance directly addresses the harmful pressure and supports a healthier, more sustainable team culture.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their onboarding was inadequate, leaving them without a clear understanding of certain foundational aspects of the project even months later. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Have a supportive conversation to understand specific gaps, provide targeted catch-up support, and use their feedback to improve onboarding for future new team members
options.B: Dismiss the concern since enough time has passed that they should have figured things out independently by now
options.C: Require them to independently research all foundational knowledge without any additional support
options.D: Assume their concern reflects a personal shortcoming rather than a genuine onboarding gap

justification: Correct. Understanding specific gaps, providing targeted support, and using the feedback to improve future onboarding directly addresses both the individual's need and a broader process improvement opportunity.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their part-time schedule (due to caregiving responsibilities) is viewed negatively by the rest of the team, even though it was formally approved by management. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Ignore the concern since the part-time arrangement was already formally approved
options.B: Suggest they hide their caregiving responsibilities from the rest of the team
options.C: Explicitly reinforce with the whole team that the part-time arrangement is a legitimate, valued arrangement, and address any specific negative comments or behaviors directly if identified
options.D: Require them to work full-time hours to eliminate the perceived stigma

justification: Correct. Explicitly reinforcing the legitimacy of the arrangement and addressing any specific negative behaviors directly tackles the cultural perception issue while supporting the team member's wellbeing and inclusion.

text: A project manager wants to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a team member consistently completes their assigned work but shows minimal engagement or enthusiasm during team discussions. What is the BEST way to explore this?

options.A: Have a genuine, curious conversation to understand their experience, which could reveal various factors such as personal circumstances, communication style, or unaddressed concerns
options.B: Publicly call out their lack of enthusiasm during a team meeting
options.C: Assume they are simply disengaged and address it as a straightforward performance issue
options.D: Ignore the pattern since their assigned work is being completed satisfactorily regardless

justification: Correct. A genuine, curious conversation allows for understanding the actual underlying factors, which could range from communication style to personal circumstances, before assuming any particular cause.

text: Which of the following are examples of appropriate ways to support a team member experiencing significant personal stress that is affecting their work? (Select TWO)

options.A: Offer flexibility in deadlines or workload where reasonably possible
options.B: Connect them with available organizational support resources, such as an employee assistance program
options.C: Publicly discuss their personal situation with the rest of the team without their consent
options.D: Increase their workload to help them stay distracted from personal issues

justification: Correct. Offering reasonable flexibility in deadlines or workload directly supports a team member managing significant personal stress, reflecting compassionate, practical leadership. / Correct. Connecting them with available organizational support resources, like an employee assistance program, provides appropriate professional support beyond what a project leader can personally offer.

text: Match each type of team development challenge to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: A team member contributing less effort when working in a group compared to working individually
A team prioritizing consensus and harmony over critically evaluating alternative viewpoints
A team member benefiting from group output while contributing minimal individual effort
No single team member takes ownership of a task because everyone assumes someone else will

justification: Social loafing occurs when individuals exert less effort in a group setting than they would working alone, often due to reduced individual accountability. / Groupthink happens when the desire for consensus and harmony overrides critical evaluation of alternatives, potentially leading to poor decisions. / The free rider problem occurs when a team member benefits from the group's collective output while contributing disproportionately little effort themselves. / Diffusion of responsibility occurs when tasks go unaddressed because each team member assumes someone else will take ownership, resulting in no one actually doing so.

text: A project manager inherits a team where a previous conflict between two senior members resulted in the team informally splitting into two competing factions, each aligned with one of the original disputants, even though the original disputants have since reconciled somewhat. What is the BEST way to address this lingering team dysfunction?

options.A: Formally recognize and maintain the two factions as separate permanent sub-teams to avoid further conflict
options.B: Assume the factional split will resolve on its own now that the original disputants have reconciled
options.C: Replace the entire team to eliminate the lingering dysfunction entirely
options.D: Facilitate structured team-building activities that deliberately mix members across the former factional lines, combined with reinforcing shared team goals and values to rebuild unified team identity

justification: Correct. Deliberately mixing members across former factional lines through structured activities, combined with reinforcing shared goals, directly works to rebuild a unified team identity and address the lingering dysfunction.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment lacking adequate error handling for scenarios that weren't explicitly specified in the original requirements. What is the BEST practice to address this?

options.A: Only implement error handling for scenarios explicitly listed in the original written requirements
options.B: Incorporate error handling and edge case consideration as a standard part of the team's Definition of Done, encouraging developers to proactively consider reasonable failure scenarios beyond what was explicitly specified
options.C: Skip error handling entirely to speed up delivery of the primary functionality
options.D: Assume users will never encounter any unspecified error scenarios in practice

justification: Correct. Incorporating error handling consideration as a standard Definition of Done practice encourages proactive, professional judgment about reasonable failure scenarios beyond narrow, explicit specification.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Product Backlog Item's priority being based on outdated assumptions about market conditions. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Periodically review backlog priorities against current market conditions and available data, adjusting as needed to reflect genuinely current understanding
options.B: Set priorities once at project initiation and never revisit them regardless of market changes
options.C: Randomly reshuffle priorities on a fixed schedule regardless of whether market conditions have actually changed
options.D: Assume market conditions never meaningfully change once initial priorities are set

justification: Correct. Periodically reviewing priorities against current market conditions and data ensures the backlog remains aligned with genuinely current understanding, reflecting good adaptive planning practice.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment being incompatible with browsers or devices used by a significant portion of the actual user base. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Test only on the development team's own personal devices and browsers
options.B: Incorporate cross-browser and cross-device testing based on actual user analytics data showing which platforms the real user base predominantly uses
options.C: Assume all users use the same browser and device configuration as the development team
options.D: Skip compatibility testing entirely since it is considered too time-consuming

justification: Correct. Incorporating testing based on actual user analytics data ensures testing efforts focus on the platforms genuinely used by the real user base, directly addressing the compatibility risk.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being inaccurate due to inconsistent story point interpretation as new team members join over time. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Reset the team's story point scale entirely every time a new member joins
options.B: Include story point calibration as part of new team member onboarding, using reference stories to help them align their estimation scale with the established team baseline
options.C: Exclude new team members from estimation activities indefinitely to avoid calibration issues
options.D: Assume new team members will automatically understand the team's story point calibration without any specific onboarding

justification: Correct. Including story point calibration in onboarding, using reference stories, directly helps new members align with the established scale, supporting continued forecast accuracy as team composition evolves.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a critical Product Backlog Item being delayed due to reliance on a single subject matter expert who is the only one with relevant knowledge. What is the BEST way to manage this?

options.A: Assign the item exclusively to that single expert with no plan for knowledge distribution
options.B: Proactively schedule knowledge-sharing sessions or pairing with the subject matter expert to distribute relevant knowledge across additional team members, reducing single-point-of-failure risk
options.C: Remove the item from the backlog entirely to avoid the dependency risk
options.D: Accept the dependency as unavoidable since specialized knowledge naturally concentrates in individuals

justification: Correct. Proactively scheduling knowledge-sharing sessions or pairing directly reduces the concentration risk, building broader team capability and reducing dependency on a single individual.

text: Which of the following are appropriate ways to handle a Product Backlog Item where the Product Owner and Development Team disagree about relative priority? (Select TWO)

options.A: Facilitate a discussion where the Development Team shares relevant technical context that might inform the Product Owner's prioritization decision
options.B: Ultimately respect the Product Owner's final prioritization authority once the discussion has occurred, even if the Development Team's initial preference differed
options.C: Have the Development Team unilaterally reorder the backlog without any Product Owner involvement
options.D: Refuse to work on any item until the Product Owner and Development Team achieve complete, unanimous agreement on every prioritization decision

justification: Correct. Facilitating a discussion where the Development Team shares relevant technical context supports informed prioritization decisions, respecting both perspectives' value. / Correct. Ultimately respecting the Product Owner's final prioritization authority, after genuine discussion, reflects the standard Scrum accountability structure while still valuing team input in the process.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a vendor's deliverable meets contractual specifications but the underlying technology has since become industry-obsolete due to rapid technological change during the project. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Accept the deliverable as-is since it technically meets the original contractual specifications
options.B: Ignore the obsolescence issue entirely since the contract has already been technically fulfilled
options.C: Automatically reject the deliverable and terminate the vendor contract without any discussion
options.D: Assess the practical impact of the obsolescence on the project's actual objectives, and discuss with stakeholders whether a formal change to update the specification is warranted

justification: Correct. Assessing the practical impact and discussing with stakeholders whether a formal specification update is warranted reflects responsible, thoughtful management of an emergent technological change affecting project value.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where the actual resource costs for a specific role are significantly higher than what was budgeted, due to an unexpected market-wide salary increase for that specialization. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Assess the magnitude of the cost impact, update cost forecasts accordingly, and communicate the situation and any needed budget adjustment to the sponsor
options.B: Immediately terminate the affected role entirely without exploring any alternative options
options.C: Ignore the cost increase and hope the overall project budget absorbs it without any communication
options.D: Absorb the cost increase by reducing quality standards elsewhere without informing anyone

justification: Correct. Assessing the actual impact, updating forecasts, and transparently communicating with the sponsor reflects proactive, responsible cost management in response to an external market factor affecting the budget.

text: Match each agile metric to what it primarily helps a team understand.

colonne_droite.texte: How much work the team typically completes per Sprint, useful for forecasting future capacity
How long it takes an individual work item to move from start to completion
How many defects reach production that should have been caught earlier in the process
How often the team achieves the specific objective they committed to for each Sprint

justification: Velocity measures the amount of work completed per Sprint, providing a basis for forecasting future team capacity based on historical performance. / Cycle time tracks how long individual items take to move through the workflow, helping identify flow efficiency and potential bottlenecks. / Escaped defects measure how many issues reach production that should have been caught by earlier quality processes, indicating the effectiveness of the team's quality practices. / Sprint Goal success rate tracks how consistently the team achieves its committed Sprint objective, providing insight into planning accuracy and delivery reliability.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a project's actual schedule performance has been consistently ahead of plan for several consecutive reporting periods. What is the BEST way to interpret and respond to this?

options.A: Assume this is always purely positive and requires no further investigation
options.B: Ignore the trend since being ahead of schedule is never a cause for concern
options.C: Investigate the reasons behind the consistent positive variance, which could reveal either genuine efficiency or potentially inaccurate original estimates, informing appropriate response
options.D: Immediately reduce the project schedule baseline without any investigation into the cause

justification: Correct. Investigating the reasons behind consistent positive variance helps distinguish between genuine efficiency and potentially inaccurate original estimating, informing whether any baseline or forecast adjustment is warranted.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a formally submitted change request that would significantly benefit the project but falls outside the currently approved budget. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Automatically approve the change since it would benefit the project, regardless of budget impact
options.B: Analyze the full cost and benefit impact of the proposed change, and present this analysis to the appropriate governance body (e.g., Change Control Board) for a funding decision
options.C: Automatically reject the change since it exceeds the current budget, without any further analysis
options.D: Implement the change immediately without going through any formal change control process

justification: Correct. Analyzing the full impact and presenting it to the appropriate governance body for a funding decision reflects proper, standard change control process for a change with significant budget implications.

text: A project manager discovers that three separate change requests, each individually approved by different stakeholders through informal email exchanges over the past month, collectively represent a 15% scope increase that was never formally processed through the project's defined change control process. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Formally document all three changes retroactively through the proper change control process, assessing their cumulative impact on scope, cost, and schedule, and obtaining proper governance approval
options.B: Ignore the process gap since the changes are already being worked on regardless
options.C: Reverse all three changes immediately without any stakeholder discussion, since they weren't properly processed
options.D: Continue proceeding with the informally approved changes since stakeholders already agreed to them individually

justification: Correct. Formally documenting the changes retroactively, assessing cumulative impact, and obtaining proper governance approval addresses the process gap responsibly while still respecting stakeholders' original informal agreement, ensuring proper baseline integrity going forward.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting biometric authentication (e.g., fingerprint, facial recognition) for the product, which would require handling highly sensitive biometric data. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Immediately implement biometric authentication without researching applicable biometric data privacy regulations
options.B: Refuse to explore biometric authentication since it deviates from the current authentication approach
options.C: Research applicable biometric data privacy regulations across target markets, and assess technical and legal implications before committing significant backlog investment
options.D: Assume biometric data can be handled with the same practices as regular user data without any specific research

justification: Correct. Researching applicable regulations and assessing implications before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a feature involving particularly sensitive data with significant regulatory considerations.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring entering a market with a state-owned enterprise as a required local partner due to government regulations. What should the product leader consider?

options.A: Refuse to support market entry since state-owned enterprise partnerships are inherently too complex
options.B: Assume the partnership requirement has no bearing on actual product development decisions
options.C: Understand how the required partnership might affect product requirements, data handling, or governance, and incorporate any resulting considerations into relevant backlog planning
options.D: Ignore the state-owned enterprise partnership requirement since it is purely a business development matter

justification: Correct. Understanding the partnership's potential product implications and incorporating relevant considerations into planning reflects thoughtful integration of a significant business environment factor into product decisions.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward offering carbon offset purchasing as an add-on feature for environmentally conscious customers. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Research legitimate, verifiable carbon offset providers and relevant industry standards, and validate genuine customer interest before committing significant backlog investment
options.B: Ignore the feature idea since it deviates from the product's current core functionality
options.C: Partner with any available carbon offset provider without verifying their legitimacy or actual environmental impact
options.D: Immediately build the carbon offset feature without researching legitimate carbon offset providers or verification standards

justification: Correct. Researching legitimate providers and standards, and validating genuine customer interest before major investment, reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a feature with real reputational and environmental integrity stakes.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward offering the product's data insights as a standalone data licensing product to third parties. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Assume existing customer agreements already permit this type of data licensing without any verification
options.B: Immediately begin licensing data to any interested third party without any privacy or contractual review
options.C: Assess the privacy, legal, and contractual implications of data licensing, ensuring compliance with existing customer agreements and privacy regulations before proceeding
options.D: Refuse to explore data licensing since it represents a significant departure from the current product-only business model

justification: Correct. Assessing privacy, legal, and contractual implications before proceeding reflects responsible, thorough evaluation of a business model shift involving genuinely sensitive customer data and significant compliance stakes.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring accepting a significant investment from a venture capital firm with a reputation for pushing rapid, aggressive growth strategies. What should the product leader consider regarding potential product implications?

options.A: Assume the investment will have no bearing on product strategy or priorities regardless of the investor's typical approach
options.B: Refuse to provide any input on the investment decision since it is purely a financial/executive matter
options.C: Immediately overhaul the entire product roadmap based on assumptions about what the investor might want, before any actual investment or direction has been confirmed
options.D: Consider how the investor's typical growth-focused expectations might influence future product priorities and roadmap discussions, preparing to have informed conversations about sustainable value delivery

justification: Correct. Considering the potential influence on future priorities and preparing for informed conversations about sustainable value delivery reflects thoughtful, proactive engagement with a likely significant business environment factor.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a newly enacted right-to-repair law affecting how the project's hardware product must be designed for consumer serviceability. What is the BEST way to address this for a current product development project?

options.A: Redesign the entire product from scratch without first understanding the specific requirements of the new law
options.B: Ignore the law since it primarily concerns product design, not project management
options.C: Continue with the current design approach without any assessment of right-to-repair compliance
options.D: Review the specific right-to-repair requirements, assess design gaps, and incorporate necessary design changes into the project plan with appropriate prioritization

justification: Correct. Reviewing specific requirements, assessing gaps, and incorporating necessary changes with appropriate prioritization reflects responsible, proactive integration of a legitimate new regulatory requirement into project planning.

text: A project manager's organization is bidding on a contract that requires meeting specific accessibility standards for government use (e.g., Section 508 in the US or equivalent). What is the BEST way to prepare?

options.A: Assume the current product already meets the required accessibility standards without any verification
options.B: Ignore the accessibility requirement since it is unlikely to be strictly enforced
options.C: Bid on the contract claiming full compliance without conducting any actual accessibility assessment
options.D: Conduct an accessibility audit against the specific required standards, and plan necessary remediation work if gaps are identified before or during the bid process

justification: Correct. Conducting a proper accessibility audit and planning necessary remediation reflects responsible, evidence-based preparation for meeting a legitimate, likely enforced government accessibility requirement.

text: Which of the following are examples of legitimate reasons an agile product team might need to pause or delay a planned feature release? (Select TWO)

options.A: A newly discovered critical security vulnerability that must be addressed before the feature can safely go live
options.B: A pending regulatory review that could affect the legality of the feature as currently designed
options.C: A single team member's personal preference to delay for no substantive reason
options.D: The release date happening to fall on a day the team finds personally inconvenient with no other substantive concern

justification: Correct. A newly discovered critical security vulnerability is a legitimate, serious reason to delay a release until it can be properly addressed, protecting users and the organization. / Correct. A pending regulatory review that could affect the feature's legality is a legitimate business environment reason to pause, avoiding potential compliance violations.

text: Which of the following are appropriate considerations when an agile team's organization is evaluating a potential merger with another company? (Select TWO)

options.A: Compatibility between the two companies' technology stacks and product architectures
options.B: Potential impact on the current product roadmap and customer commitments
options.C: The specific brand of coffee served in each company's office kitchen
options.D: The exact number of parking spaces at each company's headquarters

justification: Correct. Technology stack and architecture compatibility is a genuinely important consideration for evaluating integration feasibility and potential technical challenges of a merger. / Correct. Potential impact on the current roadmap and customer commitments is a critical consideration for understanding how a merger might affect ongoing product delivery and customer relationships.

text: Match each type of regulatory body to an example of its typical area of oversight.

colonne_droite.texte: Enforcing compliance with personal data privacy laws
Overseeing compliance with financial reporting and market conduct rules
Enforcing fair business practices and protecting consumers from deceptive practices
Enforcing compliance with environmental impact and emissions standards

justification: Data protection authorities enforce compliance with laws governing how personal data is collected, processed, and protected. / Financial regulators oversee compliance with financial reporting standards and market conduct rules to protect market integrity. / Consumer protection agencies enforce fair business practices, protecting consumers from deceptive or unfair conduct. / Environmental regulatory agencies enforce compliance with environmental standards, such as emissions or waste disposal requirements.

text: Match each type of business risk to its correct example.

colonne_droite.texte: A sudden shift in customer preferences away from the product's core value proposition
A key business partner defaulting on a financial obligation
A critical internal process failure disrupting normal business operations
Exposure to litigation due to a contractual dispute or regulatory violation

justification: Market risk relates to potential losses from adverse market movements or shifts, such as changing customer preferences affecting demand. / Credit risk relates to the potential for financial loss if a counterparty, such as a business partner, fails to meet their financial obligations. / Operational risk relates to potential losses from failures in internal processes, systems, or people disrupting normal operations. / Legal risk relates to potential losses from litigation, regulatory violations, or contractual disputes.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to new mandatory conflict minerals disclosure requirements affecting the sourcing of certain materials for a manufacturing project. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the requirement since sourcing verification is considered purely a procurement department matter
options.B: Work with procurement to trace and verify the sourcing of relevant materials, ensuring compliant disclosure and sourcing practices within the required timeline
options.C: Continue current sourcing practices without any verification against conflict minerals requirements
options.D: Provide estimated rather than verified sourcing information to save time and effort

justification: Correct. Working with procurement to properly trace and verify sourcing reflects responsible, proactive compliance with a legitimate, ethically significant regulatory requirement.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory algorithmic bias auditing requirement for AI systems used in hiring-related decisions. The current project includes an AI-powered candidate screening tool. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Conduct the required algorithmic bias audit using appropriate methodology, and incorporate any necessary remediation into the project plan based on the audit's findings
options.B: Assume the current screening tool is already free of bias without any actual auditing
options.C: Ignore the requirement since algorithmic bias is considered a purely technical/data science matter, not a project management concern
options.D: Discontinue the AI screening tool entirely without conducting any audit, simply to avoid the compliance burden

justification: Correct. Conducting the required audit and incorporating necessary remediation reflects responsible, proactive compliance with a legitimate and ethically important new regulatory requirement.

text: Which of the following are appropriate steps when a project's business case needs to be reassessed due to a major, unexpected external event (e.g., a global economic disruption)? (Select TWO)

options.A: Reassess the project's costs, benefits, and assumptions in light of the new external conditions
options.B: Communicate the situation transparently to the sponsor and relevant governance bodies for an informed continue/modify/cancel decision
options.C: Continue the project exactly as originally planned, assuming the external event has no relevance
options.D: Unilaterally cancel the project without any sponsor or governance consultation

justification: Correct. Reassessing costs, benefits, and assumptions in light of new external conditions is essential for understanding whether the business case remains valid. / Correct. Transparently communicating with the sponsor and governance bodies for an informed decision reflects proper governance and respects the appropriate decision-making authority for a significant business case reassessment.

text: A project manager's organization is bidding on an international contract that requires compliance with anti-bribery and corruption laws across multiple jurisdictions with varying standards. What is the BEST way to ensure compliance?

options.A: Assume standard business courtesy gifts are always acceptable regardless of jurisdiction-specific anti-bribery thresholds
options.B: Apply only the most lenient jurisdiction's anti-bribery standards across the entire project
options.C: Apply the strictest applicable anti-bribery and corruption standards across all relevant jurisdictions, consulting legal experts to ensure comprehensive compliance
options.D: Ignore anti-bribery requirements in jurisdictions where enforcement is perceived to be weaker

justification: Correct. Applying the strictest applicable standards across all relevant jurisdictions, with expert legal consultation, ensures comprehensive compliance regardless of jurisdiction-specific variations, protecting against legal exposure everywhere the project operates.

text: A project manager notices that a team member consistently defers to others during technical disagreements, even when their own expertise is directly relevant to the topic. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Have a private conversation to understand the reason for their deference, and encourage them to share their expertise confidently when directly relevant
options.B: Publicly call on them to speak during every technical discussion regardless of their comfort level
options.C: Assume they simply have nothing valuable to contribute in these situations
options.D: Ignore the pattern since deferring to others is generally a sign of good teamwork

justification: Correct. A private conversation to understand the reason and encourage confident sharing of relevant expertise addresses the root cause supportively while respecting their communication style.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint Review lacking substantive discussion because stakeholders passively accept whatever is shown without providing genuine feedback. What is the BEST way to encourage more substantive engagement?

options.A: Require stakeholders to provide written feedback forms with no verbal discussion opportunity
options.B: Accept the passive responses as sufficient feedback and move on
options.C: Ask specific, open-ended questions about particular aspects of the Increment, and create space for stakeholders to share concerns or alternative perspectives, rather than simply asking if everything looks good
options.D: Stop asking for any feedback since stakeholders seem satisfied with the current approach

justification: Correct. Asking specific, open-ended questions and creating space for genuine concerns actively encourages more substantive engagement than a simple yes/no acceptance check.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward supporting multi-language localization for the product, targeting several new international markets simultaneously. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Ignore localization needs since the current single-language approach has generated some revenue
options.B: Assume localization is purely a translation task with no other technical or cultural considerations
options.C: Immediately localize the product into every possible language without prioritizing based on actual market opportunity
options.D: Research the relative market opportunity and localization complexity for each target language/market, and prioritize backlog work accordingly, starting with the highest-value markets

justification: Correct. Researching relative market opportunity and complexity, then prioritizing accordingly, reflects responsible, evidence-based backlog planning for a significant multi-market expansion effort.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a critical activity's actual resource requirement turned out to be significantly different from the original plan, though the activity has not yet started. What is the BEST way to proceed?

options.A: Update the resource plan to reflect the newly identified actual requirement, reassessing schedule and cost impact before the activity begins
options.B: Cancel the activity entirely due to the resource discrepancy without exploring adjustment options
options.C: Ignore the discrepancy since the original plan was already approved
options.D: Proceed with the original resource plan despite the newly identified discrepancy

justification: Correct. Updating the plan to reflect newly identified accurate requirements, and reassessing impact before execution begins, reflects proactive, responsible planning adjustment based on improved information.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their questions during Sprint Planning are dismissed as 'slowing things down.' What is the BEST way for the Scrum Master to address this?

options.A: Ignore the concern since Sprint Planning does have a timebox that must be respected
options.B: Agree that questions do slow things down and should be minimized
options.C: Tell the team member to save all questions for after Sprint Planning concludes
options.D: Reinforce with the team that clarifying questions during Sprint Planning genuinely improve shared understanding and reduce later rework, and address any specific dismissive behavior directly

justification: Correct. Reinforcing the genuine value of clarifying questions, while addressing any specific dismissive behavior, corrects the harmful dynamic while still respecting the event's purpose and timebox.

text: Which of the following are valid inputs to the Sequence Activities process? (Select TWO)

options.A: Activity list
options.B: Milestone list
options.C: The final project closure report from a previous, unrelated project
options.D: The organization's marketing budget

justification: Correct. The activity list is a fundamental input needed to determine the logical sequence and dependencies between activities. / Correct. The milestone list provides key reference points that can inform and constrain how activities are sequenced relative to important project checkpoints.

text: A project manager's organization is subject to a new mandatory whistleblower reward program related to government contract fraud reporting. What is the BEST way to prepare the project team for this?

options.A: Ensure the team understands the organization's ethical standards and reporting channels, reinforcing a culture where genuine concerns can be raised appropriately, regardless of this specific external program
options.B: Ignore the program since it primarily concerns fraud, which the project manager assumes doesn't apply to their well-run project
options.C: Assume the program has no relevance to project-level operations or team awareness
options.D: Actively discourage team members from ever raising any concerns to avoid triggering whistleblower processes

justification: Correct. Ensuring team understanding of ethical standards and reporting channels, reinforcing a culture supporting appropriate concern-raising, reflects responsible integration of the underlying ethical principles this program is designed to support.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that during Sprint Retrospectives, one team member consistently proposes the same solution to every problem raised, regardless of the specific issue's nature. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Ignore the pattern since having a consistent go-to solution shows valuable decisiveness
options.B: Automatically implement their proposed solution every time to save discussion time
options.C: Facilitate a discussion exploring whether the proposed solution genuinely fits each specific problem, encouraging the team to consider a broader range of potential approaches
options.D: Exclude their input entirely from future Retrospectives

justification: Correct. Facilitating discussion about whether the proposed solution genuinely fits each specific problem encourages more thoughtful, tailored problem-solving while still respecting the team member's input.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment containing usability issues that automated tests cannot detect. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Assume automated tests cover all necessary quality dimensions including usability
options.B: Rely exclusively on automated testing for all quality verification
options.C: Skip any human-centered quality evaluation since it is considered too subjective to be useful
options.D: Incorporate periodic usability testing with real or representative users as part of the team's broader quality practice, complementing automated testing

justification: Correct. Incorporating periodic usability testing with real or representative users directly addresses the usability quality dimension that automated tests typically cannot capture, complementing rather than replacing automated testing.

text: Match each type of customer segmentation approach to its correct description.

colonne_droite.texte: Grouping customers based on characteristics like age, income, or education level
Grouping customers based on their actions, such as purchase history or product usage patterns
Grouping customers based on values, interests, and lifestyle characteristics
Grouping customers based on their physical location or region

justification: Demographic segmentation groups customers based on measurable characteristics like age, income, education, or occupation. / Behavioral segmentation groups customers based on their actual actions and patterns, such as purchase frequency or product usage behavior. / Psychographic segmentation groups customers based on more subjective factors like values, interests, attitudes, and lifestyle. / Geographic segmentation groups customers based on their physical location, which can inform region-specific product or marketing decisions.

text: A project manager wants to help a team member who has expressed anxiety about an upcoming high-visibility presentation to senior executives. What is the BEST way to provide support?

options.A: Dismiss their anxiety as an overreaction requiring no support
options.B: Take over the presentation entirely to eliminate their anxiety
options.C: Tell them not to worry since the presentation isn't that important
options.D: Offer practical support such as reviewing their materials together, practicing the presentation, and providing constructive feedback, while validating that some anxiety about high-visibility presentations is normal

justification: Correct. Offering practical support like reviewing materials and practicing together, combined with validating that some anxiety is normal, provides genuine, actionable help while respecting their feelings.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a project's actual quality inspection pass rate has been steadily declining over several consecutive periods, despite no known process changes. What is the BEST way to investigate this?

options.A: Assume the decline is random noise and requires no investigation
options.B: Lower the quality inspection pass rate threshold to match the declining trend
options.C: Immediately replace the entire quality inspection team without any investigation
options.D: Conduct root cause analysis to identify what might be driving the steady decline, considering factors like team fatigue, changing work complexity, or gradual process drift

justification: Correct. Conducting root cause analysis to identify potential drivers, such as fatigue, complexity changes, or process drift, provides the evidence-based understanding needed to address a genuine, sustained quality decline.

text: A team member consistently expresses that they feel their part-time contractor status makes them feel like a 'second-class' team member compared to full-time employees. What is the BEST way for the project leader to address this?

options.A: Agree that contractors inherently have a different, lesser status on the team
options.B: Exclude the contractor from all team decisions to formally reflect their different status
options.C: Ignore the concern since contractor status differences are simply an unavoidable organizational reality
options.D: Explicitly reinforce that all team members, regardless of employment classification, are valued equally for their contributions, and ensure inclusive practices genuinely reflect this in day-to-day team interactions

justification: Correct. Explicitly reinforcing equal value and ensuring genuinely inclusive practices directly addresses the concern, supporting a fair, collaborative team culture regardless of employment classification.

text: A team wants to reduce the risk of a Sprint's Increment being deployed with configuration errors due to manual deployment processes. What is the BEST proactive practice?

options.A: Assign deployment responsibility to the most junior team member to build their experience, without any additional safeguards
options.B: Continue relying entirely on manual deployment processes since the team is already familiar with them
options.C: Skip deployment validation entirely to speed up the release process
options.D: Implement automated deployment pipelines with configuration validation checks to reduce the risk of human error in the deployment process

justification: Correct. Implementing automated deployment pipelines with validation checks directly reduces the risk of human error inherent in manual deployment processes, a standard best practice for reliable delivery.

text: An agile team's organization is exploring a shift toward offering a lifetime access purchase option in addition to the current subscription model, which could significantly affect long-term revenue projections. What should the product leader do FIRST?

options.A: Work with finance to model the long-term revenue implications of offering lifetime access, and validate the concept's viability before committing significant backlog investment
options.B: Assume lifetime access pricing can be set arbitrarily without any financial analysis
options.C: Ignore the idea since it deviates from the current subscription-only business model
options.D: Immediately implement the lifetime access option without any financial modeling of its long-term revenue impact

justification: Correct. Working with finance to model long-term implications and validating viability before major investment reflects responsible, evidence-based evaluation of a business model change with significant financial stakes.

text: A project manager needs to determine the appropriate way to handle a situation where a formally documented assumption used in project planning has proven to be incorrect, discovered mid-execution. What is the BEST FIRST step?

options.A: Assess the impact of the incorrect assumption on the current plan, and update relevant documents and communicate with stakeholders as needed through appropriate change processes
options.B: Immediately halt the entire project without any assessment of the actual impact
options.C: Ignore the incorrect assumption since the plan is already approved and in execution
options.D: Quietly correct the assumption in documentation without informing any stakeholders

justification: Correct. Assessing the impact and updating documents/communicating through appropriate change processes reflects responsible, transparent management of an incorrect assumption discovered during execution.

text: A team's Scrum Master notices that team members frequently express uncertainty about who has final decision-making authority on certain types of technical choices. What is the BEST way to address this?

options.A: Assume the ambiguity will naturally resolve itself over time without any intervention
options.B: Ignore the uncertainty since technical decisions will eventually get made regardless of clarity around authority
options.C: Assign the Scrum Master personally as the final decision-maker for all technical choices
options.D: Facilitate a team discussion to explicitly clarify decision-making authority for different types of technical choices, documenting the agreed approach as a team working agreement

justification: Correct. Facilitating explicit clarification and documenting an agreed team working agreement directly resolves the ambiguity, providing clear, shared understanding going forward.

text: Which of the following are valid ways to reduce the risk of a Sprint's forecast being disrupted by unclear acceptance criteria discovered mid-Sprint? (Select TWO)

options.A: Strengthen Backlog Refinement practices to ensure acceptance criteria are clarified before items enter Sprint Planning
options.B: Encourage Developers to ask clarifying questions of the Product Owner as soon as ambiguity is noticed, rather than making unverified assumptions
options.C: Have Developers guess at acceptance criteria without any Product Owner involvement to save time
options.D: Avoid discussing acceptance criteria at all during Sprint Planning to move faster

justification: Correct. Strengthening refinement practices to clarify acceptance criteria before Sprint Planning directly reduces the risk of mid-Sprint ambiguity discovery. / Correct.
